processes.description:
ABAP Core Data Services Extraction for SAP Data Intelligence (53M)

Overview

Accelerate your ABAP core data services extraction from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Data Intelligence. You must perform additional configuration steps to activate the ABAP core data services integration scenario between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Data Intelligence.

Key Process Flow

  • Use SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition core data services views to integrate with SAP Data Intelligence extraction

Business Benefits

  • Expose services from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Data Intelligence Platform

  • Create connection in SAP Data Intelligence Platform to access these services

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant if you require integration with SAP Data Intelligence.

This scope item is an integration scenario. It should only be requested for the extraction of ABAP core data services views from SAP Data Intelligence.
processes.name: ABAP Core Data Services Extraction for SAP Data Intelligence

ABAP Core Data Services Extraction for SAP Datasphere (53L)

Overview

Accelerate your ABAP core data services extraction from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Datasphere. You must perform additional configuration steps to activate the ABAP OData integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Datasphere.

Business Benefits

  • Create cloud data integration connection in SAP Datasphere to access these OData services

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant if you require integration with SAP Datasphere.

This scope item is an integration scenario. It should only be requested for the extraction of ABAP core data services views from SAP Datasphere.
processes.name: ABAP Core Data Services Extraction for SAP Datasphere

ABAP Core Data Services Extraction for SAP HANA (6N4)

Accelerate your ABAP core data services data extraction from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP HANA by performing the configuration steps to bridge the integration between the two systems.

Business Benefits

processes.description:
Account Reconciliation – SAP Solution Extensions by BlackLine (6IL)

Overview

This service automates and standardizes the balance sheet account reconciliation process to produce high-quality and accurate financial statements. It drives accuracy in the financial close by providing accountants with a streamlined method to verify the correctness and appropriateness of their balance sheets.

Accountants can quickly compare general ledger, bank, and other data, at the balance or line-item level, investigate discrepancies, attach supporting documentation, and take required actions from an intuitive, unified workspace.

This scope item covers the integration to the BlackLine Cloud connector.

Key Process Flow

  • Auto-import G/L balances and line items

  • View reconciliations and supporting Items

  • Add comments and supporting documents

  • Certify account

Business Benefits

  • Streamline decentralized and disjointed workflows

  • Reduce the threat to the integrity of financial statements

  • Reduce the risk of control failure

  • Shorten cycle times

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires an additional SAP Solution Extensions by BlackLine product license.
processes.name: Account Reconciliation – SAP Solution Extensions by BlackLine

processes.description:
Accounting and Financial Close – Group Ledger IFRS (1GA)

Overview

General Ledger Accounting provides a comprehensive overview of external accounting and accounts and supports parallel accounting.

General Ledger Accounting serves as a complete record of all business transactions, providing a centralized, up-to-date reference for the rendering of accounts. Actual individual transactions can be checked at any time in real-time processing by displaying the original documents, line items, and transaction figures at various levels to support parallel accounting. These transactions include:

  • Manage Journal Entries

  • Post with Clearing for Ledger Group

  • Run Automatic Clearing Specific to Ledger Groups

  • Trial Balance Comparison

  • Financial Statement Ledger Comparison

Key Process Flow

  • Manage journal entries

  • Maintain accounts: Automatic and manual clearing to ledger group

  • Perform day-end, month-end, and year-end closing

Business Benefits

  • Record all business transactions to ensure complete and accurate accounting data in parallel accounting

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is applicable for businesses adhering to IFRS accounting standards.
processes.name: Accounting and Financial Close – Group Ledger IFRS

processes.description:
Accounting and Financial Close – Group Ledger US GAAP (2VA)

Overview

The central tasks of General Ledger accounting are to provide a comprehensive picture of external accounting and accounts and to support parallel accounting.

General Ledger Accounting serves as a complete record of all business transactions providing a centralized, up-to-date reference for the rendering of accounts. Actual individual transactions can be checked at any time in real-time processing by displaying the original documents, line items, and transaction figures at various levels to support parallel accounting. These transactions include Manage Journal Entries, Post with Clearing for Ledger Group, Run Automatic Clearing Specific to Ledger Groups, Trial Balance Comparison, and Financial Statement Ledger Comparison.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage journal entries

  • Maintain accounts: Automatic and manual clearing to ledger group

  • Perform day-end, month-end, and year-end closing

Business Benefits

  • Record all business transactions to ensure complete and accurate accounting data in parallel accounting

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

All starter, demo, and trial systems are set up by default with group ledger IFRS. This scope item is therefore excluded. Customers can decide to use this scope items in their system landscape based on the selected scope bundle.
processes.name: Accounting and Financial Close – Group Ledger US GAAP

processes.description:
Accounting and Financial Close (J58)

Overview

The central task of general ledger accounting is to provide a comprehensive overview of external accounting and accounts. By recording all business transactions, including primary postings and settlements from internal accounting, in a system that is fully integrated with all the other operational areas of a company, you ensure accuracy and completeness for accounting data.

General ledger accounting serves as a complete record of all business transactions, providing a centralized, current reference for the rendering of accounts. Actual individual transactions are reviewed with real-time processing, displaying the original documents, line items, and transaction figures at various levels (such as account information, journals, totals, transaction figures, and balance sheets).

This process describes all required period end-closing steps, related to performing local period-end closing and steps that are identical for local and parallel ledgers.

Key Process Flow

  • Post general ledger account documents

  • Display the document journal

  • Display G/L balances (list)

  • Perform recurring entries

  • Maintain accounts with automatic and manual clearing

  • Perform day-end closing

  • Perform month-end closing

  • Perform year-end closing

Business Benefits

  • Record all business transactions to ensure complete and accurate accounting data
processes.name: Accounting and Financial Close

processes.description:
Accounting Enhancements for Banking (5NU)

Overview

Accounting enhancements for banking focus on delivering a banking-specific solution for general ledger accounting. A key feature is the ready-made global chart of accounts (YCOA) tailored for banks. This is combined with dimensions that support multi-dimensional accounting, aiding both financial and regulatory reporting. Alongside banking-specific accounts, banks receive a financial statement version.

We offer starter content that includes banking-specific cost centers, cost center groups, profit centers, and profit center groups. Additionally, we provide dimensions like product group, branch, data source, customer group, industry, and country/region. These dimensions enable banks to perform multi-dimensional accounting effectively.

Ensure that scoping in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition starts with the Baseline Accelerator bundle.

Key Process Flow

  • Post general ledger account documents

  • Display the document journal

  • Display G/L balances (list)

  • Perform recurring entries

  • Manage values for banking-specific dimensions

Business Benefits

  • The recording of all business transactions ensures complete and accurate accounting data for banking

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item creates additional accounts in YCOA that are only needed for financial accounting for banks.

Before you activate this scope item, check whether you need the capabilities of the scope item.

You can activate this scope item only if you use a 3-system landscape and if you configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as the configuration environment.
processes.name: Accounting Enhancements for Banking

processes.description:
Accounting Enhancements for Insurance (78J)

Overview

This scope item provides an insurance-specific solution for general ledger accounting. The main feature is a ready-made global chart of accounts (YCOA) for insurance carriers that is combined with dimensions for financial services to enable multi-dimensional accounting to support both financial and regulatory reporting. In addition to insurance-specific accounts, a financial statement version is provided for insurance carriers.

We provide starter content that includes an insurance-specific product group hierarchy, cost centers, cost center groups, profit centers, and profit center groups. We also provide dimensions, such as product group, branch, data source, customer group, industry, and country/region, to enable multi-dimensional accounting for insurance carriers.

Ensure that scoping in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition starts with the Baseline Accelerator bundle.

Key Process Flow

  • Post general ledger account document

  • Display the document journal

  • Display G/L balances (list)

  • Perform recurring entries

  • Manage values for insurance-specific dimensions

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item creates additional accounts in YCOA that are only needed for financial accounting for insurance carriers.

Before you activate this scope item, check if you need the capabilities of the scope item.

This scope item can only be activated if you use a 3-system landscape and if you configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as the configuration environment.
processes.name: Accounting Enhancements for Insurance

processes.description:
Accounting Interface for Contract and Lease Management (7OD)

Overview

This scope item facilitates seamless integration between third-party applications and SAP Contract and Lease Management, enabling efficient event-based postings to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. This integration is particularly crucial for organizations utilizing external applications for order-based transactions, ensuring that all financial activities are accurately captured and reflected within the SAP S/4HANA ecosystem.

Two major business scenarios end up in a cost collection on the third-party side for allocation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: event-based (such as reservation of a meeting room), and internal space/workplace occupancy.

Key Process Flow

  • Create real estate cost allocation accounting notifications via third-party applications

  • Post real estate cost allocation accounting notifications

  • Automatically create journal entry item if posting date is due

Business Benefits

  • simplified efficient and accurate financial postings to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • supports multiple business scenarios

  • leverages key accounting objects to provide comprehensive financial management

  • enables insights on financial figures to optimize the real estate portfolio with SAP Analytics

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires additional manual set-up steps. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Accounting Interface for Contract and Lease Management

processes.description:
Accounts Payable (J60)

Overview

With Accounts Payable, you manage your open payable invoices that are automatically created from purchasing processes.

You manage and control open items with various analytical tools. You plan future payables and analyze the outcome of payments, such as utilization of cash discounts and days payables outstanding.

Automate processing of your outstanding payables and monitor payment progress. Optionally, you can also include a two-step approval for all outgoing payments.

Connect to SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (MBC) to streamline the connectivity to the banks for payments and bank statements. Alternatively, you can also download generated payment files.

For applicable countries or regions, you can also print checks.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage and complete supplier master data

  • Create invoice from logistics

  • Analyze outstanding payables

  • Pay invoices

  • Approve payments (optional)

  • Forward payments to banks via SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (MBC) or download payment file

  • Analyze efficiency of payment processing

Business Benefits

  • Integrate accounts payable into procurement

  • Record accounts payable posting directly in the general ledger

  • Use payment program to automatically create instructions for bank transfers

  • Use payment approval for workflow

  • Use simple and secure connectivity for transacting with multiple financial institutes or download the payment instruction file for further manual processing

  • Analyze the efficiency of your payment processing
processes.name: Accounts Payable

processes.description:
Accounts Receivable (J59)

Overview

With Accounts Receivable, you manage open receivables invoices that are automatically created from sales processes. Using various analytical tools, you can manage and control open items to optimize accounts receivables handling. The primary source of incoming payments is incoming bank statements that are loaded within the Cash Management process and automatically reconciled with open invoices. User-friendly views simplify and streamline the post processing of open items.

Alternatively, you can manually post incoming payments and easily reconcile the payment with an open item. Several analytical tools are available to monitor the receivables, allowing you to react quickly if you discover a declining payment discipline among your customers. You can effortlessly generate dunning letters for overdue items and track your customers' dunning history.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage and complete customer master data

  • Analyze open items

  • Reconcile open invoices with incoming payments automatically

  • Process unassigned incoming payments to open invoices easily and efficiently

  • Analyze efficiency of payment collection processing

  • Process customer correspondence

  • Process overdue item interest calculation

Business Benefits

  • Provide more detailed and comprehensive analysis of Accounts Receivable

  • Provide automatic incoming payments clearing with the Electronic Bank Statement and rule-based reprocessing for incomplete items

  • Process dunning of overdue items easily

  • Process customer correspondence such as account statement or balance confirmation easily

  • Provide item level interest calculation for overdue invoices
processes.name: Accounts Receivable

processes.description:
Actual Costing (33Q)

Overview

This solution process enables actual costing for material inventory. Initially, all goods movements in a period are valuated based on standard price. All price and exchange rate differences for the material are collected in the material ledger. Similarly, all confirmations are valuated based on a standard activity rate.

At the end of the period, an actual price (called the periodic unit price) is calculated for each material based on actual costs within the period, and an actual activity rate is calculated based on the actual costs for the cost center. This calculated actual price can then be used to revalue inventory, COGS and WIP at period end. For actual costing, to calculate the periodic unit price for your materials, you need to activate actual costing in addition to the material ledger. You also need to choose single-level or multilevel price determination for your materials and use price control standard price for all materials you want to use in actual costing.

Key Process Flow

  • Execute actual price calculation

  • Create a costing run

  • Analyze total material price related to movement and current stock

  • Monitor material quantity

Business Benefits

  • Revalue ending inventory, COGS, WIP, and ending material inventory at period-end based on actual costing

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is excluded from standard scope as this enables actual costing, a more complex costing method that is only required by some businesses.
processes.name: Actual Costing

processes.description:
Advanced Available-to-Promise – Consumer Products (6N0)

Overview

The scope item outlines the process for configuring and checking availability in several key areas. It allows you to replace the original requirement in an order document with a default storage location using Alternative-Based Confirmation (ABC). This feature is particularly useful when substituting a product for a specific period, such as during a company's jubilee celebration with a limited edition product. Once the limited edition stock is depleted, the remaining quantity will be fulfilled with the originally requested product using ABC.

Furthermore, you can optimize product availability during order creation and modification by prioritizing incoming demand through Supply Protection (SUP).

This scope item builds upon the capabilities provided by Basic Available-to-Promise Processing (2LN).

Key Process Flow

  • Manage characteristic combinations

  • Configure alternative determination (Optional)

  • Configure substitution strategy

  • Configure alternative control

  • Create reason for storage location substitution (Optional)

  • Create storage location substitution

  • Create reason for substitution (optional)

  • Create product substitution

  • Configure supply protection (SUP) characteristics (Optional)

  • Create master data for supply protection (SUP)

  • Check availability in sales order

  • Handle sales order before jubilee period

  • Handle sales order during jubilee period

  • Handle large sales order during jubilee period

  • Handle large sales order during jubilee period with SUP

Business Benefits

  • Execute a product availability check at order creation

  • Configure and schedule backorder processing

  • Monitor the results of backorder processing

  • Adapt and extend characteristic catalogs for product allocation, backorder processing, and alternative-based confirmation

  • Display if ordered products can be delivered in time and quantity

  • Display when and how much of the ordered product will presumably be delivered

  • Display if and which alternative shipping locations were found and used

  • Fine-tune and optimize confirmations

  • Monitor product availability
processes.name: Advanced Available-to-Promise – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Advanced Available-to-Promise Processing (1JW)

Overview

This scope item details the process for configuring and checking availability against defined quantities during specific time periods. Furthermore, this scope item enables you to manually prioritize requirements in order documents for materials in limited supply and release them for subsequent delivery.

You can also use this scope item to perform substitution of an originally requested delivery plant or storage location (with an alternative plant or storage location) or material when a requested requirement can't be confirmed in terms of material, requested quantity, or date. Additionally, you can pass the order along to a third-party supplier who then ships the goods directly to the customer.

This scope item enables you to define protected quantities for prioritized supply protection groups so that even in shortage situations some minimum quantities are left for these groups.

The SAP Fiori app Configure Activity Attributes can be used to flexibly determine duration and working times of scheduling activities based on document characteristics to address your business needs.

This scope item builds on the features from the Basic Available-to-Promise Processing (2LN) scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Configure, manage and monitor product allocation

  • Manually prioritize due order documents for materials with limited availability and release reprioritized documents for delivery

  • Fulfill a requirement by replacing the originally requested delivery plant/storage location with an alternative plant/storage location

  • Fulfill a requirement by replacing the originally requested material with an alternative material

  • Define supply protection groups that are considered as virtual demands in the product availability check to restrict the available quantity dependent on the importance of the demand

Business Benefits

  • Plan and manage allocations for products and perform availability checks against these allocations

  • Fulfill order requirements manually when quantities are insufficient and trigger subsequent logistics processes

  • Substitute the delivering plant for sales order items with an alternative plant (either for an entire line item or a subitem) or storage location

  • Substitute a requested material with an alternative material

  • Protect stock and supply according to the importance of the demand of defined protection groups in supply protection to guarantee at least minimum quantities for important groups even in shortage situations.
processes.name: Advanced Available-to-Promise Processing

processes.description:
Advanced Bank Account Management (J77)

Overview

With Advanced Bank Account Management, the cash managers and the bank accountants can manage the bank and account master data centrally and maintain signatories in multiple bank accounts. The result of the maintenance can be activated with different control patterns. They can also view the bank and bank account related master data with reports and fact sheets and look at an annual review.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage banks and bank accounts (in Direct Revision Activate; Dual Control Revision Activate; Workflow Revision Activate mode; Two-Person mode)

  • Maintain signatory in multiple bank accounts (in Direct Revision Activate; Dual Control Revision Activate; Workflow Revision Activate mode)

  • Review bank account yearly

  • View bank account reports and fact sheets

Business Benefits

  • Centrally manage global banks and bank accounts, in different control patterns

  • Centrally maintain signatories in multiple bank accounts, in different control patterns

  • View bank and bank account related master data with reports and fact sheets

  • Review bank account yearly
processes.name: Advanced Bank Account Management

processes.description:
Advanced Bank Statement Automation (4X8)

Overview

Advanced Bank Statement Automation creates templates for reprocessing rules by learning from past patterns of the manual actions taken during the reprocessing of the bank statement items. Instead of only being able to create reprocessing rules manually, you can use the templates to create reprocessing rules more easily.

Moreover, with the scope item activated, the reprocessing of bank statement items is triggered automatically following the initial posting. Thus, the system applies the corresponding reprocessing rules to the pending items to complete the postings.

Key Process Flow

  • Reprocess bank statement based on the automated reprocessing rules

  • Propose the reprocessing rules based on the past manual reprocessing actions

Business Benefits

  • Save effort in this labor-intensive process

  • Consume the fully integrated business process easily
processes.name: Advanced Bank Statement Automation

processes.description:
Advanced Cash Operations (J78)

Overview

Advanced Cash Operations offers a consistent view of your actual cash position and short/mid-term cash forecasts. Drill-down features are provided for the detailed transactions and rich dimensions are provided for the analysis. You can also compare the actual and forecasted cash flow with forecasted figures.

This scope item also allows you to make bank transfer and track its status, and to approve the bank payments and monitor the payment processing status.

Key Process Flow

  • Perform and track bank transfers

  • Approve and monitor bank payments

  • Monitor bank statement processing status

  • Check cash reports (for example, Check Cash Position, Check Cash Flow Items, Cash Flow Analyzer, Cash Flow Comparison)

Business Benefits

  • Analyze cash position with finest granularity drill-down

  • Forecast the liquidity trend and analyze the actual cash flows with rich dimensions (planning level, G/L account, planning group) in cash reports such as CCFI (Check Cash Flow Items) and CFA (Cash Flow Analyzer)

  • Use advanced capabilities of Cash Flow Analyzer with bank account group view and liquidity item hierarchy view

  • Compare the forecast snapshots made in the history with the actual cash flows

  • Facilitate cash operations such as making bank transfers, tracking transfer statuses, approving payments (BCM integration), and monitoring payments

  • Monitor the status of bank statement import processing easily
processes.name: Advanced Cash Operations

processes.description:
Advanced Credit Management (1QM)

Overview

Your company's business outcomes are directly impacted by the creditworthiness and payment practices of your business partners. Effective management of receivables and credit can mitigate financial loss risks, thereby enhancing relationships with the said partners. Advanced Credit Management aids your company in recognizing possible receivables loss risks early on and in making efficient credit decisions. The Credit Controller can rapidly make credit decisions using flexible, automatic calculation formulas.

Advanced Credit Management compares the existing credit limit with your business partner's exposure. The credit limit can be verified when sales documents, service contracts, or service orders are changed. Additionally, you can execute credit limit requests. Other checks, such as the oldest open item, maximum dunning level, or last payment, can also be conducted. If a new order is blocked, authorized personnel can either release or reject it.

Key Process Flow

  • Calculate rating, risk class, and credit limit for new and existing customers

  • Create or change sales order, service order, or service contract

  • Check exposure against credit limit

  • Manage credit accounts

  • Manage blocked orders

  • Perform credit limit request

  • Run credit management reports

  • Import credit account hierarchies

Business Benefits

  • Reduce risk of bad debt

  • Calculate rating, risk class, and credit limit automatically (eventing)

  • Perform credit limit requests

  • Focus on reliable and profitable customers

  • Check credit worthiness quickly

  • Accelerate the process of checking a customer credit limit
processes.name: Advanced Credit Management

processes.description:
Advanced Down Payment in Retail (7ZJ)

Overview

Advanced down payments enable customers to make either a partial or full payment for a product upfront at the store. In a retail context, this is useful for high-value items such as appliances and furniture, where an initial payment is required to initiate the order fulfilment process.

The system handles the entire process starting with creating the sales order, generating the down payment request, recording the payment at the Point-of-Sale (POS), and creating a final invoice that automatically deducts the already paid down payment amount. The final invoice is also be paid at the POS.

This process leverages the billing plan functionality within sales orders, supports delivery-related billing with down payment settlement, and ensures seamless integration between sales and financial transactions through a consistent and transparent document flow.

The scope also covers the seamless integration of the retail logistics for picking and handing over the eligible items with down payments to the customers.

In essence, the advanced down payment process provides a unified approach to managing customer prepayments, logistics, and billing ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and a superior retail experience.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order and assign billing plan

  • Create down payment request

  • Remove delivery block through payment at point-of-sale (POS)

  • For immediate pickup items: Create the outbound delivery, complete picking, post the goods issue and generate final invoice with down payment settlement

  • For later (scheduled) pickup items: Perform picking using the Process Picking Requests application, complete the handover using the Hand Over Orders application and create the customer invoice (final invoice) with down payment settlement

Business Benefits

  • Enhance liquidity and enable more effective financial risk management with flexible customer down payment options

  • Improve store employee productivity by providing an efficient and user-intuitive application to pick and fulfill the orders with down payments

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

You can only activate this scope item if you have a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and have activated the retail bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Advanced Down Payment in Retail

processes.description:
Advanced Financial Closing Integration (4HG)

Overview

SAP Advanced Financial Closing is a standalone public cloud solution delivered on SAP BTP to orchestrate the financial close process. The solution supports the planning, execution, monitoring, and analysis of recurring financial tasks for all entities of a corporation. You can define closing task lists, assign responsibilities, parameters, and dependencies. Besides embedded workflows and approval functionality, the cockpit also contains detailed analytical apps and KPIs to monitor the closing process in real time.

This scope item provides connection setup between SAP S/4HANA Cloud and SAP Advanced Financial Closing, and the steps on SAP Advanced Financial Closing to orchestrate the financial closing activities.

Key Process Flow

  • Set up connection between SAP S/4HANA Cloud and SAP Advanced Financial Closing

  • Monitor communication systems

  • Manage closing task lists

  • Process closing task lists

Business Benefits

  • Streamline closing cycles and earlier insights into the financial figures with full process modeling and analytics functions

  • Provide transparency, compliance, and governance enhanced within the closing process, including a full audit trail

  • Increase level of automation and efficiency to achieve an accelerated closing process

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is a container for the Financial Tasklist Integration communication scenario (SAP_COM_0566). The communication scenario is managed by the customer. If your business needs require it, you can activate it and set up the integration.

This scope needs additional products license.
processes.name: Advanced Financial Closing Integration

processes.description:
Advanced Intercompany Sales – Make-to-Order and Variant Config (7DM)

Overview

This scope item enables advanced variant configuration (Make-to-Order Production with Variant Configuration (1YT)) in advanced intercompany sales. It partially combines those functions and requires the following scope items as business conditions:

  • Advanced Intercompany Sales Processing (5D2)

  • Make-to-Order Production with Variant Configuration (1YT)

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order with configure product (single level)

  • Create purchase order

  • Create intercompany sales order

  • Manufacturing steps:

    • Run MRP

    • Create planned order

    • Create production order

    • Post goods receipt (to sales order stock)

  • Create outbound delivery

  • Post stock transfer (valuated stock in transit) from delivering to selling company and from selling company to customer

  • Create intercompany billing document

  • Create supplier invoice

  • Create customer invoice

  • Use value chain monitor to track postings

Business Benefits

Support for make-to-order processing and variant configuration with advanced intercompany sales processing

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This is an advanced intercompany-relevant scope item and requires significant additional manual setup steps.

If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Advanced Intercompany Sales – Make-to-Order and Variant Config

processes.description:
Advanced Intercompany Sales (5D2)

Overview

This scope item enables you to sell from stock and manage intercompany sales transactions seamlessly between affiliated organizations. A new process creates an additional purchase order in the selling company and a sales order in the delivery company.

This process utilizes valuated stock in transit (VSIT) to support several key functions. It allows for profitability reporting for both affiliated companies and ensures a seamless change of control between affiliates and the customer. Additionally, it supports event-based revenue recognition and provides detailed insights through the material ledger and cost component split. The process also includes integrated product and trade compliance checks and is fully integrated into transportation management, including the management of freight costs.

Key Process Flow

  • Create Sales Order

  • Create Purchase Order

  • Create Intercompany Sales Order

  • Create Outbound delivery

  • Post Stock Transfer (Valuated Stock in Transit) from Delivering to Selling Company and from Selling Company to Customer

  • Create Intercompany Billing document

  • Create Supplier Invoice

  • Create Customer Invoice

  • Use Value Chain Monitor to track postings

Business Benefits

  • Design, run, and monitor intercompany sales processes – fully integrated, highly automated, and end to end

  • Support legal compliance (IFRS 15 matching principle and arm's length principle)

  • Support consistent flow of values throughout logistical transactions

  • Get harmonized data from logistics to finance to consolidation

  • Keep financial and material ledger postings in sync with full audit transparency

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This is an advanced intercompany-relevant scope item and requires significant additional manual setup steps.

If you requested this scope item, please see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.

.
processes.name: Advanced Intercompany Sales

processes.description:
Advanced Intercompany Stock Transfer (5HP)

Overview

The Advanced Intercompany Stock Transfer process begins with a requirement to transfer material from one company to another company. The purchaser creates purchase orders under the receiving plant.

A warehouse clerk at the issuing plant monitors the materials due to be shipped and creates deliveries as required. Once the delivery is complete, the delivery quantities are issued, appropriate documentation is generated, and the goods are shipped, ending the process for the issuing plant.

At the receiving plant, goods are received that reference the purchase documents. Inventory is received into a storage location based on fixed parameters proposed from the material master, which can be changed at the time of transactional data capture (purchase order creation or goods receipt).

Intercompany Invoicing is performed and a supplier invoice is created.

Key Process Flow

  • Create intercompany stock transport order

  • Create replenishment delivery for stock transport order

  • Pick and post goods issue for stock transport order

  • Perform inbound delivery

  • Check the status of stock transfer

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create intercompany billing document

  • Check supplier invoice

  • Use the Monitor Value Chain app to track postings

Business Benefits

  • Keep track of postings with the Monitor Value Chain app

  • Meet sales KPIs

  • Reuse the Valuated Stock in Transit (VSIT) for transfer of control

  • Use VSIT for both the delivering and receiving company

  • Support the matching principle for financial bookings, so that cost of goods sold (COGS) and revenue recognition always can happen at the same time, leading to IFRS 15 compliance

  • Hide complexity from the regular business activities and keep the users’ daily work simple

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item sets up an advanced intercompany process and requires significant additional manual setup steps.

If you requested this scope item, check the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.

processes.description:
Advanced Payment Management (4MT)

Overview

Advanced Payment Management supports the monitoring and approval of payments for both SAP systems and non-SAP systems. In the overall process, there’s a seamless integration with cash management. The conversion of various payment formats is also supported (for example, converting CSV or TXT files to XML).

Key Process Flow

  • Approve payment batch file

  • Approve payment batch

  • Process payment batch

Business Benefits

  • Provide a single source of truth for payment approval and monitoring for SAP and non-SAP systems

  • Increase the level of automation along the entire end-to-end process

  • Increase transactional throughput of payments in an environment where payment volumes are significantly increasing

  • Handle formats centrally

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires licenses for Advanced Payment Management and Advanced Cash Management.

As a prerequisite for this scope item, you must execute the Advanced Bank Account Management (J77) and Advanced Cash Operations (J78) scope items. SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (16R) is not mandatory but strongly recommended.
processes.name: Advanced Payment Management

processes.description:
Overview

Solution Business, XaaS and PaaS require the combination of products of different types, such as subscriptions with services or subscriptions with equipment. When these products in a bundle are configurable products that depend on each other, implementing them as a multi-level configurable product is the most effective and efficient solution. Advanced Solution Bundling provides easy modeling of bundles and integration into multiple sales documents.

Key Process Flow

  • Search and display existing bundles
  • Edit existing bundles
  • Create bundles
  • Add components to new bundles
  • Save new bundles to the local repository

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Advanced Solution Bundle Setup

processes.description:
Application Interface to Retrieve Payment Files (2YM)

Overview

This scope item provides a basic SOAP service to send outgoing payment files to the banks. It doesn't provide direct bank communication. When the customer implements this API, they oversee the implementation project and are responsible to operate the service. The customer must run a customer-managed middle-ware to establish the connections, develop encryption mechanisms between the middle-ware and the bank on his own, and set up a third-party solution to monitor the payments.

For inbound communication (for example, to receive bank statements), customers should use the Finance – Account Receivable Bank Statement Integration (SAP_COM_0316) communication scenario. This scenario is related to the Bank Integration with File Interface (1EG) scope item. This scope item won't be enhanced in future releases and is excluded from future developments. This scope item won't support additional message types such as payment status. Due to these limitations, SAP strongly recommends using SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (16R), providing direct bank communication and an out-of-the-box service managed by SAP.

Key Process Flow

  • Retrieve payment medium files from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition

  • Send the files to the banks

Business Benefits

  • Retrieve payment medium files from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and customer-managed middleware

  • Send payment files to banks

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Because this scope item requires significant manual configuration in their system landscape, customers must actively ask for the activation of the API. Before you request the scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Application Interface to Retrieve Payment Files

processes.description:
Assess Dangerous Goods for a Product (3FC)

Overview

This scope item supports the classification of products according to dangerous goods regulations.

When a product is intended to be transported, the product steward specialist assigns compliance purposes to the product. These compliance purposes specify the dangerous goods regulations that are relevant for the transport of the product. You, as a dangerous goods specialist, are responsible to assess the product. If the product is a dangerous good, you classify it according to the applicable dangerous goods regulations and determine whether the transport of this product is allowed in a certain country/region by the certain mode of transport. During the classification process, the system generates the dangerous goods description with rules that are specified for each dangerous goods regulation. This description can be printed on documents, such as sales order confirmations and delivery notes.

Key Process Flow

  • Flag products as relevant for a compliance assessment

  • Determine countries or regions where a product is planned to be transported

  • Derive relevant compliance purposes based on countries or regions where transport is required

  • Assess dangerous goods classification for an unpackaged product

  • Assess dangerous goods classification for all related packaged products

Business Benefits

  • Integrate the dangerous goods assessment of a product with the process of creating and changing products

  • Integrate the dangerous goods assessment of a product with your logistic processes

  • Use compliance requirements out-of-the-box for dangerous goods regulations in different countries or regions for certain modes of transport

  • Manage the impact of changing and evolving dangerous goods regulatory requirements on how and where your products can be transported
processes.name: Assess Dangerous Goods for a Product

processes.description:
Assess Marketability of a Product (31H)

Overview

For a certain country/region and business process, the result of the market assessment for a product describes if a business process for a country/region is allowed, allowed with restrictions, or not allowed.

To start the assessment process, the product stewardship specialist assigns markets (combination of country/region and business process) to the product. Based on these markets, you assign the compliance purposes that cover the relevant countries/regions and business processes (for example, selling an industrial chemical within an EU country/region).

For compliance requirements related to supply chain due diligence acts, the product stewardship specialist identifies which products require compliance declarations from suppliers. The master data specialist for product compliance provides these missing declarations and sets the compliance status of each supplier against each relevant compliance requirement. The product stewardship specialist views the results in marketability assessments of the products.

Key Process Flow

  • Flag products as relevant for a marketability assessment

  • Determine and assign markets to your products

  • Derive relevant compliance purposes from the assigned markets for your products

  • Analyze the target state and current state of compliance disclosures for suppliers

  • Assess suppliers against assigned compliance requirements

  • Automatically calculate marketability status

  • Process and release marketability assessments

  • Use the marketability status for compliance requirements as input for the market assessment

  • Assess business processes for your product in specific countries/regions as allowed, allowed with restrictions, and not allowed

Business Benefits

  • Integrate the market assessment of a product with the process of creating and changing products

  • Integrate the market assessment of a product with your logistics processes

  • Combine automatically calculated marketability status with expert judgment for the market assessment of a product

  • Use compliance requirements out-of-the-box for chemical compliance regulations in many different countries and regions

  • Manage the impact of changing and evolving regulatory requirements on the marketability of your products and the compliance of your suppliers efficiently
processes.name: Assess Marketability of a Product

processes.description:
Asset Accounting – Additional Depreciation Area (5HG)

Overview

This scope item is optional.

Some local or industry-specific rules (for example, for utility companies) may contain specific rules for depreciation and reporting. Companies may need to report insurance values to insurers for high-valued assets. To fulfill these requirements, you can activate this scope item. The scope item provides preconfigured content such as a specific valuation view and specific depreciation terms at the accounting principle level and valuation view level for asset classes.

An additional depreciation area is added when you activate the scope item. This depreciation area is for Asset Accounting purposes only and it contains statistical postings. You can define the depreciation parameters for depreciation key, useful life, and maximum amount for low-value assets for assets in this depreciation area.

Key Process Flow

This scope item provides additional content on top of the standard Asset Accounting (J62) scope item. The process flow of the standard scope applies for this scope item.

Business Benefits

  • Use a separate depreciation area for statistical postings following specific depreciation rules

  • Compare the asset’s values in additional depreciation areas also for future fiscal years and in different currencies using the asset valuation view in the Manage Fixed Assets app

  • Gain insights into asset values assigned to the additional depreciation area using analytical apps

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item provides an additional depreciation area for customer-specific configuration that can be optionally activated. However, you must make the decision to activate this scope item prior to initial activation of the solution. This cannot be activated afterwards. Customers can decide to use this scope item in addition to standard scope item Asset Accounting (J62) based on their requirements.
processes.name: Asset Accounting – Additional Depreciation Area

processes.description:
Asset Accounting – Group Ledger IFRS (1GB)

Overview

Asset accounting is a subsidiary ledger of the general ledger and is used to manage and document fixed asset transactions in detail. In general ledger accounting, you can update depreciation and changes to asset balance sheet values in asset accounting. You can also make various account assignments to cost accounting for these transactions. Because of the integration in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, Asset Accounting (FI-AA) transfers data directly to and from other SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition components like Financial Accounting (FI) components.

Ledger-specific transactions and reports support analysis of depreciation and asset balance to fulfill different accounting principle, such as Asset Revaluation, Depreciation Reporting, Manage Depreciation Runs, Asset Balance, and Asset Total Depreciation.

This scope item is for IFRS.

Key Process Flow

  • Create asset submaster

  • Valuate assets

  • Perform month-end closing

  • Perform year-end closing

Business Benefits

  • Support IFRS accounting principles

  • Calculate values for depreciation in parallel ledger

  • Analyze asset balance for various depreciation areas

  • Enable ordinary revaluation in general for IFRS

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is applicable for businesses adhering to IFRS accounting standards.
processes.name: Asset Accounting – Group Ledger IFRS

processes.description:
Asset Accounting – Group Ledger US GAAP (33F)

Overview

Asset accounting is a subsidiary ledger of the general ledger and is used to manage and document fixed asset transactions in detail. In general ledger accounting, you can update depreciation and change asset balance sheet values in asset accounting. You can also make various account assignments to cost accounting for these transactions. Because of the integration in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, Asset Accounting (FI-AA) transfers data directly to and from other components of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition such as Financial Accounting (FI) components.

Ledger-specific transactions and reports support analysis of depreciation and asset balance to fulfill different accounting principle, such as Asset Revaluation, Depreciation Reporting, Manage Depreciation Runs, Asset Balance, and Asset Total Depreciation.

  • Perform month-end closing

All starter, demo, and trial systems are set up by default with group ledger IFRS. This scope item is therefore excluded. Customers can decide to use this scope item in their system landscape based on the selected scope bundle.
processes.name: Asset Accounting – Group Ledger US GAAP

processes.description:

Overview

processes.name: Asset Under Construction – Additional Depreciation Area

processes.description:
Asset Under Construction – Group Ledger IFRS (1GF)

Overview

Assets under Construction (AuC) are a special form of tangible assets. They are usually displayed as a separate balance sheet item, requiring separate account determination and their own asset classes. During the construction phase of an asset, all actual postings are assigned to the AuC. Once the asset is completed, a transfer is made to the final fixed asset. Ledger-specific transactions such as Settlement Distribution Rule may influence the settlement result in different accounting principles.

This scope item is for IFRS.

Key Process Flow

  • Include invoice and final settlement for Assets under Construction (AuC) (a special form of tangible asset)

  • Settle asset under construction

  • Create assets for complete AuC settlement

  • Maintain settlement rule for final settlement in parallel ledger

  • Perform final settlement of the investment order (collective processing)

Business Benefits

  • Support IFRS accounting principle

  • Settle based on parallel ledger

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.
This scope item is applicable for businesses adhering to IFRS accounting standards.
processes.name: Asset Under Construction – Group Ledger IFRS

Assets under Construction (AuC) are a special form of tangible assets. They are usually displayed as a separate balance sheet item that requires separate account determination and their own asset classes. During the construction phase of an asset, all actual postings are assigned to the AuC. Once the asset is completed, a transfer is made to the final fixed asset. Asset-Backed Securities Management – Group Ledger IFRS (6B6)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for asset-backed securities management group ledger, you can use an additional valuation area besides your operative valuation area to reflect financial positions, investment, and financing results in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (9) phase I (Classification and Measurement).

Key Process Flow

  • Post to parallel ledger of IFRS for transactions

  • Perform key date valuation for security account class position

Business Benefits

  • Generate all postings for the general ledger

  • Update the general ledger according to IFRS 9 phase I (Classification and Measurement)

  • Process the valuation of position

  • Automate the month-end accounting processing

  • Increase your focus on value-added activities instead of on manual procedures

Asset-Backed Securities Management – Group Ledger US GAAP (6B7)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for asset-backed securities management group ledger US GAAP, you can use an additional valuation area besides your operative valuation area to reflect financial positions and investment and financing results in accordance with US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (US GAAP).

Key Process Flow

  • Run accrual

  • Perform key date valuation for security account class position
