processes.name: Bank Guarantee Management – Group Ledger US GAAP

processes.description:
Bank Guarantee Management (2NZ)

Overview

This scope item helps you to better manage your bank guarantee instruments. It supports common functionalities of bank guarantees without integration with sales functionality. Bank guarantee issuing and receiving are covered. In addition to functions for creating and changing bank guarantees, the system also supports functions for rollover, contract settlement, and contract termination. Cash collateral and bank guarantee fees are also covered.

Key Process Flow

  • Create financial transactions

  • Set settlement status

  • Execute payments for fees and cash collateral for bank guarantee issuing

  • Roll over transactions

  • Terminate transactions

  • Monitor and report on positions and financial transactions

Business Benefits

  • Review the status for trade finance instruments easily

  • Support the management of trade finance, including creation of the transactions, payments of cash collateral and bank fees, rollover and termination of bank guarantees

  • Make better operational and strategic decisions using the comprehensive reporting and analysis tools

  • Improve internal operational compliance
processes.name: Bank Guarantee Management

processes.description:
Bank Integration with File Interface (1EG)

Overview

In this scope item, you download the payment files for outgoing payments, which are generated by SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, to your computer. You can then upload these payment files to your banking portal or treasury workstation for payment processing.

You can also upload the electronic bank statements sent from your bank. The statements are further processed using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Key Process Flow

  • Download payment instruction file created by SAP S/4HANA

  • Upload bank statement from bank to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Business Benefits

  • Process payment and bank statements electronically

  • Take a practical approach for electronic processing of payment instructions and bank statements
processes.name: Bank Integration with File Interface

processes.description:
Bank Integration with SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (16R)

Overview

With SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (MBC), SAP establishes connections with your banks to automatically send payment instructions, receive status notifications, receive bank statements, and receive lockbox messages. Leveraging the monitoring capabilities, you can supervise the status of all payment instructions and see which bank statements are received and which expected bank statements are still missing. The monitoring is only available in combination with Advanced Cash Management (J78).

Key Process Flow

  • Connect securely with encryption between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity and the connected financial institutions or banks

  • Forward payment instructions to banks in local format

  • Receive status notification for payment instructions

  • Receive bank statements in standard formats such as MT940, CAMT.053, and BAI2

  • Receive lockbox messages BAI2

Business Benefits

  • Connect to banks via direct bank connections, SWIFT, or EBICS in a secure way (E2E-encryption embedded)

  • Route payment instructions automatically to financial institutions/banks

  • Receive bank statements automatically from financial institutions/banks

  • Update payment status (only available in conjunction with Advanced Cash Management)

  • Receive lockbox messages automatically from financial institutions/banks

  • Get SAP-managed service with no custom integration

  • Doesn't require middleware

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is non-standard. An additional license for Multi-Bank Connectivity is required.
processes.name: Bank Integration with SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity

processes.description:
Basic Available-to-Promise Processing (2LN)

Overview

A product availability check can be executed for planned orders, production orders, deliveries, sales orders, and stock transport orders, resulting in the order document containing one or more confirmed schedule lines.

If the available quantity of a material is insufficient to fulfill requirements, backorder processing can be performed for sales orders or stock transport orders in alignment with a specific business strategy. Backorder processing is scheduled to run automatically and periodically, resulting in the generation of reprioritized requirements.

Characteristic catalogs contain attributes that can be used as characteristics when you check availability and can be adapted to suit your business needs.

The review availability check result can be used to display if the ordered products can be delivered in time and quantity, and when and how much of the ordered product will presumably be delivered. The result can also list if alternative shipping locations were found, and if so, which can be used.

Key Process Flow

  • Execute a product availability check at order creation

  • Configure and schedule backorder processing

  • Configure characteristic catalogs to suit business requirements

  • Monitor the results of backorder processing and availability checks for new and changed sales orders

  • Display product availability

Business Benefits

  • Execute a product availability check at order creation

  • Configure and schedule backorder processing

  • Monitor the results of backorder processing

  • Adapt and extend characteristic catalogs for product allocation, backorder processing, and alternative-based confirmation

  • Display if ordered products can be delivered in time and quantity

  • Display when and how much of the ordered product will presumably be delivered​

  • Display if and which alternative shipping locations were found and used

  • Fine-tune and optimize confirmations

  • Display product availability
processes.name: Basic Available-to-Promise Processing

processes.description:
Basic Bank Account Management (BFA)

Overview

With Basic Bank Account Management, cash managers and bank accountants can centralize the management of bank accounts using bank account master data, using a table view of banks and bank accounts.

Bank account master processing includes creating or changing a bank account, closing an obsolete bank account, and reopening a closed bank account.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage bank and bank account master data with direct revision activation (Create, change, close, or reopen bank account)

Business Benefits

  • Manage bank and bank account master data centrally

  • Upload and download bank accounts freely
processes.name: Basic Bank Account Management

processes.description:
Basic Business Process Scheduling (6JM)

Overview

Before you can execute business process scheduling, you must perform configuration to activate business process scheduling.

First, you create or change a business document, such as a sales order, with the business process scheduling functionality activated. You can schedule logistically relevant date types that are available at the schedule line level in the sales order (for example, material availability date, delivery date) with the new Business Process Scheduling (BPS) solution using days as the time granularity. BPS is used through the creation or change of a sales document (for example, a sales order).

Key Process Flow

  • Activate business process scheduling

  • Execute business process scheduling when creating or changing business document

  • Schedule different date types

Business Benefits

  • Decouple business documents (for example, sales orders) from a concrete scheduling application

  • Enable a fully flexible configuration of duration, calendar, and time zone for each defined logistical activity

  • Schedule the relevant date types (for example, delivery date) in your business process

  • Define points in time in your logistical business process (start or end of logistical activities, for example, start of loading), for which BPS returns a scheduled date and time zone, and optionally, times
processes.name: Basic Business Process Scheduling

processes.description:
Basic Cash Operations (BFB)

Overview

Basic Cash Operations helps you to manage daily cash operations and provides general information of your current cash position and liquidity forecast.

You can get a midterm liquidity forecast based on the projected incoming and outgoing payments and manually entered planning items.

Payment medium files can either be downloaded and sent to the banks manually or automatically sent to the banks via Multi-Bank Connectivity. This scope item supports handling bank statement manually.

Key Process Flow

  • Perform bank integration for outgoing payment

  • Perform bank integration for incoming bank statement

  • View cash reports

  • Manage memo record

  • Use cash tools

Business Benefits

  • Integrate outgoing payments with banks

  • Retrieve bank statements easily

  • Monitor cash position and liquidity forecast centrally

  • Establish manual planned cash flow items with Memo Records

  • Use various tools to facilitate tasks such as flow aggregation, job scheduling, application log checking, and bank account balance reconciliation
processes.name: Basic Cash Operations

processes.description:
Basic Credit Management (BD6)

Overview

The credit worthiness and payment behavior of your business partners has an immediate effect on the business results of your company. Efficient receivables and credit management reduces the risk of financial losses and helps you to optimize business relationships with your business partners. Basic Credit Management supports your company in the early determination of the risk of losses on receivables from your business partners and supports you in making credit decisions. Basic Credit Management checks the exposure against the current credit limit for the business partner. In addition, you can also perform other checks, such as oldest open item, maximum dunning level, or last payment. If the new order is blocked, the blocked order can be released or rejected by authorized staff.

Key Process Flow

  • Calculate credit limit for new and existing customers

  • Enter sales order

  • Check exposure against credit limit

  • Manage blocked orders

Business Benefits

  • Reduce risk of bad debt

  • Focus on reliable and profitable customers

  • Check creditworthiness quickly

  • Accelerate the process of checking a customer credit limit
processes.name: Basic Credit Management

processes.description:
Basic Payment Management (7MJ)

Overview

Basic Payment Management is fully embedded in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and supports end-to-end monitoring of self-initiated payments for both SAP and non-SAP systems. This comprises internal processing states as well as external bank responses from payment status notification reports and bank statements.

In detail, this scope item allows for central monitoring an approvals of payments from various different initiating sources.

Moreover, Basic Payment Management serves as single source of truth with a concise semantic payment data model (ISO20022).

Key Process Flow

  • Monitor end-to-end payment status for payables and receivables

  • Use flexible payment approval processes based on flexible criteria such as payment source and key risk signals

Business Benefits

  • Monitor payments centrally, including bank status responses such as payment status reports, SWIFT tracker messages, and bank statements

  • Use flexible configuration of approval flows and automatic approval to speed up processing and provide high-lightened focus on most critical payment transactions.

  • Get notifications of payment rejections and overdue payment approvals via SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition situation handling

  • Use native integration to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition payment run

  • Use native integration to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for Advanced Payment Management
processes.name: Basic Payment Management

processes.description:
Batch Derivation – Consumer Products (77G)

Overview

This document outlines the production and packaging processes in the Consumer Products Industry, focusing on batch derivation of the earliest manufacturing date from component batches to the produced material. Condition records maintain the relevant inheritance characteristics. The goods receipt posting of finished products after production serves as a derivation event. Batch derivation can be performed at one or more manufacturing levels, with two alternative processes described: a single-step and a two-step batch derivation. At the start, you choose between these alternatives by selecting a corresponding production version.

The process begins with creating a demand forecast for finished goods, represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates a production plan for finished goods and explodes the entire bill of material structure. This results in planned production for finished products, semifinished products (in two-step batch derivation), and purchase requirements.

In the two-step batch derivation process, production starts with converting a planned order into a process order or directly creating a process order for the semifinished product. The goods issue of components (one or more batches per component), production confirmation, and goods receipt of the semifinished product are then executed.

The packing process applies to both single-level and two-step batch derivation. It begins with converting a planned order to a process order or directly creating a process order for the finished product. The goods issue of components, production confirmation, and goods receipt of the finished product follow.

You can check the results of the one-step or two-level batch derivation in the derivation monitor. The Batch Cockpit is available for batch traceability checks. Manual derivation is possible but not included in this scenario.

Key Process Flow

  • Make Decision to Run One- Or Two-Level Batch Derivation

  • Create Planned Independent Requirements

  • Perform MRP Run at Plant Level

  • Evaluate Stock/Requirements Situation

  • One-Level Batch Derivation

    • Process Order Creation and Processing for Finished Material

  • Two-Level Batch Derivation

    • Process Order Creation and Processing for Semifinished Material

    • Process Order Creation and Processing for Finished Material

  • Monitor Batch Derivation

  • Batch Information Cockpit – Top-Down and Bottom-Up Analysis

Business Benefits

  • Tailor available capacities and receipts on time to suit requirement quantities

  • Control the stock/requirements situation for Make-to-Stock finished goods and the components relevant for production

  • Easily review created process orders

  • Ensure sufficient material is present in stock

  • Monitor derivation to control previously performed derivations (receiver batches, attributes and their values, messages)
processes.name: Batch Derivation – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Batch Management (BLF)

Overview

Batch Management incorporates the entire logistics process, from procurement to sales. It's closely linked with classification, but can also be used without classification.

Batch Management is defined as tagging a produced or procured material with a unique 10-digit alphanumeric code. Every batch number can have an inventory quantity associated with it.

The batch number generated for the material quantity helps with uniquely sorting the material inventory and stores the characteristics values or the chemical composition or the product specifications at the time of its production or procurement.

A configuration activity Specify Batch Management Default by Plant is available, which enables you to specify whether batch management is used by default in Material Master for each plant.

If the Not Batch Managed column of a plant is selected, the plant won't use batch management by default when a new material is set as batch managed. You can still overwrite this setting later by maintaining Material Master with plant data.

Batch derivation configuration activities are available. You can use batch derivation scenario after finishing the configuration. Batch derivation enables you to do the following for batch master data and classification data of the component batches of produced batches:

  • Transfer

  • Display for selection

  • Display

Key Process Flow

  • Create and change batch master data

  • View batch history: Top-down and Bottom-up Analysis

  • Fast search and display of batches with Enterprise Search

  • Assign batch number

  • Specify batch

  • Manage batch status

  • View batch where-used list

Business Benefits

  • Manage batches from supplier receipt through distribution with full traceability

  • Identify differences in usage and monitoring of materials planning in SD and Production

  • Trace defects and initiate follow up actions

  • Comply to legal requirements, such as Good Manufacturing Practice or hazardous material regulations

  • Differentiate quantity- and value-based inventory, for example, due to heterogeneous yield or result qualities or varying constituents in Production

  • Improve settlement of material quantities based on batch specifications
processes.name: Batch Management

processes.description:
Bill of Material Management (64F)

Overview

Bill of Material Management provides the following functionalities:

  • Create and maintain single and multi-level bills of material (BOMs).

  • Using change masters, different effectivities of BOM changes on component level can be defined, revisioned planned, and released.

  • The Where-Used capability allows BOM engineers to find all occurrences of a certain component across BOMs. In combination with a mass replace function, component replacements can easily be managed.

  • BOM engineers can use BOM groupings to represent the modular structure of the product in a multilevel BOM, group component variants in variant BOMs, and group a BOM without creating additional materials.

  • Using preliminary BOM items, the BOM engineer can describe the custom engineered components in engineer-to-order and customer-to-order scenarios (such as in the tendering phase) without creating materials, and can create placeholders for later enhancement of business objects, such as documents or materials.

  • With requirements-driven development, requirements and block definition diagrams can be linked to product lifecycle management objects such as document info records, materials, and configurable BOMs.

  • Perform mass maintenance of BOMs

    The BOM Engineers can select the relevant BOMs with comprehensive search functions and then add, change, or delete BOM items, as well as change or delete BOM headers across the whole selection in one step. The BOM Engineers can also simulate BOM changes prior to executing and releasing them. The execution protocol helps to re-execute changes that could not be processed.

Key Process Flow

  • Create bill of material (BOM)

  • Change BOM

  • Use Where-Used and mass replacement of components

  • Replace preliminary items by real component

  • Link BOMs to requirements and the block definition diagram

  • Link the design document, configuration profile, or material to the block definition diagram

Business Benefits

  • Create and maintain single and multilevel bills of materials (BOM)

  • Use change masters to define effectivities

  • Use Where-Used function to find component occurrences with mass replacement across BOMs

  • Use BOM item type as placeholder for later enhancement for business objects, like document or material

  • Group BOM Items to model modularization

  • Use linked requirements to PLM objects to ensure consistency between defined requirements and changes during product development

  • Plan for intended changes with the support of impact analysis on requirements

  • Ensure the fulfillment of all requirements during the product-design process

  • Perform mass maintenance to add, change, and delete BOM items

  • Perform mass maintenance to change and delete BOM headers
processes.name: Bill of Material Management

processes.description:
Billing of Costs Between Affiliated Companies (3ZB)

Overview

A company wants to bill costs to an affiliate. The affiliate creates a purchase order to reflect that a vendor invoice is expected. In the sending company, a customer order including costs to be billed (and a margin if relevant) is created. The customer order is billed and is sent to the affiliate, creating a supplier invoice with reference to the purchase order.

Via activation of B2B scenarios, you can achieve process automation between sending company and affiliate.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a purchase order with a cost object assignment in the affiliate, including a flexible workflow for purchase orders

  • Create a sales order in the invoice sending company including costs to be billed (and if relevant a margin)

  • Create a customer invoice in the invoice sending company, including a flexible workflow for supplier invoices

  • Create a supplier invoice with reference to the purchase order in the affiliate

Business Benefits

  • Enable an automated and integrated process to bill costs (and if relevant margins) between affiliated companies

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires additional manual set-up steps. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Billing of Costs Between Affiliated Companies

processes.description:
Bond Management – Group Ledger IFRS (3WZ)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for bond management – group ledger , you can use an additional valuation area besides your operative valuation area to reflect financial positions, investment, and financing results in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (9) phase I (Classification and Measurement).

Key Process Flow

  • Post to parallel ledger of IFRS for transactions

  • Perform key date valuation for security account class position

  • Reclassify from long term to short term

Business Benefits

  • Generate all postings for the general ledger

  • Update the general ledger according to IFRS 9 phase I (Classification and Measurement)

  • Process the valuation of position

  • Automate the month-end accounting processing

  • Increase your focus on value-added activities instead of on manual procedures
processes.name: Bond Management – Group Ledger IFRS

processes.description:
Bond Management – Group Ledger US GAAP (3X0)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for Bond Management – Group Ledger US GAAP, you can use an additional valuation area alongside your operative one. This allows you to reflect financial positions and investment or financing results in accordance with US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (US GAAP).

Key Process Flow

  • Post to parallel ledger of US GAAP for transactions

  • Run accrual

  • Perform key date valuation for security account class position

  • Reclassify from long term to short term

Business Benefits

  • Generate all postings for the general ledger

  • Update the general ledger according to US GAAP

  • Process the valuation of position

  • Automate the month-end accounting processing

  • Increase your focus on value-added activities instead of on manual procedures

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

All starter, demo, and trial systems, by default, are set up with group ledger IFRS. This scope item is therefore excluded. Customers can decide to use this scope item in their systems based on the selected scope bundle.
processes.name: Bond Management – Group Ledger US GAAP

processes.description:
Bond Management (3WY)

Overview

The Bond Management process helps you to manage issued bonds and bond investments. You can automate labor-intensive processes, such as payment handling and accounting postings, giving you more time to focus on value-added activities. You can manage operational and accounting requirements. The process covers fixed-rate, floating-rate, and zero-coupon bonds.

Key Process Flow

  • Create security account

  • Create security class

  • Create financial transactions

  • Process payments

  • Transfer values to general ledger

  • Fix interest rates

  • Perform month-end accounting processes

  • Perform reclassification

  • Monitor and report on class positions and financial transactions

Business Benefits

  • Review the financial status

  • Automate the management of bond issuance and investments, including creation of security account, security class and financial transaction, payments, interest rate fixing, and accounting

  • Make better operational and strategic decisions using the comprehensive reporting and analysis tools

  • Improve internal operational compliance

  • Increase your focus on value-added activities instead of on manual procedures
processes.name: Bond Management

processes.description:
Overview

Business Abroad (5RP) enables companies to manage VAT and indirect tax obligations in foreign countries and regions where they operate through foreign plants without having a legal entity registered in those localities. The Foreign Plant feature in SAP Central Business Configuration is activated by adding this scope item to your scope, allowing you to designate plants in a country or region different from the company code country or region. Depending on the target locality, certain supporting scenarios for VAT tax calculation and reporting, Intrastat processing, and compliance format preparation may be required alongside this scope item.

For a subset of RITA-enabled and foreign plant-enabled countries or regions (you can see the full list of countries where 5RP is available on SAP Help Portal), foreign plants can be used without adding those countries to your scope, provided the associated tax and reporting scenarios are active. For all other RITA-supported countries or regions, the country must be explicitly added to your scope before it can be selected for a foreign plant.

Note:

We strongly recommend that you review SAP Note 2907372 to understand the business abroad logistics and financial processes related to RITA.

Key Process Flow

  • Activate this scope item in SAP Central Business Configuration
  • Define scope for required supporting scenarios (VAT calculation, Intrastat, compliance formats) per target country or region
  • Create foreign plant in the Set Up Organizational Structure app
  • Assign foreign plant to the applicable country or region (distinct from the company code country or region)
  • Configure VAT registration and indirect tax settings for the foreign jurisdiction
  • Execute cross-border logistics involving the foreign plant (depending on locality)
  • Execute financial transactions involving the foreign plant (depending on locality)
  • Generate VAT and Intrastat reports for the foreign country/region

Business Benefits

  • Enable companies to operate foreign plants without establishing a separate legal entity in each jurisdiction
  • Fulfill indirect tax registration and reporting obligations in foreign countries or regions directly within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
  • Reduce compliance risk by applying country-specific VAT calculation, Intrastat, and statutory reporting scenarios automatically
  • Simplify organizational setup by managing foreign business operations centrally through a single system
  • Support cross-border logistics and financial processes for goods movements involving foreign plants

Exclude from Default Activation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

Only include the Business Abroad (5RP) scope item manually during initial activation if you intend to add a foreign plant at the start of the project. This scope item isn't required for companies operating exclusively within their company code's country or region.
processes.name: Business Abroad

processes.description:
Business Event Handling (1NN)

Overview

With a standardized event mechanism, you can provision the event catalog for all business objects across the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition application, to enable applications, partners, and customers to consume events related to all business objects in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

With event activation management, you can propagate only subscribed events to the messaging infrastructure and to those subscribers or receivers.

Side-by-side extensions provide a powerful way of extending SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition applications on SAP Business Technology Platform for customers and partners without impacting the digital core, by building decoupled extension applications running side-by-side with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Business Benefits

  • Consume events based on business objects

  • Use front-end application to maintain subscription

  • Manage all the active, in-active subscriptions in one place

  • Manage event handling subscriptions effectively

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The activation of this scope item requires an additional SAP Enterprise Messaging license to consume the business events.
processes.name: Business Event Handling

processes.description:
Business Partners for Retail (5FH)

Overview

A supplier or vendor is a business partner who delivers and sells goods and services to a retailer. A supplier master holds information about the supplier such as its name, address, bank details, tax details, and billing preferences. This supplier information is used and stored in transactions such as purchase orders, goods receipts, and supplier invoices. Some supplier information is specific to a company (known as the company code) or purchasing unit (known as the purchasing organization) within a retailer’s organization.

A customer is a business partner to which goods and services are sold and delivered. A customer master holds information about the customer such as its name, address, bank details, tax details, and delivery and billing preferences. This customer information is used and stored in transactions such as sales orders, deliveries, and billing documents. Some customer information is specific to a company (known as the company code) or sales unit (known as the sales area) within a retailer’s organization.

Business partners have several different functions, described as partner functions. For example, typical partner functions for a supplier are ordering address, goods supplier, invoicing party.

A business partner can be a customer and a supplier at the same time if, for example, the customer also supplies goods or if a supplier is also a customer.

For internal suppliers and customers, see the Sites for Retail (3I3) scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Create supplier master data – general, company code, purchasing organization data

  • Extend supplier master data – sales area data, return supplier

  • Block supplier

  • Create customer master data – general, company code, sales area

Business Benefits

  • Improve operational procurement FTE productivity by generating central purchase contracts from the awarded central supplier quotation

  • Reduce customer billing, credit, and collections cost by providing consistent and correct article and price information

  • Reduce customer churn by centrally managing business partner data to ensures master data quality and data checks

  • Reduce days sales outstanding by automating the payment reconciliation process and removing manual processing

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Business Partners for Retail

processes.description:
Cash Application Integration (1MV)

Overview

The SAP Cash Application uses the past data in your system to propose invoice matching prediction results. It helps lower the manual effort in the time-consuming clearing process of open items.

With this scope item, remittance advice can also be created automatically by the system based on the advice file sent from your customers or payees.

To use this solution's functions, you must purchase the extra license on SAP BTP.

Key Process Flow

  • Extract unstructured remittance advice data and make it available to be used for standard clearing process

  • Extract and replicate historical data to machine learning platform as machine training data

  • Extract and replicate open receivable items to Machine Learning Platform for scoring

  • Perform payables line-item matching – Self-initiated

  • Get automated training process

  • Reprocess bank statement by matching the open receivable items to the proposed bank statement

Business Benefits

  • Save effort in this labor-intensive process

  • Consume the fully integrated business process easily with the SAP Cash Application solution

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The license for SAP Cash Application is required. This scope item provides integration and must be activated before customers can make additional integration settings. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Cash Application Integration

processes.description:
Cash Journal (1GO)

Overview

The cash journal is a subledger of Financial Accounting. It is used to manage a company's cash transactions. The system automatically calculates and displays the opening and closing balances and the receipts and payments totals. You can run several cash journals for each company code, and you can run a separate cash journal for each currency. You can also carry out postings to G/L accounts, supplier accounts, and customer accounts.

Key Process Flow

  • Post cash journal entries

  • Display cash journal entries

Business Benefits

  • Have multiple cash journals for each company code

  • Separate cash journal for each currency

  • Integrate cash journal documents into FI system

  • Prevent redundant data entry with automatic journal entry generation

  • Post to G/L accounts, customer accounts, and supplier accounts

  • Print journals repeatedly
processes.name: Cash Journal

processes.description:
CDS-Based Extraction with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (35D)

Overview

You can accelerate your virtual data model data extraction and replication to SAP BW/4HANA, SAP BW on SAP HANA, or other target applications from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Use the Operational Data Provisioning (ODP) framework, which supports the delta mechanism for change data capture (CDC).

Key Process Flow

  • Verify the source system, data flow, and extracted data for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Core Date Services Views to BW Extraction

Business Benefits

  • Get direct guidance on how to access CDS-ODP Source functionality

  • Consume core date services Views within SAP BW/4HANA and SAP BW on SAP HANA Modeling tools

  • Perform delta extraction of CDS-ODP Source to SAP BW/4HANA and SAP BW on SAP HANA

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires SAP BW/4HANA or SAP BW on SAP HANA.
processes.name: CDS-Based Extraction with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

processes.description:
Central Governance for Business Partner (1N7)

Overview

This scope item provides comprehensive capabilities for managing business partner data within the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. It supports both single and mass processing scenarios. Users can create new Business Partners or modify existing ones individually using the Manage Business Partners Central Governance app. For broader updates, the Manage Governance Processes Central Governance app enables mass processing, allowing changes to be applied across multiple Business Partners. Additionally, automated mass processing includes a derivation step that streamlines governance workflows. The scope item also facilitates inbound processing by enabling the system to integrate replicated Business Partner data and relationships through SOAP-based services.

Key Process Flow

Cloud-Ready Processes

  1. Single Request for Create / Change Business Partners

    • Create or change Business Partners

    • Maintain Business Partner data

    • Validate if the records can be activated in the system

    • Activate the Business Partner

  2. Mass Request for Business Partners

    • Define Selection

    • Edit Business Partner data using Single record or Mass record level

    • Validate if the records can be activated in the system

    • Activate the Business Partner

  3. Inbound Process for Business Partner

    • Create inbound processes for the incoming replicated business partner or relationship

    • Perform and complete the process automatically

    • Verify the activated Business Partner

Business Benefits

  • Save time when editing multiple master data records by providing a central mass maintenance functionality

  • Perform the master data maintenance process more efficiently
processes.name: Central Governance for Business Partner

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item provides comprehensive capabilities for managing Product Master data within the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. It supports both the classic mass processing approach and the new cloud-ready governance process for products.

In classic mode, users can perform mass processing of Product Master data, enabling efficient updates across multiple Product records simultaneously. To update records, select the fields and records to change. Once you enter your changes, the system provides statistics on the changed fields and validates the data. You check the validated data and activate it for use in business transactions. Classification is supported. You can also download active data for mass processing.

In cloud-ready mode, dedicated governance applications support streamlined single requests, mass requests, and inbound processing scenarios for Product Master data. Users can create, change, validate, and activate Product records using simplified cloud-ready governance flows. To use the cloud-ready Product Governance applications, the feature toggle MDC_PRODUCT_GOVERNANCE must be activated.

Key Process Flow

Classic Mode

Mass Processing Products:
  • Define all fields to change
  • Select Product records subject to change
  • Make mass changes to records by replacing existing values
  • Validate whether records can be activated in the system based on customizing
  • Update records in the system
  • Download active data for mass processing (optional)

Cloud-Ready Mode

Single Request for Create/Change Product Master Data:
  • Create or change Product Master data
  • Maintain Product data
  • Validate whether records can be activated in the system
  • Activate the Product
Mass Request for Products:
  • Define selection criteria
  • Edit Product data using single-record or mass-record processing
  • Validate whether records can be activated in the system
  • Activate the Product
Inbound Process for Products:
  • Create inbound processes for incoming replicated Product data
  • Perform and complete the process automatically
  • Verify the activated Product

Business Benefits

  • Enables centralized maintenance of Product Master data
  • Supports efficient mass processing of multiple Product records
  • Reduces manual effort and maintenance time
  • Improves Product data quality through validation checks
  • Simplifies Product governance with streamlined cloud-ready applications
  • Supports both single-record and mass-record Product maintenance scenarios
  • Accelerates inbound replication and automated Product processing
  • Enhances governance efficiency with automated validation and activation processes
  • Provides scalable and cloud-ready Product governance capabilities within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Central Governance for Product

processes.description:
Central Procurement with SAP Ariba Sourcing (4QN)

Overview

The SAP S/4HANA Hub system offers a centralized RFQ process with a deep integration into the customer's landscape. It connects SAP Ariba Sourcing to the customer’s SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system (on-premise or Cloud).

With the SAP S/4HANA Hub system, you can pool or aggregate purchase requisitions created in multiple connected backend systems. This allows you to create a single central RFQ and thus get support for better pricing.

SAP Ariba Sourcing provides access to intuitive RFX tools (for requests for information and requests for proposals). It connects you to more than two million companies for quick and easy supplier discovery. It also offers automated and adjustable negotiation procedures.

Once the award process is completed in SAP Ariba Sourcing, the supplier contract created in the SAP S/4HANA Hub system generates either purchase orders or contracts in the respective connected backend system.

This scenario is recommended for the indirect sourcing process only. This scope item requires an additional license for SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a central RFQ in SAP S/4HANA Hub system for purchase requisitions that are created in the connected backend systems (central purchaser)

  • Send the central RFQ to the SAP Ariba Sourcing application, which triggers a sourcing request in SAP Ariba

  • Access your worklist and convert sourcing requests into sourcing projects/ events (sourcing manager)

  • Monitor sourcing projects that result in RFP and discover suppliers via Ariba Network and monitor suppliers’ responses (sourcing manager)

  • Award one or more bids in SAP Ariba Sourcing (sourcing manager)

  • Send awarded bids automatically to SAP S/4HANA central hub to create a central supplier quotation

  • Use central supplier quotation to create operational purchase orders or operational contracts in the respective connected backend ERP systems of SAP S/4HANA Central hub

Business Benefits

  • Aggregate demand by pooling requisitions created in multiple connected backend systems into one central RFQ

  • Source the best supplier based on the aggregated demand, using the power of SAP Ariba Sourcing and Ariba Network

  • Create purchase orders and contracts seamlessly in the respective backend systems upon finalization of the award process in SAP Ariba Sourcing

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is dependent on the other priced scope items (such as Central Purchasing (2XT), Central Purchase Contracts (2ME), and Central Sourcing (3ZF)).
processes.name: Central Procurement with SAP Ariba Sourcing

processes.description:
Central Procurement with SAP Business Network for Procurement (6BJ)

Overview

Integrating SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with SAP Business Network through SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network supports the exchange of documents related to standard procurement processes, such as purchase orders and order confirmations.

Create central purchase orders in central procurement hub system by pooling purchase orders from connected systems, such as SAP ERP, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, SAP S/4HANA or ECC. The purchase orders are sent to SAP Business Network and the required suppliers are notified. Suppliers submit their order confirmation through SAP Business Network. The supplier's order confirmation is sent from SAP Business Network to either hub or connected system. As soon as the supplier starts the release and approval process for a purchase order, the status is updated in the connected system.

Key Process Flow

  • Create purchase orders in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition connected system

  • Extract purchase orders to the central procurement hub system (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition)

  • Approve purchase orders to view it in the Manage Purchase Orders Centrally app in in the hub system

  • Send purchase order output electronically from central procurement hub system

  • Receive purchase order in SAP Business Network for Procurement

  • Create order confirmation as a supplier in SAP Business Network for Procurement

  • Determine the confirmation creation based on the supplier confirmation relevance indicator

  • Transfer the order confirmation to the Manage Central Supplier Confirmations app in the hub system and further to the connected system

  • Transfer the order confirmation from the Manage Central Supplier Confirmations app in the hub system to the connected system

Business Benefits

  • Speed up procurement processes

  • Improve compliance

  • Increase productivity in accounts payables and procurement departments

  • Increase productivity of procurement and accounts payable staff

  • Reduce inquiries about payments from suppliers

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant if you want to integrate SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with SAP Business Network for Procurement and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. To use this scope item, you need an additional license for SAP Business Network Supplier Portal for SAP Finance Premium.
processes.name: Central Procurement with SAP Business Network for Procurement

processes.description:
Central Purchase Contracts (2ME)

Overview

Central contracts are global long-term agreements negotiated between an organization and a supplier. This helps in getting the best rates and conditions while bundling purchasing volume across multiple subsidiaries. These contracts are typically negotiated by the central purchasing organization, mostly at the headquarters, and used for globally driving operational efficiency, reduced cost while complying with regulations across multiple subsidiaries.

The central contract, created at the headquarters, can be distributed to subsidiaries to generate local contracts or scheduling agreements. Subsidiaries can then continue with the operational procurement in a seamless manner by leveraging this local contract or Scheduling agreement. Central monitoring of contract consumption across subsidiaries and renewal of expiring contracts is easily managed by the headquarters.

Key Process Flow

  • Create central purchase contract and distribution

  • Release central purchase contract (optional)

  • Check distributed purchase contracts or scheduling agreements in the back-end system

  • Create purchase order or schedule lines in the back-end system

  • Import release orders

  • Post goods receipt in the back-end system

  • Create supplier invoice in the back-end system

  • Create credit memo (optional) in the back-end system

  • Perform mass changes to central purchase contracts

  • Monitor central purchase contract items (optional)

  • Create hierarchy central contracts

  • Display version history in central purchase contracts

  • Maintain formula and rate for commodity pricing

Business Benefits

  • Lower your costs for contract negotiation

  • Lower your costs based on scaled purchasing
processes.name: Central Purchase Contracts

processes.description:
Central Purchasing (2XT)

Overview

Central Purchasing provides centralized access and visibility to processes across industries with a deep integration into the system landscape. It is connected to the customer’s ERP systems and exchanges purchasing documents (such as purchase requisitions and purchase orders) in the connected systems. It also offers central approval process, central portal, central output management, analytics, and responsibility management of product categories.

This scope item offers one platform where a procurement specialist can work centrally on purchase requisitions and purchase orders from different backend systems. Operational procurement processes are not the only tasks to profit from the hub approach. Strategic procurement tasks (such as Supplier Management) benefit from the transparency and the ability to initiate strategic activities from a central digital procurement control center.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain purchase requisitions centrally

  • Maintain and approve purchase orders centrally

  • Update edited purchase orders and purchase requisitions to the relevant backend systems

  • Use central purchasing analytics

  • Detect critical purchase order item overdue situation

  • React to critical purchase order item overdue situation

  • Automate purchase requisitions

  • Integrate with central purchase contracts (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Harmonize business processes

  • Get full transparency over all activities across all backend systems

  • Provide single data access for purchasers and ability to process procurement activities centrally when in a multi-system environment (for example, editing of purchase requisitions and purchase orders, approval of purchase orders)

  • Reduce TCO significantly for procurement departments through centralized process
processes.name: Central Purchasing

processes.description:
Central Requisitioning (1XI)

Overview

Central Processing of Purchase Requisitions offers a centralized requisitioning processes across industries with a deep integration into the customer's landscape. It is connected to the customer’s ERP systems, and exchanges master data and business documents to ensure end-to-end business processes into Finance and Logistics that run in the connected Systems.

This scope item offers one platform where a procurement specialist can work centrally on requisitions from different organizations. Operational procurement processes are not the only tasks to profit from the hub approach. Strategic procurement tasks including Supplier Management benefit from the transparency and the possibility to initiate strategic activities from a central digital procurement control center.

Key Process Flow

  • Create and approve purchase requisitions

  • Assign potential sources of supply automatically

  • Create the corresponding purchase orders

  • Update the process status electronically while processing the goods receipt and the supplier invoice

Business Benefits

  • Harmonize business process

  • Get full transparency over all activities

  • Ensure usage of centrally negotiated prices and contracts

  • Provide single data access for employees and possibility to process procurement activities centrally (for example, sourcing, completion of requisitions, approval, and so on)

  • Reduce TCO significantly for procurement departments through centralized process
processes.name: Central Requisitioning

processes.description:
Central Sourcing (3ZF)

Overview

Central Sourcing provides centralized access and visibility into sourcing process across industries with deep integration into the system landscape. It is connected to the customer's ERP systems and exchanges purchasing documents (such as purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and contracts) in the connected systems.

This scope item offers one platform where a procurement specialist can work centrally on purchase requisitions from multiple ERP systems to identify the ideal source of supply. A request for quotation (RFQ) can be created for multiple requisitions from different ERP systems. The supplier quotations received can be maintained and an RFQ can be awarded. Follow-on actions (like creating a central contract or purchase order in the corresponding ERP system) can be centrally controlled in the hub system.

Strategic procurement tasks including Supplier Management benefit from the transparency and the possibility to initiate strategic activities from a central digital procurement control center.

Key Process Flow

  • Create and approve purchase requisitions

  • Create central request for quotations

  • Manage central request for quotations

  • Create supplier quotations and award request for quotations

  • Create the corresponding central contracts or purchase orders

  • Update the purchase requisition process status electronically while processing the goods receipt and the supplier invoice

Business Benefits

  • Harmonize business process

  • Get full transparency over all activities

  • Ensure usage of centrally negotiated prices and contracts

  • Provide single data access for employees and possibility to process procurement activities centrally (for example, sourcing, completion of requisitions, approval, and so on)

  • Reduce TCO significantly for procurement departments through centralized process
processes.name: Central Sourcing

processes.description:
Characteristic Value Conversion for Retail (7DL)

Overview

In the retail and fashion industries, a characteristic of a product can be measured using different standards or scales in different countries or geographical regions. For example, a shoe that is considered size 9 in the UK may be a size 11 in the US. Hence, the shoe has both the sizes marked on it. To facilitate this, a characteristic conversion mechanism is necessary to ensure that on every product, sizes in all relevant size standards are correctly marked.

Characteristic value conversion only applies to variant-creating characteristics that are attached to the article master.

Characteristic

Characteristics refer to properties of an article such as the color of a shirt or the size of a shirt. The variant-creating characteristics are used to create variants of the generic product. The non-variant-creating characteristics are for information purposes only.

Characteristic Values

Characteristic values are the attributes of a characteristic. For example, if the characteristic is color, the characteristic values can be red, blue, or yellow. Characteristics can be valuated differently for each individual article. For example, an article with the characteristic color can receive the value red and another article can receive the value blue.

The system converts the characteristic values based on the conversion defined for the article. The system converts the characteristic value for selected items in the document or for the entire document.

Characteristic value conversion can be carried out in documents such as sales orders, purchase orders, and so on.

Key Process Flow

  • Create conversion types

  • Maintain conversion parameters for characteristic value and description

  • Create articles using the characteristics

  • Apply the required conversion type in the application documents

Business Benefits

  • View the converted characteristic value and text in different application documents depending on the conversion type applied.

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item can only be activated if you have a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and have activated the retail bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Characteristic Value Conversion for Retail

processes.description:
Chemical Compliance Approval for Purchased Material and Supplier (31G)

Overview

This scope item manages the compliance assessment of purchased materials and their suppliers for fulfillment.

Raw or purchased materials must cover the compliance requirements of the associated products that are produced by using the raw materials.

The compliance data is requested from raw material suppliers. This process lets you first approve or block a supplier, and second, assess whether the raw material fulfills the requirements. When this assessment is done, you have approved suppliers and raw materials. Additionally, detailed compliance data is available for audits.

Key Process Flow

  • Set compliance relevance for the raw material master

  • Process request for external sourcing

  • Assign supplier to raw material

  • Maintain supplier compliance data

  • Assess compliance of raw material

Business Benefits

  • Summarize usage of purchased material requirements

  • Manage coverage of requirements on a supplier level

  • Perform the supplier approval process

  • Aggregate and assess the compliance of a purchase material based on supplier data
processes.name: Chemical Compliance Approval for Purchased Material and Supplier

processes.description:
Chemical Compliance in the Value Chain (31J)

Overview

This scope item manages the compliance marketability checks in sales order processes and during outbound delivery.

For every product included in a sales order or sales quotation that is defined as relevant for compliance, it must be verified if the sale into the specified country/region and to the specified customer is allowed. The result of the marketability check may block the follow-on documents or initiate a request for the product stewardship department.

If selling is possible only under restrictions, the internal sales representative can initiate an approval process. The product stewardship department processes the approval request and approves or rejects the sale.

The sales documents are also blocked if selling isn't possible or hasn't yet been assessed. A request is created for the product stewardship department if the assessment for a country/region and customer hasn't yet been done.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order

  • Perform compliance marketability check

  • Verify compliance information

  • Process request for approval

  • Create outbound delivery and execute compliance check

Business Benefits

  • Mitigate compliance risks with up-to-date information integrated into the value chain

  • Integrate compliance marketability checks into selling processes

  • Get informed about new markets as a product stewardship specialist

  • Go through the approval process to validate restrictions for selling
processes.name: Chemical Compliance in the Value Chain

processes.description:
Classification for Customs Tariff Number and Commodity Code (2U3)

Overview

This scope item provides the business processes to maintain tariff codes and commodity codes. The defined codes can be assigned to products for proper classification.

Key Process Flow

  • Load commodity codes from an external data provider

  • Manage customs tariff numbers

  • Classify or reclassify products with customs tariff numbers

Business Benefits

  • Help to ensure accurate product classification for customs processes

  • Keep international trade processes frictionless
processes.name: Classification for Customs Tariff Number and Commodity Code

processes.description:
Collaborative Project Management (6JN)

Overview

SAP Project and Resource Management enhances the project management capabilities of SAP Cloud ERP by providing intuitive tools for collaborative project planning and execution. With features such as project structuring, project scheduling, document handling, and built-in task and issue tracking, it enables project managers to plan effectively, coordinate stakeholders, and execute projects with greater accuracy and transparency.

Key Process Flow

  • Create collaborative project

  • Invite stakeholders

  • Import project plan

  • Schedule Project Plan

  • Identify and Capture Risk

  • Share execution plan

  • Define and assign tasks

  • Capture and Track Issues

  • Execute Tasks

  • Upload documents

  • Monitor and Mitigate Risks

Business Benefits

  • Improved collaboration and efficiency: Digitizes and streamlines the exchange of project information across internal teams and external stakeholders, reducing manual coordination and ensuring everyone works with the latest data.

  • Flexible and adaptable project structures: Supports multi-layered project breakdowns, enabling different teams or phases to manage work using structures that suit their specific responsibilities while maintaining overall project consistency.

  • Aligned planning and execution: Ensures a seamless transition from plan creation to execution to closure by providing real-time visibility into progress, changes, risks, and issues—helping project managers respond quickly and make informed decisions.

  • Enhanced control and outcome reliability: Integrated management of tasks, issues, and risks enables early identification of challenges, improving project predictability and reducing delivery risks.

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

To execute this scope item, the SAP Project and Resource Management license is required in addition to the SAP S4HANA Cloud license.
processes.name: Collaborative Project Management

processes.description:
Collections and Dispute Automation (7MA)

Overview

This scope item streamlines collections activities for accounts receivable, supports resolution of customer invoice disputes, and manages overdue items efficiently. It helps reduce exposure to potential write-offs through earlier, targeted follow-ups.

With tools in the dispute resolution process, processors can efficiently manage disputes, as well as proactively manage and collect overdue receivables. Specialists have all the information and support they need to collect payments faster and provide improved customer service.

Collection specialists can proactively manage and collect overdue receivables with receivables collections tools and dunning integration. The specialists have all the information and support they need to collect payments faster and provide improved customer service. They can identify bad debt risk potential and take preventative steps to reduce further exposure.

Key Process Flow

  • Create, manage and close disputes

  • Manage and collect overdue receivables

Business Benefits

  • Standardize processes for resolving customer invoice disputes

  • Streamline collections activities for accounts receivable

  • Accelerate dispute resolution with advanced workflows

  • Increase the productivity of process assignees

  • Minimize bad debt write-offs

  • Reduce days sales outstanding (DSO)

  • Optimize data quality and transparency

  • Collect payments faster

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

SAP provides two scope items related to dispute resolution: Collections and Dispute Management (BFC) and Collections and Dispute Automation (7MA). Before you make the choice to use the dispute resolution process of 7MA, see the Integration with Other Components topic on SAP Help Portal for more information.
processes.name: Collections and Dispute Automation

processes.description:
Collections and Dispute Management (BFC)

Overview

This scope item helps you to streamline debt collection processes, resolve customer invoice disputes, and manage overdue receivables. You can also reduce your exposure to the risks and costs of bad debt.

Dispute management provides dispute managers with tools to process disputes centrally and protect customer relationships. They can effectively manage disputes by using dispute resolution tools, dunning integration, and workflow integration.

Collection specialists can proactively manage and collect overdue receivables by using receivables collections tools and dunning integration. The specialists have all the information and support they need to collect payments faster and provide improved customer service. They can identify bad debt risk potential and take preventative steps to reduce further exposure.

Key Process Flow

  • Define organizational structure

  • Capture dispute cases

  • Investigate and assign dispute cases to responsible staff

  • Manage and follow up on dispute case

The SAP Complaint Handling solution helps companies to manage complaints holistically. It provides a transparent view of complaints and follow-up activities to increase customer satisfaction and unlock additional supplier recovery potential.

Key Process Flow

  • Use built-in integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for claims and return processing

processes.description:
Complementary Procurement Functions (2TW)

Overview

The scope item covers the usage of complementary functions in sourcing and procurement. By enabling a lightweight process, the scope item enables the user to procure operating supplies as well as batch and serial-number-managed materials. Both processes can be summarized by the three following steps: purchase order creation, posting of a goods receipt, and invoice creation. The scope item focuses on the main process steps but can be enhanced by additional optional steps.

Operating supplies are externally procured materials that are used to manufacture products and comprise auxiliary materials and expendable supplies.

The procurement of batch managed materials enables the user to work with homogeneous partial quantities of a material. This can be leveraged for example to meet legal requirements, to track defects, or to ensure procedural requirements throughout the production process.

In alignment with the batch process, you can also procure serial-number-managed materials.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage purchase orders

  • Manage goods receipts

  • Manage invoices

Business Benefits

  • Streamline procurement processes in an efficient and cost-effective manner

  • Enable highly automated processes for the procurement of operating supplies

  • Enable highly automated processes for the procurement of batch and serial number managed materials

  • Reduce manual effort greatly

  • Support the user to meet legal requirements and track defects with batch and serial number managed material

  • Ensure procedural requirements throughout the production process with batch and serial number managed material

  • Enable monitoring for batch and serial-number-managed materials
processes.name: Complementary Procurement Functions

Overview

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (formerly SAP S/4HANA Cloud for advanced compliance reporting) is SAP’s solution for the fulfillment of real-time and statutory reporting requirements including end-to-end processing of transaction controls, digital link, and online submission requirements. This scope item activates the display and output of the country content for manual submission processes.

For information on covered process flows, see the following SAP note (list of covered legal obligations by country):

SAP S/4HANA for advanced compliance reporting is a global legal reporting platform that caters to companies’ indirect tax reporting requirements. This scope item covers company codes outside of Belgium with tax registration in Belgium.

processes.description:
Compliance Management for Environment, Health, and Safety (4C8)

Overview

This scope item helps you to manage compliance, and as a result, reduce operational risk in your company. You can manage compliance information about permits, regulations, and policies. You can import compliance requirements from a spreadsheet and streamline compliance planning by associating tasks directly with compliance requirements. The process also enables you to handle deviations.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage location master data

  • Plan, monitor, and manage compliance tasks

  • Execute task – My Inbox

  • Identify and manage compliance requirements

  • Manage deviations

Business Benefits

  • Manage requirements easily to support legal compliance for operational processes

  • Plan task activities related to the requirement to ensure that they're covered

  • Track and record keeping of the execution of the tasks to prove compliance

  • Handle noncompliance cases with an incident deviation process to cover the reporting requirements in such cases

processes.description:
Compliance Management with SAP Global Trade Services (24J)

Overview

You can utilize existing rules in SAP Global Trade Services on-premise by integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

This scope item enables the communication scenario and the appropriate RFC calls for synchronizing the relevant import and export documents. Successfully processing documents requires that the relevant customers and material masters already exist in the SAP Global Trade Services system.

Key Process Flow

  • Create applicable documents in SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to trigger document transfer to SAP Global Trade Services

Business Benefits

  • Integrate SAP Global Trade Services Compliance Management fully with SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Leverage an existing investment in SAP Global Trade Services 11.0 for a best-of-breed deployment of an international trade solution with minimal new configuration

This scope item changes the business process when activated. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Compliance Management with SAP Global Trade Services

processes.description:
Condition Contract with Customer Hierarchy – Consumer Products (6V0)

Overview

This scope item describes a sales process in the consumer products industry focusing on the subsequent settlement of rebate agreements using customer hierarchy.

For this purpose, three agreements (condition contracts) are created for different levels of the customer hierarchy:

  • An agreement for the entire customer hierarchy

  • A special agreement only for the customers in a particular state (on a particular customer hierarchy node)

  • A third agreement applies to the entire customer hierarchy except the customer hierarchy node with the special agreement

The process starts with the creation of standard sales orders. After confirming stock availability, the shipping specialist creates the outbound deliveries. When the goods issue is posted, the costs of the goods sold are recorded in Financial Accounting.

Once the goods are delivered and the proof of delivery (POD) is confirmed by the ship-to party, you can bill the delivery. After the invoice is posted and transferred to FI, you have the basis for a subsequent settlement of rebate agreements with your customers, the business volume base.

Key Process Flow

  • Create customer hierarchy

  • Create sales order

  • Review, release or reject a sales order

  • Create delivery

  • Execute picking

  • Post goods issue

  • Confirm proof of delivery

  • Create billing document

  • Create invoice list

  • Create condition contracts

  • Check business volume (optional)

  • Perform final settlement

Business Benefits

  • Run business volume evaluation and settlement based on customer hierarchy

  • Use a setup based on the customer structure
processes.name: Condition Contract with Customer Hierarchy – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Consumable Purchasing (BNX)

Overview

This scope item contains the creation and approval of purchase orders for consumables. Alternatively, the process can also be triggered via a purchase requisition, which can then be converted to a purchase order. Subsequently, the goods receipt and invoice processes are triggered.

Both standard and limit items can be procured with this scope item. As the value of the consumable goods is directly expended to an account assignment category, no inventory is provided.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage purchase requisitions

  • Manage purchase orders

  • Manage goods receipts

  • Manage invoices

Business Benefits

  • Streamline procurement processes in an efficient and cost-effective manner

  • Ensure highly automated processes for the procurement of consumables

  • Reduce manual effort greatly

  • Monitor the procurement progress in real-time

  • Monitor purchase order items with analytical list page
processes.name: Consumable Purchasing

processes.description:
Continuous Control Monitoring with SAP Process Control (2OH)

Overview

With this scope item, SAP Process Control customers can include SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition processes in continuous control monitoring.

Embedded compliance allows data to be retrieved from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and analyzed in SAP Process Control.

Key Process Flow

  • Define data sources and rules

  • Perform query

Business Benefits

  • Get real-time insight into status of internal controls and risks in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and reduced total cost of ownership

  • Create and get visibility of key indicators and metrics by business users

  • Deploy and automate routine tasks easily

  • Get auditability without effort

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item changes the business process when activated. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
