processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Cash Application (47I)

Overview

In this process, when you transfer your bank statement to payment lots, standard rule-based proposals are generated and the automatic posting and clearing is executed. If you've activated this scope item, the new machine learning service is triggered for payment lot items where the clearing isn't successfully completed. This service proposes selection categories and selection values for triggering the FI-CA clearing control. If you choose to trigger the automatic clearing and the confidence level is above the threshold, the FI-CA clearing control is automatically processed with consideration to the machine learning proposals.

Key Process Flow

  • Connect to machine learning service and configure machine learning confidence level

  • Train your machine learning model

  • Run payment lot, send data to machine learning service, and fetch the proposal

  • Process the clarifications

Business Benefits

  • Automate the clearing of incoming payments to open receivables

  • Improve the automatic clearing rate by applying machine learning techniques to the bank statement incoming payment and clearing process

  • Reduce manual work and save costs

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is a prerequisite for the usage of the SAP Cash Application, add-on for contract accounting. It requires manual configuration in the systems for integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Cash Application, add-on for contract accounting.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Cash Application

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Company Initiated Payments (2DP)

Overview

This process allows you to start the collect payment procedure from the company perspective. Using different methods, the company can receive the customer’s payment and perform further processing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create SEPA mandate

  • Create SEPA direct debit

  • Create SEPA credit transfer

  • Create return lots with or without bank statement

  • Perform clarification of lot

Business Benefits

  • Clear credit notes automatically in the payment run

  • Process return transactions provided in an electronic bank account statement to reverse failed payments

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The Contract Accounting – Master Data and Basic Functions (2AR) scope item is a prerequisite for this scope item. Before you can use this scope item, you must complete the set-up instructions of scope item 2AR.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Company Initiated Payments

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Contract-Based Revenue Recognition (3L3)

Overview

In this process, you integrate contract-based revenue recognition with contract accounting. You can create provider contracts with service-based products and invoice documents. A back-end service transfers revenue accounting items to contract-based revenue recognition. In addition, you can make a change scenario to provider contracts such as upsell, cross sell, down sell, renewal, and so on.

Key Process Flow

  • Create provider contract with service-based product

  • Create invoice document

  • Update provider contract

  • Transfer revenue accounting items to revenue accounting

  • Display revenue accounting items

Business Benefits

  • Get end-to-end scenarios from contract accounting to revenue recognition

  • Get complete lifecycle change scenarios for provider contracts

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The Contract Accounting – Master Data and Basic Functions (2AR) scope item is a prerequisite for this scope item. Before you can use this scope item, you must complete the set-up instructions of scope item 2AR.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Contract-Based Revenue Recognition

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Customer Initiated Payments (2BI)

Overview

Paid invoice processing allows you to post invoices that are already paid. You can also manage the payment card settlement process, ending in either a successful transfer to the General Ledger (FI-GL) or returns processing. The payment card process requires an integration of Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA) and Payment Hub (digital payments).

Key Process Flow

  • Post incoming payment data from bank statement file

  • Perform payment lot processing and check lot processing

Business Benefits

  • Post invoices with automatic clearing due to payment card information in one step

  • Perform automatic charge-back processing

  • Reconcile payment card transactions with payment advice provided by the Payment Hub

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Customer Initiated Payments

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Daily and Monthly Closing (2BK)

Overview

Daily and monthly closing allows you to prepare and carry out the activities required for day-end and month-end closing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA). The major activity for closing is the reconciliation between Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable and General Ledger (FI-GL). In addition, you can write off uncollectible receivables in Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA).

Key Process Flow

  • Close reconciliation keys

  • Close an accounting period

  • Transfer FI-CA total records to the General Ledger

  • Check the reconciliation between open items and the General Ledger

  • Write off open receivables and credits of a business partner

  • Display write-off history

  • Reveiew doubtful receivables

  • Perform foreign currency valuation

Business Benefits

  • Perform simple write-off process using reason codes

  • Ensure consistency between Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable and G/L during closing

  • Guarantee audit-proof data with reconciliation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The Contract Accounting – Master Data and Basic Functions (2AR) scope item is a prerequisite for this scope item. Before you can use this scope item, complete the set-up instructions of scope item 2AR.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Daily and Monthly Closing

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Enabling of Products with Variant Configuration (3L8)

Overview

Based on the Contract Accounting – Master Data and Basic Functions (2AR) scope item, you can enable variant configuration material in provider contract with variant pricing for the subsequent Convergent Invoicing – Recurring and One-Off Items (2T3) scope item. Rating, billing, and invoicing takes variant configuration materials into consideration. As a result, contract accounting can cover variant pricing for variant configuration products.

Key Process Flow

  • Create provider contract of product with variant configuration

  • Create subsequent rating, billing, and invoicing for provider contract with variant configuration product

Business Benefits

  • Cover variant pricing for variant configuration products in contract accounting

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is cross-topic, relating to both variant configuration and FICA-CI. This scope item is designed for FICA customer to create provider contracts for products with variant configuration.

This scope item shouldn't be activated by variant configuration customers, and is marked non-standard for such customers.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Enabling of Products with Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – External Tax Audit and Compliance Reporting (2SJ)

Overview

This process allows internal and external auditors to view, analyze, and extract accounting-relevant data from Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA). Accounting data covers the relevant customizing extracts, business partner extracts, and FI-CA documents. Extracts are exported by the Administrator – Accounts Payable and Receivable (FI-CA) and are analyzed by the External Auditor – Accounts Payable and Receivable (FI-CA). Extracts can also be imported into standard tax auditor software. This scope item supports the three legally required access types: direct system access, indirect system access, and file access.

Key Process Flow

  • Create data extracts

  • Import data extracts

  • Export data extracts

  • Get an overview of data extracts

  • Delete document extracts

Business Benefits

  • Analyze FI-CA documents from a tax auditor perspective

  • Extract accounting data for standard tax auditor software

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The Contract Accounting – Master Data and Basic Functions (2AR) scope item is a prerequisite for this scope item. Before you can use this scope item, complete the set-up instructions of scope item 2AR.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – External Tax Audit and Compliance Reporting

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Group Ledger IFRS (33X)

Overview

In this scope item, you handle ledger-specific transactions and reports for IFRS within contract accounting. This includes Doubtful Receivables, Foreign Currency Valuation, Day-End Closing, and Month-End Closing.

Key Process Flow

  • Review doubtful receivables

  • Perform foreign currency valuation

  • Perform day-end and month-end closing

Business Benefits

  • Support IFRS accounting principles

  • Ensure complete and accurate accounting data in parallel accounting

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The Contract Accounting – Master Data and Basic Functions (2AR) scope item is a prerequisite for this scope item. Before you can use this scope item, you must complete the set-up instructions of scope item 2AR.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Group Ledger IFRS

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Group Ledger US GAAP (33V)

Overview

In this process, you handle ledger-specific transactions and reports for US GAAP within contract accounting. This includes transactions such as Doubtful Receivables, Foreign Currency Valuation, Day-End Closing, and Month-End Closing.

  • Review doubtful receivables

  • Perform foreign currency valuation

  • Perform day-end and month-end closing

  • Support US GAAP accounting principles

  • Ensure complete and accurate accounting data in parallel accounting

processes.name: Contract Accounting – Group Ledger US GAAP

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Integration with Sales Documents (43Y)

Overview

This process enables you to post open items in Contract Accounting for billing documents from Sales Billing. Once the invoicing order is processed in Sales Billing, the document is posted in Contract Accounting as a follow-on document. You can use then the central functions for payment handling and collection management in Contract Accounting for these open items.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order

  • Bill the invoice

  • Check FICA document

Business Benefits

  • Enable end-to-end invoicing process in contract accounting in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Transfer SD billing documents to contract accounting

Business partner and contract management allows you to create and manage master data of a business partner and a contract account for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA). In addition, you can analyze whether business partner data can be deleted to satisfy data privacy constraints in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Furthermore, you can create and print correspondence.

If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Master Data and Basic Functions

processes.description:
Contract Accounting – Open Item Management (2UJ)

Overview

In this process, you handle open item management for contract accounting. This includes dunning, installment plans, interest calculation, and credit clarification.

Key Process Flow

  • Handle dunning

  • Handle installment plans

  • Handle interest calculation

  • Handle credit clarification

Business Benefits

  • Create and send payment reminders or dunning letters to your business partners to remind them of overdue payables and to request payment

  • Divide source items to several installment receivables that have a due date in the future

  • Determine and post interest receivables and payables

  • Process existing credits in accounts for your business partners

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Contract Accounting – Open Item Management

processes.description:
Contract for Central Procurement with SAP Ariba Contracts (4B0)

Overview

In this scope item, you can integrate value and quantity contracts. These are agreements for a company to order certain quantities of products during a specified period. In SAP Ariba Contracts, users can negotiate prices for goods and lean services to be procured, and they can sign a legally binding contract with a supplier. Pricing details are passed on from SAP Ariba Contracts to the operational system, so that operational purchasers can use these prices to buy goods or services as required.

Central procurement offers a centralized contract process across industries with a deep integration into the customer's landscape. It connects SAP Ariba Contracts to the customer’s ERP or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition systems, and exchanges business documents to ensure end-to-end business processes into finance and logistics that run in the connected systems.

Key Process Flow

  • Create contract in SAP Ariba Contracts

  • Set up and review contract terms

  • Approve contract

  • Send contract to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Create operational purchase contract automatically

  • Approve and release operational purchase contract automatically

  • Use operational purchase contract as source of supply

  • Create purchase order against operational purchase contract

Business Benefits

  • Manage purchase contracts for materials and lean services

  • Automate and accelerate the contract lifecycle

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item describes a cross-plant Kanban process in the Consumer Products industry.

The Kanban method for managing material replenishment between plants is based on the actual stock situation at the receiving location. When a Kanban container is set to empty, the system triggers a stock transfer from a supplying plant. The material is staged in defined quantities and transported to the receiving plant to ensure a continuous and demand-driven material supply at the consumption location.

According to the pull principle, replenishment isn't initiated by central planning, but directly by the receiving location when additional stock is required. The process is executed with predefined control cycle data to ensure that each Kanban status change automatically initiates the required logistical activities.

In this stock transfer scenario, the process starts when a Kanban container is set to empty. This action automatically triggers the creation of an outbound delivery in the supplying plant. The substeps include executing picking and posting goods issue. As soon as the material arrives at the receiving plant, the Kanban container is set to full, which automatically posts the goods receipt in the system.

Key Process Flow

Classic Kanban: Stock transfer cross plant

  • Set available Kanban to empty
  • Option 1: Create and execute outbound delivery
  • Option 2: Create outbound delivery with order reference
  • Create outbound delivery manually
  • Print the delivery pick list
  • Execute picking
  • Post goods issue
  • Evaluate stock/requirements situation
  • Monitor replenishment situation
  • Post goods receipt
  • Option 1: Set Kanban to full
  • Option 2: Post goods receipt directly
  • Analyze Kanban control cycles
  • Monitor replenishment situation

Business Benefits

  • Handle material management between plants
  • Improve monitoring of replenishment situation

processes.description:
Customer Consignment (1IU)

Overview

In this scenario, the goods are initially posted to the customer consignment stock and thus remain the property of the company (consignment fill-up).

At regular intervals, the customer reports how many articles are sold and how many articles are in the current stock (inventory). When the inventory is performed, the batch number may be entered to do a correct material posting. A corresponding sales order is entered that documents the issue from the customer consignment, meaning that the goods are no longer the property of the company (consignment issue).

Goods that are not required can be returned from the consignment stock to the central warehouse. The goods must not be defective. They are posted directly into the free stock (consignment pick-up).

In some cases, goods are returned to the customer consignment stock (by its own customer or based on erroneous consumption posting) after the consignment issue has already taken place. A return order is then created (consignment return).

Key Process Flow

  • Fill up the consignment stock assigned to the customer (consignment fill-up)

  • Issue from the consignment stock (consignment issue)

  • Return materials from the external customer consignment stock to the company warehouse (consignment pick-up)

  • Return order to the consignment stock (consignment return)

Business Benefits

  • Save costs on inventory for consignor

  • Restock as it sells – beneficial for both parties

  • Save time for consignor

  • Use the consignment stock to generate product exposure (especially new or unknown products) for their customers
processes.name: Customer Consignment

processes.description:
Customer Returns (BKP)

Overview

This scope item covers three customer return scenarios:

1.) Return to seller: A returns order is created (optionally with reference to the original billing document or sales document). Once saved, a returns delivery is automatically generated. After goods receipt, the inspection takes place at the warehouse. The user can influence when the refunding documents are created: either directly, when releasing the returns order, or after the inspection. Finally, the user can decide on the compensation type for the customer: either shipping a replacement or paying a credit memo.

2.) Return to seller with inspection at customer site: The seller decides to perform the inspection at the customer site before initiating a physical return.

3.) Return to supplier via seller: After inspection at seller, the products should be shipped back to supplier. The supplier decides on the refund towards the seller, while the seller decides on the compensation towards the customer.

The progress of the return process can be monitored using returns overview.

Key Process Flow

Return to seller:

  • Create returns order

  • Perform product inspection

  • Process logistical follow-up activities, as for instance transfer to free available stock or scrap

  • Determine compensation

  • Create credit memo or replace product free of charge

  • Display returns overview and track customer returns processes

Return to seller with inspection at customer site:

  • Create returns order

  • Change returns order after inspection at customer site

  • Reject return, specify compensation, or initiate physical return

  • Create credit memo or replace product free of charge

Return to supplier via seller:

  • Create returns order

  • Perform product inspection

  • Generate returns purchase order: Request return to supplier

  • Ship to supplier

  • Issue refund via credit memo or product replacement (shipped free of charge) from supplier to seller

Business Benefits

  • Generate follow-up documents automatically

  • Perform refund in one step

  • Include goods inspection

  • Reduce transportation costs and save time while performing inspection at customer site

  • Return goods to supplier via seller

  • Provide end-to-end support and monitoring of the return process
processes.name: Customer Returns

processes.description:
Customer Returns for Material with Variant Configuration (7KW)

Overview

The scope item is dedicated to handle material with variant configuration for a customer returns process.

A configurable material using the Advanced Variant Configuration can be included in returns order. It can be single-level and multi-level configurable material. Configuration can be copied over from a sales order when created with reference or maintained during creation without reference. Sales price is calculated with condition for configurations. A returns delivery is automatically generated once the returns order is released. After goods receipt, the inspection takes place at the warehouse and final logistical follow up is decided. Refund can be determined either directly when releasing the returns order, or after the inspection. Compensation to customer by credit memo is available.

Key Process Flow

  • Create returns order for material with variant configuration

  • Generate returns delivery

  • Post goods receipt

  • Perform material inspection

  • Determine refund

  • Create credit memo

Business Benefits

  • Improve your customer returns end to end process for configurable material covering single-level and multi-level configuration.

  • Transfer configuration information among different sales documents.

  • Get sales pricing and print-out according to the configuration.
processes.name: Customer Returns for Material with Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Customer Returns for Non-Stock and Service Materials (3TE)

Overview

A non-stock or service material can be used in the returns order. Non-stock and service materials are not included in inventory management. With creation of a returns delivery, the goods receipt is reflected by a confirmation posting. Non-stock and service items can be handled along with stock items in one returns order.

The user can influence when the refunding documents are created: either directly when releasing a returns order, or after materials are received physically. Finally, the user can decide on the compensation type for the customer: paying a credit memo or shipping a replacement.

Key Process Flow

  • Create returns order

  • Generate returns delivery

  • Post goods receive (statistical confirmation)

  • Determine refund

  • Create credit memo or send replacement free of charge

Business Benefits

  • Take back items from your customer that do not need maintenance in inventory, simplifying data entry for the items

  • Integrate return of non-stock and service materials fully in returns order processing

  • Decide immediate on compensation options
processes.name: Customer Returns for Non-Stock and Service Materials

processes.description:
Customer Returns for Sales Kits (5CX)

Overview

Companies often want to return individual products that are bundled into a sales kit (for example selling a PC together with monitor, keyboard, mouse, license, and so on). In such cases, sales kits are commonly used to sell and return individual products independently from the bundled product. Bills of materials (BOMs) are used to bundle sales kits.

The process of customer returns in returns management supports BOMs. The process starts with customer returns order creation. The sales kit material is then logistically received into the plant. Subsequently, a credit memo or replacement material is provided to customer as compensation.

Once you enter a bill of material in a customer returns order, the system runs pricing and logistics execution at the following levels:

- Header level (ERLA): usually used when product is assembled

- Item level (LUMF): usually used when product is not assembled

- Both levels (CPFH): pricing is run on header level and logistics (goods movements) on item level

- Both levels (DISH): pricing is run on item level and logistics (goods movement) on header level

Key Process Flow

  • Create customer returns order

  • Pick and post goods receipt

  • Perform material inspection

  • Send back to customer, move to free available stock or scrap

  • Create credit memo or send replacement

  • Display return overview

Business Benefits

  • Increase process flexibility within returns order processing

  • Enhance efficiency in the comprehensive returns process
processes.name: Customer Returns for Sales Kits

processes.description:
Customer Returns Involving Supplier by Message Exchange (3QD)

Overview

1.) Seller returning to supplier:

After lean inspection at seller side, a returns purchase order is created to ask for authorization to return goods back to supplier. A return material authorization (RMA) is sent via message exchange to supplier.

If the supplier rejects the RMA, the seller's receiving specialist decides on alternative follow-up actions. Further processing options are according to the customer returns scope item.

If the supplier approves the RMA, the goods are returned to the supplier.

2.) Supplier receiving return request by seller:

The supplier, using message exchange, asks for authorization to return goods to the plant for credit. The RMA request creates a returns order with seller being customer.

The return and refund specialist approves or rejects the RMA and notifies the seller via message exchange.

If approved, the return delivery is automatically created. The goods are inspected after they are received in return stock. Further processing options are according to the customer returns scope item.

If the return and refund specialist decides on paying a credit memo, a corresponding EDI message is sent to the seller.

Key Process Flow

1.) Seller returning to supplier:

  • Create returns order

  • Perform material inspection

  • Generate return purchase order: Request return to supplier via RMA

  • Ship to supplier if RMA is approved

  • Refund from supplier to seller

  • Refund to customer from seller with credit memo

  • Ship free-of-charge material replacement from seller

2.) Supplier receiving return request by seller:

  • Create return order via message exchange

  • Decide on return material authorization (RMA) and notify seller

  • Receive goods and perform product inspection if RMA is approved

  • Determine refund for seller

  • Create credit memo towards seller via message exchange

Business Benefits

  • Process return orders end-to-end between seller and supplier using return material authorizations (RMA)

  • Experience more automation in returning goods between seller and supplier

  • Increase productivity, performance, and work satisfaction
processes.name: Customer Returns Involving Supplier by Message Exchange

processes.description:
Customer Returns Management – Consumer Products (61V)

Overview

This scope item covers the Return to Seller process for a customer return scenario in the Consumer Products industry.

A return order is created in reference to the original billing document. Once saved, a return delivery is automatically generated. The goods, once received, are inspected at the warehouse.

The user can influence when the refunding documents are created: either directly, when releasing a return order, or after the inspection. Finally, the user can decide on the compensation for the customers: full or partial refund.

The progress of the return process can be monitored using a returns overview.

Key Process Flow

  • Create Return Order

  • Perform Picking for the Return Delivery

  • Post Goods Receipt

  • Perform Material Inspection

  • Determine Refund

  • Display Return Overview

  • Create Credit Memo

Business Benefits

  • Use an automated process to cover customer returns
processes.name: Customer Returns Management – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Customer Returns with Direct Shipment from Customer to Supplier (1Z3)

Overview

The customer contacts the seller and informs the internal sales representative that they want to return products. The sales representative decides that the products must be returned directly to the supplier. This can be the case, for example, when products are initially shipped to the customer via third-party delivery by the supplier.

The sales representative creates a returns order to initiate the return of products to the supplier. Once the returns order is saved and released, a returns purchase order is generated automatically. After the supplier has received the returned products, the seller gets a credit memo from the supplier. The seller compensates the customer with a credit memo or replacement product.

The progress of the customer return processes is monitored by tracking the follow-up documents of returns orders.

Key Process Flow

  • Create returns order

  • Create returns purchase order (automatically)

  • Perform logistical return of products from customer directly to supplier

  • Perform logistical goods receipt at supplier side

  • Receive credit memo (seller) from supplier

  • Issue credit memo or replacement (seller) to customer

Business Benefits

  • Enable return of materials from customer directly to supplier
processes.name: Customer Returns with Direct Shipment from Customer to Supplier

processes.description:
Customs Management with SAP Global Trade Services (2U1)

Overview

SAP Global Trade Services Customs Management installations can be integrated with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to handle global trade scenarios for import before goods receipt and export management.

Key Process Flow

  • Transfer customers, suppliers, and products from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Global Trade Services

  • Create customs declaration prior to goods receipt for imports and for exports

Business Benefits

  • Integrate SAP Global Trade Services Customs Management with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Leverage an existing investment in SAP Global Trade Services for a best-of-breed deployment of an international trade solution with minimal new configuration

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item changes the business process when activated. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Customs Management with SAP Global Trade Services

processes.description:
Dangerous Goods in the Value Chain (3G8)

Overview

This scope item supports a dangerous goods transport permissibility check that is carried out in business documents within the value chain and the printing of the dangerous goods description on certain documents as follows:

  • In sales documents and outbound delivery documents, a transport permissibility check is carried out for all compliance-relevant products. For each compliance-relevant product that is added to a business document, the system checks if the product is classified as a dangerous good. If so, the system checks if the transport of the product is allowed. If the product is not classified or if transport is not allowed, this check can result in a block. If a dangerous goods assessment is not yet completed, a corresponding request to the product steward specialist or the dangerous goods specialists is created.

  • Dangerous goods descriptions are printed on sales order confirmations, delivery notes, and picking lists.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a sales order

  • Carry out the dangerous goods check in the sales order

  • Trigger a dangerous goods assessment if it is missing

  • Print the dangerous goods description on a sales order confirmation

  • Trigger outbound delivery creation

  • Carry out the dangerous goods check in the outbound delivery

  • Perform picking/packing

  • Print the dangerous goods description on the picking list and the delivery note

  • Post the goods issue

  • Carry out the dangerous goods check at goods issue in the outbound delivery

Business Benefits

  • Mitigate compliance risks with up-to-date information integrated into the value chain

  • Integrate dangerous goods checks in the selling, delivery, transportation, and purchasing processes

  • Inform the product steward specialist and the dangerous goods specialists about new countries/regions where products are intended to be transported
processes.name: Dangerous Goods in the Value Chain

processes.description:
Data Migration to SAP S/4HANA from SAP (BH3)

Overview

Customers can use the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit as part of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition license. If the customers choose to migrate data directly from an SAP system, they use a communication arrangement to connect the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit to the source system. The migration cockpit selects data from the source system by using specific criteria.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a project

  • Create or update communication arrangement

  • Select the migration objects that are relevant for your migration project

  • Select data

  • Optional: Use staging tables as intermediate storage. This requires a database connection to a remote SAP HANA schema.

  • Process any open mapping tasks to ensure that the source data is mapped correctly

  • Simulate the migration of data

  • Rework data and repeat mapping tasks (if required)

  • Repeat the simulation process (if required)

  • Migrate the data to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system

Business Benefits

  • Deliver migration projects on time and within budget

  • Provide trusted data to users

  • Ensure quality master data for your core business processes

  • Validate the data against specific customer business rules

  • Load data into your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system
processes.name: Data Migration to SAP S/4HANA from SAP

processes.description:
Data Migration to SAP S/4HANA from Staging (2Q2)

Overview

With SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, you can use the included SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit to migrate your data. When you choose the Migrate Data Using Staging Tables approach, the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit creates staging tables for the migration objects that are relevant for your project and migrates the data from these staging tables to the target SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

  • If you use the Local SAP S/4HANA Database Schema option, the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit generates the staging tables in the local ABAP schema of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. We recommend using this option if you want to populate the staging tables using the template files provided by SAP.

  • If you use the Remote SAP HANA Database Schema option, you specify the relevant connection to a remote SAP HANA system. The SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit generates the staging tables there. The set-up instructions provided for this scope item are only relevant for this option.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a project

  • Select the migration objects that are relevant for your migration project

  • Fill the staging tables with data using SAP or third-party ETL tools or by using the template files provided by SAP

  • Process any open mapping tasks to ensure correct source data mapping

  • Simulate the migration of data

  • Rework data and repeat mapping tasks (if required)

  • Repeat the simulation process (if required)

  • Migrate the data to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Business Benefits

  • Deliver migration projects on time and within budget

  • Provide trusted data to users

  • Increase data load performance by changing to table read rather than file upload

  • Ensure quality master data for your core business processes

  • Validate the data against specific customer business rules

  • Load data into your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system
processes.name: Data Migration to SAP S/4HANA from Staging

processes.description:
Overview

With this scope item, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition simplifies the separation of business partner master data based on legal entities (data controllers) and purposes. This approach supports privacy by design and default.

Many business processes that involve personal data begin with the creation of master data. When you create and manage a business partner, you can add several types of data to that business partner. Examples include contact details, financial information, and employment history. Each type of data creates different levels of privacy risk for individuals. To manage these risks, this scope item provides a switch to a data model that lets you manage personal data according to the legal entities responsible for the data (data controllers) and the purposes for collecting and processing the data. This helps you comply with legal standards.

After you centrally define data controllers and purposes and assign these to business partners, you can restrict access to business partner master data based on these assignments. This ensures that only authorized users access the personal data of business partners. You can activate these authorization checks separately for data controllers and purposes. This gives you flexibility in your implementation. You can start by separating data based on data controllers and then introduce purpose-based authorization checks if required.

Key Process Flow

  • Define data controllers and manage assignments to business partners.
  • Define purposes for processing personal data and manage purpose assignments for master data and transactional data.
  • Restrict access to business partner master data. For example, edit, display, or search. The restrictions are based on assigned data controllers and purposes.
  • Relate data categories of transactional application object instances to purposes.

Business Benefits

The assignment of personal data to data controllers and purposes:

  • Provides clarity about which organizations are responsible and authorized to handle the data.
  • Clarifies which business partners’ personal data is processed by which legal entities and for what purpose.
  • Improves transparency regarding applicable retention rules, which differ among legal entities and their businesses.
  • Supports data subject requests regarding information, correction, and deletion.

Exclude from Default Activation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

This scope item has a significant impact on business partner objects in your system. The activation occurs in separate phases.

  1. Data Controller Assignment

    Activate the data controller assignment feature in your configuration environment. You can then create data controllers in your system and assign them to your business partner master data. Once you've set this up, you can either enable authorization checks on master data directly or implement purpose assignment as a next step.

  2. Purpose Assignment

    Activate purpose assignment in your configuration environment. You can assign purposes to both transactional data and business partner master data.

  3. Header-Level Authorization Checks for Business Partner Master Data

    To restrict access to business partners based on data controller and purpose assignments, activate authorization checks as a final step.

    Note: Once you activate authorization checks based on data controller and purpose assignments, an incomplete setup might cause you to lose access to your master data.
processes.name: Data Protection and Privacy – Data Controller and Purpose

processes.description:
Data Protection and Privacy (5LE)

Overview

When configuring, applying, or operating an IT landscape, companies have always regarded general, country/region-specific, local, and industry-specific legislation. General data protection regulation is associated with numerous legal requirements and privacy concerns that may affect the configuration and setup of an IT system. For example, this may include commercial, fiscal, accounting, or specific tax requirements.

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition supports customers in their journey to comply with relevant data protection and privacy requirements. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition supports data protection by providing security features and specific data-protection-relevant functions, such as simplified blocking and deletion of personal data, information retrieval framework, read access logging, and consent management. SAP doesn't provide legal advice in any form. The used definitions and other terms don't necessarily refer to specific legislation.

Key Process Flow

  • Set up blocking processes for business partner, customer, and supplier master data

  • Set up request reasons for unblocking of business partner, customer, and supplier master data

  • Configure the residence and retention periods for business partner master data in relation to business partner referencing the application data

  • Import, search, and display consent records

  • Display the search results subdivided according to the purpose for which the data was collected and processed

  • Import, search and display consent records

  • Configure and activate read access logging for personal sensitive data

Business Benefits

  • Block and delete personal data based on SAP Information Lifecycle Management

  • Include business partner end-of-purpose functionality with blocking and unblocking of business partner, customer, and supplier master data

  • Read access logging of sensitive personal data

  • Search and retrieve personal data of a specified data subject according to purpose with the information retrieval framework

  • Manage consent data (import, search, and display consent records) with consent administration
processes.name: Data Protection and Privacy

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item enables you to define data quality rules and KPIs for business partner master data. You can evaluate the quality of business partner data according to these rules and monitor the current state of the data quality as well as its trend.

To define rules, you can use machine learning capabilities and detect patterns with rule mining. These patterns from rule mining can be transferred to data quality rules.

By analyzing the evaluation results, you can identify areas of data with errors and potential reasons for errors, and you can then initiate the correction. You can also use the data quality rules to validate data in Master Data Consolidation for Business Partner (‏1N3‏) and Mass Processing for Business Partner (‏1N7‏).

Several business catalogs can be assigned to a business role to perform various functional needs. The business catalog details can be found in the test script.

Key Process Flow

  • Create master data quality rule for business partners
  • Configure data quality scores
  • Perform evaluation run for business partner data
  • Get data quality evaluation overview

Business Benefits

  • Create data quality rules that can be used for evaluating data quality of business partners
  • Provides dashboards showing a high-level overview of your data quality and data quality trends across an entire business object

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Data Quality Management for Business Partner

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item enables you to define data quality rules and KPIs for product master data. You can evaluate the quality of product master data according these rules and monitor the current state of the data quality as well as its trend.

To define rules, you can use machine learning capabilities and detect patterns with rule mining. These patterns from rule mining can be transferred to data quality rules.

By analyzing the evaluation results, you can identify areas of data with errors and potential reasons for data with errors, and you can then initiate the correction. Furthermore, you can use the data quality rules to validate data in Master Data Consolidation for Product (‏1N1‏) and Central Governance for Product (‏1N5‏).

Several business catalogs can be assigned to a business role to perform various functional needs. The business catalog details can be found in the test script.

Key Process Flow

  • Create master data quality rule for products
  • Configure data quality scores
  • Perform evaluation run for products
  • Get data quality evaluation overview

Business Benefits

  • Create data quality rules that can be used for evaluating data quality of products
  • Provide dashboards showing a high-level overview of your data quality and data quality trends across an entire business object

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Data Quality Management for Product

processes.description:
Debit Memo Processing (1F1)

Overview

A debit memo request is created with the amount to be debited and placed on a billing block for review. It is then released to become billing relevant and appear on the billing due list. Periodic billing process creates a debit memo to be sent to the customer and posts a journal entry.

Key Process Flow

  • Create debit memo request

  • Remove billing block (review debit memo request)

  • Create debit memo

Business Benefits

  • System integrated debit memo processing
processes.name: Debit Memo Processing

processes.description:
Debt and Investment Management – Group Ledger IFRS (1X7)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for Debt and Investment Management – Group Ledger IFRS, you can use an additional valuation area besides your operational valuation area according to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS 9) phase I (Classification and Measurement).

Key Process Flow

  • Generate and post accounting postings

  • Run accruals

  • Perform valuation of financial instruments

  • Reclassify from long term to short term

  • Post realized profit and loss

Business Benefits

  • Generate all postings for the general ledger

  • Update the general ledger according to IFRS 9 phase I (Classification and Measurement)

  • Process the valuation of transactions and position

  • Automate the month-end accounting processing
processes.name: Debt and Investment Management – Group Ledger IFRS

processes.description:
Debt and Investment Management – Group Ledger US GAAP (34C)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for Debt and Investment Management – Group Ledger US GAAP, you can use an additional valuation area besides your operational valuation area according to US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (US GAAP).

Key Process Flow

  • Post flows to general ledger

  • Perform period-end closing

  • Reclassify from long term to short term

  • Post realized profit and loss

Business Benefits

  • Generate all postings for the general ledger

  • Update the general ledger according to US GAAP

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

All starter, demo, and trial systems, by default, are set up with group ledger IFRS. This scope item is therefore excluded. Customers can decide to use this scope item in their systems based on the selected scope bundle.
processes.name: Debt and Investment Management – Group Ledger US GAAP

processes.description:
Debt and Investment Management (1WV)

Overview

The debt and investment management process helps you to secure short-term liquidity at optimal interest rates while effectively managing medium- to long-term debt and investments. This functionality automates labor-intensive tasks like confirming financial transactions and accounting postings, allowing you to focus on more strategic activities. It supports both operational and accounting needs and includes products such as fixed-interest and variable-interest investments and borrowing, commercial paper transactions, and deposit facilities.

Key Process Flow

  • Create financial transactions

  • Automate confirmations

  • Process payments

  • Transfer values to general ledger

  • Adjust interest rates

  • Perform month-end accounting processes

  • Perform reclassification

  • Calculate and post realized profit and loss

  • Monitor and report on positions and financial transactions

Business Benefits

  • Review the financial status

  • Automate the management of investments and borrowings, including creation of the financial transaction, confirmation of contract with counterparty, payments, interest rate adjustments, and accounting

  • Make better operational and strategic decisions using the comprehensive reporting and analysis tools

  • Improve internal operational compliance

  • Increase your focus on value-added activities instead of on manual procedures
processes.name: Debt and Investment Management

processes.description:
Overview

The process begins with the creation of a standard delivery, assuming the necessary master data (such as the Business Partner for Customer) is already maintained. From this delivery document, a picking list is generated to prepare products for shipment.

For deliveries with batch-managed materials, a batch number can be assigned to each item. If items from different batches are used, delivery items can be split to accurately record quantities for each batch.

Delivery documents can be split into multiple deliveries to accommodate changes in transportation planning. Freight costs can also be added to ensure accurate invoicing.

After picking, the shipping specialist posts a goods issue to relieve inventory, recording the physical quantity shipped. This action also records the cost of goods sold in financial accounting.

Once inventory is relieved, the delivery can be invoiced. If a proof-of-delivery is required, the customer must confirm the delivered quantity. Invoicing is then based on these confirmed quantities, and both revenue and cost of goods sold are recorded in management accounting.

Key Process Flow

  • Create delivery
  • Create attachment for delivery
  • Enter batch number
  • Execute picking
  • Execute packing
  • Split outbound delivery
  • Add freight costs
  • Post goods issue
  • Create pro forma invoices
  • Get proof of delivery
  • Create billing documents
  • Create attachment for billing

Business Benefits

  • Enable customers to:
  • Pick goods from manufacturer’s warehouse without advance order
  • Directly pick, pack, and send

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Delivery Processing Without Order Reference

processes.description:
Demand-Driven Buffer Level Management (1Y2)

Overview

Demand-driven replenishment (DD) helps to plan and manage supply chains efficiently based on customer demand, rather than through traditional MRP procedures. It forms the basis for a reliable material flow by defining buffers at strategically important points and adjusting these buffers regularly.

Products at all Bill-of-Material (BoM) levels are classified based on average demand, lead time, BoM usage, and variability to identify if they are relevant for demand-driven replenishment. A well-balanced buffer level is proposed for DD-relevant products to ensure that they are sufficiently stocked to meet average demand, but in low enough quantities to prevent excessive storage costs or losses due to expiry. An app helps planners manage safety stock, reorder point, and maximum stock through the buffer level proposals. To support the calculation of buffer levels, predictive material and resource planning (pMRP) can be deployed.

Key Process Flow

Buffer Positioning:

  • Classify products based on their goods issue value, usage across BoMs, and variation in actual demand to help identify whether they are relevant for Demand-Driven Replenishment

  • Display and change master data records relevant to Demand-Driven Replenishment for several products simultaneously

  • Optionally, use different scenarios, such as inbound protection, to position buffers efficiently within your supply chain

Buffer Sizing:

  • Classify products relevant to Demand-Driven Replenishment based on their decoupled lead time, and helps define inputs for their buffer settings

  • Review and maintain buffer profiles for variability and lead-time factors depending on product classification

  • Generate buffer (stock) level proposals for products based on their average daily usage, decoupled lead time, buffer profiles, and several other factors

  • Manage safety stock, reorder point, and maximum stock using buffer level proposals

  • Use predictive Material and Resource Planning (pMRP) for average daily use calculations (optional)

  • Optionally, use machine learning capabilities for the prediction of lead times

Business Benefits

  • Avoid the bull-whip effect in production by providing decoupling points with strategic stock positions

  • Enable immediate production of individualized products using adaptive component buffers

  • Ensure highest service levels at lowest possible inventory along all BoM levels

  • Improve material requirements planning based on high-quality data that is updated regularly and is used as input, such as for stock levels

  • Use predictive Material and Resource Planning (pMRP) for reliable input to buffer level calculations (optional)
processes.name: Demand-Driven Buffer Level Management

processes.description:
Demand-Driven Replenishment Planning and Execution (2QI)

Overview

Demand-driven replenishment (DD) helps you efficiently plan and manage supply chains based on customer demand, rather than through traditional MRP procedures. It forms the basis for a reliable material flow by defining buffers at strategically important points and adjusting these buffers regularly.

Dedicated apps provide views for replenishment planning and execution. With replenishment planning, an overview of the buffer information sorted by planning priority is shown. With this, you can trigger replenishment on time to avoid stock shortages and delays in the completion of production or sales orders due to insufficient stock. With replenishment execution, you can view the current stock situation for each product and check that sufficient on-hand stock is available for production. You can expedite replenishment directly, and by using readily available contact details, such as contacting the supplier of a purchase order or the production supervisor of the component production order.

Key Process Flow

Replenishment Planning:

  • Review replenishment planning status of buffered components

  • Create demand for buffered component via the finished good (two options) with dependent requirement covering discrete and process industry as well as repetitive manufacturing

  • Create supply for buffered component after change of planning status

Replenishment Execution:

  • Review replenishment execution status of buffered components after conversion of supply into production execution

  • Reduce on-hand stock to stimulate replenishment need (optional)

  • Expedite supply and run production execution to bring replenishment execution status to green

Review Projected On-Hand Alerts:

  • Review different on-hand alerts, such as safety stock alert, threshold alert, and stock-out alert, indicating potential upcoming on-hand stock issue

Review Historical Buffer Performance

Business Benefits

  • Avoid the bull-whip effect in production by providing decoupling points with strategic stock positions

  • Ensure highest service levels at lowest possible inventory along all BOM levels

  • Relieve users of manual supply creation for demand-driven materials

  • Support user in identifying issues with current stock levels and in prioritizing the issues as a starting point for taking the right action

  • Cover dependent requirements configurations for discrete and process industry as well as repetitive manufacturing
processes.name: Demand-Driven Replenishment Planning and Execution

processes.description:
Determination of Geocoordinates, Distances and Durations (46P)

Overview

To determine geocoordinates for locations, distances, and durations for location pairs within Transportation Management, you need to use SAP HANA spatial services as part of the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). You need an SAP BTP account that is enabled for consumption-based commercial models, such as the SAP BTP Enterprise Agreement (BTPEA).

This scope item delivers the necessary settings and information to activate the integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP HANA spatial services running on SAP BTP. For more information, see SAP Note 3058573 – Integration Note: SAP HANA Spatial Services / SAP Transportation Management.

Key Process Flow

  • Automatically determine geocoordinates for locations, distances and durations for pairs of locations

Business Benefits

  • Use geocoordinates of locations to determine distances and durations for pairs of locations

  • Allow scheduling of transportation activities in road freight orders as part of manual transportation planning (Scope item 6W2 – Manual Transportation Planning)

  • Get visibility on distances and durations in the Transportation Cockpit app and the user interfaces for freight units and road freight orders to enable better manual transportation planning (Scope item 6W2 – Manual Transportation Planning)

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that want to automatically determine geocoordinates for locations, distances, and durations for pairs of locations in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. To make use of this functionality, a license for SAP HANA spatial services is required, which runs on SAP Business Technology Platform. For SAP Business Technology Platform, a separate license is required.
processes.name: Determination of Geocoordinates, Distances and Durations

processes.description:
Digital Payments – Sales (1Z1)

Overview

SAP digital payments is a payment capability for payment service providers and SAP components, solutions, or applications that process incoming credit card payments.

Payment card information available in the business partner master data can be used when creating the sales order or new payment card data (one-time payment card) can be used in the sales order. When you save the sales order, the authorization of the payment card is executed through the payment provider service.

The credit card authorization can be cancelled by deleting the authorized amount in the sales order. Then a re-authorization can be done after changing the order quantity.

Furthermore, the credit card authorization can be cancelled by rejecting the sales order which has an amount authorized for credit card payment.

Key Process Flow

Using credit card data maintained in business partner in sales document:

  • Add and register credit card data in business partner

  • Assign customer payment guarantee procedure

  • Check credit card data in sales documents

  • Release sales documents with payment card

  • Proceed with all succeeding steps of related scope items (such as BD9) until billing document is created

  • Check credit card data in billing document

Using one-time credit card data in sales document:

  • Check credit card data in sales documents

Direct Debit (19M)

Overview

For SEPA countries/regions: In this scope item, you can use the direct debit payment method in the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) to collect payments from your customers in Euro and certain non-SEPA countries/regions to collect payments from your customers in your local currency.

For countries/regions in SEPA, a debtor grants mandates to a creditor as part of a direct debit procedure. Using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, you create and maintain the SEPA mandates from the customers, which are the legal basis for the direct debit payment in SEPA.

The system checks that a valid SEPA mandate exists during the payment run. For SEPA countries/regions, the system saves the ID of the SEPA mandate in the payment data and creates a SEPA-specific payment medium.

You can print out SEPA mandates on paper and repeat the printing.

For non-SEPA countries/regions: In this scope item, you can use the direct debit payment method to collect payments from your customers in your local currency.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain customer master data

  • Create and print direct debit mandate for SEPA countries/regions

  • Run payment program

  • Create payment instructions file

  • Send payment instruction file to bank

Business Benefits

  • Reduce workload in accounts receivables

  • Reduce customer credit risk

Overview

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (formerly SAP S/4HANA Cloud for Advanced Compliance Reporting & SAP Document Compliance) allows a customer to comply with electronic invoicing (e-invoicing), electronic reporting (e-reporting), and statutory reporting obligations. With the activation of this scope item, you can enable and control the visibility of advanced features on a country or region level. To see a full list of the advanced features, check the latest version of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition feature and scope description.

Key Process Flow

Business Benefits

  • Perform analytics and preview data for statutory reports and electronic documents (e-documents)
  • Make manual adjustments for statutory reports
  • Collaborate with SAP CoPilot
  • Exchange e-invoices and e-documents in real-time scenarios
  • Adapt statutory reporting and e-invoicing scenarios to your needs by extending our solution and building your own reports and scenarios

Exclude from Default Activation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

This scope item requires an additional license when the customer uses advanced features of Document and Reporting Compliance (formerly part of Advanced Compliance reporting).

For a customer with an SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition license before Q4/2021:

If more than 24 declarations using Advanced Compliance Reporting are made, either the additional license is required, or advanced features need to be switched off.

How the 24 declarations work:

Identify the number of legal entities across countries/regions and corresponding legal reports required by the customer. Sum up the number of declarations required per legal entity, per report per year (for example, one company code with a monthly VAT return = 12 declarations), additional or correction runs are counted as well.

How to switch off advanced features:

For customers who bought SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition before Q4/2021, advanced features are automatically visible. If Document and Reporting Compliance (5XU) is activated, visibility is controlled according to the maintenance of this scope item.

Earmarked Funds (78S)

Overview

Earmarked funds are business transactions that claim already allocated budget for expected expenditures. The following business transactions are grouped together under the term Earmarked Funds:

  • Funds commitments

Earmarked Funds for Real Estate Contracts (6R3)

Overview

Lease contracts describe contractual agreements between two partners: the lessor and the lessee. The lessor is the owner of an asset, whereas the lessee has a right to use this asset during the period agreed in the lease contract. For the use of the asset, the lessee must pay lease payments, which are agreed in the lease contract.

When a public sector organization enters into a lease-in contract, they may need to commit budget for such an obligation. Earmarked funds are used to create such a commitment for a lease-in contract. This scope item automates your lease-in obligation process for contract management by automatically creating earmarked funds for a lease-in contract at the time of contract creation and reducing the obligation with an actual posting when you generate invoices during periodic posting for both valuated and non-valuated leases.

Key Process Flow

  • Create RE-FX Contract

  • Generate earmarked funds automatically

  • Make periodic postings of RE-FX Contract

  • Perform automatic reduction of earmarked funds

Business Benefits

  • Create earmarked funds automatically when you create a lease-in contract

  • Reduce earmarked funds and consume it automatically when you post an invoice through periodic postings

  • Determine your budget account for valuated leases

This scope item is only applicable if the Public Sector Management Bundle / Government Budget Management has been selected into scope.

The technician can identify an issue affecting a piece of equipment, immediately fix the issue, and later report the time spent and the material consumed. The technician can enter required data quickly. It can then be used for planning objects (such as maintenance orders) and for actual recording (order confirmation, notification data, and goods movements). Planned data does not differ from the actual data, which is the work recorded on an operation corresponding to the confirmed actual work. The order is created, released, and if required, technically completed. In addition, you can install, dismantle, or replace pieces of equipment.

processes.description:
Empties for Retail (5FK)

Overview

Some retailers sell articles to which deposit-relevant packaging articles are assigned to. Consumers buy the packaging article with the main article and pay a deposit price for it. This packaging article can later be returned by the consumer and the deposit is refunded.

Beverages are the most common example. In some countries or regions, the empty bottle (and potentially also the crate containing multiple bottles) are subject to deposit handling. For example, an empty bottle is sold along with the lemonade (the full article), and twelve empty bottles and an empty crate are sold together with a crate of lemonade.

The article master for the full article is set up with a bill of material, reflecting the assignment of the full article to the relevant empties. The relationship of full and empty articles is carried through all supply chain processes and respective operational documents, starting with the procurement from external suppliers (purchase orders), and ending with the sale to consumer (sales in the store).

In inventory management, two types of empties stock are distinguished. The tied empties stock reflects the quantities attached to the full articles, but the untied stock considers only the inventory of stand-alone empties (for example, an empty bottle returned by the consumer on its way back to the supplier). Inventory reporting considers both types of stock. From a financial perspective, tied and untied empties are typically held in different accounts.

Key Process Flow

  • Create article master data for empties

  • Create article master data for full articles, and assign empties as components

  • Process full articles in all operational documents, such as purchase order, sales order, inbound and outbound deliveries, goods movements, billing document, and so on

  • Perform POS transaction for sale of full article

  • Get Stock overview including empties

Business Benefits

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by optimizing and accelerating logistics for empties

  • Reduce logistics cost by efficiently handling full articles with empties throughout the entire value chain

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item can only be activated if you have a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and have activated the retail bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.

Enable Manufacturing Subsidiary to Handle Assembly for Headquarter (2WL)

This scope item runs a Make-to-Order scenario (assembly processing) at a subsidiary. A sales order is automatically uploaded to the subsidiary system when a subcontracting purchase order is created in the headquarters system. The receipt of the sales order is electronically confirmed to headquarters. Components are issued manually from the headquarter and received at subsidiary with zero price. The delivery process occurs after the ordered goods are produced by the manufacturing subsidiary. The process includes the electronic sending of an advance shipping notification to the headquarters. Afterwards, the billing process runs at the subsidiary, and an electronic invoice is sent to the headquarters.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales orders from external source, such as headquarters, and send order confirmation

  • Plan production at subsidiary for semi-finished goods ordered by headquarters

  • Execute production of ordered goods

  • Process deliveries including picking, goods issue, and sending advanced shipping notifications

  • Process billing documents including sending electronic invoices to headquarters

  • Align sales data for production at subsidiary with procurement application at headquarters

  • Resolve manual errors, integration failures, and inconsistent data between headquarters and subsidiary

Enablement of SAP Excise Tax Management (4LO)

Overview

The integration scenario described here deals with available APIs from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for integration with the SAP Excise Tax Management. The APIs are in the areas of Master Data (business partners, materials, organizational data), Materials Management (Material Documents), Logistics Execution (Delivery for Excise Movement and Control System (EMCS)), Sales (pricing in Sales Order and Billing), and Financials (posting of excise taxes to Accounting).

Country- and customer-specific details aren't covered and must be implemented on an individual basis to meet both legal and customer requirements.

Key Process Flow

  • Replicate organizational data (storage locations and plants) and master data (material master and business partners)

  • Replicate material documents

  • Replicate financial documents for tax accruals (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Enable SAP Excise Tax Management

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers who want to integrate with the SAP Excise Tax Management service.
processes.name: Enablement of SAP Excise Tax Management

processes.description:
Enablement of SAP Excise Tax Management by Vistex (7Z8)

Overview

SAP Excise Tax Management by Vistex for Public Cloud extends SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition by providing a cloud-native framework for excise tax compliance. The solution runs on the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) and integrates with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for transactional, master, and financial data. Organizations can track excise-relevant goods, calculate accurate tax amounts, and generate legal reports required by authorities. The Stock Ledger Workspace allows users to validate, reprocess, and monitor excise transactions through a modern SAP Fiori user interface. For EU countries, the solution integrates with SAP GTS or third-party service providers to exchange transport information for excise-suspended goods. It also supports compliance with the Excise Movement and Control System (EMCS). The solution supports regulated industries such as alcoholic beverages, tobacco, sugar-based products, and coffee. It offers preconfigured templates to help organizations accelerate compliance readiness.

Key Process Flow

  1. Data Integration from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

    • Integrate master data, enterprise structures, and material movements into Excise Tax Management on SAP BTP

    • Maintain excise-specific attributes within ETM (materials, partners, tax rates)

  2. Stock Ledger Processing

    • Determine excise-relevant transactions based on configurable rules and validations

    • Book transactions into the excise stock ledger in ETM

  3. Tax Calculation & Posting

    • Calculate statistical and actual excise tax values

    • Transfer accrual postings back to SAP S/4HANA Finance

  4. Reporting & Compliance

    • Generate legal reports from the excise stock ledger and provide via SAP Document & Reporting Compliance (DRC)

    • Send transport data for excise-suspended goods to SAP GTS or third-party providers for EMCS compliance (EU region)

  5. Monitoring & Adjustments

    • Reprocess errors and exceptions in the Stock Ledger Workspace

    • Ensure full auditability of excise tax–relevant movements

Business Benefits

  • Deliver cloud-based compliance on SAP BTP for scalability, resilience, and faster innovation cycles

  • Enable end-to-end integration with seamless data exchange from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (master data, logistics, and finance)

  • Adapt rapidly to new excise tax rules and local authority requirements for regulatory agility

  • Automate tax determination, calculation, and postings to reduce manual effort

  • Provide audit-ready visibility of excise transactions through Stock Ledger Workspace for operational transparency

  • Accelerate industry adoption with preconfigured templates that reduce time-to-market for regulated industries

  • Lower compliance, reporting, and risk management costs while reducing manual data handling for cost efficiency

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Excise Tax Management by Vistex is not activated by default in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition because of the following reasons:

  • Cloud Extension Model: The solution is designed as a side-by-side extension on SAP BTP, not as a core capability of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Customers must opt-in and can activate it based on their business need.

  • Industry-Specific Usage: Excise tax applies primarily to industries dealing in regulated goods (alcohol, tobacco, sugar, and so on). Enabling it globally would impose unnecessary complexity on industries where excise is not applicable.

  • Jurisdictional Diversity: Excise regulations vary significantly by country. Default activation could introduce compliance risks in regions where local adaptation is mandatory.

  • Project-Based Reporting: Many excise tax reports (for example, EU EMCS) require country-specific configurations or integration with external systems, which must be implemented as part of a project.
processes.name: Enablement of SAP Excise Tax Management by Vistex

Overview

This scope item updates calculations for work-in-process, overhead, and variance by linking postings to specific events. These events can include goods issues, activity confirmations, goods receipts, or manually set technically complete orders within both make-to-stock and make-to-order scenarios. Additionally, it addresses variance by category when the order status is either fully delivered or technically complete. The supported variance categories are input quantity variance, input price variance, output price variance, resource usage variance, lot size variance, and remaining variance.

Key Process Flow

  • Review event-based overhead costs, work in process and variances

  • Monitor and postprocess event-based overhead, WIP and variance posting errors

  • Automate the work-in-process calculation, overhead calculation, and event-based variance calculation

  • Provide event-based insight for work in process

processes.description:
Event-Based Revenue Recognition – Project-Based Sales – IFRS (4GR)

Overview

In this scenario, you create an enterprise project using the Project with Revenue profile. You then assign this project to sales order items to capture the costs and revenues of sales order processing. The accounting object is the WBS billing element you assign to the sales order items. The actual cost of the project is considered from the sales order item goods issue. You can also assign additional costs to the project, such as time confirmation. Revenue recognition is triggered by each accounting event, enabling real-time margin analysis. If necessary, period-end closing corrects real-time revenue recognition postings. The functionality is provided for dedicated sales order item categories; the supported scenarios are continuously enhanced.

Key Process Flow

Overview

Event-Based Revenue Recognition allows you to manage revenue recognition for service contracts and service orders, using group ledger IFRS functionality. For a service contract, revenue is recognized over time based on the billing plan of the service contract item. For a service order, revenue is recognized based on an event, such as the completion of a service order, and the associated cost is recognized in the same period in which the revenue is recognized. Manual adjustments of revenue and costs are possible. In the Service Actuals app, revenue and costs on service documents are reported in real time and the margin can be easily analyzed.   • Automate recognition activities and reduce manual effort during the period and at period-end closing

  • Avoid the need for additional reconciliation

The integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central enables the transfer of worker data for both internal employees and contingent workers. processes.description:
Extended Intercompany Processes for Sales (1WO)

Overview

This scope item provides the intercompany settings for the Credit Memo, Debit Memo, and Free of Charge Delivery scope items.

Free-of-charge delivery is a sales order from one business unit in a group company created and confirmed based on the availability of goods. A delivery from another affiliate business unit is created and the goods are picked and delivered to the end customer. A customer invoice (net value = 0) is generated. The internal invoice based on delivery from the delivering business unit to the selling business unit is handled as a full charged internal pricing.

For credit memo and debit memo, a credit memo or debit memo is created by the delivering business unit and sent to the selling affiliate business unit. The journal entries are posted automatically.

Key Process Flow

Free-of-Charge Sales Order

  • Create sales order with free-of-charge items

  • Create delivery from the affiliated company

  • Execute picking

  • Post goods issue

  • Create customer invoice

  • Create intercompany invoice

Credit Memo Process

  • Create intercompany credit memo

  • Create journal entries for cross company automatically (accounts receivable and accounts payable)

Debit Memo Process

  • Create intercompany debit memo

  • Create journal entries for cross company automatically (accounts receivable and accounts payable)

Business Benefits

  • Get system-integrated free-of-charge sales order processing for intercompany

  • Allow the intercompany invoice with full charged prices with free-of-charge sales order processing

  • Reduce effort for Credit Memo and Debit Memo between business units in a group company by automation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This is an intercompany relevant scope item and requires additional manual setup steps. If you requested this scope item, you should check the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
