processes.description:
External Occupancy and Contract Management – Group Ledger IFRS (5YV)

Overview

This scope item is only relevant for the Integration with SAP Cloud for Real Estate.

After you group real estate objects (buildings, floors, spaces, land, and land areas) in the Group Real Estate Object for Occupancy SAP Fiori app, you can maintain them in the Manage Occupancy Groups SAP Fiori app.

It enables the functionality to manage lease-out contracts for real estate objects with external customers. It supports the relevant lease-out processes like partner posting, valuation posting, or rent adjustment.

You can use the Contract Management SAP Fiori app to create lease-out contracts. You can easily create contracts and execute periodic postings for existing contracts.

You can change the customer of an existing contract and run reports of your existing contracts as part of your daily business.

You can create reminder rules for every contract, for example, to check the contract conditions, the contract term, or the renewal options, saving time and effort and freeing up capacity for more strategic tasks.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a group of real estate objects for external occupancy

  • Create lease-out contract and assign the external occupancy group to the object assignment

  • Manage the lease valuations for the lease-out contract

  • Execute periodic postings

Business Benefits

  • Use single repository for all real estate assets in the entire portfolio independent of back-end system

  • Collect costs by real estate location, supporting financial reporting and location analysis

  • View vacancy/occupancy reporting for each location based on space type

  • See what fixed assets are used to support each enabled object

processes.description:
External Transportation Planning (6W1)

Overview

With this process, you can plan transportation requests created in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition in a decentralized transportation management system. The freight units that are created in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition can be sent to a decentralized transportation management system for planning. After transportation planning is finalized there, the planning result is received in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition as freight orders. The transportation charges for the freight orders are automatically calculated when the freight orders are transferred to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Subsequently, deliveries can be triggered based on freight orders.

  • Monitor road and rail freight orders

processes.description:
External Workforce Procurement via SAP Fieldglass (22K)

Overview

Integrate SAP Fieldglass with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition through SAP Cloud Integration and SAP Master Data Integration service to support, automate, and extend the processes for hiring external workers and managing statements of work.

This integration benefits you when you digitize the processing of job postings and proofs of employment. After hiring an external resource, a work order is created in SAP Fieldglass. In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, a purchase requisition and a purchase order are automatically created. When the project manager approves the external worker's submitted time, a service entry sheet is created in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Finally, a supplier invoice is generated in SAP Fieldglass based on the purchase order and the service entry sheet. Once the supplier accepts this invoice, it's posted to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for the accounts payable accountant to process.

Key Process Flow

  • Create purchase requisitions in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for each job posting (after creation of work order) and statement of work

  • Approve purchase requisitions in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Optional)

  • Create purchase orders for each work order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Approve purchase orders in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Optional)

  • Submit time in SAP Fieldglass for manager approval

  • Create service entry sheets in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Propose invoices to suppliers based on submitted time in SAP Fieldglass

  • Post invoices in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition after supplier approves invoice proposals

Business Benefits

  • Enable timely and automated payment while reducing the cost and risk of outstanding payments

  • Support accurate, consistent, and compliant booking of time and expenses for external workforce

  • Increase productivity with integrated creation of purchase requisitions, purchase orders, service entry sheets, and supplier invoices

  • Increase data consistency throughout the systems by replicating master data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Fieldglass

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item describes a process in the consumer products industry to manage the first article inspection (FAI) and regular inspection of a raw material. As an example material, a foil is used, which becomes a viewing window bag during production. Before the foil is released to production, the material must meet the specifications negotiated with the supplier. To ensure this, a small sample quantity is ordered with the first purchase order and inspected with a special inspection plan. The Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) in the quality info record controls this, where the purchase order item is maintained.

At goods receipt, the inspection lot is created with the special first article inspection plan for first check. This plan contains a general goods receipt inspection by the quality team as well as an additional inspection by a special team responsible for the print layout inspection. After results recording and the usage decision, you can monitor the result of the first article inspection in the quality info record.

If the FAI is accepted, the print layout is shared with the supplier. A new purchase order with normal quantity can be created. The process continues with the goods receipt and the regular goods receipt inspection. If the FAI is rejected, the same process can be repeated with a new purchase order item and a new quality info record maintenance.

This type of first article inspection requires an inspection plan structure with several operations. However, the structure of this inspection plan can be simpler in your company, as you may not need different operations and work centers, though you may need different inspection plans with the corresponding inspection plan usage.

Key Process Flow

  • Perform first article inspection (FAI) – integrate QM in production part approval process (PPAP)

  • Approve FAI (case 1): conduct regular quality inspection for second purchase order

  • Reject FAI (case 2): initiate new FAI inspection for second purchase order

Business Benefits

  • Check specifications of a product before it gets included in the production process
  • Ensure that the production process of a purchased material meets your requirements

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

Using the financial transactions provided for this process you can mitigate the FX risks.

The functionality helps you to automate labor-intensive processes, such as confirmation of financial transactions and accounting postings, giving you more time to focus on value-added activities. The process starts with the creation of a customer standard sales order using a material for which a free goods condition record is maintained. Depending on the ordered quantities, customers receive free goods.

After the completion of picking, the shipping specialist relieves the inventory. This inventory relief is the actual recording of the physical quantity that is being shipped to the customer.

With the goods issue posting revenue is recognized and cost of goods sold is recorded in Financial Accounting.

Once goods are delivered, you can invoice the delivery.

For details on bundling functionalities for IFRS 15, see note 2524569.

Key Process Flow

  • Create delivery

  • Execute picking

processes.description:
Freight Settlement (6W4)

Overview

Freight costs calculated for the freight documents (freight orders and freight bookings) are to be posted in financial accounting to record such costs in accounting as accruals and to pay the carriers or freight forwarders. Once the freight documents are in a status in which the transportation has been initiated or completed, the freight costs can be posted to financial accounting. If there are errors during the posting of accruals, the freight documents can be monitored for such posting errors. The invoice received from the carrier or freight forwarder is verified against the expected costs calculated in the freight document. Depending on the number of invoicing parties involved for a freight document, multiple invoices can be received from different carriers executing the transport. For example, for an ocean freight booking, you can receive invoices from different invoicing carriers to execute different stages of the ocean booking (for example, one for the pick-up, one for the main carriage, and another one for the delivery). During invoice verification, price variances and unplanned freight costs can be captured. Freight cost allocation capabilities are used to manage freight costs that occurred during the transportation processes. The costs are posted to a material valuation in an inbound process, and to an expense account (general ledger) in an outbound process.

Key Process Flow

  • Confirm freight cost for accrual postings

  • Monitor freight cost allocation documents

  • Perform carrier settlement for freight orders and freight bookings

  • Post invoice with variance

Business Benefits

  • Support the accrual of freight costs in financial accounting and the preparation for invoice processing of freight documents

  • Allocate freight costs at freight document level and delivery item in a freight document. The system posts the costs to material valuation in an inbound process and to expense account (general ledger) in an outbound process

This scope item is only relevant for customers who want to do freight settlement in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Government Budget Management (6YU)

Overview

Budgetary accounting is an accounting method for recording financial resources that are limited by a governing agency, authority, or by law. It places emphasis on accountability and control of budgetary resources instead of on profitability. The budget is a legal compliance standard against which the operations for funds are evaluated.

This process showcases the budgeted master data objects and the relationship to general ledger accounts and controlling objects. The approved budget is uploaded using the defined master data. Budget transfers are executed throughout the year as business is transacted and budget is consumed. In this fully integrated solution, all budget-relevant financial and commitment postings automatically check for available budget and communicate the status (success, warning, or error) according to the tolerance settings. Users are assured both an exact control of financial resources and accuracy in managerial and statutory reporting.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage funds

  • Manage budget periods

  • Manage functional areas

  • Upload budget data

  • Perform budget transfers

  • Execute budgetary reports

Business Benefits

  • Record all budgetary, financial and encumbrance transactions for public sector entities in a single cloud environment

  • Close alignment with planning and budget formulation tools

  • Check budget availability immediately to ensure regulatory compliance

  • Get real-time reporting to help make time-sensitive managerial decisions

  • Reduce manual processes

  • Simplify production of statutory financial reports

processes.description:
Group Reporting – Financial Consolidation (1SG)

Overview

This scope item provides statutory financial consolidation capabilities for SAP S/4HANA customers.

The key features included in this release include data integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, avoids replication (using the main actual table as a data source), flexible upload capability to collect financial data from non-SAP S/4HANA subsidiaries, product validations to ensure data integrity, consolidation methods to produce statutory consolidation, and key audit reports and consolidated financial statements including Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet reports.

This scope item also provides two optional scenarios. You can choose whether to perform them or not according to your own needs:

  • Hierarchy Elimination

    Hierarchy Elimination covers consolidation for management-oriented organizational units such as profit center and business segment. This functionality addresses the needs of business unit managers and group controllers who need to respond rapidly to changes resulting from internal organization unit restructuring and who need to focus on specific internal performance figures and not the entire group financial statement.

    Hierarchy Elimination introduces new reporting dimensions that are derived at report run-time and not persisted in the universal journal. These virtual organizational units allow the reporting user to show inter-unit eliminations at the correct hierarchy level.

  • Consolidation with Multiple Group Currencies and Restatement Versions

    We provide the following major scenarios of version concept: group currency extension versions, restatements, and simulations.

    Group currency extension versions allow you to consolidate in different group currencies.

    Restatement versions can be used when new accounting standards are adopted or management organizations are changed. By restating the prior periods, you can compare financial data between prior and current periods.

    Simulation versions are used when you need to consolidate the current period using different settings (for example, group structure, cons methods).

    Note

    The version configuration in this document is only for testing purposes only. In your projects, design your version stack based on your own version settings and requirements.

Key Process Flow

  • Prepare data (Financial statement item preparation, update for group transactions types)

  • Load data from SAP S/4HANA and outside sources

  • Validate data with sets of built-in controls

  • Consolidate data

  • Perform reporting and auditing

Business Benefits

  • Integrate fully with SAP S/4HANA

  • Provide flexible upload for non-SAP S/4HANA companies

  • Validate product to ensure data integrity (built-in)

  • Produce statutory financial consolidation with powerful calculation engine

  • View reporting using the SAP Fiori launchpad

processes.description:
Guided Buying Capability with SAP Ariba Buying (2NV)

Overview

The guided buying capability creates a simple, smart, and elegant purchasing experience that increases user engagement across all spend areas. Guided buying serves as a central place where all buyers can shop across all goods and services. It enables procurement and individual line-of-business owners to specify procurement policies and inform and guide users whenever there appear to be policy conflicts. These capabilities enable purchasers to collaborate directly with suppliers and other procurement users in the context of the procurement need, making procurement more efficient.

Users find items across catalogs, including partial items, forms, and suppliers in a single search box. All spend contracted through supplier-provided catalogs and punch-out catalogs is available for the user to search. Using online shopping as an example, users can filter items by price or manufacturer.

Key Process Flow

  • Access a customized guided buying app to search for items across catalogs, including partial items, forms, and suppliers, using a single search box

  • Receive policy guidance as items are added to the requisition

  • Perform budget checks in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition before submitting the requisition

  • Approve decisions based on the configured workflow

  • Replicate approved requisition into SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition as purchase requisitions

  • Automatically create purchase orders from those requisitions

  • Receive and account for items in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition using the Goods Receipt app

  • Receive and post supplier invoice in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Update the SAP Ariba requisitions with follow-on document record IDs for traceability

Business Benefits

  • Enhance employee performance with simple guided user experience

  • Automatically apply procurement policies through the guided process, enforcing compliance during the purchasing process, not afterward

  • Use flexible configuration to allow line-of-business-specific definition of forms, permissions, and system behavior at field level and for workflows, ensuring each persona in the process enters only their respective data, avoiding clerical errors and streamlining purchasing for each line of business

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The scope item can be activated provided that you have the additional license for SAP Ariba Buying.

Overview

Guided buying in SAP Ariba Buying creates a simple, smart, and elegant purchasing experience that increases user engagement across all spend areas. It serves as a central place where all buyers can shop across all goods and services. It enables procurement and individual line-of-business (LoB) owners to specify procurement policies and inform and guide users whenever there appear to be policy conflicts. Central Procurement offers a centralized requisitioning process across industries with a deep integration into the customer's landscape. It connects guided buying in SAP Ariba Buying capability to the customer’s ERP or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition systems, and exchanges business documents to ensure end-to-end business processes into finance and logistics that run in the connected systems. The integration allows the transfer and updates of the requisition between the two as well as necessary master data.

Key Process Flow

  • Access customized guided buying app and search for items across catalogs, including partial items, forms, and suppliers in a single search box

  • Get policy guidance as items are added to the requisition

  • Enable tactical sourcing by the employee easily

  • Validate and submit requisition for simulation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Simulate requisition creation in the connected satellite back end

  • Create purchase requisition and send a request for a guided buying requisition

  • Perform budget checks and other validations in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition before submitting the requisition

  • Approve decisions as per the configured workflow

  • Replicate approved requisition into SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition as purchase requisitions

  • Replicate the purchase requisition in the connected satellite system and receive confirmation that the replication was successful

  • Create purchase orders, goods receipts, and supplier invoices in a connected satellite system with updates of the references in the guided buying requisition history

Business Benefits

  • Run guided buying for the whole organization using SAP Ariba to leverage the central requisitioning processes

  • Increase employee performance with simple guided user experience

  • Apply procurement policies automatically through the guided process

  • Reduce TCO significantly for procurement departments through centralized process

  • Use flexible configuration to allow LoB-specific definition of forms, permissions, and system behavior at field level and for workflows, so each persona in the process only enters their respective data, avoiding clerical errors and streamlining purchasing

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The scope item can be activated provided that you have the additional license for SAP Ariba Buying. It is dependent on other priced scope items (such as Central Purchasing (2XT)).

Handling Unit Management (4MM)

Overview

A handling unit is a physical unit consisting of packaging materials (load carriers or packing material) and the goods contained on or in it. A handling unit is always a combination of products and packaging materials. All the information contained in the product items (for example, about batches) is retained in the handling units and is always available.

This scope item sets up packaging of materials in outbound, inbound, inventory, and production, including batches and serial numbers. Because it only includes the steps for packaging, it requires a standard process scope item to work with.

This scope item does not have its own master data and only describes the steps for packing (it is not self-contained with a complete E2E process). It can be used for goods movements with handling units in inbound, production, outbound and inventory.

Key Process Flow

  • Execute packing automatically in Outbound Delivery

  • Manage handling units in inventory

  • Execute packing manually in Inbound Delivery

  • Execute packing automatically in Inbound Delivery

  • Plan and create handling units in discrete and process manufacturing

  • Confirm handling units in production (discrete and process)

  • Execute Intracompany

  • Execute Intercompany Stock Transfer

  • Execute Intercompany Stock Transfer Return

  • Execute Customer Consignment

Business Benefits

  • Use a unique identifier across all locations (such as GTL, SSCC, or other number formats)

  • Print labels

  • Reflect packing-based logistic structures across logistic unit levels – such as production and distribution, across plants, or across a plant and customer (Outbound)

  • Track movements of packed goods in logistics easily

Hedge Accounting for FX Forward – Group Ledger IFRS (1XD)

Overview

The Hedge Management and Hedge Accounting process helps you to mitigate profit and loss volatility from the use of derivatives.

Currently, the scope item supports IFRS 9 and covers Cash Flow Hedge using FX Forwards (including NDF) as Hedging Instruments.

The functionality helps you to automate labor-intensive processes, such as calculating net open exposure amount, creating hedging relationship for hedge item and hedge instrument, determining the key figures calculation (NPV, Forward, CCBS, CVA/DVA), performing the valuation of FX transaction, checking classification, dealing with the dedesignation, and generating posting journal reports.

Key Process Flow

  • Define hedging area based on hedging policy

  • Enrich, upload and release forecast and planning data

  • Determine net open exposure and make hedging decision

  • Execute FX transactions

  • Prepare and release designation

  • Determine NPV, execute valuation and classification at period end

  • Perform de-designation and reclassification at contract close

  • Perform postings

Business Benefits

  • Provide an overview of net open exposure amount

  • Support the management of hedge accounting

  • Reduce manual operation, such as hedge relationship mapping, designation, and classification

  • Make better operational and strategic decisions using the comprehensive reporting and analysis tools

IFRS 18 Compliance in Treasury and Risk Management (83D)

Overview

Starting on January 1st, 2027, IFRS 18 becomes effective. Under IFRS 18, profit and loss postings, including those from Treasury and Risk Management (TRM), should be classified into Operating, Investing, or Financing to meet the new subtotals and categorization requirements. For more information on implementing IFRS 18 Financial Reporting in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, with particular attention to the Treasury and Risk Management (TRM), see SAP Note 3694359 .

This scope item is designed to accelerate your journey to IFRS 18 compliance for managing treasury and risk management transactions. This scope item is available only if you use SAP Central Business Configuration.

By activating this scope item, you can leverage the reference configurations for IFRS 18 compliance based on the functional area approach, including:

  • New Account Assignment References (AARs) that carry IFRS 18 categorization

  • Account determination entries that map existing account symbols to existing G/L accounts via those new AARs

Before you activate this scope item, we highly recommend that you conduct a careful evaluation of your TRM customization extent and project timeline. You can leverage this scope item when one of the following conditions applies:

  • Existing TRM Environment: TRM is already in productive use and predominantly based on SAP TRM reference content. For example, account assignment references (AAR), G/L accounts, and account determinations are consistent with or closely aligned with the reference content.

  • New or In-Progress Implementation: The TRM implementation (including non-IFRS 18 settings) hasn't started yet, or is in progress but isn't live at the time of the scope item release, and with a clear intention to predominantly use SAP reference content.

Key Process Flow

  • Check position indicator

  • Check posting journal

Business Benefits

  • Provides ready-to-use reference configurations to speed up your transition to IFRS 18 for Treasury and Risk Management (TRM) transactions

  • Delivers new Account Assignment References (AARs) with IFRS 18 categories (Operating, Investing, Financing) out of the box, reducing manual configuration work

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

You can request this scope item only if you configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as the configuration environment.

processes.description:
Overview

In-house banking offers bank accounts for all subsidiaries in different account currencies. Subsidiaries send their payment files using standard payment processes offered within financial accounting. In-house banking sends electronic bank statements back to clear the open items accordingly.

In-house banking supports payments between subsidiaries (intercompany and cross-bank area intercompany payments), payments towards external business partners (payments on behalf), and central incoming payments (for example, resulting from external zero balancing postings).

In-house banking offers the calculation of interests and fees on internal bank accounts. With help of limits that can be assigned to the internal bank accounts, the cash situation can be monitored easily.

The financial accounting of the in-house banking owner is automatically updated via the general ledger transfer. By leveraging Finance Business Integration Interface (FIBTI) and Account Business Transaction Interface (ABTI) the subledger applications Advanced Payment Management and In-house banking are fully decoupled from Financial Accounting.

In-house banking is fully embedded into SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, advanced payment management and benefits from the scope of features involved.

Key Process Flow

  • Create internal bank accounts individually, via mass creation, or via the eBAM integration for in-house banking account opening process through electronic messaging
  • Assign interest conditions to internal bank accounts
  • Assign interest conditions backdated either within the current settlement period or within an already settled period
  • Assign withholding tax calculation if needed
  • Assign maintenance fees and transaction fees to internal bank accounts
  • Assign maintenance fees and transaction fees backdated either within the current settlement period or within an already settled period
  • Assign limits and backdated limits
  • Conduct account settlement simulation to either forecast interest and fees for the current period or to analyze past periods
  • Conduct payments between subsidiaries within one in-house bank area (intercompany payments) or between more than one in-house bank area (cross-bank area intercompany payments)
  • Conduct payments towards external business partners (payments on behalf) including payment returns and payment rejects.
  • Conduct central incoming payments (for example resulting from external zero balancing postings)
  • Conduct internal cash pooling
  • Conduct interest compensation
  • Create correction postings for interests, withholding tax, maintenance fees and transactions fees, initial balance and correction for central incoming payment including back dated value date
  • Get an overview of payments, end-of-day processes, overdraft accounts, and the current bank balance for the respective bank area with help of the In-House Banking Dashboard.
  • Close an internal bank account and transfer the positive account balance either to another in-house bank account within the same bank area or to an external house bank account
  • Perform end-of-day processes including interest and fee calculation, withholding tax calculation, creation of internal bank statements, balance notifications and interest scale notifications updating the financial accounting system of the in-house bank owner with help of the general ledger transfer
  • Perform an automatic resettlement process to recalculate the account settlement of already settled periods related to backdated postings

Business Benefits

  • Settle intercompany account payables and receivables in a cashless manner

  • Monitor payments centrally

  • Track the cash situation on internal bank accounts, including internal limit considerations

  • Maintain accounts using mass creation tools

  • Maintain accounts using eBAM integration

  • Provide bank statements for in-house banking accounts within the day

  • Transfer all postings on in-house banking accounts to the general ledger once a day or within the day

  • Integrate in-house banking fully into standard financial accounting processes for payments and electronic bank statements

Exclude from Default Activation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

The following scope items are a prerequisite for using this scope item and must be activated: Advanced Payment Management (4MT), Advanced Bank Account Management (J77), and Advanced Cash Operations (J78)

SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity (16R) is not mandatory, but strongly recommended.
processes.name: In-House Banking

processes.description:
In-House Repair (3XK)

Overview

The scope item covers the in-house repair process in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

The in-house repair supports selecting the repair objects, performing prechecks, run a diagnosis and aiding in decision making to provide a repair quotation or repair order. Warranty and service contracts are considered. When the customer agrees to the repair, repair orders are created automatically.

The repair order is then planned and released for execution. Credit checks and ATP/reservation for spare parts safeguard the repair. A purchase requisition is created automatically for the applicable spare parts or external service items.

In repair execution, repair confirmations are posted against the repair order. The time-sheet entry, spares cost, and expenses are posted to finance and controlling.

Once the repair is done, the recorded effort is released for billing, automatically creating a billing document request to invoice the customer.

For logistics, in-house repair integrates with customer returns.

Key Process Flow

  • Receive repair objects using customer returns

  • Create in-house repair

  • Add or remove repair objects

  • Check service contracts and warranty

  • Perform prechecks and decide repair (including mass decisions)

  • Run a diagnosis by a service technician to prepare the quotation and charge diagnosis efforts to the customer

  • Create and share a repair quotation with one or multiple repair objects in a quotation (time-and material or fixed-price)

  • Accept or reject repair quotation

  • Create repair order per repair object (time-and-material or fixed-price)

  • Add or change repair order items

  • Plan repair

  • Check creditability

  • Run ATP and initiate reservations for spare parts

  • Create purchase requisitions for the non-stock spare parts and external service items in the repair order

  • Review the assigned repair orders

  • Create repair confirmations

  • Create a billing document from the billing document request for invoicing the customer

  • Post revenues automatically against the repair order

  • Trigger outbound delivery to send back the repair object to the customer

Business Benefits

  • Provide functionality to select, plan, and execute the in-house repair of serialized devices

  • Provide cost estimates in the form of repair quotations to the customer

  • Determine service contracts for repair orders and repair quotations

  • Link procurement process with repair order execution

  • Post timesheet, cost of spares, cost of external services and expenses automatically

  • Invoice the customer based on repair confirmations or repair order

  • Provide APIs that support triggering the in-house repair from an external system such as a call center solution

  • Integrates with accelerated customer returns

processes.description:
In-Store Customer Order Management (3HU)

Overview

In the typical in-store process, the customer gathers the products from the shelf, and pays at the cash-register. For specific purposes, it can be required that a sales order is created for the customer. For example, in case the product isn't available in the store and must be ordered for the customer. Another reason can be the need to document the sale, for example for warranty purposes, or to gather the serial number of a high-value article.

The process starts with capturing information about customer, like name, address, phone number, followed by entering product-related information, which is then stored in the sales order. Then, there are two main process variants, depending on whether the goods are available in the store, see below. In both scenarios, the process ends with the customer paying at the cash-register with reference to the billing document (which is created as a follow-on document to the sales order).

Key Process Flow

Immediate pick up in the store:

  • Customer picks the products from the sales floor

  • Maintain customer, create sales order, and generate follow-on documents

  • Customer pays at cash-register with reference to billing document

Pick up later:

  • Maintain customer and create sales order

  • Procure products from distribution center via stock transport order, or from external supplier via purchase order

  • Receive products in-store

  • Pick and move the products to hand-over area

  • Hand over products to customer

  • Accept payment from customer at cash register with reference to billing document

Business Benefits

  • Reduce revenue loss due to fulfillment issue by supporting customer in-store pick up processes

  • Reduce order-to-cash cost by supporting the capture and fulfillment of customer orders in the store

  • Increase customer satisfaction by providing outstanding customer service

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

processes.description:
In-Store Inventory Management (3HR)

Overview

In-Store Inventory Management aims to ensure an accurate and rebalanced stock, providing, for example, a sound basis for replenishment.

It enables store associates to:

  • Transfer articles from one store to another or to a distribution center using handling units that enable efficient logistics processes within the store.

  • Create a physical inventory document and make it visible to the count stock application

  • Perform a physical inventory count of all articles in the store, or a cycle count of selected articles

  • Use the Manage Stock Counting app as a store manager to review counts submitted by store associates

  • Perform an ad-hoc physical inventory count for selected articles at a given point of time by the retail associate

  • Adjust the stock quantity for different reasons such as shrinkage, damage, or spoilage, and subtract the article quantity from the current on-hand stock

Key Process Flow

  • Transfer Products app: Send articles to other stores or to distribution centers

  • Physical inventory document: Created in the headquarters and made visible in the count stock application.

  • Count Stock app: Perform and review a physical inventory count of all articles in the store, or a cycle count of selected articles

  • Count Stock Ad-hoc app: Perform and post an ad-hoc physical inventory count of the selected articles in a store

  • Adjust Mass Stock app: Perform stock adjustments for a specified reason (such as shrinkage, transfer to other or own departments, and so on)

Business Benefits

  • Reduce sales cost by giving store employees real-time access to critical information during sales and service discussions with customers

  • Reduce store operating cost by letting store employees access article and inventory data from anywhere in stores and any time thus improving productivity and accuracy

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by efficiently managing inventory and stock movements to reduce obsolescence and shrinkage costs

  • Improve supply chain FTE productivity by increasing automation and improving access to real-time information

In-Store Merchandise Management (3HQ)

Overview

For a retail associate, having all necessary article information at their fingertips using an app is essential for both customer-facing activities and efficient store operations. The Look Up Retail Product app combines crucial data from a variety of sources. This includes article descriptions, units of measurement, sales pricing, available-to-promise stock information, procurement lead times, real-time stock information considering unprocessed POS sales, procurement lead times, and upcoming planned goods receipts. You can identify the article through bar-code scanning of the Global Trade Identification Number (GTIN), using the search function, or through cross-navigation from another application.

The Print Labels app enables retail associates to search or scan the required product and print the product labels. Additionally, you can print labels for lists of articles. Correct labels support on-shelf availability and proper labeling of prices, which is a key requirement for brick-and-mortar stores.

Key Process Flow

    • Check on-hand stock

    • Check availability of different variants of an article

  • In Print Labels app:

    • Print single standard labels on a mobile printer

    • Print standard labels in bulk

    • Print promotion labels on mobile printer

  • Reduce store operating cost by letting store employees access article and inventory data from anywhere in stores and any time thus improving productivity and accuracy

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by efficiently managing inventory and stock movements to reduce obsolescence and shrinkage costs

In-Store Purchase Order Management (5FY)

Overview

Having the optimal quantity of merchandise on the sales floor is of major importance. Out-of-stock situations reduce customer satisfaction and decrease revenue, but overstock increases capital binding.

Order Products app: Typically, stores are replenished centrally. Store personnel can be involved in the process by reviewing and adjusting the order proposal. In addition, ad hoc manual ordering is available, allowing mitigation of exceptions. Decision support for both scenarios through information such sales history, current stock, and open order quantity is provided to help store personnel to decide on the right order quantity. Articles are ordered from the distribution center or from an external supplier. The purchase requisition is generated once the order proposal from the app is submitted.

Receive Products app: Once the articles arrive at the store, a store associate triggers receiving to update the inventory (from an inventory and finance perspective). The associate can do trusted receiving (no item level scanning, posting everything at once) or detailed receiving (item level scanning is required). If necessary, labels can be printed ad hoc.

Key Process Flow

  • Generate purchase requisitions based on required quantities at the store

  • Review order proposal quantities and revise if necessary

  • Create order proposals (purchase requisitions) manually

  • Generate purchase orders (for external suppliers) or stock transfer orders (for distribution centers) out of the purchase requisitions

  • Create outbound deliveries for stock transfer orders at distribution center

  • Pick articles and post goods issue at distribution center

  • Post goods receipt at store

  • Print labels ad-hoc at store (optional)

  • Look up products at store (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Reduce out-of-stock situations by allowing store employees to review and adjust centrally generated order proposals

  • Increase order management FTE productivity by reducing the time and effort associated with manual corrections and work exception-driven

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by efficiently managing store order and replenishment processes

  • Improve supply chain FTE productivity by increasing automation and improving access to real-time information

processes.description:
Inbound Logistics for Distribution Centers (5FU)

Overview

The purchase order is the basis for all goods receipt processing. The purchase order is communicated to the external supplier. As the goods are shipped, the supplier can optionally send the corresponding shipping documents to the recipient. These Advance Shipping Notices (ASN) can be posted up front in the system as an inbound delivery before the actual arrival of the merchandise in the distribution center (DC). Compared to the purchase order and an optional order confirmation, the ASN gives more accurate information about the expected quantities and dates, thus enhancing supply chain transparency.

Part of the goods receipt articles and their quantities can be prefilled by data from the purchase order or inbound delivery. After counting, the quantities can be adjusted if needed. As a result of posting the good receipt, the inventory is adjusted accordingly and the respective financial accounts are posted.

If differences are discovered later, you can make the necessary corrections, partially cancelling the goods receipt.

A variant of goods receipt handling is the receiving of merchandise returned from a store to the DC.

Key Process Flow

  • Create inbound delivery with reference to purchase order

  • Print inbound delivery as counting list (optional)

  • Post goods receipt with or without reference to the inbound delivery

Business Benefits

  • Reduce total logistics cost by improving the efficiency of the logistics execution function using well-integrated picking, packing, and shipping processes

  • Reduce order fulfillment lead time by using real-time information on timely completion of picking, packing, and shipping activities

  • Reduce transportation spend by making informed decisions based on accurate demand and supply data

processes.description:
Inbound Storage Tank Management – Process Manufacturing (3UK)

Overview

This scope item enables the storage tank management process, which supports the procurement of a new batch into the day tank and then mixing of this new batch with an existing batch in the main tank with a special mixing process order type. Quality inspection, results recording, and usage decision are performed both on the externally procured batch and the batch after mixing.

The characteristics of storage tank management are:

  • Separate storage locations are created for day tank and main tank.

  • An existing batch is already available on the main tank.

  • Only one batch can normally be managed on these storage tanks.

  • Batch determination is at order level.

Key Process Flow

  • Initialize stock of Batch #1

  • Create purchase order to procure Batch #2

  • Receive goods from Batch #2 into day tank from vendor

  • Get a stock overview of batches

  • Monitor inspection lots

  • Record inspection results

  • Record usage decisions

  • Display batch characteristic values of Batch #2

  • Create process order for mixing

  • Create process order confirmation

  • Record results

Business Benefits

  • Get a controlled process for mixing two batches of a material

  • Get availability of a dedicated process order type to manage inbound storage tank mixing process
processes.name: Inbound Storage Tank Management – Process Manufacturing

processes.description:
Information Lifecycle Management (1KA)

Overview

Personal data in SAP applications must be protected according to the data protection laws. This is achieved by blocking and deleting data according to residence and retention rules. Residence rules are set to define the time for which data can stay in the database, after which it is archived. Retention rules are defined to store the archive files for a set amount of time, after which they can be destroyed.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain retention rules

  • Analyze archiving variant distribution

  • Schedule and monitor archiving jobs

  • Data Controller Rule Framework

Business Benefits

  • Block data once the primary purpose of the data is complete

  • Move data from the database to archive files using rules

  • Define rules based on several factors (for example, residence time, authorization group, retention time)
processes.name: Information Lifecycle Management

processes.description:
Integrated Financial Planning (4RC)

Overview

This process supports detailed financial planning to set operational targets and to provide a baseline for the valuation of operational processes. It includes:

  • Cost and activity planning to determine cost flows and activity rates

  • Sales and profitability planning to determine volume and price targets, expected discounts, and cost of goods sold

  • Product cost simulation to determine raw material prices and activity usage

  • Project planning to provide a baseline for revenue recognition and for capital expense projects

  • Financial statement planning, including profit and loss, balance sheet, and cash flow

Key Process Flow

  • Access reference data relevant for planning

  • Capture planning assumptions from key stakeholders

  • Aggregate plan as basis for financial statement

Business Benefits

  • Calculate activity rates for production and service activities including all relevant cost inputs and activity flows

  • Calculate product rates for manufactured products, leveraging detailed information from cost estimates

  • Calculate sales profitability including detailed quantities, prices discounts, and cost of goods sold

  • Calculate capital expenses

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item describes business content delivered with SAP Analytics Cloud for Planning that can be used in combination with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Overview

This scope item enables the integration of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with external output management solutions, helping business applications meet advanced output needs. You can enable this functionality at the application level to support the diverse requirements of different applications. By default, the output solution offered by SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is used.

  • Trigger the output as a business user

  • Collect and queue output data for internal and system tasks

  • Factor in the customers' advanced needs (depending on the capabilities of the external solution), such as high volume output, special form layout requirements, and additional channels

  • Support customers who already have an external output management solution as part of their landscape and want to continue using it with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Integration of Payment Advice with Buyers and Suppliers (2MB)

Overview

For organizations whose suppliers or buyers use traditional data exchange protocols like electronic data interchange (EDI), this scope item provides robust application programming interfaces (APIs) to simplify and automate exchanging procurement documents.

The following documents are supported via the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) messaging protocol:

- Payment Advice Notification (Trigger Outbound message)

- Payment Advice Notification (Receive Inbound message)

- Payment Advice Cancellation Notification (Trigger Outbound message)

- Payment Advice Cancellation Notification (Receive Inbound message)

You can benefit from intercompany integration by enabling this scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Trigger payment advice message

  • Trigger payment advice cancellation message

  • Receive payment advice notification

  • Receive payment advice cancellation message

  • Support customer returns process

Business Benefits

  • Experience a higher degree of automation in exchanging financial documents as the Payment Advice Notification with suppliers

  • Save time by reducing manual communication efforts with suppliers

  • Increase productivity, performance, and job satisfaction among procurement professionals and accounts payable accountants

  • Save costs associated with paper, postage, mailing, and records management

  • Enable greater scalability through process efficiency gains

processes.description:
Integration of Procurement with External Suppliers (2EJ)

Overview

For purchasing organizations whose suppliers use traditional data exchange protocols like electronic data interchange (EDI), or in Two-Tier scenarios, where subsidiaries are on SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, this scope item provides a set of robust application programming interfaces (APIs) to simplify and automate exchanging procurement documents and their follow-on messages.

The following documents and functions are supported:

Procurement Process:

  • Create, change, or cancel purchase order (outbound message)

  • Receive purchase order confirmation (inbound message)

  • Receive Advance Shipping Notification (ASN, inbound delivery message)

  • Receive supplier invoice (inbound message)

Return Process:

  • Create return purchase order (outbound message)

  • Receive return purchase order confirmation (inbound message)

  • Receive supplier invoice: Credit Memo (inbound message)

The Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) messaging protocol is supported.

You can enable B2B integration with the corresponding Integration of Sales with External Buyers (2EL) scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Create, change, or cancel purchase order

  • Send purchase order to supplier

  • Receive purchase order confirmation from supplier (optional)

  • Receive advance shipping notification from supplier and process inbound delivery (optional)

  • Receive invoice or credit memo from supplier

  • Perform customer return process

Business Benefits

  • Experience a higher degree of automation in exchanging procurement documents with suppliers

  • Reduce time and manual efforts required to correspond with suppliers

  • Increase the productivity, performance, and job satisfaction of procurement professionals and accounts payable accountants

  • Save costs associated with paper, postage, mailing, records management

  • Enable greater scalability through process efficiency gains

Integration of Sales with External Buyers (2EL)

Overview

For sales organizations whose buyers use traditional data exchange protocols such as electronic data interchange (EDI), or in Two-Tier scenarios, where subsidiaries are on SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, this scope item provides a set of robust application programming interfaces (APIs) to simplify and automate exchanging sales documents and their follow-on messages.

processes.description:
Integration to Icertis for Contract Assembly (6V2)

Overview

With Enterprise Contract Management, you can integrate SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system with external contract assembly product Icertis Contract Intelligence. This integration enables users to create and manage legal content that is generated out of various business scenarios in a company, such as procurement processes, sales, policies, or intercompany agreements. The users can further collaborate on the document until it's agreed on by all the internal and external stakeholders and ready for execution through signature.

Key Process Flow

  • Assemble contract from template

    • Create a transaction to act as a source of important and critical attributes for document creation.

    • This document is further assembled using a template that consists of all the attributes of a contract.

    • Once the contract is assembled, it is signed and approved.

  • Edit external contracts

  • View external contract statuses to know the progress of the contract assembly

  • Update attributes and reassemble external contracts

  • Discard content from a document without deleting the document itself

Business Benefits

  • Perform process automation with rule-based authoring and assembly of clauses and documents

  • Optimize contract performance ​ with collaboration with both internal and external stakeholders for contracts

  • Ensure legal compliance​ with full traceability of signatures and responsibilities

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

  • The customer must purchase a separate license with Icertis along with the adapter.

  • Before you start to use any apps in the SAP Fiori launchpad of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, you must set up the following communication scenarios: SAP_COM_0869 and SAP_COM_0890.
processes.name: Integration to Icertis for Contract Assembly

processes.description:
Integration to SAP Enterprise Contract Assembly (2OQ)

Overview

The SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, enterprise contract management solution enables digitization of legal transactions within an organization. This application facilitates creation and management of legal content in enterprises in alignment with core business processes and provides an integrated platform to run enterprise-wide legal process more efficiently.

SAP Enterprise Contract Assembly is an SAP BTP application that enables the authoring and assembly of the following legal content:

  • Templates and text blocks as elements to reuse content

  • Virtual documents as a result of the assembly of a template based on and specific business context

The integration of SAP Enterprise Contract Assembly with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, enterprise contract management enables enterprises to integrate with all core business processes, assemble all types of documents based on templates, text blocks, rules, and simultaneously store all documents in a central online repository.

Key Process Flow

  • Author or edit legal templates and documents

  • Assemble legal templates and documents

  • Generate legal documents

  • Manage legal documents

Business Benefits

  • Increase transparency on lifecycle of legal content creation and assembly

  • Experience efficient and faster provisioning of legal content

  • Get faster reaction times, lower risks, and improve compliance

As of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2602 release, this scope item is deprecated.

This scope item delivers integration content between SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management (1XV) and SAP Enterprise Contract Assembly (SAP BTP-based solution). Scope item 1XV, which is priced separately, is a prerequisite scope item to consume 2OQ for customers.

Integration with Data Quality Management (2UZ)

Overview

Data Quality Management (DQM) supports address cleansing with a long history as an SAP Suite add-on, and is also used in the SAP S/4HANA on-premise stack. For SAP Cloud deployments, we effectively act as a third-party product to support address cleansing via OData access to the DQM microservice hosted on the SAP BTP, ABAP environment. Our DQM cloud deployment supports an integration is with the SAP Master Data Governance Consolidation use case in the SAP BTP, ABAP Environment.

Key Process Flow

2UZ is a technical scope item and has no key process flows.

Business Benefits

  • Enable the master data governance consolidation use case access to the DQM microservice

  • Validate, standardize, and correct addresses

  • Improve the quality of address detail

  • Improve the quality of customer and vendor records in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item delivers a communication scenario that is leveraged by the Master Data Governance (MDG) team to access the DQM microservice for address validation. Note that this scope item is consumed by other scope items (such as Master Data Consolidation for Business Partner (1N3) for the MDG Consolidation use case) that may require additional licenses.
processes.name: Integration with Data Quality Management

processes.description:
Integration with SAP Document AI (7TC)

Overview

This scope item integrates SAP Document AI with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, enabling automated document inbound processing for various application scenarios. SAP Document AI supports multiple document ingestion channels, allowing documents to be uploaded manually, via API or email ingestion.

By leveraging preconfigured schemas and AI models, SAP Document AI automatically extracts structured data from uploaded documents. This extracted data is then utilized within application scenarios to create or update business records.

Additionally, by reviewing and correcting extraction results, the AI extraction logic can be fine-tuned to better accommodate client-specific documents.

Key Process Flow

This scope item sets up the integration with SAP Document AI. The following key process flow is exemplary, it may vary based on the application scenarios.

  • Upload document to SAP Document AI

  • Execute OCR (system task)

  • Automatically extract structured data, in the form of key-value pairs, from document (system task)

  • Validate and correct extracted data (optional)

  • Check and correct application data

  • Confirm application data

Business Benefits

  • Automate document processing to streamline inbound document handling and reduce manual effort

  • Leverage a central platform for managing data extraction and document ingestion across multiple channels

  • Benefit from state-of-the-art AI and preconfigured document schemas for efficient and structured data extraction

  • Use advanced business logic to accurately match and derive application data from extracted document content

  • Continuously improve AI accuracy by fine-tuning models through user corrections of extraction results

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item configures the integration with SAP Document AI, which requires additional licenses in the form of AI units. With the scope item activation, you enable additional SAP Fiori tiles that are only functional after the set-up of the integration.
processes.name: Integration with SAP Document AI

processes.description:
Integration with SAP SuccessFactors Payroll (6V9)

Overview

For customers who want to integrate SAP SuccessFactors Payroll and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, this scope item enables the integration, giving you the security of direct connectivity to post your payroll results to your financial system in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition using Web services. This can be used to validate cost centers, check accounting assignments, or display journal entries.

Key Process Flow

  • Transfer payroll postings configuration to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Check documents

  • Release documents

  • Transfer posting documents

  • Transfer payroll postings

processes.name: Integration with SAP SuccessFactors Payroll

processes.description:
Intercompany Billing for Cross-Company Cost Accounting Postings (4AN)

Overview

Applications (such as Time Recording for EPPM or Services) can create cross-company cost accounting documents. Additionally, cross-company cost accounting documents can be created manually in Controlling with the Manage Direct Activity Allocation app. For these FI documents, you must still create legal invoices, including tax. Based on resource-related intercompany billing functionality, you can create the necessary customer invoices with the affiliated company as customer. After the invoices are created, the system can automatically create mirroring accounts payable documents in the receiving affiliated company.

Key Process Flow

  • Create an intercompany sales order in the affiliated cost-sending company where the customer represents the affiliated cost-receiving company

  • Create a debit memo request or billing document request for cross-company cost accounting postings in the affiliated cost-sending company

  • Create a customer invoice in the affiliated cost-sending company

  • Create an accounts payable document in the affiliated cost-receiving company

Business Benefits

  • Enable an automated and integrated process of intercompany billing for cross-company cost accounting postings

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires additional manual set-up steps. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.

processes.description:
Intercompany Billing for Service Documents (53Y)

Overview

A company has an affiliate company. The affiliate company delivers a service to the ordering company while delivering a service to a customer. The affiliate company posts expenses and records time on the service order or repair order. These expenses are transformed into debit memo requests. An intercompany invoice with reference to the debit memo request is created by the delivering company.

Key Process Flow

  • Create service order or repair order

  • Create service confirmation or repair confirmation

  • Generate intercompany billing request

  • Generate intercompany invoice

  • Display service actuals

Business Benefits

  • Create debit memo requests for intercompany billing based on intercompany travel postings and time confirmation from the delivering company

  • Create billing document (intercompany invoice)

  • Post intercompany invoice automatically from company to accounts payables of ordering company

  • Display service actuals

processes.description:
Intercompany Financial Posting (1GP)

Overview

In an intercompany posting across company codes, the system posts a separate document with its own document number in each of the company codes. Individual documents are linked by a common cross-company code number. The system generates line items to balance the debits and credits in each document.

The company codes involved must be part of a single legal entity for tax purposes if one of the following is true:

  • The receivables or payables are posted in a different company code from the one in which the revenue or expenses (costs) are posted

  • The business transaction is relevant to taxes

In addition, the customer can assign a paying company code to each company code. You can have a company code process the payment transactions centrally for several company codes. However, these company codes must be in the same country/region and have the same local currency and parallel currencies. They must have the same settings for enhanced withholding tax functions (active or inactive).

Key Process Flow

  • Post general journal entries between two company codes

  • Display, change, or reverse journal entries for cross-company codes

Business Benefits

  • Allocate costs in general ledger across company codes effectively

  • Reduce the efforts of cross company code journal entry

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This is an intercompany relevant scope item and requires additional manual setup steps. If you requested this scope item, check the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.

Intercompany Occupancy and Contract Management – Group Ledger IFRS (5YW)

Overview

This scope item is only relevant for the integration with SAP Cloud for Real Estate.

After you group real estate objects (such as buildings, floors, spaces, land, and land areas) in the Group Real Estate Object for Occupancy SAP Fiori app, you can maintain them in the Manage Occupancy Groups SAP Fiori app.

Intercompany contract management functionality enables contracts for the lessee company and lessor companies automatically. It supports all relevant leasing processes like partner posting, valuation posting, or rent adjustments.

You can use the Contract Management SAP Fiori app to create lease contracts. You can easily create contracts and execute periodic postings and valuation postings for existing contracts.

You can change the supplier or customer of an existing contract and run reports of your existing contracts as part of your daily business.

You can create reminder rules for every contract, for example, to check the contract conditions, the contract term, or the renewal options, saving you time and effort and freeing up capacity for more strategic tasks.

Key Process Flow

  • Open Group Real Estate Object for Occupancy (F5592) app

  • Search for building or land to be occupied by an affiliated company by company code and object type

  • Create object group with intercompany object category

  • Check occupancy of real estate objects

Business Benefits

  • Use single repository for all real estate assets in the entire portfolio independent of back-end system

  • Collect costs by real estate location, supporting financial reporting and location analysis

  • View vacancy/occupancy reporting for each location based on space type

  • Simplify contract management for leasing between affiliated companies

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

By default, all starter, demo, and trial systems are set up with group ledger IFRS. Intercompany scenarios are excluded. This scope item is excluded because it is an intercompany scenario. Customers can decide to use this scope item in their system landscape based on the selected scope bundle.

Intercompany Process for Customer Returns (2F4)

Overview

This scope item helps the company to manage customer returns and refunds using affiliated plants. It integrates customer processes with intercompany processes. Material returned to the affiliated plant is internally credited. Accounts payable documents can be created automatically.

If the customer gets a free-of-charge delivery (from the affiliated plant) as a refund, an intercompany invoice can be created. Accounts payable documents can be created automatically.

Key Process Flow

  • Generate return order

  • Generate return delivery

  • Post goods receipt

  • Perform material inspection

  • Create intercompany credit memo with subsequent intercompany accounts payable document

  • Determine refund

  • Refund customer with credit memo

    • Create credit memo request

  • Refund customer with free-of-charge replacement material

    • Create order for free-of-charge delivery

    • Create intercompany invoice for free-of-charge delivery

    • Trigger creation of accounts payable document

  • Create customer invoice

Business Benefits

  • Provide end-to-end support and monitoring of the whole return process with customer and affiliated company

  • Generate follow-up processes automatically: Return delivery, customer credit memo, and free-of-charge delivery

  • Handle refunds in one step

  • Offer a scenario with immediate refund

  • Refund customers with a credit memo or with a free-of-charge replacement delivery

  • Includes a scenario where return goods are inspected at customer site

  • Includes goods inspection

  • Integrate follow-up processes for intercompany billing

  • Trigger automatic creation of accounts payables document from Intercompany billing documents

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This is an intercompany relevant scope item and requires additional manual setup steps. If you requested this scope item, check the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.

Intercompany Process for Debt and Investment Mgmt (1YI)

Overview

This scope item allows a company to handle loans with an affiliate company.

If the loans contract is created in the issuing company, a mirror transaction is automatically generated in the receiving company.

The mirroring change feature is available for interest rate instrument (product category 550). This means if a mirror-relevant change (such as roll over, give notice / terminate and reverse) is made to one transaction, its mirror transaction is updated automatically.​

Key Process Flow

  • Analyze cash position

  • Determine interest rate on loan contract

  • Agree on loan contract between both companies

  • Create loan contract by issuing company

  • Review mirrored loan contract by receiving company

  • Perform follow-up activities with standard debt and investment management

Business Benefits

  • Adjust your cash position easily among affiliate companies to avoid a cash shortfall

  • Shift cash easily into a company (such as the headquarters) where the funds are aggregated for investment purposes

  • Aggregate cash within companies that use a common currency, rather than sending in funds from a foreign location that are subject to exchange rate fluctuations

processes.description:
Intercompany Stock Transfer (1P9)

Overview

The stock transfer process begins with a requirement to transfer material from one company or plant to another company or plant within the same country. The Purchaser creates purchase orders under the receiving plant.

A warehouse clerk at the issuing plant monitors the materials due to be shipped and creates deliveries as required. For international processes, a proforma invoice is generated. Once the delivery is complete, the delivery quantities are issued, appropriate documentation is generated, and the goods are shipped, ending the process for the issuing plant.

Goods are received at the receiving plant referencing the purchase documents. Inventory is received into a storage location based on fixed parameters proposed from the material master, which can be changed at the time of transactional data capture (purchase order creation or goods receipt).

Key Process Flow

  • Create intercompany stock transport order

  • Create replenishment delivery for stock transport order

  • Create proforma invoice

  • Pick and post goods issue for stock transport order

  • Inbound delivery

  • Check status of stock transfer

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create intercompany billing document

  • Create supplier invoice

Business Benefits

  • Fulfill the requirement for intercompany stock transfer process between two companies with one country and cross countries

  • Leverage the stock balance between companies and reduce storage value

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This is an intercompany relevant scope item and requires significant additional manual setups. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Intercompany Stock Transfer

processes.description:
Intercompany Stock Transfer Returns (2TS)

Overview

The Intercompany Stock Transfer Returns process begins with a requirement to return material from one company or plant to another company or plant within the same country.

The buyer creates a stock transfer return order in the system. A shipping specialist at the issuing plant monitors the materials due to be shipped and creates deliveries as required. Once a return delivery is created, a pick list is generated for the materials. A warehouse clerk gathers the materials and confirms the picked quantities. The delivery quantities are issued when the return delivery is complete. Once the delivery quantities are issued, an inbound delivery is automatically created in the receiving plant as a follow-up document. A receiving specialist confirms the putaway, then receives and inspects the goods to stock, referencing the inbound delivery. An internal credit memo is generated that transfers the liability to the received company.

Key Process Flow

  • Create stock transfer return order

  • Create return delivery for stock transfer return order

  • Post goods issue for stock transfer return order

  • Post goods receipt for inbound delivery

  • Create internal credit memo with return delivery

  • Create credit memo in invoice verification

Business Benefits

  • Fulfill the requirement for intercompany stock transfer return process between two companies within one country

  • Reduce manual effort with automatic process

  • Monitor the return progress in real-time

This is an intercompany-relevant scope item and require significant additional manual setup. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.

processes.description:
Internal Commissions Settlement for Sales (3TD)

Overview

The internal commissions settlement capabilities support you in offering sales commissions as incentives to employees and paying commissions on schedule. The internal commission settlement can be based on workforce condition contracts, or you can import commission data from SAP SuccessFactors Incentive Management. The payout of commissions happens with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll.

In the first business scenario for internal commissions settlement, you use condition contracts from Condition Contract Management to enter the sales commission agreements for internal sales representatives. In a condition contract, you specify the personnel number of the commission recipient, organizational and process control parameter, the business volume selection criteria, the sales commission conditions, and the settlement calendar with settlement dates for delta accrual and final settlement. The delta accruals settlement reflects a procedure in which accruals for commissions aren't posted together with the transactional documents but subsequently in a specific settlement run. In final settlements of condition contracts, usually aligned with the salary process for employees, you perform the sales commission calculation based on business volume and commission conditions and you create the personnel settlement documents.

In the second business scenario, the process starts in SAP SuccessFactors Incentive Management with the calculation of the commissions amount for the employees and continues with the import of this data to create the personnel settlement documents in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Usually, personnel settlement documents created in both processing variants are automatically released to accounting leading to postings to the corresponding accounts for commissions in Finance. Optionally, the workflow functionality can be used in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for the release of the personnel settlement documents to accounting.

The commission data contained in personnel settlement documents is transferred to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and then to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll. The payroll run is executed in the payroll system. The payout to the employee is run and finally the posting on the liability account in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system is done.

Key Process Flow

Sales Commissions Based on Workforce Condition Contracts:

  • Create workforce condition contracts

  • Post accruals (optional)

  • Post incoming payments (optional)

  • Check business volume

  • Final settlement with reversal of accruals

Sales Commissions with Integration to SAP Sales Cloud:

  • Calculate commissions in SAP Sales Cloud

  • In SAP S/4HANA, schedule import of commission data from SAP Sales Cloud

  • Check personnel settlement documents

  • Release personnel settlement documents to accounting

Business Benefits

  • Benefit from an efficient end-to-end scenario from commissions calculation to payout

  • Administer commission agreements for internal sales representatives with workforce condition contracts and settle sales commissions accurately and automatically with the subsequent settlement features of Condition Contract Management

  • Apply sophisticated commission calculation algorithm of SAP Sales Cloud

  • Streamline the payout with SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

To run the end-to-end process, you need to set up the integration between SAP Sales Cloud, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central, and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll.

Intra-Company Returns Stock Transfers (5WI)

Overview

The intra-company returns stock transfer process begins with a requirement to return a material from one plant to another plant within the same company code. The return of the material is triggered for a number of reasons, such as damage during transportation, product defect or damage, over-delivery or wrong delivery, end of promotion or season, and so on.

The issuing plant creates a returns stock transport order in the system. A shipping specialist at the issuing plant monitors the materials due to be shipped and creates deliveries as required. Once a return delivery is created, a pick list is generated for the outbound delivery. A warehouse clerk gathers the materials and confirms the picked quantities. The delivery quantities are issued when the return delivery is complete. When you post the goods issue for the outbound delivery, the system automatically creates an inbound delivery for the receiving plant.

Key Process Flow

  • Create returns stock transport order

  • Create return outbound delivery for returns stock transport order

  • Pick materials and post goods issue for returns outbound delivery

  • Process inbound delivery and post goods receipt for returned material

  • Perform material inspection and specify logistical follow-up activities

Business Benefits

  • Fulfill the requirement for intra-company returns stock transfer process between two plants within the same company code

  • Use efficient and cost-effective returns processes

Intrastat is a statistical system used to collect information from enterprises regarding trade between European Union (EU) member states. When the EU was created in 1993 and the initial EU member states became part of the single market, information about their trade with other EU member states could no longer be obtained from customs documents. Intrastat evolved as a replacement to collect information directly from enterprises about dispatches and arrivals of commodities among member states. Today, Intrastat is used for collecting statistics on the trade in goods (services are excluded) between the EU member states.
