Inventory Management for Distribution Centers (5FQ)

Overview

Articles held by a retailer are known as inventory. Inventory management comprises analytical (for example, stock overview) and operational processes (for example, moving goods within a site or changing the status of the stock). In inventory management, you can keep information on the quantities and valuation of the article stock. The valuation is kept in financial accounts and is needed for legally required financial closing statements. Typically, a retailer needs both quantity and valuation information.

Two main types of activities are relevant for inventory management: first, processes where articles are physically moved (goods movements), such as goods receipts, goods issues, or transfers from one storage location to another; second, processes where the status of stock is changed, such as from unrestricted use to scrapping, or from blocked quality management to unrestricted use. Both types of activities are recorded in article documents. Posting such an article document results in quantity updates, and in some cases also leads to postings to financial accounts. For example, a movement from one storage location to another leads to a quantity update of the article for the storage location but doesn't need to be reflected in financial accounting, as the value hasn't changed.

Article documents also serve auditing purposes; every change in quantity or value is reported, as well as who executed it (including the link to the resulting financial posting).

The stock overview displays the current stock situation on different levels (for example site group, site, or storage location) and different status (for example unrestricted use, quality inspection, or in transit).

Key Process Flow

  • Manage stock

  • Display stock overview

  • Post goods movements

  • Transfer stock within a site

  • List and display article documents

Business Benefits

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by improving inventory accuracy, reducing shrinkage and obsolescence costs

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by accurately tracking inventory at the product location level and taking appropriate merchandising decisions

  • Reduce revenue loss due to stock-outs by monitoring in real-time inventory across all locations and quickly addressing low or no inventory situation

This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.

Invoice Correction Process with Credit Memo (BKL)

Overview

A credit memo request is created with the amount to be credited and placed on a billing block for review. The amount to be credited is calculated as the difference between the original amount and the correct amount entered manually in the credit memo request. It must then be released to become billing-relevant and to appear in the billing due list. The credit memo can be created manually. Alternatively, the periodic billing process automatically creates a credit memo to be sent to the customer and posts a journal entry.

Key Process Flow

  • Create credit memo request

  • Approve workflow for credit memo requests

  • Remove billing block (review credit memo request)

  • Create credit memo

Business Benefits

  • Integrate credit memo processing in the system

processes.description:
Invoice Correction Process with Debit Memo (BDQ)

Overview

This scope item makes it possible to correct errors in pricing or sales tax calculations. If errors are detected, debit memo requests can be created with a correction of the amount to be debited. This is then placed on a billing block for review. The amount to be debited is calculated as the difference between the original amount and the correct amount. This is entered manually into the debit memo request. Once checked, it is released and becomes relevant for billing. The amount then appears in the billing due list. The debit memo can be created manually. Alternatively, the automatic periodic billing process creates a debit memo to be sent to the customer and posts a journal entry.

Key Process Flow

  • Create debit memo request

  • Remove billing block (review debit memo request)

  • Create debit memo

Business Benefits

SAP Ariba Invoicing supports the display of invoice attachments in a split screen, as well as a seamless navigation to SAP Fiori apps for invoices or SAP GUI transactions from connected systems. It also provides various options to authorize specific invoice access to different user groups. The SAP Ariba Invoicing, inbound processing module provides embedded invoice inbound processing services, including OCR. This additional module allows users to upload invoice files, edit draft invoices, and save supplier invoices directly to the connected backend system.

processes.description:
Invoice Processing with SAP Ariba Invoicing (7YH)

Overview

SAP Ariba Invoicing is deployed on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP), the next generation platform for AI native solutions from SAP. The solution provides a single solution for receiving, managing, and approving supplier invoices from virtually any source, simultaneously supporting multiple SAP ERP systems and SAP S/4HANA Cloud systems.

SAP Ariba Invoicing seamlessly integrates with SAP Business Network for e-Invoicing, regulatory compliance, and supplier collaboration. With SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, it integrates with government invoice portals or Peppol networks. Scanned paper or PDF invoices can be uploaded natively via simple drag-and-drop, Joule chat bot, received via email, or use one of several API’s. The solution includes conversion (OCR) of invoices out-of-the-box, leveraging an ensemble of technologies such as SAP Document AI and other AI solutions, or use a custom OCR provider via an API. AI/ML automatically perform cost assignment of non-PO invoices, and smart line-item matching of your PO invoices to achieve higher levels of touchless invoice processing and less work for AP. Automatic exception handling, including duplicate invoice check against any SAP ERP invoice, and subsequent AP queue allocation on an SAP Fiori interface ensures efficient processing by AP when needed. The solution provides full view of invoices and their status across all SAP ERP systems, and not only invoices processed by the solution. Finally, user approvals of invoices can be done natively in the solution, or configured to work seamlessly with S4HANA, and once fully approved, these are automatically posted to the corresponding finance system for payment.

When you select this solution process, SAP takes responsibility for the initial provisioning, integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, and operations. This includes tasks such as technical monitoring of the integrated product.

Key Process Flows

  • Process invoice data

  • Approve invoices

  • Reduce invoice processing costs both on a per invoice basis and overall

  • Shorten payment cycles and reduce late payments

  • Process invoices from virtually any source, globally (see documentation for country coverage), and with native OCR capabilities where needed

  • Automatic AI/ML account assignment and smart PO line-item matching

  • Automatic exception handling and AP queue allocation to reduce AP workload

  • Use SAP Fiori interface for seamless user experience

processes.description:
Invoice Verification for Retail (5FN)

Overview

Once goods are procured from a supplier and placed on the company’s premises through goods receipt, the retailer (recipient) must pay the supplier for the acquired goods. The amount to be paid and the material details are provided by the supplier in the form of an invoice document. Before paying to the supplier, the retailer must verify the invoice. This scope item covers the verification of the invoice before making a payment.

Before the procurement from external suppliers, the retailer carries out a logistics invoice verification. The content of invoice sent from the supplier is compared with the content of the two preceding main documents (the purchase order and the goods receipt). This process is also called three-way matching. The values of the articles and the quantities from the invoice are compared with those of the actual goods receipts. Prices and other conditions from the invoice are compared with those of the purchase order. When the values match, the invoice can be posted directly or after an optional release step. As a result, the respective financial accounts are posted to and handed over for payment. If there are discrepancies, you can decide either to accept or reject them, triggering the corresponding communication to the supplier.

Key Process Flow

  • Create invoice memos that are received

  • Check the accuracy of invoices with respect to content, prices, and quantities

  • Execute the account postings resulting from an invoice

  • Check invoices that were blocked because the details varied from the purchase order

Business Benefits

  • Improve discount achievement by making quicker payment decisions and expanding capture of early-payment discounts

  • Improve supplier or external partner compliance by streamlining invoice processing by three-way matching of invoice data

  • Improve accounts payable FTE productivity by simplifying and automating invoice processing

processes.description:
Just-In-Time Supply to Customer (2EM)

Overview

The process starts with receiving Just-In-Time (JIT) calls from customers.

JIT calls are sent via an EDI integration and contain the component details with the requirements date and time. The material planner (JIT supply) monitors and manages the JIT calls. The production planner releases production-relevant component group materials or package units for production for summarized and sequenced JIT calls respectively.

The production operator then confirms the production of the components. The production supervisor reprocesses failed stocks.

The shipping specialist (JIT supply) creates deliveries that reflect the status accordingly. Advanced shipping notifications are sent via EDI to the OEM. The shipping specialist and material planner can create handling units as well.

After picking and posting of goods issue, the JIT call status is updated. Optionally, for summarized JIT calls, picking and post goods issue can be done in Extended Warehouse Management.

After the billing is created, the JIT call is updated to completed status.

Key Process Flow

  • Create, manage, and monitor Just-In-Time (JIT) calls

  • Release JIT calls to production

  • Confirm JIT calls from production

  • Reprocess failed stock posting

  • Release for packing

  • Confirm packing

  • Create delivery from JIT calls (sequenced or summarized)

  • Update JIT call based on subsequent outbound delivery split

  • Reorder process of JIT calls (before and after delivery)

  • Integrate with handling unit management

  • Integrate with extended warehouse management for summarized JIT calls

  • Execute picking

  • Post goods issue

  • Send advance shipping notice

  • Create billing document

  • Send invoice

Business Benefits

  • Support the business process for Just-In-Time supply to customers

  • Enable the visibility of fulfillment progress and alerts based on processing errors

  • Support the business process for in-house repetitive manufacturing production

  • Help process the supply efficiently

  • Provide flexibility through configuration and extensibility

  • Support integration with handling unit management and EWM for summarized JIT calls

  • Support updates from external systems, such as manufacturing execution systems

  • Enable analytical capabilities to manage demand, stock, and materials

processes.description:
Just-In-Time Supply to Customer with Delivery Confirmation (53X)

Overview

The process starts with receiving a Just -In- time (JIT) call from customers (see the Just-In-Time Supply to Customer (2EM) scope item). During the processing of such JIT calls, the goods are posted as consignment stock. Consignment goods are stored at the customer location but owned by suppliers.

The customers are not obligated to pay for these goods until they remove it from consignment stock. As the goods are consumed, customers send JIT delivery confirmations via SOAP API with information about materials, quantity, and reference JIT calls.

The delivery confirmation is matched with the existing JIT calls within the supplier system. The material planner (JIT supply) has an option to release them manually.

Once the delivery confirmation is released, subsequent documents (such as customer consignment issue order and outbound delivery related to customer consignment issue order) are created and the goods issue is posted.

After the billing is done, the JIT call lifecycle status is updated.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage and monitor the JIT delivery confirmation

  • Release the JIT delivery confirmation

  • Create customer consignment issue order and outbound delivery automatically

  • Post goods issue

  • Create billing documents

Business Benefits

  • Manage inventory of delivered products in customer consignment stock until confirmed by the customer

  • Process billing or self-billing based on JIT delivery confirmations from customers

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is relevant only for self-billing scenarios. If a customer follows self-billing business processes, they can request for activation of this scope item.

If this scope item is active, delivery confirmation documents can be triggered by initiating the self-billing process.

Lot Size of One based on Make to Order (7DW)

Overview

The scope item focuses on Lot Size of One based on make-to-order end to end scenario using standard material as an example. The business flow depicts from creation of sale order, covering deficit by material requirement planning runs, production executions followed by logistics and billing.

In this scope item articulation of the make-to-order flow depicted with example of robotic base. The process flow starts with creation of sale order with a billing plan where sale executive details the requirement. Based on the order the MRP run is scheduled to procure or produce the components needed for the production staging and execution. The procured components like steel plates are batch managed.

The procured materials are staged for production. On confirmation of manufacturing operations the finished product is identified as special stock for a sale order at all times. The manufactured product is subject to quality inspection, the quality technician records the inspection results on the inspection lot and confirms the usage decision of the manufactured product. The material is ready for outbound delivery involving picking, packing and goods issue. The story line concluded by creation of billing documents, and completing the outgoing and incoming financial settlements.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a sales order with billing plan to initiate make-to-order process

  • Execute MRP runs

  • Create purchase orders

  • Receive goods and manage batches for raw materials

  • Convert planned orders to production orders

  • Stage materials and release production orders

  • Confirm production operations for final assembly

  • Complete production with order confirmation

  • Perform quality inspection and record usage decisions

  • Create outbound delivery covering pick, pack, and goods issue

  • Execute customer billing and vendor invoices

  • Post incoming and outgoing payments

Business Benefits

  • Experience end-to-end manufacturing flow based on make-to-order scenario

  • Trigger production execution based on sales order

  • Gain insight to material deficits by MRP runs

  • Reduce inventory costs by initiating production on confirmed sale order

  • Increase transparency into production and inventory costs by enabling sales-order-specific cost estimates

  • Shorten order-to-cash cycle time by enabling flexible billing plan including down payments

  • Increase transparency and tracking raw material/sub-assemblies using batch management
processes.name: Lot Size of One based on Make to Order

processes.description:
Lot Size of One with Advanced Variant Configuration (55E)

Overview

This scope item focuses on a Make-to-Order scenario (Lot Size of One) that integrates with production planning and execution, procurement, inquiry, quotation, sales, and logistics execution up to invoicing and incoming and outgoing payments, covering multilevel configurable materials. The configurable material is defined as a bill of material.

In this process, the storyline starts with an inquiry for a robot, proceeding to a quotation and on confirmation a sales order is created with an individual configuration. This is captured by defining the different component characteristics desired by the customers and considering the constraints and dependencies of the components. The sales price calculation is then based on the individually chosen characteristics of the components. The sales order is considered for production planning when doing the materials requirements planning (MRP). Configured subassemblies are procured externally based on the procurement proposal generated during MRP. Another configured subassembly is transferred to production plant from another plant belonging to the same company code. Special procurement indicators are used to define stock transfer locations.

Stock is placed in special sales order stock at all times and serialized (as of level subassembly). By serializing stock throughout the process, this allows customers to gain transparency for items that are built in the configured finished good.

The production execution for the individual robot takes place after one subassembly is procured externally (including configuration information), while another subassembly is internally produced. The finished good (robot) is subject to quality inspection at the end of production.

Once production is complete, the goods are delivered to the customer and invoiced. The process finishes with posting of incoming payments from the customer as well as outgoing payments to the vendor for purchased subassemblies.

Related SCN Blog for material BOM graphical representation:

  • Understanding variations in Lot Size of One (LS1) E2E scenario

Related SCN Blog for E2E process flow of 55E:

  • Working with E2E Lot Size of One (CTO scenario) with Advanced Variant Configuration | Scope Item '55E'

  • Insights into Lot Size-of-One End to End Scenario (55E) based on Configure to Order / Make to Order

Key Process Flow

  • Exhibit multilevel configuration of products in sales orders using advanced variant configuration

  • Perform material requirements planning and evaluation of stock requirement list based on inquiry, quotation translating to sales order demand

  • Procure configured subassemblies including inbound delivery

  • Procure configured subassembly via intracompany stock transfer

  • Perform quality inspection in production

  • Handle production order processing: Material staging, order release, order confirmation, material movement postings for goods issue and goods receipts of serialized product

  • Execute purchasing, easing direct procurement

  • Perform outbound delivery and pick items

  • Post goods issue

  • Execute customer billing

  • Post incoming and outgoing payments

Business Benefits

  • Exhibit multilevel configuration and handover of configured products from inquiry, quotation and sales to procurement and production

  • Trigger production execution based on sales orders

  • Explode the bill of material automatically when running the material requirements planning

  • Gain transparency by serialization of products for subassemblies and finished goods

  • Integrate quality management in production process

  • Create billing document and postings for financials and controlling

This scope item is only relevant for customers that want to use Advanced Variant Configuration capabilities in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Maintenance Order Processing with SAP Field Service Management (7Z2)

Overview

This scope item describes end-to-end business scenarios that connect SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition reactive maintenance order processing with SAP Field Service Management. The reactive maintenance process lets users perform maintenance on assets when a breakdown or failure occurs.

After users create and release a reactive maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the system creates a corresponding service call in SAP Field Service Management. The system creates an activity for each operation in the maintenance order. It also replicates components as reserved materials.

Users assign an activity to a technician on the planning board in SAP Field Service Management. When users release the activity, the system automatically updates the technician in the corresponding maintenance order operation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

When users approve confirmations such as efforts, expenses, or materials in SAP Field Service Management, the system creates a confirmation in the maintenance order and automatically completes it in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Key Process Flow

  • Create maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and release it to SAP Field Service Management

  • Create maintenance order operation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when an activity is created in SAP Field Service Management (optional)

  • Navigate from an SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition maintenance order to SAP Field Service Management (optional)

  • Update maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when service call or activity is updated in SAP Field Service Management (including planned start and end date, and executing service employee)

  • Re-release maintenance orders after changes from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Field Service Management

  • Update execution status from SAP Field Service Management to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition maintenance order

  • Create a completed maintenance order confirmation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when efforts, expenses, and spare parts are approved in SAP Field Service Management

  • Support unplanned effort, expense, and material confirmations from a service technician on a service activity

  • Handle reassignment of service technician in SAP Field Service Management and update of the same on maintenance order operation level

  • Handle duplicate activities in SAP Field Service Management and update of the same on maintenance order operation level

  • Complete a maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and technically complete the corresponding service call in SAP Field Service Management

  • Assign attachment to the service call or activity in the SAP Field Service Management system and replicate it to the corresponding maintenance order or operation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Update service call ID and activity ID in maintenance order transaction history after replication

Business Benefits

  • Optimize your field service processes with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition maintenance order processing integration.

  • Ensure a seamless, fast, and flexible delivery of field services

  • Provide more efficient customer services

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

To use this scope item, you need an additional license to use SAP Field Service Management.

processes.description:
Make-to-Order Production – Finished Goods Sales and Final Assembly (BJE)

Overview

The Make-to-Order process starts with a customer quotation and ends with the clearing of a customer account after a payment is received.

The process starts with the creation of a quote that includes a price and lead time estimate. Once the customer accepts the quote, a sales order is created that references the quote. The billing plan containing multiple customer payments (including down payment) may be set up in the order.

The production process is triggered by a material requirement planning (MRP) run for the finished product and BoM components. Once the finished product is manufactured (and confirmations entered and components issued) and received into stock, the delivery and final billing occurs.

Optionally, you can set up an order BoM that contains the components required for the customer’s specific requirements. A cost estimate can be generated based on an order-specific BoM.

Components can be preplanned using the Semi-finished Goods Planning and Assembly (1BM) scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Plan production in a make-to-order scenario, optionally with a sales order bill of material

  • Execute production specific to customer requirements and specification

  • Improve usability with intuitive confirmation of production operations

  • Use billing plan including down payments

Business Benefits

  • Reduce inventory costs by initiating production after you receive a customer order

  • Reduce time between initial customer inquiry to sales order receipt by streamlining the quote to order process

  • Enable Make-To-Order production

processes.description:
Make-to-Order Production – Process Manufacturing (3OK)

Overview

The standard sales process (make-to-order) for batch-managed finished goods starts with a customer quotation or sales order and ends with the clearing of a customer account after a payment is received.

The process starts with the creation of a quotation and then a sales order that references it, or by creating a sales order directly.

The production process based on process orders is triggered by a material requirement planning (MRP) run for the product ordered by the customer and all its components. Once the finished product with a batch is in stock, the delivery and billing of the goods completes the process.

The process can be enhanced by executing optional steps, such as procurement of components or period-end closing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create quotation for customer

  • Create referenced sales order from the quotation

  • Plan and execute the production process with process orders

  • Deliver the produced goods

  • Bill customer based on billing plan from sales order

Business Benefits

  • Plan production in a make-to-order scenario based on customer sales order

  • Drive production of customer requirements using process orders
processes.name: Make-to-Order Production – Process Manufacturing

processes.description:
Make-to-Order Production – Semifinished Goods Planning and Assembly (1BM)

Overview

This scope item supports production planning for semifinished components within a Make-to-Order (MTO) environment before the receipt of incoming sales orders. This reduces the lead time of sales orders for finished goods received that are received later.

Demand forecast is created for semifinished components that are represented through planned independent requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) creates a production plan for the component and explodes the bill of material structure for higher low-level codes. As a result, the demand for semifinished component production and raw material is planned.

The production process is made up of the following: Conversion of planned orders to production orders, order release, confirmation of order operations with automatic backflush of components, and goods receipt posting.

The scenario is completed with the receipt of an incoming sales order and either the consumption of the component part of this scope item, or by reference to the entire MTO scenario in the BJE scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage demand forecast for semifinished products as Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs)

  • Schedule MRP run

  • Start production for semifinished product before incoming sales orders

  • Consume PIRs and stock of semifinished product in sales orders

Business Benefits

  • Reduce total lead time in make-to-order production scenarios

  • Create purchase requisitions for raw materials early

  • Produce semifinished products early

  • Improved usability with intuitive confirmation of production operations
processes.name: Make-to-Order Production – Semifinished Goods Planning and Assembly

processes.description:
Make-to-Order Production for Sales Kits with Variant Configuration (4OC)

Overview

Customers want to have a way to use variant configuration and show the component as sales kits (SET) during order taking and follow up processes.

This scope item shows a make-to-order production scenario for sales kits using advanced variant configuration for an efficient state-of-the-art configuration of a material ordered by a customer.

The configurable material is defined as a SET material. In this process, a sales order is created with an individual configuration for a robot bundle. This is captured by defining the different component characteristics desired by the customers and considering the constraints and dependencies of the components. The sales price calculation is then based on the individually chosen characteristics of the components. The sales order is considered for production planning when doing the materials requirements planning. The production execution for the individual robot bundle takes place before delivering it to the customer. The process finishes with the billing to the customer.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a customer sales order

  • Show the variant configurable materials in the sales order (as sales BOM)

  • Calculate sales prices based on the customer's chosen characteristics for the configurable product

  • Execute the make-to-order production of the robot bundle ordered by the customer with routings according to the configuration

Business Benefits

  • Improve your company's sales and manufacturing performance with sales kits that cover integrated advanced variant configuration

  • Enable your business processes to handle highly individualized products in sales and manufacturing

  • Leverage the sophisticated algorithms in the performance-optimized rules engine within a state-of-the-art configurator

  • Use dependencies to select exactly the right components and to prevent combinations of options that aren’t allowed

  • Get sales pricing and printout according to the configuration

Overview

This scope item enables production planning in make-to-stock scenarios and quick reactions to incoming sales orders. The focus is on process manufacturing (for example, supported through process orders or batch management).

The process starts with the creation of a demand forecast for finished goods represented by planned independent requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) creates a production plan for finished goods, semifinished components, and raw materials. Production planners can analyze and change the planned-order-based production plan manually.

Raw material demand leads to purchase requisitions that trigger alternative procurement scenarios referenced in this scope item.

The production process itself is entirely covered via conversion of planned into process orders, order release, direct material issue or backflush, confirmation of operations, and goods receipt posting. processes.description:
Make-to-Stock Production – Repetitive Manufacturing (BJH)

Overview

Repetitive Manufacturing is commonly used when a production process meets the following criteria:

  • The same or similar products are produced over an extended period

  • Products aren't manufactured in individually defined lots (instead, a total quantity is produced over a specific period at a certain rate)

  • Items always follow the same sequence through the machines and work centers in production

  • Routings tend to be simple and don't vary significantly

This scenario begins with Planned Independent Requirements (PIR), which are used to perform demand management functions. Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates planned orders for the materials to be produced. By using the planning table, the production of materials and capacity on the production lines can be planned. Confirming Repetitive Manufacturing triggers multiple activities, such as finished product goods receipt, backflushing of component materials, posting costs to cost collectors, and creating material and journal entries.

In Repetitive Manufacturing, the master plan is represented by the planning table, which is a tool for operative planning and is used to plan production quantities. In a repetitive manufacturing environment, planning and control are usually performed on a period and quantity basis. The planning table's layout has been designed to support this requirement and is also based on periods to provide a clear, easy-to-interpret overview of materials and production lines.

The planning table is the Production Planner's or MRP Controller's most important tool for planning production quantities. At a glance, they can check production quantities, monitor the available capacity of the production lines, and check the availability of the products produced on each line.

Production quantities can be directly entered and changed in the planning table. 'Nonassigned' production quantities can be assigned to the production lines, or production quantities can be reassigned to alternative production lines.

The planning table can be used for planning with planned orders and production orders. The only prerequisite is that a valid production version must be created in the material master record.

Key Process Flow

  • Creation of planned independent requirements

  • Planning of material requirements at plant level

  • Adjustment of planning in planning table

  • Checking range of stock coverage

  • Material staging

  • Confirmation of assembly activities and repetitive manufacturing backflush

  • Post processing of error records

Business Benefits

  • Make-to-stock production based on run schedules without reference to sales orders

  • Simplified handling of the production process with full cost control

  • Confirmation of assembly activities without using production or process orders
processes.name: Make-to-Stock Production – Repetitive Manufacturing

processes.description:
Make-to-Stock Production with Variant Configuration (21D)

Overview

This scope item shows the Make-to-Stock Production with Variant Configuration in which Advanced Variant Configuration enables efficient state-of-the-art configuration for configurable products variants that reflect common definitions of a configurable material. The material variant is defined as a Bill of Material (BOM) where the components meet certain criteria. Initially, this material variant is produced and put into stock as later sales of it are anticipated by collection of Planned-Independent Requirements (PIRs). When a customer orders a fork lifter where the characteristics of the components meet those of the material variant, the fork lifter is taken directly from stock as production already happened based on PIRs. The sales price calculation is then based on the characteristics of the material variant. Since the material variant is available on stock, the fork lifter is directly delivered. The process finishes with the billing of the delivered fork lifter.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a customer sales order for a configured fork lifter resulting in a material variant

  • Calculate sales prices based on characteristics of the material variant

Business Benefits

  • Produce material variants upfront to incoming sales orders based on expected demand

Placing chemical products on the market requires an efficient system support for handling mandatory documentation as defined by regulators. processes.description:
Managing Material Price Changes and Inventory Values (1ZT)

Overview

This scope item provides users with an example of a process description that they can use to upload material inventory prices, change material valuation prices, manage material valuations, and view and analyze material inventory values.

You can make a price change in the following ways:

  • One-step procedure with immediate effect: When material costs are changed, inventory is revaluated with all price controls, including valuation with the standard price and periodic unit price.

  • Debit/Credit Material-Related Account: When debiting or crediting a material, the revaluation amounts are posted as follows:

    • For standard price materials (price control S), the revaluation amount is posted to a price difference account. The standard price of the material is not changed.

    • For moving average price materials (price control V), the revaluation amount is posted to the material stock account, provided there is sufficient stock coverage. If not, only the portion for the available stock is posted to the stock account, with the remainder posted to a price difference account.

  • Two-step change via Determine Future Prices and Releasing Planned Prices:

    • When future prices are entered, the new future valuation prices are updated in all currencies and valuations within the material ledger data, and in the company code currency in the material master record.

    • When planned price changes are released, the system updates the valid future prices (in various currencies and valuations) as the current standard price or valuation price. It calculates a revaluation amount for the specific inventory quantity, adjusting the inventory value by this amount. The offsetting entry occurs in the revaluation account according to account determination. If there is no material stock, only the price is updated.

Key Process Flow

  • Upload inventory prices

  • Choose between alternatives to change material prices and view the results

  • View the balance summary of inventory values

  • Review the journal entries that affect the value of material inventories during a particular period

Business Benefits

  • Maintain material valuation prices independently in up to three currencies

  • Manage material valuations

  • View and analyze the material inventory values from various perspectives
processes.name: Managing Material Price Changes and Inventory Values

processes.description:
Manual Transportation Planning (6W2)

Overview

Manual planning allows you to create or change a transportation plan. To create a transportation plan, you assign transportation demands (such as freight unit stages) to transportation capacities (such as equipment types, for example, truck types, railcar types, or container types). The system creates capacity documents (freight orders or freight bookings). Scheduling runs automatically after you perform a planning activity for a road freight order. Manual planning is done in the Transportation Cockpit app. You can then create deliveries for these freight documents.

Key Process Flow

  • Supports various activities for freight documents, such as road freight order, rail freight order, ocean freight booking, air freight booking, and advanced intercompany documents

  • Perform manual transportation planning for freight documents created in your transportation process

  • Perform subcontracting for relevant freight documents

  • Receive confirmation for involved freight documents

  • Trigger delivery creation and monitor freight documents

Business Benefits

  • Support your company's transportation planning in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Reduce freight costs with early transportation planning capabilities based on orders

  • Get fewer delivery changes during logistics execution with late delivery creation based on the transportation plan and warehouse activity closeness

  • Improve on-time deliveries

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers who want to manually create and edit freight orders and freight bookings (freight documents) using the Transportation Cockpit app and other supported apps in the Freight Order Management area in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.
processes.name: Manual Transportation Planning

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item supports production planning for make-to-stock scenarios involving a single retail article produced as a finished good (material type FERT).

The process begins with the creation of a demand forecast, which is represented through Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs). Based on these PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates a production plan for the retail article and performs a complete bill of material (BOM) explosion. As a result, demand for semi-finished components and raw materials is determined. Production planners can review, analyze, and manually adjust the planned order–based production plan as required. The demand for raw materials generates purchase requisitions, which trigger alternative procurement processes referenced within this scope item.

The production execution process includes the conversion of planned orders into production orders, order release, material staging and picking, confirmation of order operations, and goods receipt posting for the finished goods. Throughout the process, order-based target and actual costs are recorded, ensuring fully integrated material and value flows across the production lifecycle.

Key Process Flow

  • Process planned independent requirements
  • Execute material requirements planning (MRP) and ​evaluate stock requirement list​
  • Execute production order processing, including material staging, order release, order confirmation, goods issue and goods receipt postings, and Available-to-Promise (ATP) checks.
  • (Optional) Run scrap reports after production​

Business Benefits

  • Initiate production execution seamlessly using a structured production plan.
  • Automatically explode the bill of materials (BOM) during material requirements planning (MRP) runs.
  • Calculate target costs automatically at the time of order creation.
  • Enhance usability with intuitive confirmation of production operations.

Exclude from Default Activation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

This scope item can only be activated if you have a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and have activated the retail bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.

processes.description:
Margin Analysis (J55)

Overview

This scope item enables you to analyze profit and contribution margins by market segment or strategic business unit, such as a sales organization or business area. You can analyze contribution margins for individual products and services, and monitor the profitability of project-based services you provide to your clients. You can also see unbilled project costs and revenues.

The cost and revenue information is always current and fully reconciled with the income statement.

After performing allocations and top-down distributions, the application offers several reports to analyze the data.

Key Process Flow

  • Run universal allocation to transfer cost center costs to market segments in margin analysis

  • Post expenses to central cost center, create and execute top-down distribution cycle

  • Create and execute a profitability realignment run and analyze its results

  • Run reports on projects: project profitability overview, project profitability, and project financial booklet – professional services

  • Run report on products: product profitability with production variances

  • Run reports for service business: solution order margins, service profitability review booklet

  • Run reports on market segments: market segments actual report, market segments actual versus plan report

  • Run margin analysis reports across objects: display line items – margin analysis, product and service margins

Business Benefits

  • Derive reporting dimensions (market segments) in real-time

  • Ensure cost and revenue information is always current and fully reconciled with the income statement

  • Gain more insight into the profitability of market segments (product, customer, customer orders, projects) or strategic business units (sales organizations, business areas) with respect to your company's profit or contribution margin

  • Offer predefined financial KPIs and adaptable views on customer projects, projects with revenues, and overhead projects
processes.name: Margin Analysis

processes.description:
Margin Optimization – SAP Solution Extensions by Vistex (7UQ)

Overview

This scope item covers the integration of SAP margin optimization solutions by Vistex to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

The SAP margin optimization solutions by Vistex include:

  • SAP Extended Price Management by Vistex

  • SAP Price Staging Hub by Vistex

  • SAP Channel Program Management by Vistex

  • SAP Vendor Program Management by Vistex

  • SAP Rights & Royalty Management by Vistex, cloud edition

Each of these solutions addresses a critical business process in the buying or selling of goods or services: setting pricing and discounting strategies, negotiating incentive or promotional programs, tracking applicable benefits, and managing the lagged payment cashflow. When combined, these solutions offer deep insight into the true gross-to-net margins and profitability of complex and overlapping incentives and ensure full utilization and compliance of program terms and conditions.

Key Process Flow

  • Add attributes to materials and business partners for deeper classification and to drive automated grouping

  • Define global and regional list prices, customer-specific prices, and pricing formulas for derivative pricing

  • Define, model, and execute agreements for discounted pricing, rebates, reimbursements, royalties, and other incentives or promotions

  • Forecast and analyze gross-to-net margins across product lines, customer groups, or lines of business considering costs, pricing, and applicable payments

  • Import, cleanse, validate, and process external transaction data sets, and reconcile adjustments with original submissions when necessary

  • Forecast, accrue, and settle eligible benefits from sales and purchasing transacted through SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Business Benefits

  • Improve margins through an accurate understanding of net-net costs and sales pricing

  • Automate transaction processing, calculation of benefits, and reconciliation of claims to reduce operational time and cost of incentive programs

  • Increase revenue by monetizing intellectual property with more accurately licensing

  • Reduce the risk of customer churn, partner dissatisfaction, and inaccurate cashflow management

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires an additional SAP Solution Extensions by Vistex product license.

processes.description:
Overview

Mass load and mass maintenance of business partner data provides capabilities to load and update multiple business partner master data records.

To load records, you import data from file. The system starts the checking, cleansing, validation, and activation processes. To update records, you select the fields and records you want to change. Once you enter your changes, the system provides statistics on the changed fields and validates the data. You check the validated data and activate it for use in business transactions.

Key Process Flow

For Mass Load:

  • Import source data using files from your desktop to import into the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system
  • Review initial data quality of the uploaded data
  • Check if data can be activated
  • Activate data in the system

For Mass Maintenance:

  • Define all fields to change
  • Select records to change
  • Apply changes to dataset
  • Validate if records can be activated in the system based on system customizing
  • Activate master data records to update master data

For Export Master Data:

  • Select several fields from tables
  • Select all fields from all tables
  • Export the master data to an Excel or CSV (ZIP file)

For Remediation Process:

  • Select business partner data to be validated
  • Check items for remediation and get detailed information of the issue (rule description of violated rule, product details)
  • Trigger the correction process of business partner master data for a single object or multiple objects

Business Benefits

  • Optimize business partner data load
  • Increase business performance with superior master data quality
  • Save time when editing multiple master data records
  • Perform the master data maintenance process more efficiently

Exclude from Default Activation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

processes.name: Mass Load and Mass Maintenance for Business Partner

processes.description:
Mass Load and Mass Maintenance for Business Partners (7MI)

Overview

Mass Load and Mass Maintenance of business partner data provides capabilities to load and update multiple business partner master data records simultaneously.

To load records, you import data from a file. The system starts the checking, cleansing, validation, and activation processes.

To update records, you select the fields and records you want to change. Once you enter your changes, the system provides statistics on the changed fields and validates the data. You check the validated data and activate it for use in business transactions.

Key Process Flow

For Mass Load:

  • Import source data using files from your desktop to import into the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system

  • Review initial data quality of the uploaded data

  • Check if data can be activated

  • Activate data in the system

For Mass Maintenance:

  • Define all fields to change

  • Select records to change

  • Apply changes to dataset

  • Validate if records can be activated in the system based on system customizing

  • Activate master data records to update master data

For Export Master Data:

  • Select several fields from tables

  • Select all fields from all tables

  • Export the master data to an Excel or CSV (ZIP file)

For Remediation Process:

  • Select business partner data to be validated

  • Check items for remediation and get detailed information of the issue (rule description of violated rule, product details)

  • Trigger the correction process of business partner master data for a single object or multiple objects

Business Benefits

  • Optimize business partner data load

  • Increase business performance with superior master data quality

  • Save time when editing multiple master data records

  • Perform the master data maintenance process more efficiently

Overview

Mass Load and Mass Maintenance of Product Data provides capabilities to load, update, validate, remediate, and export multiple Product Master data records simultaneously within the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

The scope item supports both the classic applications and the new cloud-ready applications with the same business processes and capabilities. Users can perform mass load, mass maintenance, export, and remediation activities using either application framework.

To load records, users import Product data from files. The system validates and activates the data before it becomes available for business processes.

To update records, users define the fields and records to be changed. The system validates the changes, provides statistics for the updated data, and activates the records for productive use.

To use the cloud-ready applications, the feature toggle MDC_PRODUCT_GOVERNANCE must be activated.

Mass Load:

  • Import source data using files from your desktop into the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system
  • Review the initial data quality of the uploaded data
  • Check whether the data can be activated
  • Activate the data in the system

Mass Maintenance:

  • Define scope by selecting all fields to change
  • Select Product records to be updated
  • Apply changes to the selected dataset
  • Validate whether records can be activated in the system based on system customizing
  • Activate and update the Product Master data records

Export Master Data:

  • Select several fields from tables
  • Select all fields from all tables
  • Export Product Master data to Excel or CSV (ZIP file)

Remediation Process:

  • Select Product data to be validated
  • Review items requiring remediation and analyze detailed issue information, including violated rules and Product details
  • Trigger correction processes for single or multiple Product Master records

Business Benefits

  • Optimize data load for product data
  • Ensure superior master data quality for increased business performance
  • Save time when editing multiple master data records

The Master Data Consolidation for Business Partner scope item provides capabilities to load master data from various sources and to detect duplicates during the load process as well as during regular housekeeping activities.

For each of the resulting match groups, the system calculates a best record out of the duplicates in that group using survivorship rules on the master data attributes. These best records can then be used in dedicated analytical or business scenarios.

Optionally, you can import the source file without source system to prevent key mapping generation. This is preferred for the mass creation use case.

We also provide a process template that supports automation. This process contains a derivation step in which derivation scenarios are executed.

  • Identify duplicates and display of a list of all matched records
  • Merge the records based on the specified rules
  • Verify data before activating
  • Activate data in the system

Business Benefits

  • Performs business partner data load with the master data consolidation functionalities
  • Ensures creation of master data records with a high-quality standard
  • Helps to establish a single source of truth of your business partner master data

processes.description:
Material Replenishment with Kanban – External Procurement (1E3)

Overview

The Kanban method for controlling production and material flow is based on the actual stock quantity in production. Material that is required on a regular basis is continually provided in small quantities into production. With Kanban, instead of being pushed through production by higher-level planning, materials are called from the supply source by production at the manufacturing level where they are needed (pull principle). Replenishment or production of a material is only triggered when a higher production level requires the material. This replenishment is triggered directly in production using previously maintained master data.

Kanban replenishment is commonly used in – but not restricted to – repetitive manufacturing environments when a production process requires that the same or similar products are produced over a certain period at a certain rate per period. The products produced always follow the same sequence through the machines and work centers in production. Routings tend to be simple and do not vary much.

Key Process Flow

  • Create and maintain Kanban control cycles

  • Maintain output control for Kanban summarized JIT call

  • Create independent planning and material requirements at plant level

  • Replenish Kanban container with Kanban just-in-time calls and event-driven Kanban

Business Benefits

  • Reduce work in progress

  • Increase supply chain visibility

  • Reduce manufacturing supply chain costs

  • Reduce inventory and assets

  • Improve flexibility and visibility of manufacturing and supply chain processes

processes.description:
Material Requirements Planning (J44)

Overview

This process enables your material requirements planning (MRP) department to automate the procurement planning. The main function of MRP is to guarantee material availability and to avoid delays in order fulfillment. The planning run checks availability of each material and, in case of shortages, creates purchase requisitions, or delivery schedules if a scheduling agreement exists. Remaining shortages are displayed in the MRP app where the material planner can analyze the situation.

Procurement lead time can be longer than the time available to fulfill a demand. For this reason, you must procure the material in advance and cover your demand from stock. This process starts by creating forecast demands that are interpreted as expected customer demand. The MRP schedule runs. The system creates purchase requisitions or scheduling lines that trigger external procurement.

Optionally, you can handle time-dependent stock levels, purchase requisition handover and MRP material exceptions.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage demand forecast as Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs) manually

  • Calculate from consumption data to forecast and forecast to PIRs automatically

  • Monitor and manage material coverage

  • Run materials requirements planning (MRP) for materials with shortages

  • Evaluate the results of the MRP run

  • Display MRP run material issues and key figures

  • Maintain time-dependent stock levels for safety stock or days of supply for replenishment

  • Hand over the purchase requisitions if needed (optional)

  • Detect and resolve MRP material exceptions

Business Benefits

  • Detect shortages quickly

  • Create purchase requisitions or scheduling lines to cover demand automatically

  • Get higher accuracy of purchased quantities

  • Make use of time-dependent safety stock or time-dependent days of supply definition for replenishment

  • Do a hand over for the purchase requisition (optional)

  • Save costs through process automation

  • Detect and resolve MRP material exceptions
processes.name: Material Requirements Planning

processes.description:
Merchandise Allocation (5FL)

Overview

Most retailers must push merchandise to stores to support certain scenarios. This is for various reasons, such as one-off articles, stock reduction in distribution centers, special offer from supplier, end-of-season clearance, and so on.

The push scenario complements the pull scenario realized via consumption-based replenishment. For more information, see the Replenishment Planning for Stores (3I7) scope item . The planning tool for the push scenario is the so-called allocation table. First, the user enters relevant articles, the quantities to be distributed, store groups, and various dates (order date, receiving dates for stores and distributions centers, and optionally, delivery phases). One of several available types of merchandise distribution is then selected, including:

  • Distributions centers procure from an external supplier and distribute merchandise to stores

  • Available stock of distribution centers is distributed to stores

  • Direct store delivery from external suppliers

The quantities for each receiving store are calculated based on different available options (such as ratios or strategies). Once the planning is finalized, the respective orders can be created automatically; the orders are handed over to operational procurement for execution.

Key Process Flow

  • Create an allocation table with details such as articles to be distributed, quantities planned, and the group of receiving stores

  • Create an allocation table with reference to an existing purchase order

  • Change an allocation table to update any item details

  • Create the follow- on documents, such as purchase orders or stock transport orders based on the business process

  • Display an allocation table

  • Delete an allocation table that is no longer needed, or was created by mistake (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by matching location-based inventory with store-specific demand, avoiding over- and under-stocking

  • Reduce revenue loss by allocating merchandise across retail stores based on rules, business strategies, and key performance indicators

  • Increase total logistic costs by automating the creation of all follow-on logistical documents ordering, receiving, and distributing merchandise for push scenarios

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Merchandise Allocation

processes.description:
Merchandise Distribution and Collective Purchase Order (71O)

Overview

Through collective purchase order processing, you can consolidate procurement for stores for efficient processing by an external supplier. Merchandise distribution manages the planned quantities for the stores, makes necessary adjustments, and efficiently executes logistics processes in the distribution center.

This scope item describes merchandise procurement through a pull process. First, you determine the demand for the stores and create the resulting documents as described in the scope item Replenishment Planning for Stores (3I7). If the supply source is a distribution center, you can combine the demand from stores into a collective purchase order for the distribution center at the external supplier.

You can create collective purchase orders either online or by scheduling a batch job run in the background. At the same time, the information for the merchandise distribution is created, and the quantities for the stores along with further data are being recorded.

After receiving the goods in the distribution center, you can adjust the quantities for the stores if the received quantities differ from those in the purchase order. You can adjust the merchandise distribution quantities either through a merchandise distribution monitor or in the background through a batch run. After the adjustment, the system creates and processes outbound deliveries for pickup and posts the goods issue. Finally, the stores receive the merchandise.

In case of automatic adjustment, the quantities are distributed to the stores and outbound deliveries are generated automatically at the time of goods receipt at distribution center.

The distribution center uses putaway, flow-through, and cross-docking methods (using Supplementary Logistics Services (SLS)) to process merchandise distribution.

Key Process Flow

  • Create stock transfer orders for stores

  • Construct collective purchase orders for distribution centers for all the demand from stores

  • Generate collective purchase order with pre-packing information at store or article level and send it to the supplier (optional)

  • Receive goods on purchase orders from external suppliers in the distribution center

  • Adjust merchandise distribution data based on actual goods receipt manually or automatically (optional)

  • Create and process outbound deliveries in the distribution center (applicable only in case of manual adjustment)

  • Receive goods from stock transfer orders in the stores

  • Verify stock data in stores

Business Benefits

  • Increase order management FTE productivity by moving merchandise through the distribution center quickly to fill customer orders and avoid customer service issues

  • Reduce total logistics cost by reducing overall costs for distribution processing and storage

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item can only be activated if you have a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and have activated the retail bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.

Mobile RF Devices in Warehousing (63V)

Overview

This scope item allows you to use mobile RF devices in warehouse processes. There's a set of out-of-the-box transactions available to perform mobile warehouse activities in inbound, internal, and outbound processes such as put away, physical inventory counting and picking. This process activates the necessary configuration to determine queues during warehouse task creation. Based on these queues, the workload can be distributed to multiple resources working in the warehouse. Once you set up the relevant master data, you can assign resource groups to resources and thus control the activity areas of a warehouse where a resource is active. Resource planners can choose to have the system guide them, or manually choose their next warehouse order. Using verification profiles, you can define which verification fields are mandatory and which can be skipped during the scanning process.

Key Process Flow

  • Confirm warehouse task in RF environment

  • Perform physical inventory in RF environment

Business Benefits

  • Perform warehouse operations with a mobile device

  • Ease the management and distribution of work via queues by enabling the execution of work by resources in a radio frequency (RF) and non-RF environment

  • Optimize the selection of warehouse orders for resources requesting work by enabling the effective monitoring and controlling of resources

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

You can request the scope item if you want to use RF functionality in warehousing.

processes.description:
Money Market Mutual Fund Management (2UN)

Overview

The scope item helps you to better manage your Money Market Mutual Fund instruments.

The Money Market Mutual Funds (MMMF) are traditionally traded at a stable 1.00 Currency Unit. An SEC rule in the U.S. for investment companies requires the MMMFs to declare their Net Asset Value (NAV) to be floating on a daily basis. This scope item incorporates the processes to manage both traditional and floating NAV MMMFs.

The scope item covers the processes to create a securities class, and to purchase, bookkeep, and receive dividends of and sale of a money market mutual fund.

Key Process Flow

  • Create security account and class

  • Create fund purchase transaction

  • Set settlement status

  • Create payment to depository bank

  • Recognize dividend distribution

  • Capitalize dividend distribution

  • Perform period-end closing

  • Create fund redemption transaction

  • Receive payment from depository bank

Business Benefits

  • Review the status for Money Market Mutual Fund instruments easily

  • Support the management of Money Market Mutual Fund, including creation of security class, security accounts and the transactions, payments, recognize and capitalize dividend distribution, and so on

  • Make better operational and strategic decisions using the comprehensive reporting and analysis tools

  • Improve internal operational compliance

Monitoring of Goods and Invoice Receipts (2V7)

Overview

The GR/IR monitor is an application in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition that helps the accountants to process the cases where the goods receipts and the invoices receipts are not exactly matched and written off automatically. The processors set the statuses to purchase orders to indicate the next actions that must be taken in the context of certain purchase order. A machine learning feature of the GR/IR application makes a prediction of the next status based on the history of processing. The predictions are provided by a Machine Learning (ML) service that runs on the Cloud Foundry. This communication scenario is related to the connection of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system and the ML service.

Key Process Flow

  • Reconcile GR/IR accounts

  • Monitor GR/IR account reconciliation

  • Use a Situation Handling template for the GR/IR Reconciliation Monitor

Business Benefits

  • Propose status of goods and invoice receipts

  • Propose status dependent on the situation of a purchase order item

  • Reduce efforts in manual checks

  • Integrate with Machine Learning for Monitoring of Goods and Invoice Receipts (2ZS) scope item
