Planning Apps for Sales (1O0)

Overview

For sales and distribution scenarios, this scope item provides key information that a sales manager needs regarding the creation and maintenance of Sales planning apps, effectively handling the different stages in sales planning. The Sales Manager can also select some existing sales plans to compare with actual data. In addition to this, they can navigate to the corresponding app for further analysis.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales plan

  • Update a sales plan

  • Copy sales plan

  • Release and search for a sales plan

  • Compare plan and actual data

  • Navigate to the corresponding apps for further analysis

Business Benefits

  • Flexibility for the sales manager to handle the sales planning effectively

  • Create, manage, update and copy a sales plan to enable easier access to a sales manager

  • Access various sales plans at the click of a link

  • Ability to export master data for the sales managers to use customer or customer group as a dimension

  • Compare the planning data and actual data in the sales plans
processes.name: Planning Apps for Sales

processes.description:
PLM Integration with SAP Integrated Product Development (6U3)

Overview

SAP Integrated Product Development (SAP IPD) delivers comprehensive capabilities and process support for R&D and product development. By activating the required services and APIs within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, you enable seamless communication with SAP IPD services, creating an integrated, end-to-end product development environment.

Key Process Flow

  • Requirements and specification management to ensure design accuracy

  • CAD integration for smooth data exchange between engineering and ERP

  • Collaboration tools to connect engineering, procurement, and production teams

  • Change management for controlled updates across complex product lifecycles

  • Enterprise product structure for managing multi-level BOMs and configurations

  • Advanced recipe and formulation management to optimize product quality, cost, and scalability

  • Product and asset visualization for better decision-making and faster approvals

  • Integration with SAP Ariba for streamlined procurement and sourcing

  • Handover to manufacturing for efficient transition from design to production

Business Benefits

  • For discrete manufacturing, SAP Integrated Product Development streamlines engineering by connecting CAD data, requirements, and Bills of Materials (EBOM, MBOM, routing) directly into ERP workflows. This eliminates manual handovers, ensures design accuracy, and accelerates the design-to-operate cycle.

  • For process industries, SAP Integrated Product Development provides an integrated environment for managing specifications, formulations, and recipes. R&D teams can design, adjust, and optimize formulas with ease, while ensuring smooth transition from development to production.

  • Across both industries, SAP Integrated Product Development enables real-time collaboration with customers, partners, and suppliers, reducing complexity and fostering co-innovation. Automated data synchronization minimizes errors and operational overhead, delivering faster time-to-market, improved product quality, and a unified cloud experience.

This scope item is excluded from default activation.

Only request this scope item if you use an SAP Product Lifecycle Management system and want to integrate this system with your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.
processes.name: PLM Integration with SAP Integrated Product Development

processes.description:
PLM System Integration (6U2)

Overview

PLM system integration for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition enables seamless, bi-directional integration of product-related data and processes between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and an external PLM system. The following PLM systems can be integrated using the PLM system integration add-on:

  • Siemens Teamcenter

  • Dassault 3DEXPERIENCE

  • PTC Windchill

  • Autodesk Vault

The integration provides a solid foundation for scenarios centric to product development and manufacturing.

It is possible to transfer configurable or non-configurable plant-specific information (material master, bill of material, routing) with or without relationship knowledge into the SAP system.

The two systems communicate through a shared meta domain model using REST protocol and JSON for data exchange.

Key Process Flow

Seamless, bi-directional exchange of information between the external PLM system and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition whose broad functional scope supports business scenarios such as Make-to-Stock, Make-to-Order, Configure-to-Order. The capabilities address and include among others:

  • Material Management

  • Product Structures

  • Document Management

  • Change Management

  • Variant Configuration

  • Quality Management

  • Production Engineering & Planning

  • Vendor Part Management

  • Customer Order Exchange

  • Data Federation

  • Visualization

The meta domain model serves as the central coupling point between the PLM system(s) and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Business Benefits

  • Enables integration of the digital product through a process-oriented architecture based on a state-of-the-art technology stack

  • Uses a shared, extensible meta domain model for cross-application data access

  • Employs a reliable and scalable architecture that supports high performance and efficient operation

  • Preconfigured, harmonized processes provide a ready-to-use solution that can be further customized through extended options

This scope item is excluded from default activation.

This scope item involves the integration to third-party software. You can request this scope item if you want to integrate an external PLM system.
processes.name: PLM System Integration

processes.description:
Predictive Accounting for Sales Orders (2FD)

Overview

This scope item provides a more comprehensive overview of all orders and their values for the period regardless of billing status. When a sales order is created, a revenue posting is created in extension ledger 0E.

A report displays all incoming sales orders for a given fiscal period. The Presumed Gross Margin app displays prediction journal entries along with actuals, and allows you to analyze the expected results at the end of a period/quarter.

Key Process Flow

  • Review incoming sales order report

Business Benefits

  • Provides a comprehensive overview of all orders and their values for the period regardless of billing status

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is excluded from the standard activation as this functionality may create high amounts of data volume and impact the performance, depending on the customer's specific business. This scope item should be activated only if the customer wants to implement incoming sales order reporting in predictive accounting.
processes.name: Predictive Accounting for Sales Orders

processes.description:
Predictive Accounting for Service Contract Management (4V7)

Overview

This scope item provides a more comprehensive overview of all service contracts including future postings for recognized, deferred, and accrued revenues resulting from the billing plan and regardless of their billing status. When a service contract is created, revenue postings reflecting the billing plan of a service contract are created in extension ledger 0E.

The Display Line Items – Margin Analysis app displays prediction journal entries along with actuals and allows users to analyze the expected results at period or quarter end.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage service contracts

  • Display line items – margin analysis

  • Run revenue recognition – service documents

  • Display line items – margin analysis

  • Monitor predictive accounting – predictive quality

Business Benefits

  • Forecast revenues from service contracts in future periods

  • Integrate predictive accounting with service management and revenue recognition

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is excluded from the standard activation as this functionality may create high amounts of data volume and impact the performance, depending on the customer's specific business. This scope item should be activated only if the customer wants to implement service contract reporting in predictive accounting.
processes.name: Predictive Accounting for Service Contract Management

processes.description:
Predictive Accounting for Travel and Expense Management (4Q0)

Overview

Use the integration between travel and expense management in SAP Concur and finance in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to forecast the impact of your employees' business trips on the budget planned and allocated to cost centers or projects.

Key Process Flow

  • Create travel request in SAP Concur

  • Create a predictive journal entry automatically in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition including commitment creation (cost center or project budget check, if activated)

  • Create expense reports with reference to the travel request in SAP Concur

  • Post expense reports automatically and reduce commitment

Business Benefits

  • Integrate travel requests between SAP Concur and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Use a deeply integrated travel request process with commitments and automatic budget check functionality

  • Extend the reach of traditional accounting

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is excluded as this functionality can create high amounts of data volume and can impact performance. Only activate this scope item if the customer explicitly wants to implement Commitment Management for travel expenses with Concur Travel & Expense.
processes.name: Predictive Accounting for Travel and Expense Management

processes.description:
Predictive Analytics Model Training – Sales (2YJ)

Overview

With this scope item, you can utilize the embedded predictive analytics functionality in the sales business processes available in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

The scope item provides the following functionalities in different business scenarios:

The Quotation Conversion Rates scenario provides reliable predictions for the sales manager or sales representative to monitor the probability of a sales quotation being converted to a sales order, assisting the sales manager to plan more reliably.

The Sales Performance app allows the sales manager to forecast the achievable sales volumes and develop the sales plans periodically.

With the SAP Fiori app Predicted Delivery Delay, a sales representative can monitor the current delivery performance situation, and instantly recognize the effect of the delivered-as-requested ratio of sales orders, to prevent a critical delay of delivered goods, and thus increase customer satisfaction.

Key Process Flow

  • Train an embedded predictive model from the released predictive scenarios

  • Leverage embedded predictive analytics functionalities

Business Benefits

  • Decrease manual effort for sales planning and deliver more accurate sales forecasts

  • Provide reliable predictions for achievable sales volume

  • Increase customer satisfaction by achieving a better delivery performance

  • Increase working efficiency by providing better insight to sales manager for decision making
processes.name: Predictive Analytics Model Training – Sales

processes.description:
Predictive Analytics Model Training – Supply Chain (20N)

Overview

This scope item allows customers to use the embedded predictive analytics functionality in various supply chain scenarios, including production, manufacturing, inventory management, and logistics execution. It enables users to select parameters for training and activating predictive models. Currently, the following use case leverages embedded predictive modeling:

  • Tracking materials in transit or open stock transport orders that have exceeded the estimated time in transit but haven't had a goods receipt posted by the receiving plant

Key Process Flow

  • Train a predictive model for stock in transit with available data

  • Update the forecasted date column which shows the predicted delivery date based on the embedded predictive model

  • Update to the stock-in-transit process, stock transport order process with predictions

Business Benefits

  • Out of the box predictive model that can be leveraged in the stock in transit app

  • Get a predicted date for the stock in transit based on the delivery data for the customer

  • Adjust time schedule based on empirical data

  • Overall more reliable planning / scheduling of goods in transit process

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

As of SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2608, this scope item is being deprecated and cannot be requested by new customers.
processes.name: Predictive Analytics Model Training – Supply Chain

processes.description:
Predictive Commitments Management (2I3)

Overview

Commitment management is part of the cost monitoring process. Commitment items for projects are triggered by material purchase requisitions and purchase orders and are reduced by various business transactions such as goods receipt. A project cost report shows commitments versus plan and actual costs.

If this scope item is activated and the prerequisite scope item of Project Financial Control (1NT) is performed, the Project Financial Controller can monitor purchase order commitments against plan and actual costs in a report.

If the scope item is activated, and the prerequisite scope item of Overhead Cost Accounting (J54) is performed, the Cost Accountant-Overhead can monitor purchase order commitments by cost center and cost element in a report.

Key Process Flow

  • Monitor projects

Business Benefits

  • Analyze project costs with information on commitments compared with actual and plan costs

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is excluded as this functionality can create high amounts of data volume and can impact performance. Only activate this scope item if the customer explicitly wants to implement Commitment Management.
processes.name: Predictive Commitments Management

processes.description:
Predictive Material and Resource Planning (4B5)

Overview

Predictive Material and Resource Planning (pMRP) enables you to create, schedule, and evaluate pMRP simulations that support you in making informed decisions for your production planning.

You can create and schedule pMRP simulations with your top-level demands and resource constraints. During the simulation creation, the system creates simplified data, based on your forecasted product demand and master data for material- and resource-planning, which is used as reference data in pMRP.

After the creation, you can process and evaluate your simulation. The number of capacity issues and a delivery performance KPI are constantly updated to enable you to compare your simulated changes so that you can assess the impact of changes to your simulation.

Finally, after you decide which simulation best fits your production plan, you can take over the resulting component demand and release it to your operational data as planned independent requirements.

Key Process Flow

  • Create planned independent requirements

  • Schedule pMRP simulation creation

  • Evaluate and process pMRP simulations

  • Check and (if desired) apply changes to planned independent requirements

Business Benefits

  • Simulate MRP runs to evaluate impacts of possible changes to production plans

  • Helps you create optimized production plans by giving the ability to make informed decisions for changes based on the simulations
processes.name: Predictive Material and Resource Planning

processes.description:
Preference Management with SAP Global Trade Services (3JX)

Overview

This scope item integrates SAP Global Trade Services Preference Management with SAP S/4HANA Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Customers can use their existing SAP Global Trade Services installations to manage long-term vendor declarations and the preference determination for static bills of materials.

Key Process Flow

  • Transfer customers, suppliers, and products from SAP S/4HANA Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Global Trade Services

  • Manage long-term vendor declarations

  • Manage preference determination for static bills of materials

Business Benefits

  • Use existing installations of SAP Global Trade Services for handling all global trade scenarios (enhancement with preference management)

  • Leverage an existing investment in SAP Global Trade Services Preference Management for a best-of-breed deployment of an international trade solution

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant if you want to integrate with SAP Global Trade Services for preference management. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Preference Management with SAP Global Trade Services

processes.description:
Preventive Maintenance (BJ2)

Overview

This scope item describes the processes you perform to prevent system breakdowns or breakdowns of other objects that have high repair costs. Such breakdowns result in greater costs due to production downtime. Preventive maintenance support processes to plan the scope and time of maintenance work for inspections, maintenance, and repairs, in advance. The quality of products manufactured is substantially affected by the operational condition of the production plant. There is a requirement for quality assurance to be more cost effective to maintain objects regularly, and in return avoid a more expensive breakdown. You determine the data required for preventive maintenance by using previous data supplied by the system. In addition to internal company aspects for planned maintenance, you should consider external factors due to an increasing number of conditions set by legislative bodies demanding more stringent requirements on planned monitoring and maintenance of objects.

Key Process Flow

Preventive Maintenance – Time Based

  • Oversee maintenance strategies

  • Create general task list

  • Create maintenance plan

  • Schedule maintenance plan

  • Release Maintenance Order for Preparation

  • Review Maintenance Backlog

  • Schedule Maintenance Orders

  • Execute Maintenance Order Operations

  • Post Execute Maintenance Order Operations

  • Technically Complete Maintenance Order

Preventive Maintenance – Performance Based

  • Oversee maintenance strategies

  • Create general task list

  • Create maintenance plan

  • Create measurement document

  • Schedule maintenance plan

  • Release Maintenance order for Preparation

  • Review Maintenance Backlog

  • Schedule Maintenance Orders

  • Execute Maintenance Order Operations

  • Post Execute Maintenance Order Operations

  • Technically Complete Maintenance Order

Business Benefits

  • Plan better by changing from reactive to proactive maintenance

  • Ensure high availability of equipment and therefore better performance and utilization of assets

  • Reduce total maintenance costs by reducing breakdowns

  • Support external requirements, such as manufacturer recommendations, and legal and environmental requirements

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

As of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2602, this scope item is deprecated. For customers seeking similar capabilities, we recommend the successor scope item Proactive Maintenance (4HI).
processes.name: Preventive Maintenance

processes.description:
Privacy Risk Detection with SAP Risk and Assurance Management (3KX)

Overview

With SAP Risk and Assurance Management data protection and privacy controls, SAP establishes effective means to analyze and detect data protection and privacy anomalies in your connected SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

The use of personal information is strictly regulated by various regulations. Privacy risks exist when this type of data is collected and processed. As a supplement to manual governance, this scope item enables the automatic detection of privacy risks for personnel information and relevant documents (such as sales orders), providing insights on regulatory reporting and proactive auditing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create automated procedures

  • Create controls

  • Create work packages

  • Run automated procedures

  • Display automated procedure run result

Business Benefits

  • Automate data protection and privacy risk detection based on legality check for data stored within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition in relation to privacy regulations

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item integrates with SAP Risk and Assurance Management. Additional products requiring licenses do not have SAP Risk and Assurance Management as an option.
processes.name: Privacy Risk Detection with SAP Risk and Assurance Management

processes.description:
Proactive Maintenance (4HI)

Overview

Proactive maintenance allows you to prevent the failure or breakdown of an asset by implementing preventive maintenance and using proactive measures.

You can create a maintenance schedule in the form of a maintenance plan. Maintenance plans include task lists and relevant assets. A task list contains a sequence of tasks that can be planned for resources such as material, service, capacity, and so on. Maintenance planning is carried out based on the performance of an asset or by using time-based strategy or both, which creates maintenance demand. This process supports all the phases of business cycle such as planning, approval, preparation, scheduling, execution, post execution, and completion.

To enable safety instructions, you need to activate the scope item Health and Safety Management (54A).

Key Process Flow

Proactive Maintenance – Time-Based

  • Maintain a maintenance strategy

  • Create a task list

  • Create a maintenance plan

  • Schedule a maintenance plan

  • Release a maintenance order for preparation

  • Review maintenance backlog for readiness

  • Schedule a maintenance order

  • Perform time confirmation of pre- and main order operations

  • Perform time confirmation of post maintenance order operations

  • Complete technically

Proactive Maintenance – Performance-Based

  • Maintain a maintenance strategy

  • Create a task list

  • Create a maintenance plan

  • Create a measurement document

  • Schedule a maintenance plan

  • Release a maintenance order for preparation

  • Review maintenance backlog for readiness

  • Schedule a maintenance order

  • Perform time confirmation of pre- and main order operations

  • Perform time confirmation of post maintenance order operations

  • Complete technically

Business Benefits

  • Ensures high availability and utilization of assets

  • Ensures optimal performance of assets

  • Reduces total maintenance costs by minimizing breakdowns
processes.name: Proactive Maintenance

processes.description:
Process Integration of SAP S/4HANA Finance with Central Finance (88K)

Overview

This scope item establishes an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and Central Finance, enabling you to replicate financial transaction data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to Central Finance. Data replication can be activated at the company code level in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

The integration uses Cloud Integration technologies (SAP Business Connector, Cloud Connector, WebSocket Remote Function Call) and the SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain relevant company codes for Central Payments in Central Finance

  • Activate communication scenario Integration of FI Public Cloud into CFIN (SAP_COM_0B45)

Business Benefits

  • Integrate public cloud systems with Central Finance to unify financial operations and streamline payment processing, cash management, and reconciliations, reducing costs and minimizing errors

  • Automate and standardize data flows to reduce manual effort, speed up financial close, and ensure reliable financial information

  • Improve administrative oversight by monitoring data replication, increasing transparency, detecting issues early, and providing assurance of data integrity and compliance

  • Enhance flexibility and scalability to easily add new business units, processes, or regulatory requirement

  • Support business continuity by integrating historical data and enabling better analysis and forecasting

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item applies only if you intend to integrate SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with Central Finance. For more information on restrictions that apply to this integration, see SAP Note 3752551 .
processes.name: Process Integration of SAP S/4HANA Finance with Central Finance

processes.description:
Procurement for Retail (5FM)

Overview

The typical starting point for operational procurement from external suppliers is the purchase requisitions, which mainly comprise articles, quantities, and dates of the procurement for a site. Purchase requisitions are either generated by the Material Requirements Planning (MRP) process or manually by a requester. The conversion from a purchase requisition to a purchase order can be done manually (if adoptions are necessary) or automatically (applicable for large volumes). Of course, you can also create purchase orders manually. Recipients of the purchase order can be stores or distribution centers.

Purchase order maintenance is rich in functionality. For example, purchase order quantities can be rounded according to different types of rounding rules, with the goal to take advantage of negotiated conditions or to optimize utilization of existing transport capacities. To track status and to mitigate exceptions, various reporting and monitoring capabilities are offered.

Key Process Flow

  • Create purchase orders directly

  • Create purchase order with reference to a purchase requisition

  • Convert the purchase requisition out of the stock/requirements list

  • Convert purchase requisitions to purchase orders automatically

  • Optimize article quantities in a purchase order

  • Display purchase orders

  • Display status data of the purchase order headers

  • Display the purchase order history

  • Create purchase order output messages (print/EDI)

Business Benefits

  • Improve procurement FTE productivity by providing automated purchase order creation from purchase requisitions

  • Improve savings on direct spends by increasing bundling purchase requirements across the organization and increasing buying power

  • Reduce days in inventory by enabling suppliers to prepack merchandise based on individual store demand information and increase warehouse inventory flow

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Procurement for Retail

processes.description:
Procurement for Service Management (3NI)

Overview

The scope item covers the integration of service management with procurement of non-stock materials and external workforce. This facilitates automatic purchase requisition creation against service order line items and corresponding purchase order processing. A message is sent to the service order regarding purchase order creation. The purchasing manager can use a workflow to approve the purchase order. The goods receipt is executed, resulting in subsequent update of costs against the service order line item. The goods receipt against the purchase order sends a message to the service order.

The supplier invoice posting also updates the procurement costs in the confirmation against the service order line item. In case of billing the customer on sales price basis rather than the cost-plus basis, the sales price is copied from the sales condition instead of procurement costs. A workflow can be used to approve parked supplier invoices by the purchaser.

Key Process Flow

Procurement for Service Management (Non-Stock)

  • Check purchase requisitions created against service order line items (optional)

  • Convert purchase requisitions against service order line item into purchase orders

  • Send an automated message to the service order regarding the account assignment

  • Approve purchase order (optional)

  • Perform goods receipt against the purchase order to update the costs against the service order line item

  • Cancel goods receipt, canceling the cost assignment against the service order line item (optional)

  • Create supplier invoice with reference to a purchase order

  • Approve supplier invoice (optional)

  • Post supplier invoice and update the costs in the confirmation against the service order line item for billing to the customer

Procurement for Service Management (External Workforce)

  • Check purchase requisitions (external workforce) created against service order line items (optional)

  • Convert purchase requisitions (external workforce) against service order line item into purchase orders

  • Send an automated message to the service order regarding the account assignment

  • Approve purchase order (optional)

  • Maintain service entry sheet (Optional :procured material can be added into Service entry sheet )

  • Approve service entry sheet

  • Create the goods receipt document and service confirmation automatically against service order line item (based on service entry sheet approval).

  • Create supplier invoice with reference to purchase order (external workforce)

  • Create supplier invoice through evaluated receipt settlement (optional)

  • Post supplier invoice and update the costs in the confirmation against service order line item for billing to the customer

Business Benefits

  • Integrate seamlessly between service management and procurement

  • Use messages sent to the service order to automatically inform about the progress of the Purchase Order (for example, creation, goods receipt, and so on)

  • Experience flexible workflows for purchase order and supplier invoice
processes.name: Procurement for Service Management

processes.description:
Procurement of Direct Materials (J45)

Overview

This purchasing process uses purchase requisitions that are generated either by the Material Requirements Planning (MRP) process or manually by a requester. The conversion from a purchase requisition to a purchase order can either be done manually (in case adoptions are necessary) or automatically (applicable for large volumes). Alternatively, the purchase orders can be generated manually.

The purchase order can be subject to approval before being issued to a supplier. Goods are shipped from the supplier and the goods receipt is created with reference to the corresponding purchase order. Subsequently the invoicing process is triggered. The user can monitor the progress throughout the entire procurement process and can initiate reactive actions if needed.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage purchase requisitions

  • Manage purchase orders

  • Manage goods receipts

  • Manage stock

  • Manage invoices

  • Manage down payments

Business Benefits

  • Streamline procurement processes in an efficient and cost-effective manner

  • Ensure highly automated processes for the procurement of direct materials

  • Reduce manual effort greatly

  • Monitor the procurement progress in real-time

  • Use an analytical list page to monitor purchase order items
processes.name: Procurement of Direct Materials

processes.description:
Procurement of Materials with Variant Configuration (2XU)

Overview

Variant configuration is an important tool in the manufacturing process. Improve your company's product Engineering, Sales, Procurement, and Manufacturing performance with SAP software for integrated variant configuration and classification. Enable your business process to handle highly individualized products in sales, Procurement and Manufacturing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a customer sales order (optionally based on a sales quotation) for a product configured per customer requirement

  • Identify and create a purchase order for required configurable material for the supplier

  • Post goods receipt and invoice for payment to supplier

  • Process delivery and billing to customer

Business Benefits

  • Improve your company's manufacturing and procurement performance with integrated Advanced Variant Configuration covering single-level as well as multi-level configurable materials

  • Enable your business processes to handle highly individualized products in manufacturing and Procurement

  • Leverage the sophisticated algorithms in the performance-optimized rules engine within a state-of-the-art configurator

  • Use dependencies to prevent combinations of options that are not allowed and can be used to select exactly the right components

  • Set pricing according to the configuration
processes.name: Procurement of Materials with Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Procurement of Pipeline Materials (41F)

Overview

The pipeline process begins with the creation of a pipeline info record and is followed by the posting goods issue from the pipeline. The process is closed with the settling of pipeline liabilities.

A pipeline material is a material that flows directly into the production process from a pipeline (for example, oil), from a pipe (for example, tap water), or from another similar source (for example, electricity).

A material from the pipeline is always available; that is, it can be withdrawn from the pipeline at any time and in any quantity.

Key Process Flow

  • Create pipeline info record

  • Post goods issue from pipeline

  • Settle pipeline liabilities

Business Benefits

  • Streamline your pipeline process efficiently and in a cost-effective manner

  • Ensure highly automated process for pipeline materials

  • Reduce manual effort
processes.name: Procurement of Pipeline Materials

processes.description:
Procurement of Production Components – Consumer Products(5W3)

Overview

This scope item outlines the purchasing process in the Consumer Products industry for procuring batch-managed raw materials (for example, coffee beans) and packaging materials (for example, bags, cartons) needed for production (for example, in coffee displays).

The process operates as a procure-to-stock scenario. It uses purchase requisitions generated by the Material Requirements Planning (MRP) process or manually by a requester. You can convert a purchase requisition to a purchase order manually or automatically. Alternatively, the purchase orders can be created manually.

Purchase orders may require approval before being issued to a supplier. Once approved, goods are shipped from the supplier, and the goods receipt is created with reference to the corresponding purchase order.

For some materials, quality inspection activities may be relevant upon goods receipt. For the raw coffee beans, a quality inspection is performed. For packaging material, it isn't necessary in this scope item.

At goods receipt, the material is posted to quality inspection stock, and an inspection lot is created based on an inspection plan. The quality technician records the inspection results by selecting the relevant work center. Based on the results, the quality engineer makes a usage decision, such as accepting or rejecting the material, posting the material to unrestricted stock or blocked stock, or triggering return to the supplier, with the option of posting as a consumed sample.

Key Process Flow

  • Convert purchase requisitions to purchase orders

  • Create purchase order

  • Preview purchase order (optional)

  • Change purchase order (optional)

  • Monitor purchase order items (optional)

  • Execute mass changes to purchase orders (optional)

  • Post goods receipt

  • Preview goods receipt slip and label (optional)

  • Check goods receipt details (optional)

  • Reverse goods receipt (optional)

  • Analyze stock overview (optional)

  • Analyze material document (optional)

  • Manage stock (optional)

  • Create supplier invoice

  • Option A: Create supplier invoice with PO/GR relation

  • Option B: Create supplier invoice with PO/GR relation (with invoice reduction) (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Support an integrated purchasing process based on MRP or manually by a requester

  • Enable quality inspection for purchased material
processes.name: Procurement of Production Components – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Produce and Sell Standard Products – Inventory Management (54U)

Overview

This scope item enables production planning and execution for a serial-number-managed finished good in make-to-stock scenarios, as well as prompt reactions to incoming sales orders (sell from stock).

The process starts with the creation of a demand forecast for finished goods, represented by planned independent requirements (PIRs).

Predictive Material and Resource Planning (pMRP) enables you to create, schedule, and evaluate pMRP simulations with constraints that support you in making informed decisions for your production planning. You can take over the resulting simulated demand and release it to your operational data as planned independent requirements.

Based on PIRs, material requirements planning (MRP) creates a production plan for finished goods and explodes the entire bill of material (BOM). As a result, raw material demand is planned. Production planners can analyze and manually change the planned order-based production plan.

The process of capacity leveling (scheduling) enables production planners to assign orders and operations from the production plan to available timeslots of capacities, letting the planners schedule the best option for their manufacturing.

Raw material demand leads to component demands that trigger procurement scenarios (external procurement via purchase orders and inbound delivery as well as procurement based on scheduling agreements and Kanban). Upon goods receipt, the materials are quality inspected.

Subcontract Purchasing enables you to process Subcontract Purchase Orders, to create outbound deliveries for the components shipped to the subcontractor. With the supply of the finished material, the goods receipt is created. The consumption of the sent components is recorded upon the receipt of the value-added finished material.

The production process itself covers the conversion of planned orders into production orders, order release, material staging and picking, confirmation of order operations, and goods receipt posting.

Raw materials within production can be replenished by Kanban procurement. A semifinished good is produced via a repetitive manufacturing scenario integrated with in-process inspection and Kanban.

Order-based target and actual cost is created, ensuring fully integrated material and value streams. For an additional subassembly, repetitive manufacturing is executed.

The process continues with the creation of a sales order, checking the legal compliance with international trade regulations, performing the delivery with picking and quality inspection at goods issue, invoicing, ending with the clearing after incoming payment. In addition, the Intrastat declaration can be executed.

Key Process Flow

  • Create planned independent requirements

  • Schedule pMRP simulation creation

  • Evaluate and process pMRP simulations

  • Check and (if desired) apply changes to planned independent requirements

  • Process planned independent requirements

  • Perform material requirements planning and evaluation of stock requirement list

  • Perform capacity leveling

  • Procure components including inbound delivery and subcontracting

  • Perform quality inspection in procurement

  • Replenish material with Kanban

  • Handle production order processing: Material staging, order release, order confirmation, material movement postings for goods issue and goods receipt including available-to-promise checks

  • Perform in-process inspection (Quality Management) for repetitive manufacturing

  • Execute purchasing, facilitating direct procurement, and procurement using scheduling agreements

  • Create and confirm sales orders

  • Check compliance with international trade regulations

  • Perform process delivery, quality management, and pick and ship items

  • Post goods issue

  • Execute billing

  • Post incoming and outgoing payments

  • Generate Intrastat declarations

Business Benefits

  • Simulate MRP runs to evaluate impacts of possible changes to production plans

  • Trigger production execution with a production plan

  • Showcase repetitive manufacturing

  • Explode the bill of material automatically when running the material requirements planning

  • Calculate target costs during order creation

  • Streamline subcontracting processes efficiently and cost-effectively

  • Perform availability check and automatically determine a shipping point when an order is entered

  • Perform legal control checks to be compliant with international trade regulations

  • Integrate quality management in outbound delivery processing, procurement, and repetitive manufacturing

  • Create billing document and postings for financials and controlling
processes.name: Produce and Sell Standard Products – Inventory Management

processes.description:
Produce and Sell Standard Products – Warehouse Managed (54V)

Overview

This scope item enables production planning and execution for a finished good in make-to-stock scenarios, as well as prompt reactions to incoming sales orders (sell from stock).

The process starts with the creation of a demand forecast for finished goods represented by planned independent requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, material requirements planning (MRP) creates a production plan for finished goods and explodes the entire bill of material. This planning results in raw material demand. Production planners can analyze and manually change the planned order-based production plan.

Raw material demand leads to component demands that trigger external procurement via purchase orders and inbound delivery.

The semi-finished product is produced via repetitive manufacturing into the warehouse. With the repetitive manufacturing confirmation, semi-finished material is received into the specified warehouse goods receipt bin and raw material is issued from stock. The goods receipt (movement type 131) and the goods issue (movement type 261) are posted synchronously in one material document. In addition, the system automatically generates a warehouse task.

The production process of the finished product via discrete manufacturing includes converting planned orders to production orders, releasing orders, staging and picking materials, confirming order operations, and posting goods receipts. Upon acceptance of quality inspection results, finished product is moved to unrestricted stock.

The process continues with creating sales orders, performing deliveries from the stock present in a warehouse-managed location, invoicing, and clearing after incoming payment.

All products in this scenario use warehouse-managed storage locations. Quality inspection is triggered during goods receipt for production orders.

Key Process Flow

  • Create demand forecast for finished goods represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIR)

  • Run material requirements planning (MRP) and evaluate the results for finished, semi-finished and raw material demands

  • Perform repetitive manufacturing for semi-finished product

  • Purchase raw materials based on material requirements

  • Receive goods from supplier into a warehouse-managed location

  • Execute billing

  • Stage components for finished product to production supply area

  • Perform discrete production process for finished product and quality inspection

  • Perform outbound delivery based on sales orders

  • Receive payment from customer

Business Benefits

  • Trigger production execution with a production plan

  • Use warehouse-managed stock in production and outbound deliveries

  • Trigger production execution with a production plan

  • Explode the bill of material automatically when running the material requirements planning

  • Purchase raw materials from external supplier

  • Create billing document and postings for financials and controlling

  • Integrate quality management in production

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that want to use warehouse management capabilities including storage bin management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Caution:

Caution
Additional organizational entities (for example, storage location, warehouse number, warehouse, and storage types) are activated as part of the warehouse management scope items. Before activation of this scope item, the following scope items must be set in scope and activated:

  • Warehouse Inbound Processing (3BR)

  • Warehouse Outbound Processing (3BS)

  • Warehouse Production Integration (3DV)

  • Warehouse Ad Hoc Goods Issue (3BT)

  • Warehouse Internal Repacking (3BW)

  • Warehouse Goods Receipt from Repetitive Manufacturing (41U)

  • Warehouse Advanced Production Integration (6NI)

  • Quality Management in Discrete Manufacturing (1E1)
processes.name: Produce and Sell Standard Products – Warehouse Managed

processes.description:
Produce to Sell – Process Industry – Consumer Products (830)

Overview

This document describes an integrated end-to-end scenario for the consumer products industry that combines batch-managed production in the process industry, quality assurance through first article inspections, and commercial settlement within a customer hierarchy using condition contracts.

For this, three scope items are combined:

  • Batch Derivation - Consumer Products (77G): The production process in process manufacturing focuses on the batch derivation of key characteristics such as the earliest manufacturing date of component batches for semifinished and finished products.

  • First Article Inspection – Consumer Products (7L4): This embeds the PPAP (production part approval process) in the existing production planning and production process and controls subsequent goods receipts depending on the inspection result of the first article inspection.

  • Condition Contract with Customer Hierarchy - Consumer Products (6V0): The main focus of the sale of the manufactured product to different customers is the subsequent settlement of rebate agreements across the customer hierarchy through three different agreements (condition contracts) for different levels of the customer hierarchy: one agreement for the entire customer hierarchy, a special agreement only for customers on a specific customer hierarchy node, and one agreement for the entire customer hierarchy except the customer hierarchy node with the special agreement.

The process starts with requirement planning for finished goods using PIRs. You use Material Requirements Planning (MRP) to create a plan by exploding the BOM and generating requirements to produce semifinished and finished products, as well as purchasing requirements for externally procured components. Incoming quality assurance is integrated via first article inspection for purchased materials. After you create a purchase order and post the goods receipt, inspection plans are referenced to record inspection results and make a usage decision. If first article inspection is accepted, subsequent purchase orders follow a regular goods receipt inspection. If the first article is rejected, a new purchase order with first article inspection is created. Optional overviews before and after a goods receipt inspection for quality technician and quality engineer support transparency without being mandatory for the core flow.

For two-stage batch derivation, the production process starts by executing a process order for the semifinished material, followed by goods issue of batch-managed components, production confirmation, and goods receipt. The final processing and packaging level is started with a process order for the finished product followed by the confirmation of component consumption, production times, and goods receipt of the finished product. Each goods receipt triggers a batch derivation and updates batch attributes according to the configured strategy. The results can be verified in the derivation monitor, with end-to-end traceability checks available in the Batch Information Cockpit (top-down and bottom-up). Manual derivation is possible but not included in this scope.

The stock produced is used to fulfill demand for the sale from stock. After sales order processing via order creation, delivery, and billing, the business completion is done via condition contract management within the customer hierarchy: condition contract creation, business volume determination based on executed sales, execution of final settlement, and verification of settlement documents to confirm the correct calculation and posting of rewards and rebates.

Key Process Flow

  • Generate anonymous forecast and run MRP

  • Perform first article inspection with QM integration in Production Part Approval Process (PPAP)

  • Accept first article inspection and conduct regular quality inspection for second purchase order

  • Reject first article inspection and trigger new first article inspection for second purchase order

  • Create and process process orders for semi-finished material

  • Create and process process orders for finished material

  • Monitor batch derivation

  • Analyze batches using batch information cockpit (top-down and bottom-up)

  • Execute sell-from-stock process

  • Maintain and settle condition contracts

Business Benefits

  • Tailor available capacities and receipts on time to suit requirement quantities

  • Review created process order easily

  • Ensure sufficient material is present in stock

  • Monitor derivation to control previously performed derivations (receiver batches, attributes and their values, messages)

  • Check specifications of a product before it gets included in the production process

  • Ensure that the production process of a purchased material meets your requirements

  • Run business volume evaluation and settlement based on customer hierarchy

  • Use a setup based on the customer structure
processes.name: Produce to Sell – Process Industry – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Product Change Management with Change Records (64E)

Overview

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, product change management with change records flexibly orchestrates the management of enterprise product changes. It can handle several types of objects that are affected by the intended changes, such as materials, BOMs, master recipes, and documents. The change record keeps all information in one place. The progress of the change is controlled by a dedicated status management, and the change process is supported by workflow capabilities of process routing. Collaboration using comments during the change process allows effective communication with all involved parties.

Key Process Flow

  • Create change record

  • Start workflow

  • Review change request (optional)

  • Assign product masters and bill of materials

  • Assign attachments

  • Approve or reject change record

  • Modify validity date in change master

  • Perform design changes

  • Perform product master changes

  • Perform engineering structure changes

Business Benefits

  • Handle various object types with and without change numbers and model workflows flexibly

  • Gain transparency with visual workflow capability combined with a status-driven change control

  • Improve efficiency with all change information in one easy-to-navigate place

  • Get a single source of truth of all the data involved in a change

  • Drive the change process efficiently through best practices and workflow templates

  • Allow ad-hoc communication with stakeholders

  • Leverage insights from engineering cockpit
processes.name: Product Change Management with Change Records

processes.description:
Product Compliance Document Authoring (7DO)

Overview

Products might pose risks throughout the value chain that many industries handle by creating structured communication documents (often regulated by law). This scope item covers the main process steps for generating product-compliance-relevant documents, using the structure of a safety data sheet as an example.

To create product compliance documents, you may need to gather a large amount of data that must be systematically structured and assessed. To facilitate this, a work view provides you with easy access to both compliance requirements and apps for entering relevant properties. You can efficiently control document output by adapting the template structure to your needs.

Key Process Flow

  • Link a safety data sheet template to the relevant compliance requirement version for safety data sheet management

  • Create a chemical composition for the mixture on the level of an unpackaged product

  • Create identifiers for the product that can be used in documents, such as safety data sheet and labels

  • Use the work view for easy access to relevant apps for managing product’s properties, such as safety-related properties, physical-chemical properties, and toxicological information

  • Use compliance requirements and assessments to enter and update regulatory data, such as GHS classification or hazardous ingredients

  • Generate a base safety data sheet and release the safety data sheet assessment

Business Benefits

  • Mitigate compliance risks by keeping the compliance data up to date

  • Have unified compliance data that enables coherent compliance processes

  • Integrate data from different solution capabilities, such as Dangerous Goods Management and Product Marketability and Chemical Compliance, and print it in one document

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

To enable use of this function, create an incident on component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV to request activation of the SAP_COM_1083 communication scenario.

For more information, refer to SAP Note 2844426 .
processes.name: Product Compliance Document Authoring

processes.description:
Product Cost Breakdown in Plan/Actual Value Flow (7NH)

Overview

This scope item provides a detailed breakdown of production costs and origin costs for a manufactured product with quantity structure:

  • The production cost breakdown explains the cost of goods manufactured (COGM) from the perspective of the manufacturing process including material usage, internal activities, and external activities.

  • The origin cost breakdown is an alternative view of the cost of goods manufactured including original production factors. It allows you to identify the impact of any changes to your primary costs on product profitability, such as increases in energy prices, higher wage costs, or changes in depreciation rules. Without the origin cost breakdown these costs are grouped under activity rates and classified as production activity costs.

The product cost breakdown details product costs and forms the basis for the cost of goods sold (COGS) breakdown in product profitability analysis. ​The cost breakdown structure and its corresponding cost components are defined based on configuration settings, with cost breakdown results generated automatically during the creation of material standard cost estimate and the posting of costs from manufacturing and selling process.

To enable the origin cost breakdown, this scope item must be activated along with the following mandatory prerequisite scope items:

  • Integrated Financial Planning (4RC)

    • Cost Rate Planning and Cost Rate Split activities

  • Import Connection Setup with SAP Analytics Cloud (1YB)

    • Integrate Cost Rate Split with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Key Process Flow

  • Determine cost breakdown (production cost breakdown and origin cost breakdown) for manufactured products

  • Display cost breakdown for manufactured products in material cost estimates

Business Benefits

  • Gain insights into production cost compositions to understand the effect of each cost component

    • Evaluate changes in the ratios between direct or indirect costs, increased raw material expenses, or subcontracting costs

    • Influence decisions for in-house production or outsourced manufacturing

  • Obtain original production factors to see the impact of changes to your primary costs

    • Analyze increases in energy prices, higher wage costs, or changes in depreciation rules

  • Understand product cost components or original cost factors and their deeper impact on product profitability

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The solution delivered in this scope item can be used alongside the existing cost component split solution in scope item BEG.

Currently, scope item 7NH is non-standard as it doesn't cover all planned scope at this time. In the meantime, use scope item BEG for productive usage.

Before you activate this scope item, see SAP note 3544173.
processes.name: Product Cost Breakdown in Plan/Actual Value Flow

processes.description:
Product Cost Related Master Data Changes – Consumer Products (61W)

Overview

This scope item gives you an example of possible handling options for updating standard costs outside of the annual operations planning within a Consumer Products industry process. Updates in standard costs are necessary when unforeseen events influence the material valuation significantly. As examples, the valuation-related changes are based on the following business situations:

  1. A quantity structure change in the Bill of Material (BOM) is needed because of quality problems with a component. A change-master-controlled update of a production BOM is used for the exchange of a production component. The change-number-controlled approach allows a date-effectivity-based attribute management on both the BOM header and BOM items levels. The BOM header and items can only be changed with a new active change number. Setting the change number status to active releases the scope per change number. Once the status becomes inactive, changes are no longer possible.

  2. Significant price change for a raw material.

After the unforeseen valuation-related changes are done, a new off-cycle costing run is created and executed to reflect the changes accordingly in the master data.

Analytics, such as material price analysis and costing run comparison, complete the process.

This scope item can also support parallel standard costing. However, the current test process is to use the costing variant PYC1 based on the related delivered standard settings.

Key Process Flow

  • Check Purchasing Info Record

  • Check Bill of Material

Business Benefits

  • Support updating on standard costs of outside the annual operation planning process

  • Enable update on standard costs in case unforeseen events are influencing the material valuation significantly

  • Update required master data changes

  • Maintain valuation prices independently in up to three currencies or valuations (cloud only)

  • Support group and local currencies in predelivered content

  • Control updates in bill of materials for production centrally with change master
processes.name: Product Cost Related Master Data Changes – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Product Footprint Management (5IM)

Overview

This scope item enables you to integrate product footprints calculated in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management on SAP Business Technology Platform. Product footprints can be either viewed or integrated into end-to-end processes of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Key Process Flow

  • Receive calculated product footprints from SAP Sustainability Footprint Management on SAP Business Technology Platform

  • View product footprints

  • Integrate product footprints into end-to-end processes of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Business Benefits

  • Enable the integration with SAP Sustainability Footprint Management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant if you would like to integrate with SAP Sustainability Footprint Management.
processes.name: Product Footprint Management

processes.description:
Product Taxonomies for Retail (5FJ)

Overview

A merchandise category comprises articles that are similar from a process perspective. Those merchandise categories can then be organized in merchandise category hierarchies to ease the classification of the article master. The huge number of different articles causes several challenges for efficient process execution. To meet these requirements, you can select all articles of one or more merchandise categories for process steps, and furthermore specify controlling parameters at the merchandise category or merchandise hierarchy level (for example, sales price strategies or default distribution centers). This higher data retention level above the article enables a more efficient management of all items that a company procures or produces, stores, and sells. Furthermore, reporting at the article cluster level is typically more tangible and easier to comprehend, including reports on procurement, inventory management and master data.

Key Process Flow

  • Create merchandise categories

  • Maintain reference articles

  • Build up merchandise category hierarchies by assigning merchandise categories to merchandise category hierarchy levels, and merchandise category hierarchy levels to one another

  • Create characteristics and characteristics values for generic articles (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Increase efficiency in article data creation by inheriting characteristics and attributes from merchandise categories hierarchy nodes

  • Increase full-time equivalent (FTE) productivity by reporting merchandising information at article cluster level

  • Improve merchandising FTE productivity by efficiently reclassifying assignments of articles to merchandise categories and merchandise category hierarchy levels

  • Reduce operations costs by managing article or site assignments at merchandise category level

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Product Taxonomies for Retail

processes.description:
Product-Related Carbon Emission Quantities (6VN)

Overview

This process enables you to post and analyze the quantity breakdown of greenhouse gas emissions (in carbon equivalents CO2e) for product-related scenarios. Emission quantities are allocated in alignment with the flow of costs throughout the company's value chain. You can gain insights into quantities of certain greenhouse gas emission scopes connected to financial attributes and values.

This scope item runs only in combination with the following mandatory prerequisite scope items that must be activated:

  • Integrated Financial Planning (4RC)

  • Import Connection Setup with SAP Analytics Cloud (1YB)

  • Product Footprint Management (5IM)

Key Process Flow

  • Retrieve emission quantities from SAP Sustainability Footprint Management for raw materials and trading goods

  • Retrieve emission quantities from Financial Planning in SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) for activity cost rates

  • Consolidate retrieved emission quantities similar to how standard costs for manufactured products are aggregated along the structure of the bill of materials, and routings

  • Display the determined quantity breakdown for greenhouse gas emissions (in carbon equivalents CO2e) of manufactured products based on plan data

Business Benefits

  • Obtain insights into carbon emissions quantities for product-related processes

  • Plan greenhouse gas emission quantities for cost rates of manufacturing activities

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

If you choose this scope item, you must also activate the prerequisite scope item: Product Footprint Management (5IM).
processes.name: Product-Related Carbon Emission Quantities

processes.description:
Production Capacity Evaluation (31L)

Overview

This scope item enables quick capacity evaluation and planning for make-to-stock scenarios in Discrete and Process Manufacturing. You can determine the industry type selection and displayed data in the app settings.

The process starts with the creation of a demand forecast for finished goods represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs). Based on PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) creates a production plan for finished goods and explodes the entire bill of material structure.

As a result, semifinished component production and raw material demand is planned. All orders and operations that are planned with the MRP are allocated to the required capacities. Production planners can evaluate the capacity utilization for a defined time horizon and execute manual changes in orders to resolve upcoming bottleneck situations in the defined area of responsibility.

Key Process Flow

  • Evaluate capacity load

  • Apply changes to available capacity to meet the production requirements

Business Benefits

  • Get overview and transparency of capacity load and critical situations

  • Gain insight into the KPIs on capacity load and backlog

  • View a graphical presentation of utilization per work center/resource
processes.name: Production Capacity Evaluation

processes.description:
Production Capacity Evaluation and Leveling – Consumer Products (5OI)

Overview

This scope item supports production planning and capacity evaluation for a Consumer Products Industry-flavored Make-to-stock process and provides options from prompt reaction. The Consumer Products industry-flavored process describes a two-stage production process for coffee displays. The first stage reflects the roasting and packaging process of medium resp. dark roasted beans under consideration of a fixed capacity of the roasting drums. The second stage reflects a display packaging process where two different finished products (medium and dark roasted coffee beans bags) are packed into a display.

The process starts with the creation of a demand forecast for finished material (display) represented by planned independent requirements (PIRs). You can create the PIRs manually or via upload file. Predictive Material and Resource Planning (pMRP) is used to create, schedule and evaluate pMRP simulations that support you in making informed decisions for your production planning. The results can be taken over and will be released to your operational data as planned independent requirements.

As a result, component production and raw material demand are planned. All orders and operations that are planned with the MRP are allocated to the required capacities. Production planners can evaluate the capacity utilization for a defined time horizon and execute manual changes in orders to resolve upcoming bottleneck situations in the defined area of responsibility.

The process of production capacity leveling represents a central part of preparation for the manufacturing process of components. Production planners can assign orders and operations from the production plan to available timeslots of capacities. Additionally, the planners can simulate and choose other alternatives for production by assigning other available production versions, letting the planners schedule the best option for their manufacturing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create Initial Material Stock

  • Check Available Capacity in Work Center

  • Check Formulas in Work Center

  • Check Routings

  • Check Production Version

  • Create Work Center Group

Business Benefits

  • Get quick capacity planning and planning

  • Cover a central part of preparation of the manufacturing process of components

  • Allocate orders and operations with MRP properly
processes.name: Production Capacity Evaluation and Leveling – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Production Capacity Leveling (3LQ)

Overview

This scope item supports both Discrete and Process Manufacturing capacity leveling functionality for their demands. You can determine the industry type and displayed data under the app settings. The process of production capacity leveling represents a central part of preparation for the manufacturing process of components.

After you forecast a demand for finished goods represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIR) and the Material Requirements Planning (MRP) run created a production plan, the process of capacity leveling (scheduling) takes place.

This process enables production planners to assign orders and operations from the production plan to available timeslots of capacities. Additionally, the planners can simulate and choose other alternatives for production by assigning other available production versions, letting the planners schedule the best option for their manufacturing.

Key Process Flow

  • Dispatch production order or process order

  • Change production version

Business Benefits

  • Dispatch orders to available time slots of work centers or resources

  • Redispatch to alternative production versions
processes.name: Production Capacity Leveling

processes.description:
Production Operations with Manufacturing Execution System (1Y5)

Overview

This scope item covers the setup of the integration from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES).

An MES integrates business and manufacturing processes that help to run efficient, high quality production on the shop floor.

You can use this scope item as an example of how to integrate a local customer shop floor system directly into SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, giving manufacturing staff a clear overview of production operations and improving analytical capability for the management team. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is the system of record for all master data. An MES or a shop floor system is the system of record for all work in progress (WIP) data.

This communication scenario provides end points (inbound and outbound), which are needed to integrate an on-premise third-party MES solution (Manufacturing Execution System) to production operation through ALE IDocs, BAPI, and OData calls.

Key Process Flow

  • Create, schedule, and release production order in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system

  • Create and release production order in a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) or shop floor system

  • Update production order in an MES and send information back to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system

  • Confirm production order in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Editionsystem

Business Benefits

  • Simplifies the integration of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition of Manufacturing Execution Systems to Production Operation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

In exceptional cases, SAP allows temporary use of BAPIs and IDocs based on individual customer requests to integrate the solution when currently available OData and SOAP WebServices are insufficient. This permission is limited to individual customers and a well-defined set of BAPIs and IDocs technically enabled by SAP. To get this approval, customers must follow the process described in SAP Note 2653671. These BAPIs and IDocs are available as is and won't be functionally extended. They will be maintained for a limited period. Maintenance of a BAPI/IDoc will end 12 months after availability of an equivalent OData or SOAP WebService.
processes.name: Production Operations with Manufacturing Execution System

processes.description:
Production Order Combination (7TO)

Overview

This scope item enables a production order combination scenario for make-to-stock and make-to-order production orders for customers who want to reduce production costs and increase production efficiency.

The process starts with identifying production orders that are still in a created status and can be combined based on criteria (such as Material, Material Attributes, Production Plant) and combining them to create a combined production order, which takes over the execution of operations with the necessary consolidated components from the underlying production orders.

Combined orders can be released for production with their combined operations from their underlying original orders also released. Combined operations from the combined order can be confirmed. When the last combined operation is confirmed, the underlying original orders are also confirmed with the distributed yield quantity. Components for combined order are consumed in the goods issue, and the goods receipt then always happens for the receiving original orders.

Key Process Flow

  • Create and execute combined production orders in Make-to-Stock and Make-to-Order scenarios

Business Benefits

  • Streamline Production Orders: Consolidate common operation sequences across multiple production orders into a single production order - reducing complexity and boosting efficiency

  • Lower Operational Costs: Eliminate redundant setup, teardown, and labor activities through smart bundling - cutting waste and driving down per-unit production costs

  • Maximize Machine Throughput": Achieve higher output without additional equipment scheduling and utilizing existing machinery to its full potential

  • Reduce Energy Consumption: Minimize energy usage by grouping heat-intensive processes, enabling more sustainable and cost-effective manufacturing

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

The production order combination feature is valuable in industrial sectors where similar operations are repeated across multiple products, allowing for bundling and optimization. This feature is typically beneficial in the manufacturing industries sector such as steel, textile, paper, plastics, and industrial machinery and components. This functionality is not needed for every manufacturing company.
processes.name: Production Order Combination

processes.description:
Production Order Processing with Third-Party Warehouse Management (2RU)

Overview

The scope item covers production processes. The business part of the processes, including creation and confirmation of production or process orders, is performed in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. The decentralized third-party warehouse management system runs processes required for the physical and logical goods movements. The two variants of the process include material staging to ensure that all needed components or raw materials are available for production, and the goods receipt of the finished goods after production confirmation. The first variant is without automatic backflush of the components and with the assumption that all involved storage locations are managed by third-party warehouse management solution. The other variant works with automatic backflush and the assumption of a centrally managed production storage.

Key Process Flow

Production order processing for semifinished products without automatic backflush of components – all storage locations managed by third-party WMS

  • Create and release production order

  • Stage materials

  • Execute on delivery in third-party WMS

  • Pick components for production

  • Confirm production order

  • Execute goods receipt in third-party WMS

Production order processing for semifinished products with automatic backflush of components – production storage location is managed centrally

  • Create and release production order

  • Stage materials

  • Execute on delivery in third-party WMS

  • Confirm production order

  • Execute goods receipt in third-party WMS

Process order processing for semifinished product without automatic backflush of components – and all storage locations managed by third-party WMS

  • Create process order

  • Pick components for process order

  • Check web services message and execute on delivery in WMS

  • Confirm process order for semifinished product

  • Posting goods receipt for process order

  • Check web services message and execute on delivery in WMS

  • Check stock information

Business Benefits

  • Integrate third-party warehouse management systems to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with asynchronous SOAP APIs

  • Assist with sample processes and related communication arrangements

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant if you want to integrate with third-party warehouse management systems to cover production processes. The scope item Logistics with Third-Party Warehouse Management (‏1ZQ‏) is a prerequisite to 2RU. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Production Order Processing with Third-Party Warehouse Management

processes.description:
Production Subcontracting – External Processing (BJK)

Overview

This scope item demonstrates the option to execute an operation externally within a production order, which is crucial when in-house capacity is limited. When a planned order for production is converted to a production order during the manufacturing process, the system checks for routing or work center operations that require external processing. When the order is processed and the operation to be handled externally is reached, the system creates a purchase requisition. After generating a purchase order for the operation, the production step is processed by the external subcontractor. The external service is captured with a goods receipt posting. The process is finalized by receiving the subcontractor’s invoice for the service and posting the payment accordingly.

Key Process Flow

  • Create production order with subcontract operation

  • Create purchase order for external processing of services

  • Post goods receipt for subcontracted services

  • Enter incoming vendor invoice and process payment

Business Benefits

  • Certain operations of the production order can be specified for execution by an external subcontractor

  • Assign assembly procedure of finished products to a subcontractor if there are capacity bottlenecks
processes.name: Production Subcontracting – External Processing

processes.description:
Products for Retail (3I1)

Overview
