The article is the central object for a retailer, touching all steps of the supply chain, starting with the procurement from an external supplier, to distribution center handling, through selling in the store to customers. To support all these processes, data at various levels is needed, including basic data (different units of measure with dimensions and Global Trade Item Numbers (GTIN), description in multiple languages, validity periods, and so on), purchasing data for external suppliers, sales data, point-of-sale data, and logistics data for distribution centers and stores. A sophisticated referencing and defaulting mechanism allows for efficient data maintenance for all relevant levels via the integrated article maintenance. Furthermore, mass processing can maintain article master data for sets of articles. Integration scenarios are available that allow the import of article master data and the distribution to satellite solutions. In addition to the single article, there are special article categories, such as:

  • Generic article: an abstract header article. Generic articles have variants (sold to the consumer) that only differ from one another in certain characteristics values (such as colors or sizes) but typically are identical in most other data

  • Structured article: comprised of several components, structured via a bill of material

  • Sales set: a set of several articles that are bought individually by the retailer and sold together to the consumer (for example, a shirt with a matching tie)

  • Displays: a set of articles that are bought together and sold individually, including special for presentation in the store

Key Process Flow

  • Create articles with the basic data and merchandise category assignment

  • Maintain further article segment views, such as for distribution chains, or site logistics data

  • Replicate article master data (optional)

  • Perform mass maintenance of multiple articles at a time (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Reduce data management costs by improving master data management, quality, and integration functions with reference handling

  • Reduce procurement costs by providing standardized article identification numbers

  • Reduce time to market for new articles by centralizing creation of consistent, correct, and complete material master data

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Products for Retail

processes.description:
Project Billing – Project-Based Services (4E9)

Overview

This scope item realizes the standard way to bill customer projects in project-based services. It supports the billing on a fixed price, time and expense, periodic service, and usage-based basis. Additionally, it includes on-account and down payments for time and expense contracts and down payments for fixed price contracts. One of the major functionalities is the write off and postponement of recorded amounts or quantities in the time and expense scenario. Additionally, an approval workflow for project billing requests can be enabled in various ways.

Key Process Flow

  • Create, edit, and manage project billing requests

  • Create billing document requests

Business Benefits

  • Reduce time to bill for a project billing manager or billing team

  • Report and track different financial values that are relevant for billing

  • Write off or postpone the recorded amounts or quantities

  • Enable flexible material determination so that new activity types and materials can be defined
processes.name: Project Billing – Project-Based Services

processes.description:
Project Control – Capital Projects (35F)

Overview

This scenario helps you to manage and control the enterprise wide project related investments. Starting with project creation, it covers project structuring, budgeting, execution, and monitoring, enabling transparency to all project stakeholders. This helps to reduce the risk of budget overruns and project delays.

Special functions can be used for investment projects. Investment projects are used to capture the costs of assets under construction (AuC) during the construction phase. Once the AuC is complete, the final asset is created in the appropriate asset class, and the investment project is set to complete. The next settlement transfers the AuC asset value to the completed asset.

Key Process Flow

  • Predict and capture project costs

  • Assign budget

  • Review milestones

  • Record time, requisitioning, procure services, and post general journal entries

  • Monitor projects

  • Settle assets under creation

  • Technically complete project

  • Create fixed asset and run the final settlement

Business Benefits

  • Capture planned project costs and allocate budget

  • Leverage machine learning for project costs forecast

  • Integrate to Asset Accounting

  • Gain more transparency into key financial data across projects using advanced graphical reporting options

  • Assign accounts to documents in financials and procurement or external applications to capture actual costs

  • Monitor project-related purchase requisitions and purchase orders

  • Receive live insight into project costs by comparing plan and actual costs as well as commitments
processes.name: Project Control – Capital Projects

processes.description:
Project Control – Finance (1NT)

Overview

For many purposes, companies run projects to plan and coordinate the work, staff employees, and track project progress and costs. In this scenario, a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) as an accounting structure is created. Planned project costs (uploaded by the project financial controller) can be captured in SAP Analytics Cloud. After releasing all or part of the project, the project is executed. Time can be recorded, and project-related purchasing can be performed. In finance, allocations or general journal entries can be done with regard to project WBS elements. The project financial controller monitors the project costs through overview pages and detailed project reporting. At period end, depending on the type of project, different period-end closing activities such as overhead application or settlement can be executed for a project. Afterwards, the financial controller completes and closes project parts and then closes the complete project.

Key Process Flow

  • Create project

  • Predict and capture project costs

  • Capture project budget (optional)

  • Perform direct activity allocation

  • Post general journal entry

  • Perform requisitioning and service procurement

  • Record time

  • Monitor project

Business Benefits

  • Create and maintain simple project up to highly complex hierarchical projects

  • Select different project profiles

  • Capture planned project costs and allocate budget

  • Assign accounts of documents in financials and procurement or external applications to capture actual costs

  • Monitor project-related purchase requisitions and purchase orders

  • Receive live insight into project costs by comparing plan and actual costs as well as commitments

  • Settle project costs to cost centers, G/L accounts, or asset accounting
processes.name: Project Control – Finance

processes.description:
Project Control – Intercompany (4AU)

Overview

A company has an affiliate company that delivers a service to the ordering company during a project. The affiliate company posts expenses and records time on the project. These expenses are transformed into billing document requests. The delivering company creates an intercompany invoice that references billing document request. The intercompany invoice is also posted automatically to the accounts payables of the ordering company.

Note:

The intercompany process described here is sample data. In this case, the ordering company is DE, and the delivering company is US. The scenario is restricted to one direction: US delivers services for DE.

If you want to apply intercompany for other countries, adapt country-specific data as mentioned in scope item Intercompany Billing for Cross-Company Cost Accounting Postings (4AN).

Key Process Flow

  • Create/release EPPM project

  • Post intercompany expenses

  • Post intercompany time recording

  • Maintain intercompany sales order

  • Generate intercompany billing

Business Benefits

  • Automate the intercompany process in EPPM projects

  • Perform margin analysis

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

To execute intercompany processes in EPPM projects, you must add some configuration before you can run the process. Some of them are:

Maintain business partners against which you would like to post intercompany invoice

Maintain tax codes and G/L accounts

Maintain clearing accounts

Maintain the company codes

For complete setup, execute the setup guide provided in the Intercompany Billing for Cross-Company Cost Accounting Postings (4AN) scope item.
processes.name: Project Control – Intercompany

processes.description:
Project Control – Research and Development Projects (35E)

Overview

This scenario describes a project where the research and development activities related to the design of a new product are managed. Therefore, it supports the product development process by managing the related project costs, milestones, budgets, and approvals. After releasing all or part of the project, the project is executed and project-related purchasing can be performed. Through the integration with SAP Intelligent Product Design, you can leverage advanced collaboration scenarios for project execution. Period-end closing activities such as overhead application or settlement can then be executed.

Key Process Flow

  • Predict and capture project costs

  • Assign project budget

  • Approve milestones

  • Collaborate on product design

  • Perform time recording, requisitioning, and posting of general journal entries

  • Monitor project

  • Allocate overheads

  • Complete and close the project

Business Benefits

  • Capture planned project costs and allocate budget

  • Leverage machine learning for project costs forecast

  • Assign accounts to documents in financials and procurement or external applications to capture actual costs

  • Monitor project-related purchase requisitions and purchase orders

  • Receive live insight into project costs by comparing plan and actual costs as well as commitments

  • Integrate to Product Lifecycle Management objects for product engineering
processes.name: Project Control – Research and Development Projects

processes.description:
Project Control – Resourcing and Procurement (4RF)

Overview

A successful project execution requires that the right resources, services, and materials are available. With this scope item, project demands can be used to manage that, beginning from early planning stages, when some details are not yet known. You can then assign people to project demands to fill their timesheet, or trigger and monitor the procurement of services and materials.

Key Process Flow

  • Define demand of projects and WBS elements

  • Request demand

  • Assign resources

  • Monitor time confirmation and procurement

Business Benefits

  • Use a single application to define project requirement for resources, services and materials

  • Perform early project demand planning without needing to maintain all details immediately

  • Trigger and monitor procurement out of projects

  • Prefill the timesheet of involved resources

  • Support the alignment of dates and other attributes between projects and procurement
processes.name: Project Control – Resourcing and Procurement

processes.description:
Project Control – Sales (4I9)

Overview

As a core ERP functionality, project integration with sales orders enables the direct flow of revenues to the project. The margin can be easily analyzed along with the incurred costs. This scenario covers the fixed-price project billing with the possibility of a down-payment and billing plan. Using the Projects with Revenue profile, the user can create a hierarchy as an accounting structure, set up billing elements, and plan costs and revenues. As soon as the project is released, actual costs and revenues are captured, allowing the project profitability to be analyzed. At the same time, the revenue is recognized with each cost posting. At the period end, no settlement run is necessary as the postings already have the CO-PA characteristics maintained in the settlement rule or derived from the sales order.

Key Process Flow

  • Create project with Projects with Revenue profile

  • Create sales order items with billing work package as account assignment

  • Create a billing plan with down payment

  • Create delivery, execute picking and post goods issue

  • Process billing

  • Monitor the project profitability and recognized revenue

Business Benefits

  • Support fixed-price billing, down payment, and free-of-charge processes

  • Get actual revenue postings driven by sales order processing

  • Get real-time availability of revenue recognition data and profitability

  • Save manual effort for revenue recognition postings

  • Support more complex hierarchical project accounting scenarios through enablement of multiple billing elements within a project
processes.name: Project Control – Sales

processes.description:
Project Data Replication to Central Finance (3W1)

Overview

This scope item enables the setup of an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and Central Finance in SAP S/4HANA to replicate the project accounting structure data. SOAP message-based communication and SAP Cloud Connector are used as integration technology.

Key Process Flow

  • Activate the communication scenario SAP_COM_0470 to replicate subsidiary project accounting structure data

Business Benefits

  • Integrate subsidiary project accounting structure data to corporate central finance system automatically

  • Consolidate financial and management reporting Central Finance including subsidiaries running SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is needed for project integration with Central Finance in SAP S/4HANA.
processes.name: Project Data Replication to Central Finance

processes.description:
Project Review (1YF)

Overview

This scope item helps you to determine the right projects to work on by keeping all project stakeholders (such as the steering committee) informed, enabling the review and approval of project milestones, and accelerating central project review or ranking meetings.

Using the project brief (a condensed, changeable, and integrated project plan with key information such as status, milestones, costs, and contacts), you can provide a low-level entry point and common discussion basis for decision makers. The Project Ranking provides a common, integrated frame to collect all required information and organize the process of central project review.

This scope item provides two examples:

Companies where project milestones are locally reviewed and approved when a milestone is upcoming (starting with the Monitor upcoming milestone process step).

Companies where projects and/or project milestones are reviewed and approved centrally during regular review meetings (starting with the Setup central review process step).

Key Process Flow

  • Inform project manager

  • Describe project

  • Review project milestones

  • Conduct central project review

Business Benefits

  • Enable preparation and execution of milestone approvals or central review or rankings

  • Provide overview pages for project managers and steering committee members, highlighting where to act (for example, because of cost overruns)

  • Give project managers and steering committee members direct access to the financial information of their internal projects

  • Grant project specification authorizations (people can access only the projects where they are involved)
processes.name: Project Review

processes.description:
Provisioning of Overdue Receivables (2PD)

Overview

Due to the new impairment model of IFRS 9, Expected Credit Losses (ECL) on Trade Receivables are calculated using a provision matrix, where fixed provision rates apply depending on the number of days that trade receivable is outstanding. For the calculation of the provisioned amounts, you can periodically perform a valuation run to calculate the bad debt expense posting for overdue items. If you agree with the proposal of the valuation run, you can transfer the valuation to the general ledger to generate the postings. The system makes the adjustment posting for the relevant key date and reversal postings for the date after the key date.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain customer-specific provision matrix via configuration activities

  • Use a valuation program for the flat-rate value adjustment that works like the payment and dunning run

  • Define each valuation run explicitly through the execution day and an identification

  • Specify the execution type of the valuation by defining various parameters

  • Improve efficiency through reuse of parameters from existing valuation runs

  • Analyze defined accounts through the valuation run and create valuations in a proposal run

  • Create the posting in G/L accounting during the transfer and save the valuations for each line item

  • Make reversal postings for the day after the relevant key day

Business Benefits

  • Meet the legal requirements

  • Automate the valuation process of trade receivables and reduce cost by less manual effort
processes.name: Provisioning of Overdue Receivables

processes.description:
Purchase Contract (BMD)

Overview

Quantity contracts are agreements for a company to order a certain quantity of a product during a specified period. In source determination, contracts replace the purchasing information records and can be assigned in the source list as the fixed source for MRP.

Target groups are purchasing managers as well as buyers. If purchase requisitions and purchase orders do not yet exist, they are created after the contract. You can check the released purchase orders that are referenced to a contract by monitoring the contract.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a purchase contract

  • Make mass changes to purchase contracts

  • Approve purchase contract

  • Monitor notification (optional)

  • Manage source lists

  • Create a purchase requisition

  • Assign requisition and creating purchase order

  • Find purchase documents by requirement tracking number

  • Approve purchase orders

  • Monitor contract item (optional)

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create supplier invoice

Business Benefits

  • Reduce procurement costs

  • Secure supplies

  • Maintain transparency of supplier agreements
processes.name: Purchase Contract

processes.description:
Purchase Order Accruals (2VB)

Overview

Accruals must be posted when liabilities are incurred by a third party and related costs are not yet posted. This solution supports the typical period-end closing activity – accruals postings with the reference to purchase orders. You can also choose to activate the deferrals solution in Purchase Order Accruals to let accruals and deferrals for a purchase order seamlessly work together with automation.

Based on the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition accrual engine, this solution offers flexible configuration options for calculating and posting the purchase order accruals. It also provides the option to review the monthly accrual amounts and supports monitoring and the approval of accruals.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage workflows for purchase order accruals review

  • Transfer purchase orders (optional)

  • Propose periodic accruals

  • Review purchase order accruals using My Inbox

  • Review purchase order accruals for cost accountant

  • Post periodic accruals

  • Analyze accrual postings

Business Benefits

  • Get comprehensive automation of process chains for purchase order accruals

  • Reduce efforts in manual work

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item automatically generates month-end accrual postings for purchase orders for expenses. If you activate this scope item, the system replicates the corresponding purchase orders as accrual objects. If the customer doesn't have this type of business need, this replication generates useless data (for example, accrual objects data).
processes.name: Purchase Order Accruals

processes.description:
Purchasing Rebate Processing (2R7)

Overview

This scope item covers the subsequent settlement of rebate conditions agreed on with suppliers. You use condition contracts to enter the rebate conditions, together with the process control parameters, business volume selection criteria, and settlement dates for partial and final settlement.

To claim rebate payments from suppliers, you create settlement documents. Supplier invoices or material documents of goods receipt postings are used to determine business volume.

If rebates lower costs, you perform a goods-related settlement as an account payable to create a credit memo with the supplier as the payer. If a rebate agreement reflects a service rendered for the supplier, you perform settlement as an account receivable to create an invoice for the supplier.

Settlement documents are usually immediately released to accounting. You can also create a two-step condition contract to collect and post settlement documents of different condition contracts in one journal entry to accounting.

Key Process Flow

  • Create condition contract for a supplier as business partner

  • Release the condition contract (optional)

  • Run the procurement process parallel to the condition contract lifecycle

  • Check business volume (optional)

  • Post accruals (optional)

  • Run partial settlement with reversal of accruals (optional)

  • Run final settlement with reversal of accruals

  • Release the settlement of the condition contract (optional)

  • Release the settlement document of the condition contract to accounting (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Manage purchasing rebate agreements centrally

  • Create different types of purchasing rebate agreements according to your business needs

  • Settle purchasing rebate agreements automatically

  • Provide enhanced transparency and flexibility along the whole condition contract lifecycle

  • Process purchasing rebate consistently with the procurement process
processes.name: Purchasing Rebate Processing

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item describes the management of complaints against suppliers, for example, after delivery of a product.

Leveraging quality notifications, the quality engineer captures all complaint-related information including the observed defects. The quality engineer enters immediate actions for documentation purposes and requests a root cause analysis from the supplier. Furthermore, the quality engineer can keep a record of his communication with the supplier.

Leveraging the new nonconformance management business object “Complaint against Supplier”, the quality engineer records the complaint basic data, maintains the involved roles, assigns existing defects, and initiates logistical follow-up actions such as the creation of a returns purchase order — directly within the process flow. The system facilitates seamless communication with the supplier by generating a detailed complaint report to request formal feedback. Finally, the quality engineer reviews the findings, monitors the status of the complaint, and completes the process, ensuring full transparency from initial defect identification to final resolution.

The quality engineer defines tasks either globally at notification level or per defect. The quality engineer assigns one processor to each task. The task is processed, and task processors give feedback per task. After having received the supplier's root cause analysis, identified root causes can be assigned to each defect.

Finally, the quality engineer reviews each task and closes the notification.

Key Process Flow

  • QM Notification

    • Create a quality notification with basic data
    • Capture defects and document immediate actions
    • Define tasks
    • Execute tasks and document outcome
    • Review tasks
    • Document supplier root cause analysis
    • Complete notification

  • QM Complaint Processing

    • Create a complaint against supplier
    • Assign defects
    • Generate a complaint report
    • Process follow-up actions
    • Review and complete the complaint

Business Benefits

  • Capture complaint details, related defects, causes, and activities in one single place
  • Manage different types of activities (for example immediate, corrective, and preventive actions)
  • Assign a person responsible to each action and track action status and outcome

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Quality Management for Complaints Against Suppliers

processes.description:
Quality Management for Complaints from Customers (2FA)

Overview

This scope item describes the management of customer complaints, for example, after delivery of a product. Using quality notifications, the quality engineer can capture all complaint-related information provided by the customer. The quality engineer enriches the notification by adding internal logistical information, such as delivery and purchase documents. Further immediate actions can be captured for documentation purposes. To identify the complaint's root cause, the engineer documents a root cause analysis. After having identified the error and the related root cause, the quality engineer classifies this information using code groups, codes, and free text information.

The quality engineer defines corrective and preventive actions either globally at notification level or per defect. The engineer assigns one processor to each action. The action is processed, and action processors give feedback per action.

Finally, the quality engineer reviews each action and closes the notification.

Key Process Flow

  • Create quality notification with basic data

  • Capture defects, define root cause analysis, and document immediate actions

  • Define corrective actions and correction tasks

  • Execute root cause analysis, corrective actions, correction tasks, and document outcome

  • Review root cause analysis and document root cause, review corrective actions, and review correction tasks

  • Define preventive actions

  • Execute preventive actions and document outcome

  • Review preventive actions

  • Complete quality notification

Business Benefits

  • Capture complaint details, related defects, causes, and activities in one place

  • Manage different types of activities (for example immediate, corrective, and preventive actions)

  • Assign a person responsible to each action and track action status and outcome
processes.name: Quality Management for Complaints from Customers

processes.description:
Quality Management in Discrete and Process Manufacturing (1E1)

Overview

This scope item manages quality inspection in discrete and process manufacturing processes. Quality inspection activities are relevant during the production process or at goods receipt from production: At goods receipt, the material is posted to quality inspection stock and an inspection lot is created based on an inspection plan. The quality technician records the inspection results and the quality engineer makes a usage decision (acceptance or rejection of the material) and posts the material to unrestricted or blocked stock or to scrap. During the production process, a quality operation within the production order or process order triggers the quality inspection. The quality technician records the inspection results for inspection points. Based on the inspection point valuation, the quality operation is confirmed with the respective yield and scrap amounts and the inspection lot is closed by making a usage decision. In case of rejected characteristics, a defect is automatically recorded.

Key Process Flow

Quality Inspection for Goods Receipt from Production:

  • Produce material

  • Display inspection plan

  • Post goods receipt for production order

  • Display material stock before inspection

  • Display inspection lot

  • Record inspection results

  • Make usage decision

  • Review and analyze defects

  • Review material stock after inspection

Quality Inspection Within the Production Process:

  • Start production of material using a production order

  • Display routing including quality operation

  • Display inspection lot

  • Analyze and activate control chart

  • Record inspection results

  • Review and analyze defects

  • Confirm the quality operation of the production order

  • Make usage decision

Quality Inspection Within the Production Process – Make-to-Stock Production of a Batch Managed Material:

  • Create and release production order

  • Perform goods issue of batch-managed components via pick-list

  • Confirm production operations

  • Execute quality inspection with inspection points

  • Confirm production operations

  • Post goods receipt for order

  • Make usage decision

  • Review batch data

Business Benefits

  • Integrate quality inspection activities in production processes

  • Use inspection plans or inspection points for quality inspections

  • Use the statistical process control tool control chart for valuation of inspection characteristics

  • Detect nonconformities during production to avoid cost-intensive reprocessing or unnecessary waste
processes.name: Quality Management in Discrete and Process Manufacturing

processes.description:
Quality Management in Discrete Manufacturing – Consumer Products (5HK)

Overview

This scope item outlines a Consumer Products Industry-flavored production process that fully integrates Quality Management into discrete Manufacturing. It operates as a Make-to-stock scenario for batch-managed goods, incorporating QM for In-Process Control and early goods receipt inspection.

The Consumer Industry process involves a two-stage production process for coffee displays. The first stage covers the roasting and packaging of medium respective dark roasted beans, considering the fixed capacity of the roasting drums. During the roasting, cooling and packaging steps, quality inspection continuously monitors the process. During roasting, the temperature, browning of the beans and other parameters are constantly checked by QM until all parameters are fulfilled.

Moreover, the early goods receipt inspection functionality handles the End-Product Control of unpacked, semifinished products as flexibly as possible. This means users can start end-product control during the production process or after receiving goods into quality stock.

The second stage involves a display packaging process where two different semifinished products, such as bags of medium and dark roasted coffee beans, are packed into a display carton. In this step, a quality inspection is set up after receiving goods from production into quality inspection stock.

The process begins with creating a demand forecast for finished goods, represented by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs). You can create these PIRs manually or by using an upload file. Based on the PIRs, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) generates a production plan for finished goods and breaks down the entire bill of material structure. This results in the planning of semifinished component production and raw material demands. Production planners can analyze and manually adjust the planned orders according to the production plan. Raw material demands lead to purchase requisitions, which trigger alternative procurement scenarios referenced in this scope item.

The production process includes converting planned orders to production orders, order release, material staging and picking, confirming order operations or complete orders, and posting goods receipts. Order-based targets and actual costs are created to ensure fully integrated material and value streams.

Key Process Flow

  • Run anonymous forecast and material requirements planning (MRP)

  • Convert production orders and perform available-to-promise checks for semifinished materials

  • Process production orders for semifinished materials

  • Perform quality management – overview inspection lots for semifinished materials

  • Inspect semifinished materials through in-process quality control (for example, roasting, packaging) and make usage decisions

  • Confirm production orders (roasting, cooling, and packaging) for semifinished materials

  • Conduct early goods receipt inspections and make usage decisions for semifinished materials (Option 1: before goods receipt; Option 2: after goods receipt)

  • Monitor inspection lots and evaluate quality management data for semifinished materials

  • Convert and process production orders for finished materials

  • Perform evaluations

Business Benefits

  • Plan, inspect and manage the quality for internal, external, inbound processes and materials

  • Allows for scheduling and planning of checks and tests to monitor quality at all stages

  • Enables in-process control, early inspection and goods receipt inspection
processes.name: Quality Management in Discrete Manufacturing – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Quality Management in Procurement (1FM)

Overview

This scope item manages quality inspection in procurement: At goods receipt, a good is posted to quality inspection stock and an inspection lot is created based on an inspection plan. The quality technician records the inspection results. The quality engineer then makes a usage decision – for example, accepting or rejecting the material, posting the material to unrestricted stock or blocked stock, or triggering return to the supplier, with the option of posting as a consumed sample. For rejected results, a defect is automatically recorded. The supplier is rated on the quality score defined in the usage decision. With a dynamic modification rule, quality inspections can be tightened, reduced, or skipped based on previous inspection results. You can block the creation of purchase orders or limit the purchased quantity due to quality reasons. By leveraging quality certificates in procurement, you can ensure that suppliers provide the documents if required.

Key Process Flow

  • Purchase material from a supplier

  • Review quality info record

  • Review inspection plan, optionally with dynamic modification rule and sampling scheme; optionally with inspection method with documents attached

  • Post goods receipt for purchase order

  • Review material stock before inspection

  • Display open inspection lots

  • Record inspection results

  • Make usage decision

  • Review and analyze defects

  • Review material stock after inspection

Business Benefits

  • Integrate quality inspection activities in the purchasing process

  • Use inspection plans for quality inspections with dynamic modification, sampling scheme, and material-supplier release

  • Display open and completed receipts of quality certificates in procurement

  • Record nonconformities at the right point in time to avoid cost-intensive reprocessing or unnecessary waste
processes.name: Quality Management in Procurement

processes.description:
Quality Management in Sales (1MP)

Overview

This scope item manages quality inspection activities in outbound delivery processes. Quality inspection activities may be important before goods issue.

When creating an outbound delivery for a material that is the subject of an inspection in the sales and delivery process, an inspection lot is created based on an inspection plan. The quality technician records the inspection results for a sample size. Based on these inspection results, the quality engineer makes a usage decision, for example, accepting or rejecting the material. If accepted, the goods are posted and sent to the customer. If rejected, the whole quantity is posted to blocked stock and the delivery is updated. For the rejected results, a defect is automatically recorded. Any further stock of the same material must be accepted before they are delivered.

Key Process Flow

  • Sell material to a customer and create an outbound delivery

  • Review inspection plan

  • Display open inspection lots

  • Record quality inspection results

  • Make usage decision, optionally attach documents

  • Review and analyze defects

  • Post goods issue for the outbound delivery

Business Benefits

  • Integrate quality inspection activities in the sales process

  • Use inspection plans for quality inspections

  • Detect nonconformities before delivering materials to a customer
processes.name: Quality Management in Sales

processes.description:
Quality Management in Stock Handling (1MR)

Overview

This scope item manages quality inspection activities in stock handling processes. Quality inspection activities may be relevant for materials during the storage of goods.

During the storage of goods, a warehouse clerk may identify damage that must be checked and investigated. To follow up, the material is posted to quality inspection stock and an inspection lot is created automatically. The quality engineer inspects the material and makes a usage decision that triggers the posting of the material, for example, to unrestricted stock, to blocked stock, or to scrap. Additionally, the quality inspection stock may be moved from one storage location to another, for example, if a specific check can only be done at one location in the plant where the equipment is available.

Key Process Flow

  • Post material from unrestricted or blocked stock to quality inspection stock

  • Execute inspection and record results

  • Make usage decision

  • Review material stock after inspection

Business Benefits

  • Integrate quality inspection activities in the stock handling process

  • Detect nonconformities and necessary follow-up actions as soon as possible to avoid inappropriate usage
processes.name: Quality Management in Stock Handling

processes.description:
Quality Management in Warehousing (3M0)

Overview

This scope item allows you to inspect products delivered from external suppliers and from production before putaway in the warehouse. The process starts with the creation of a purchase or production order and an inbound delivery relevant for processing in the warehouse. Once the goods arrive at the warehouse, the delivery is checked, and the products are packed into handling units as required. Afterwards, the goods receipt is posted and warehouse tasks are created to execute the movements to the quality area. At goods receipt posting, the system creates an inspection lot and changes the stock type to quality stock. A quality technician inspects the delivered goods and records the inspection results. Based on these results, the quality engineer makes a usage decision. At the end of the process, you create ad-hoc warehouse tasks to move the accepted products to a final storage bin. The rejected products stay in the quality area for further processing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create handling units and print labels (optional)

  • Post goods receipt against inbound deliveries

  • Post synchronous goods receipt against purchase orders / production orders

  • Create inspection lot (system step)

  • Create warehouse tasks to move products to the quality area

  • Print warehouse task lists

  • Confirm warehouse tasks

  • Record inspection results

  • Make usage decision

  • Repack handling units (optional)

  • Create ad-hoc warehouse tasks from quality area to final bin and print warehouse task lists

  • Confirm warehouse tasks

Business Benefits

  • Inspect the products received from external suppliers and production

  • Profit from a seamless integration between quality and warehouse management

  • Make use of partial quantity decisions

  • Control and record movements of products and handling units in the warehouse

  • Map your warehouse complex in the system down to storage bin level

  • Improve visibility and control in warehouse operations

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers who use warehouse management capabilities in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and would like to extend their inbound process from supplier and production with a quality inspection process.
processes.name: Quality Management in Warehousing

processes.description:
Quality Management of Internal Problems (2QP)

Overview

This scope item describes the management of internal problems, for example, deviations observed during production or storage of goods.

Leveraging quality notifications, the quality engineer can capture all problem-related information. Further immediate actions can be captured for documentation purposes. To identify the root cause of the complaint, the quality engineer starts a root cause analysis. After having identified the error and the related root cause, the quality engineer classifies this information using code groups, codes, and free text information.

The quality engineer defines corrective and preventive actions either globally at notification level or per defect. The quality engineer assigns one processor to each action. The action is processed and action processors give feedback per action.

Finally, the quality engineer reviews each action and closes the notification.

Key Process Flow

  • Create quality notification with basic data

  • Capture defects, define root cause analysis, and document immediate actions

  • Define corrective actions

  • Execute root cause analysis and corrective actions, and document outcome

  • Review root cause analysis and document root cause, review corrective actions

  • Define preventive actions

  • Execute preventive actions and document outcome

  • Review preventive actions

  • Complete quality notification

Business Benefits

  • Capture problem details, related defects, causes, and activities in one place

  • Manage different types of activities (for example immediate, corrective, and preventive actions)

  • Assign a person responsible to each action and track action status and outcome
processes.name: Quality Management of Internal Problems

processes.description:
Reactive Maintenance (4HH)

Overview

The reactive maintenance process has nine steps from the creation of a maintenance notification to its completion. Reactive maintenance process allows you to perform maintenance of an asset whenever a breakdown or a failure occurs.

First, you create a maintenance notification (Initiation). Next, the maintenance notification is screened and accepted (Screening). The maintenance notification is converted into a maintenance order. During this phase, the required resources for processing the order are also planned (Planning). The maintenance order is then approved for execution (Approval). Next, the maintenance order is prepared for execution. Various requirements such as stock, nonstock material, purchase requisition, and capacity are reviewed (Preparation). After this, the maintenance order is scheduled for execution (Scheduling). The maintenance order is then executed to repair the malfunction (Execution). Activities such as failure data recording and other post-work activities are performed (Post Execution). Finally, the maintenance order is reviewed and is technically completed (Completion).

For minor or emergency work, not all steps need to be executed. When you select the notification processing context in the Manage Maintenance Notification app, you also decide the variation of the reactive maintenance process (minor or emergency).

To enable safety instructions, you need to activate the Health and Safety Management (54A) scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Create maintenance request

  • Screen maintenance request

  • Convert maintenance request into maintenance order

  • Plan maintenance order

  • Submit maintenance order approval

  • Release maintenance order for preparation

  • Review maintenance backlog for readiness

  • Schedule maintenance orders

  • Time confirmation of pre- and main order operations

  • Time confirmation of post-maintenance order operations

  • Record failure data

  • Complete maintenance order technically

Business Benefits

  • Reduce an asset's downtime and increase productivity

  • Enables you to save maintenance costs
processes.name: Reactive Maintenance

processes.description:
Real Estate Cost Settlement (6N8)

Overview

This scope item covers the distribution of incurred costs to tenants based on the terms and conditions of their lease agreement or the local distribution regulations. Distribution of expenses for a location may be distributed based on the service charge settlement or common area maintenance expense recovery models.

Service Groups are defined to capture the costs to be settled. They also capture the real estate objects participating in the settlement and the relevant accounting object where the costs were recorded. Additionally, the Service Group captures how the settlement should be performed.

Invoices are posted to expense accounts and are later assigned to a Service Group, Cost Category and a Service Date. This assignment may be made either manually or automatically based on information entered on the invoice or settings made in the system settings. At the end of the service period, costs are distributed to tenants based on the negotiated terms of the contract or based on the local distribution regulations.

Key Process Flow

  • Define settlement infrastructure

  • Classify journal entry items to be allocated

  • Manage contract terms and conditions

  • Execute settlement process (in simulation mode)

  • Display results of cost settlement process steps

Business Benefits

  • Provides functionality to distribute common area maintenance expenses to tenants based on the terms of the lease out contract, reducing the operating expenses of the property owner and matching the expenses incurred to maintain a building with the tenant's usage

  • Decouple the posting process of the payable invoice from the planned real estate cost settlement process, simplifying the recording of invoices that is distributed to tenants
processes.name: Real Estate Cost Settlement

processes.description:
Real-Time Reporting and Monitoring for Procurement (1JI)

Overview

The Procurement Overview Page presents key information and tasks for a purchaser. It displays all relevant information on a single page, using attractive and efficient actionable cards for various content types. The user-friendly experience makes viewing, filtering, and acting upon data simple, faster and smarter – even on mobile devices. Analytical list pages are also provided to monitor purchase contract items, supplier confirmation, and purchase order items.

The purchaser views a high-level overview of important information, such as expiring contracts, overdue purchase orders or urgent purchase requisitions as well as an overview of different procurement KPIs. With these KPIs, the purchaser can easily determine the performance of suppliers, monitor non-managed spend or purchasing spend, and quickly discover trends and potential areas of improvement.

Key Process Flow

  • Display urgent contracts, overdue purchase order items, urgent purchase requisition items, or open RFQs with impending submission deadlines

  • Navigate quickly to an object page or list app to perform a required action

  • Analyze purchasing spend, non-managed spend, and off-contract spend by supplier or material group

  • Analyze supplier performance based on their operational score in correlation with the corresponding spend

  • Display purchasing spend or supplier performance in line charts for the last 12 months

  • Analyze purchase requisition item types and purchase requisition touch rate for the last 12 months

  • Navigate from the KPI insights to the corresponding smart apps for detailed analysis

  • Filter cards by different business attributes, such as Supplier, Material, Material Group, Purchasing Group, Purchasing Organization, Plant, and so on

Business Benefits

  • Provide a dashboard for the purchaser to perform daily activities smoothly and without opening different reports and transactions

  • Provide high-level insights for a purchaser to understand the key numbers and drill down to action

  • Filter by supplier, purchasing group, or material group, for example to show urgent contracts, purchase requisition items, spend, or supplier performance information
processes.name: Real-Time Reporting and Monitoring for Procurement

processes.description:
Receivables Financing with Taulia (7DX)

Overview

Taulia Receivables Financing gives you the ability to finance your receivable invoices with a diverse network of funders directly through the Taulia platform. You will gain unparalleled flexibility with the ability to finance individual invoices as needed. The delivered automated reconciliation will streamline your processes with the end-to-end automated process from financing, to repayment to the funder.

Financing of invoices requires an agreement with Taulia.

Key Process Flow

  • Replicate customer master and receivables transaction data to Taulia platform automatically

  • Use Taulia to analyze your customer master and receivable invoices to provide the most competitive financing

  • Use Taulia to provide indicative pricing for financing

  • Execute an agreement with Taulia to start financing of selected invoices

  • Select specific or all invoies for financing

  • Record and post financing documents

  • Post repayment documents automatically

Business Benefits

  • Improve your liquidity by converting receivables to cash faster, supporting growth initiatives

  • Diversify funding sources through a multi-funder approach to mitigate risk

  • Improve operational efficiency by reducing manual workload with our automated reconciliation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is a customer-managed integration and is defaulted to be a non-standard scope item. Additionally, this scope item requires a license for SAP Taulia Solutions for SAP Finance.
processes.name: Receivables Financing with Taulia

processes.description:
Recurring Services (4X5)

Overview

This scope item covers the creation of maintenance plans in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, as well as scheduling and service order creation. Maintenance plans can be set up to release the service order automatically when you create the service order or let the user release the order manually afterwards. Service order items are copied from the service order templates that are assigned to maintenance items in the maintenance plan. A released Service contract item (Scope item 3MO) and Service order template (Scope item 3D2) is the prerequisite for this scope item.

The Service Order Management (3D2) scope item is the follow-on process to further process the service order such as planning, releasing, time and material confirmation, billing, and order completion.

The completion date is updated automatically in the maintenance plan either upon completion of service order or manually by the user. Updating the measuring counter reading is an optional step during confirmation.

Key Process Flow

  • Create maintenance plan

  • Schedule maintenance plan (individual/mass)

  • Create a service order

  • Assign service team (optional)

  • Release service order line items (optional)

  • Change service order (optional)

  • Release service order

  • Receive confirmation against the service order

  • Post the time sheet against the service technician and expenses incurred automatically based on the confirmation

  • Cancel the confirmation along with the follow-up documents (optional)

  • Release the service order (for fixed-price services) or confirmation (for time and material services) for billing and automatic creation of billing document request

  • Copy procurement costs automatically in the confirmation, based on posted supplier invoice or purchase order for billing to the customer for time and material services

  • Create a billing document from the billing document request for invoicing the customer

  • Analyze service order fulfillment (optional)

  • Update measuring counter reading (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Provide the functionality for regular maintenance planning and scheduling

  • Cover single cycle time / counter-based and multicounter plans

  • Support individual scheduling and mass scheduling via background jobs to trigger service orders with or without release

  • Provide the functionality for planning and execution of services

  • Post time-sheet and expenses automatically based on the confirmation
processes.name: Recurring Services

processes.description:
Replenishment in Warehousing (4A2)

Overview

With this process, you can plan and automate the creation of replenishment warehouse tasks to ensure the right inventory levels for your products in the areas where picking is done. This scope item supports planned and automatic replenishment of fixed storage bins. The planned replenishment can be started either interactively or as a regular application background job. In contrast, with automatic replenishment, the system starts replenishment when a warehouse task is confirmed. The system creates replenishment warehouse tasks if the current stock is below the defined threshold for the product’s fixed bin. The replenishment quantity is calculated as the difference between the maximum and the current bin quantity. At the end of the process, the warehouse operative confirms the warehouse tasks and makes sure that the stock is moved from the reserve to the picking area.

Key Process Flow

  • Variant 1: Manual replenishment run

  • Variant 2: Job-based replenishment run

  • System: Create replenishment warehouse tasks

  • Check replenishment warehouse tasks (optional)

  • Confirm replenishment warehouse tasks

Business Benefits

  • Run planned replenishment for fixed storage bins

  • Schedule background jobs for planned replenishment

  • Setup automatic replenishment, if required

  • Maintain a proper stock rotation

  • Minimize the manual creation of warehouse tasks for internal movements

  • Improve warehouse picking efficiency

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that use warehouse management capabilities in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and want to leverage the replenishment functionality in warehousing.
processes.name: Replenishment in Warehousing

processes.description:
Replenishment Planning for Distribution Centers (3I8)

Overview

The goal of the replenishment process for distribution centers is to calculate optimal dates and quantities for the procurements of reorderable articles from suppliers to best meet demand.

First, demand is determined by executing forecasting algorithms on historical consumption data, considering various factors (such as seasonality) to feed into consumption-based planning. Alternatively, demand can be expressed by planned independent requirements (PIR).

Next, material requirements planning (MRP) is executed to calculate the optimal quantities and dates for the procurement. The replenishment calculation considers demand, current stock situation, already planned goods receipts, and supplier parameters. MRP can be controlled via different MRP types (for example, time phased planning), for which it's possible to specify certain weekdays for ordering and delivery.

The result of the MRP execution is then handed over to the operational procurement via purchase requisitions.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain planning calendar for distribution centers

  • Assign planning calendars to articles

  • Maintain forecast and MRP parameters for articles

  • Execute forecast with automatic model selection

  • Transfer forecast results to Planned Independent Requirements

  • Execute Materials Requirements Planning

  • Check the stock overview and MRP planned results

  • Solve errors

  • Evaluate created purchase requisitions

Business Benefits

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost by using more accurate sales forecasting capabilities to drive order creation

  • Improve on-time delivery performance by replenishing inventories frequently based on the latest information about stock levels and demand forecasts

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Replenishment Planning for Distribution Centers

processes.description:
Replenishment Planning for Stores (3I7)

Overview

The goal of the replenishment process for stores is to calculate optimal dates and quantities for procuring reorderable articles to best meet consumer demand. This helps avoid costly out-of-stock or overstock situations. The source of supply can be a distribution center or an external supplier.

In an optional preliminary step to the replenishment run, demand can be determined by executing forecasting algorithms on historical consumption data, considering various factors (such as seasonality). Alternatively, you can create planned independent requirements (PIRs) to determine demand. Replenishment is executed to calculate the optimal quantities and dates for procurement, considering among others, forecast demand or PIRs, the current stock situation, and already planned goods receipts. Additionally, a manually (for example based on shelf size and presentation stock) or automatically determined target stock can be considered.

Replenishment triggers the creation of purchase requisitions for the determined quantities and dates.

Key Process Flow

  • Execute forecast with automatic model selection

  • Check forecast results (optional)

  • Create planned independent requirements (PIRs) (optional)

  • Run periodic background job for replenishment of the complete or a partial assortment of a store

  • Execute manual replenishment for selected planning objects (stores or articles) (optional)

  • Check follow-on documents in replenishment monitor (optional)

  • Check results of replenishment planning run (optional)

  • Run periodic background job for reorganization of replenishment runs (for example delete older replenishment logs)

Business Benefits

  • Increase FTE efficiency by automating store replenishment based on current demand and stock situation

  • Reduce revenue loss due to stock-outs by using accurate, consistent, and real-time inventory across all stores

  • Reduce operations cost by triggering the creation of procurement documents for defined quantities and dates

  • Improve customer satisfaction by improving fill rates and service levels

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Replenishment Planning for Stores

processes.description:
Request for Price (1XF)

Overview

With this scope item, you can create requests for quotations in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system and send them to a supplier via e-mail or as a printed version by mail. The suppliers provide their quotations via e-mail or by mail as well. You can manually create a quotation in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system using the Manage Supplier Quotations app. By default, a new quotation has the status In Preparation. You select a quotation that you want to award and submit it for approval. After awarding the quotation, the follow-on documents are created in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The quotations that do not meet your requirements must be manually set to Rejected/Completed.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a request for quotation and automatically submit it to the corresponding suppliers

  • Receive the supplier proposals electronically and automatically create supplier quotations

  • Compare and award the corresponding quotations

  • Create follow-on documents

Business Benefits

  • Specify individual output channels for suppliers

  • Reduce the time needed to evaluate proposals from qualified bidders with qualified responses
processes.name: Request for Price

processes.description:
Request Regulatory Documentation from Service Provider (6AV)

Overview

This scope item enables you to use compliance data that is provided by an external service provider for regulatory documentation in the Product Compliance solution. The external service provider can, for example, take over the collection of regulatory data, such as GHS classifications and dangerous goods classifications for your compliance-relevant products. In addition, the service provider generates regulatory documentation, such as safety data sheets.

This scope item supports the following processes:

  • Simulate the cooperation with a service provider for regulatory documentation

  • Cooperate with a service provider for regulatory documentation

Because the cooperation with a service provider for regulatory documentation only works in a productive environment, the test script only tests the simulation of the cooperation. You create service requests for substances and products and send data to a reference service simulating the regulatory documentation of the service provider. You can monitor the status of the service requests and check received data that is transferred from the reference service to the Product Compliance solution.

To productively use the service of a regulatory documentation service provider, a license is required.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain basic data

  • Calculate derived data

  • Receive results

Business Benefits

  • Mitigate compliance risks with up-to-date regulatory documents

  • Integrate external document generation seamlessly and profit from external expertise

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is in process of being deprecated and cannot be requested by new customers. As of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608, it has been replaced by scope item 7DO.
processes.name: Request Regulatory Documentation from Service Provider

processes.description:
Requisitioning (18J)

Overview

This scope item describes employee requisitioning activities. An employee creates a shopping cart for free text material. A purchase requisition is generated and converted to a purchase order. If the value exceeds certain criteria, the purchase order must be approved. When the employee receives the goods, they perform a goods receipt confirmation. Invoice receiving can then be performed.

Key Process Flow

  • Create purchase requisition

  • Access my purchase requisition (optional)

  • Copy purchase requisition

  • Make mass changes to purchase requisitions

  • Purchase requisition items by accounting assignment (optional)

  • Approve purchase requisition (optional)

  • Monitor purchase requisition items (optional)

  • Redistribute workload

  • Convert purchase requisition to purchase order

  • Approve purchase order (optional)

  • Confirm goods receipt

  • Create supplier invoice for single and multiple accounting assignment

  • Release blocked supplier invoice

Business Benefits

  • Configure flexible workflow based on business requirements

  • Save central resources for employee requisitioning process
processes.name: Requisitioning

processes.description:
Resource Management for Projects (6JO)

Overview

SAP Project and Resource Management allows you as a resource manager to monitor and manage the resource utilization and the staffing of resource requests, ensuring optimal resource management. It allows resources to manage their profile of skills and assignments to be matched with the right kinds of projects. It also allows the project managers to create, manage, and monitor requests for resources on their projects.

This scope item is a public cloud solution delivered on the SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP). The integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is enabled through this scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Handle staff resource requests

  • Manage resource utilization and resolve conflicts

  • Maintain employee profiles

Business Benefits

  • Get an overview on staffed and open resource requests

  • Get transparency on resource utilization

  • Get candidate recommendations for resource requests

  • Share staffing directly with project team members

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

You can request this scope item if you have the required licenses for the additional products.
processes.name: Resource Management for Projects

processes.description:
Resource Management in Warehousing (3W0)

Overview

This scope item allows you to leverage interfaces (APIs) for the development of customer-specific apps for warehouse task processing on mobile devices. In addition, it enables you to manage your warehouse resources, such as a user or equipment that executes work in the warehouse. A resource is mandatory to process warehouse orders and tasks with the APIs. A typical process on a mobile device could be designed as follows: A user starts with logon to a resource. The resource can retrieve relevant warehouse orders and tasks from the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. A warehouse task is selected by the resource for further processing. The warehouse order is blocked to prevent concurrent processing by different warehouse workers. The process ends with a confirmation of the warehouse task. With help of the resource management functionality, you can check the workload and utilization of a dedicated warehouse resource.

Business Benefits

  • Increase the efficiency of warehouse processes

  • Enable customers to manage warehouse resources

  • Optimize workload for a dedicated warehouse resource

  • Minimize time lag between execution and data entry

  • Reduce additional work caused by paperwork

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that use warehouse management capabilities in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and want to connect mobile devices for warehouse task processing.
processes.name: Resource Management in Warehousing

processes.description:
Responsibility Management (1NJ)

Overview

As we move toward an intelligent enterprise, intelligent systems need to determine agents who are automatically notified about events and who are responsible for business processes and objects. It is essential to define and manage these responsibilities, including authorizations for various contexts, and retrieve the correct contacts who can react to tasks and activities. Responsibility Management provides the Teams concept through which you can group responsible members with appropriate definitions for responsibilities. These members are assigned functions that uniquely describe the nature of their work. Functions and responsibility definitions help as a selection criterion for refining agent determination. With this scope item you can configure function, function profile, custom responsibility definitions, and team types for Responsibility Management.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a team

  • Maintain hierarchy across teams

  • Create rules

  • Extend context and map rules

  • Create custom context

  • Create custom team category

Business Benefits

  • Simplify approval processes for business scenarios that need to determine responsible people in complex organizational structures

  • Enable application scenarios in determining the people responsible for tasks, activities, and business situations

  • Save time and cost of changing an existing organizational structure when adopting dynamic approval processes

  • Achieve task management with teams, roles, rules, and responsibilities
processes.name: Responsibility Management

processes.description:
Restricted Party Screening with SAP Watch List Screening (1WE)

Overview

SAP Watch List Screening is a standalone public cloud solution delivered on the SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) to perform sanctioned party list screening of business partners and relevant documents, such as sales orders and deliveries, as part of international trade compliance.

This scope item provides connection between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Watch List Screening and enables screening against the organization's denied party lists. Self-service configuration allows organizations to define applicable regulations.

You must have a license for SAP Watch List Screening.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage legal regulations

  • Activate documents for screening

  • Activate company code checks

  • Activate business partner roles for screening

Business Benefits

  • Support compliance of international trade

  • Keep international trade processes frictionless

  • Avoid financial loss

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant if you would like to integrate with SAP Watch List Screening. If you request this scope item, see the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator. ​You must also have an additional license for SAP Watch List Screening.
processes.name: Restricted Party Screening with SAP Watch List Screening

processes.description:
Retail Logistics with Embedded Warehouse Management (69L)

Overview

A distribution center is typically the logistical entry point of a retailer to the supply chain. It connects the procurement process from external suppliers with the distribution process to the stores. The goal of the distribution process is to shorten delivery cycles to the stores, ensuring that there are no out-of-stock situations.

To achieve this, a sophisticated warehouse management is key. The following activities are supported by the embedded warehouse management:

  • Receive articles and put-away in the warehouse

  • Use different variants of inbound processing

  • Pick and pack products, and send them from your warehouse

  • Plan and conduct regular physical inventory counts of actual quantities in the warehouse, comparing them with book inventory, and posting differences

  • Transfer postings, such as changing the stock type from unrestricted to blocked stock

  • Perform planned or automatic replenishment of fixed bins

Key Process Flow

  • Warehouse inbound processing

  • Warehouse outbound processing

  • Warehouse physical inventory

  • Warehouse transfer postings

  • Replenishment in warehousing

Business Benefits

  • Improve warehouse stock transparency by providing inventory insights at storage bin level

  • Manage inventory efficiently with correct stock levels

  • Use efficient logistics processes with easy tracking of goods and orders

  • Segregate stock easily (for example, blocked stocks or generally available stocks) to enable goods movement

  • Improve warehouse strategy FTE productivity by supporting all relevant warehouse management processes

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

Additionally, the following prerequisite scope items must be activated: 3BR, 4A2, 3BS, 3BX, 3BU.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Retail Logistics with Embedded Warehouse Management

processes.description:
Retail Logistics with Third-Party Warehouse Management (69M)

Overview

A distribution center typically is the logistical entry point of a retailer to the supply chain. It connects the procurement process from external suppliers with the distribution process to the stores. The goal of the distribution process is to shorten delivery cycles to the stores, ensuring that there are no out-of-stock situations. To achieve this, a sophisticated warehouse management is key.

The decentralized third-party warehouse management system runs all processes related to inbound and outbound processes originating from procurement, sales, and distribution processes, as well as in-warehouse goods movements. The integration is covered by asynchronous SOAP interfaces compatible with most existing third-party warehouse management systems to reduce the implementation effort.

Key Process Flow

  • Inventory management processes

  • Inbound processing part of procurement processes

  • Outbound processing part of sales processes

  • Inbound processing part of returns from customers

  • Outbound processing part of returns to suppliers

Business Benefits

  • Perform easy and seamless integrated process execution that involves the third-party warehouse management processes

  • Provide easy handling of procurement, inventory management, sales, and various returns process integrated to a third-party warehouse management system

  • Provide transparency in various logistics process integrated to third-party warehouse management systems

  • Improve warehouse stock transparency by providing inventory insights at storage bin level

  • Improve warehouse strategy productivity by supporting all relevant warehouse management processes

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

Additionally, scope item 1ZQ must be activated as a prerequisite.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Retail Logistics with Third-Party Warehouse Management

processes.description:
Retail Promotions (637)

Overview

When planning a promotion, you need to define relevant factors, such as time periods, participating stores (a group of stores or all stores in a distribution chain), and included products. For these factors, among others, the planned promotional sales prices, sales and logistical units of measure, and procurement quantities must be specified. All this information is maintained via the object promotion. When operational follow-on activities are due, those can be triggered from the promotion object, including:

  • Activating promotional sales prices

  • Determining supply sources for the procurement

  • Creating an allocation table that plans the procurement and distribution of merchandise between suppliers, distribution centers and stores

  • Creating operational documents with reference to the allocation table, such as purchase orders for suppliers and stock transport orders for the procurement for the stores from the distribution centers (various process variants are supported)

For ease of maintenance, promotions can be created with reference to an existing promotion, and for a specific promotion type, which defaults in parameters like currency, price activation type, and various lead times.

Key Process Flow

  • Create promotion with validity periods, articles, sales prices, and so on

  • Determine sources-of-supply

  • Activate prices

  • Generate allocation table based on promotion data

  • Generate follow-on documents for allocation table

Business Benefits

  • Increase customer retention and boost sales volumes through price deals for consumers

  • Adjust price schedules to match customer and market needs that vary with channel and location

  • Reduce stock levels of seasonal merchandise through attractive price deals and other stock reduction strategies

  • Launch products, for example, through effective in-store presentation

  • Increase effectiveness of promotions by automating the creation of all follow-on documents to support the execution of retail promotions

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Retail Promotions

processes.description:
Return to Supplier (BMK)

Overview

The return process begins with the creation of a return purchase order and is followed by the outbound delivery. Subsequently the items are picked and shipped to the supplier. Alternatively, you can also directly post a goods issue. The process is closed with the creation of a credit memo, which transfers the liability to the corresponding supplier.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage return purchase orders

  • Manage stock

  • Manage return delivery

  • Perform picking

  • Post goods issue

  • Manage credit memos

Business Benefits

  • Efficient and cost-effective streamlined return processes

  • Ensure highly automated processes for the return of materials

  • Reduce manual effort

  • Real-time monitoring of the return progress
