  • Analytical list page: Monitor purchase order items
processes.name: Return to Supplier

processes.description:
Returnables Processing (BDW)

Overview

This scope item enables the shipping of standard pallets and their return. When you create a standard sales order, the delivery is automatically created based on this sales order. During the picking and shipping steps of this process, a pallet (returnable packaging) is added to the delivery. During the billing process, pallets can also be returned to manufacturers using a pallet return order with pallet return delivery and goods receipt, or a pallet return delivery without reference and goods receipt.

If customers do not return pallets, you can issue debit memo requests. Triggered by billing, the system issues debit memos based on such debit memo requests. Once this has been carried out, you can synchronize the consignment stock quantity and value, and then post a manual goods issue for the unreturned pallet.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order

  • Create delivery

  • Execute picking

  • Add returnable packaging to deliveries

  • Create returnable packaging return order

  • Post goods receipt for returnable packaging

  • Debit unreturned packaging

  • Post goods issue for unreturned packaging

Business Benefits

  • Consists of the management of returnables using the ERP returnable packaging logistics function

  • Track returnables
processes.name: Returnables Processing

processes.description:
Returns from Store (5FR)

Overview

A store may need to return merchandise to a distribution center for various reasons, such as quality recalls, end-of-season returns, or returns to balance stock shortages in other stores.

A store associate creates the stock transfer return order document. A store employee monitors the products due to be shipped and creates outbound deliveries as required. Once a return delivery is created, a picking list is generated for the products.

A store associate gathers the products and confirms the picked quantities. The goods issue is posted when the return delivery is complete. As a result, an inbound delivery is automatically created for the receiving distribution center as a follow-on document.

At the distribution center, a receiving specialist inspects the goods and confirms the put-away, referencing the inbound delivery.

Key Process Flow

  • Create returns stock transport order

  • Create return delivery and post goods issue

  • Create inbound delivery and post goods receipt

  • Perform goods inspection

  • Monitor the returns process

Business Benefits

  • Handle return processes in a streamlined and cost-effective manner

  • Ensure highly automated processes for the return of materials

  • Monitor the return progress in real time

  • Reduce cost of processing returns to the distribution centers by providing store associates with an application to create return orders and all required follow-on documents

  • Reduce inventory write-offs by providing efficient processes to return merchandise for recalls, clearance, or stock balancing

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Returns from Store

processes.description:
Returns to Supplier for Retail (5FO)

Overview

Returning merchandise to external suppliers is a regular process for a retailer. It’s important that the process can be executed as automatically and flexibly as possible to meet the requirements of each supplier. Returns can be initiated by different business situations, such as an agreement that the unsold quantities can be returned at the end of season, or the need to return spoiled, broken, or poor quality articles.

The return process begins with the creation of a return purchase order and is followed by the generation of an outbound delivery. The items are then picked and shipped to the supplier. The process is finalized with the creation of a credit memo, which transfers the liability to the corresponding supplier.

Returns management provides end-to-end support for both simple and complex returns scenarios by integrating all the necessary steps.

Key Process Flow

  • Create return purchase orders

  • Track supplier returns (optional)

  • Enter inspection results from suppliers (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Increase employee productivity by accelerating the handling process with triggering of all follow-up documents

  • Reduce inventory days by efficiently managing returns to suppliers for damaged goods or end-of-season clearance

  • Reduce complaints and returns cost by simplifying the complaint and return process and managing associated costs

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Returns to Supplier for Retail

processes.description:
Rework Processing – Stock-Manufactured Material (BJN)

Overview

This scope item focuses on rework activities and material postings after production execution for the original material (including goods receipt for the product), with an additional rework production order. Issues with the produced material are monitored after it is posted to inventory.

The rework process of stock-manufactured materials begins with the creation of a new production order. This is done using the material to be reworked as both input and output.

Costs are listed in the new production order, and are settled within controlling as production variants. The input component and product have the same material number.

Key Process Flow

  • Create rework production order

  • Release rework production order

  • Issue goods for defective material including printing preview

  • Confirm rework production activities

  • Post goods receipt for rework production order incl. printing preview

Business Benefits

  • Show transparent costs for rework activities

  • Use all standard shop-floor control functionalities

  • Improve usability with intuitive confirmation of production operations
processes.name: Rework Processing – Stock-Manufactured Material

processes.description:
Rework Processing – Work-in-Process (BJQ)

Overview

This scope item focuses on a rework process within production. All required rework activities are related to the production order. For this reason, defects are recognized and corrections are initiated, such as insertion of a rework operation within the same production order. The additional rework operation is confirmed and settled within the production order, causing production variances within controlling and price differences for the dedicated product.

Key Process Flow

  • Confirm production activities

  • Confirm scrap for defective material and material that can be reused

  • Confirm production order at rework operation

  • Continue shop-floor activities

Business Benefits

  • Trigger the rework process automatically with a material in a defined operation

  • Confirm additional activity and material consumption after rework

  • Integrate rework processing fully in the production process
processes.name: Rework Processing – Work-in-Process

processes.description:
Rework with Quality Management – Consumer Products (6A9)

Overview

This scope item describes two rework processes:

Rework Process 1: This rework process focuses on rework activities and material postings during production execution for the original material. Quality Management identifies deviation from the specification. The original production order is only partly confirmed, another part is booked to be relevant for rework. The result is the automatic creation of a rework production order via a trigger point.

Rework Process 2: This rework process focuses on rework activities after goods receipt for the product from production order. During goods receipt for the product, quality issues are identified and the usage decision fails. The products are booked into inventory, but the failed part is posted to blocked stock (not to unrestricted use). The products booked to blocked stock are subject to rework activities to overcome the defect. After rework, is finished the material is again subject to quality inspection to check successful rework processing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create planned independent requirements

  • Perform material requirements planning at plant level

  • Convert planned orders to production orders

  • Process production orders

  • Perform quality management – overview inspection lots

  • Perform quality inspection – within production (roasting)

  • Confirm production order of roasting and cooling process

  • Perform quality inspection – early goods receipt inspection / end-product-control

  • Perform quality inspection – in-process control

  • Execute partial production order confirmation for operation packaging

  • Adopt and release rework order

  • Confirm rework production order

  • Perform quality inspection – in-process control and usage decision

  • Confirm original production order for operation packaging

  • Post goods receipt for original production order

  • Perform cost analysis of original and rework production orders

  • Perform rework production order of stock manufactured material with quality management evaluations

  • Use batch information cockpit – to perform top-down and bottom-up analysis

Business Benefits

  • Show transparent costs for rework activities

  • Use all standard shop-floor control functionalities

  • Improve usability with intuitive confirmation of production operations

  • Use an automated process to create rework production order via a trigger point
processes.name: Rework with Quality Management – Consumer Products

processes.description:
Royalties Settlement for Sales (55I)

Overview

In this process, condition contracts are used to establish royalty agreements with licensors. These contracts specify the recipient of royalties, organizational and process control parameters, business volume selection criteria, royalty conditions, and a settlement calendar with dates for delta accrual, partial settlement, and final settlement. Delta accruals are posted separately from transactional documents during a specific settlement run. For partial and final settlements, royalties are calculated based on business volume and royalty conditions, and settlement documents are created to reflect invoices from the licensor for license rights in sales deals. Business volume is typically determined from sales and distribution (SD) billing documents. However, in the intercompany royalties scenario, business volume can also be derived from specific accounting documents (instead of billing documents) to consider only recognized revenue for royalty settlements.

Key Process Flow

  • Post billing documents

  • Enter condition contracts for royalty agreements

  • Check business volume (optional)

  • Post accruals (optional)

  • Perform partial settlement with reversal of accruals (optional)

  • Perform final settlement with reversal of accruals

  • Perform final settlement with adjustments (optional)

  • Determine royalties unlikelihood (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Create and administer royalty agreements for licensors centrally

  • Settle royalties agreements accurately and automatically

  • Provide enhanced transparency and flexibility along the whole royalty agreements lifecycle
processes.name: Royalties Settlement for Sales

processes.description:
Safety Data Sheets in the Value Chain (3VQ)

Overview

This scope item covers the main process steps for the maintenance of safety data sheets for products during sales processes.

Products flagged as relevant for compliance must have a completed safety data sheet assessment by the product steward. A missing assessment results in a country-specific automatic block of sales order fulfillment that can be resolved by the product steward, typically by assigning a relevant safety data sheet to the products.

Key Process Flow

  • Flag products as relevant for compliance

  • Determine and assign markets to your products

  • Derive relevant compliance purposes from the assigned markets for your products

  • Use dedicated compliance requirements to manage, version, and store safety data sheets

  • Assess product requirements for safety data sheets in specific countries and language variants and maintain the status and documents

Business Benefits

  • Mitigate compliance risks with up-to-date information integrated into the value chain

  • Inform product steward specialists about new markets

  • Integrate the safety data sheet requirements and management into the general product compliance management processes, providing an integrated view on the status

  • Integrate the safety data sheet processes of a product with your logistic processes

  • Integrate the product stewardship department via a release cycle into sales and distribution processes
processes.name: Safety Data Sheets in the Value Chain

processes.description:
Sale of Services (2EQ)

Overview

A service product is used in the sales order. It allows the sales of services without delivery and direct (order-related) billing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales inquiry

  • Create sales quotation

  • Create sales order – including a service item (Material Type: SERV)

  • Manage credit – set customer credit/Review of blocked sales orders

  • Bill service items

Business Benefits

  • Integrate sales of services into sales order processing in a flexible manner
processes.name: Sale of Services

processes.description:
Sales Commissions – External Sales Representative (2TT)

Overview

Condition contracts are used in this process to enter sales commission agreements with external sales agents. In a condition contract you specify the commission recipient, the organizational and process control parameter, the business volume selection criteria, the sales commission conditions, and the settlement calendar with the settlement dates for delta accrual, partial settlement, and final settlement. The delta accruals settlement reflects a procedure in which accruals for commissions are not posted together with transactional documents but are posted at a later date in a specific settlement run. When carrying out the partial and final settlements of a condition contract, you perform the sales commission calculation based on business volume and commission conditions and you create the settlement documents that reflect an invoice from the external sales agents for the arrangement of sales deals. This scope item supports two data sources for the business volume determination: sales and distribution (SD) billing documents that have already been paid and SD billing documents without check for payment.

Key Process Flow

  • Check business volume (optional)

  • Post accruals (optional)

  • Partial settlement with reversal of accruals (optional)

  • Post incoming payments (optional)

  • Check business volume

  • Final settlement with reversal of accruals

  • Final settlement with adjustments (optional)

  • Commission unlikelihood (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Create and administer commission agreements for external sales agents centrally

  • Settle sales commissions accurately and automatically provide enhanced transparency and flexibility along the whole commission contract lifecycle

  • Use different data sources for commissions: Billing documents and cleared billing documents

  • Create and administer commission agreements for external sales agents centrally

  • Settle sales commissions accurately and automatically

  • Provide enhanced transparency and flexibility along the whole commission contract lifecycle

  • Use different data sources for commissions: Billing documents and cleared billing documents
processes.name: Sales Commissions – External Sales Representative

processes.description:
Sales Contract Management (I9I)

Overview

This scope item addresses the following scenarios:

Sales quantity or sales value contract: The quantity contract contains basic quantity and price information. A value contract is a legal agreement with a customer that contains the materials and services that the customer receives within a specified time period, and for a value up to a specified target value. In this scope item, the internal sales representative creates a sales quantity or value contract. Following this, a call-off order is created against the contract.

Quantity-contract-based down payments: For the sales quantity contract, down payments can be requested via a billing plan. Upon call-off order creation, a delivery block is assigned to the call-off order schedule lines. Once the down payments are received, the delivery block is removed automatically. In the delivery-related final invoice of the call-off order, the received down payments for the quantity contract is deducted.

Quantity-contract-based price agreements: For the sales quantity contract, the price agreement can be a special pricing condition record which is maintained in sales contract items. Upon call-off order creation, the price agreements is determined on the order items, and the price agreements is applied in the follow-up businesses including invoices.

Key Process Flow

Sales quantity or sales value contract

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create quantity or value contract

  • Create call-off sales order with reference to contract

  • List sales contracts

Sales quantity contract-based down payments

  • Create sales quantity contract with billing plan to request down payments

  • Create down payment request

  • Create call-off order with delivery block

  • Post down payment

  • Remove the call-off order delivery block automatically once contract down payment is received

  • Deliver the call-off order

  • Provide delivery-related invoice of the call-off order, with deduction of contract-based down payments

Sales quantity contract-based price agreements

  • Maintain the price maintenance scenarios

  • Assign the price maintenance scenario to item categories

  • Create sales quantity contract with item categories assigned with price maintenance scenario

  • Create call-off order referencing to the sales quantity contract

  • Delivery the call-off order

  • Provide delivery-related invoice of the call-off order

Sales value contract-based price agreements

  • Maintain the price maintenance scenarios

  • Assign the price maintenance scenario to item categories

  • Create sales value contract with product related item categories or product hierarchy related item categories assigned with price maintenance scenario

  • Create call-off order referencing to the sales value contract

  • Delivery the call-off order

  • Provide delivery-related invoice of the call-off order

Business Benefits

  • Provide secure planning with the use of quantity and value contracts: the customer can only call off the quantity or value for a certain price that is defined in the quantity or value contract

  • Provide a detailed monitoring of contract call-offs

  • Request down payments from a quantity contract

  • Create call-off orders with a derived delivery block on schedule lines

  • Reduce manual steps through automatic delivery block removal in the call-off order upon down payment receipt

  • Apply the special prices or discount from the quantity and value contract to call-off orders

  • Reduce the manual steps for updating the prices in call-off orders
processes.name: Sales Contract Management

processes.description:
Overview

The process starts with the creation of a customer's standard sales order, or optionally with creation of a sales quotation. Depending on the customer and the article, various special activities are executed during the order entry, such as customer/article pricing, insertion of applicable discounts, or checking the availability of the articles. For fulfillment, an outbound delivery is created when the sales order is due. The shipping specialist picks the articles and enters the quantities in the outbound delivery. After picking is complete, the shipping specialist can post the goods issue and, as a result, inventory accounts are posted to in financial. Now, the delivery can be invoiced and the revenue posted to financial accounting. This step completes the sales from a logistic perspective. Finance covers the process of customer account clearing through payment. The debit/credit memo process is triggered if the customer is undercharged or overcharged (for example, because of a pricing or sales tax rate error).

This scope item also describes the process for standard customer consignment processing. The articles shipped to the customer are still owned by the retailer until they're sold by the customer to a third party. The articles, which are usually stored in the customer store or warehouse, are posted in a stock (consignment stock) that is assigned to the corresponding customer. This allows the current customer stock to be viewed at any time.

The process of intercompany sales is also supported. In this case, the sales originate in a sales area assigned to one company code. It's fulfilled from a distribution center belonging to a different company code. The supported process includes the respective intercompany billing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create or change sales quotation
  • Create or change sales order
  • Create delivery
  • Execute picking
  • Post goods issue
  • Create billing document
  • Create debit/credit memo
  • Create intercompany billing

Business Benefits

  • Reduce customer billing, credit, and collections cost by providing consistent and correct article and price information
  • Reduce customer churn by centrally managing business partner data to ensures master data quality and data checks
  • Reduce days sales outstanding by automating the payment reconciliation process and removing manual processing

Exclude from Default Activation

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Sales from Distribution Center

processes.description:
Sales Inquiry (1IQ)

Overview

This scope item describes the process for a standard sales inquiry. It allows you to create, edit, and reject an inquiry. You can then create a quotation or sales order based on the inquiry.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales inquiry

  • Change sales inquiry

  • Reject sales inquiry

Business Benefits

  • Collect data on what your customers request about your products and services

  • Determine reasons for inquiry rejection

  • Improve your products and services
processes.name: Sales Inquiry

processes.description:
Sales of Non-Stock Item with Order-Specific Procurement (BDN)

Overview

This scope item enables customers to order goods that may not be in stock. In this case, goods are procured from an external supplier. During sales order creation, a purchase requisition is generated and then converted into a purchase order for the supplier. Goods receipt is created for customer and special stock. After delivery and the creation of a customer invoice, the vendor invoice for the goods receipt can be created.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order

  • Convert purchase requisitions to purchase order

  • Approve purchase orders

  • Post goods receipt

  • Enter vendor invoice

  • Process outbound delivery

  • Post goods issue

  • Create billing document

Business Benefits

  • Transfer customer requirements directly to external suppliers

  • Send goods from external suppliers to trader. The trader stays in charge for the entire delivery process

  • Fulfills customer requirements despite material shortage
processes.name: Sales of Non-Stock Item with Order-Specific Procurement

processes.description:
Sales Order Automation (73P)

Overview

This machine learning solution provides recommendations for incomplete fields in sales documents.

With SAP Business AI in customer returns management, a returns clerk is supported for efficiently creating customer returns. For the most common input fields, recommendations are proposed by AI based on historical data of past return documents with the same process variants.​

The solution helps to speed up the creation of customer return objects and reduce errors by using historical data.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales document

  • Monitor auto-completion log

  • Confirm recommendations

Business Benefits

  • Capture sales orders in time and efficiently

  • Ensure sales orders are completed and can be delivered without latency

  • Reduce rate of incomplete sales documents
processes.name: Sales Order Automation

processes.description:
Sales Order Entry with One-Time Customer (BDH)

Overview

In this scope item, you process sales order documents having a customer master record with CPD (One-time Customer) account group at the beginning of the order process. This one-time customer is used for customers doing only rare business and therefore it doesn’t make sense to create an own master record. The sales order is saved using this one-time customer by entering the address manually each time when creating a sales order.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order

  • Create attachment for sales order (optional)

  • Create delivery

  • Create attachment for delivery (optional)

  • Execute picking

  • Check batches (optional)

  • Post goods issue

  • Create billing document

  • Create attachment for billing (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Process sales orders without the customer’s account number

  • Enter sales orders with material determination
processes.name: Sales Order Entry with One-Time Customer

processes.description:
Sales Order Fulfillment Monitoring and Operations (BKK)

Overview

As an internal sales representative, you use the Sales Order Fulfillment Monitor to address problems that occur during the sales order fulfillment process. You can then directly execute follow-up steps from the monitor to resolve these issues. Examples of issues are missing documents, missing or unconfirmed information, and various types of blocks as well as product and trade compliance issues. You can use the application to search for specific sales orders. You can also filter the list of issues according to the stage at which they occur (such as in order, supply, delivery, invoice, or accounting).

As an internal sales representative you use the Sales Order Cockpit to manage mass changes of different types of sales documents on the header and item levels. Flexible filter capabilities help to prepare the list of documents and items to be changed. The change jobs can be scheduled for background processing and monitoring.

Further productivity enhancements are provided for managing duplicate sales orders. The Manage Duplicate Sales Document app can be used to analyze and clear your system of duplicate sales documents. After identifying duplicates, the internal sales representative can reject them to avoid the redundant processing of duplicate sales documents.

Key Process Flow

Monitor, resolve and collaborate:

  • Incomplete data

  • Unconfirmed quantities

  • Credit blocks

  • Issues in supply, in purchase orders and manufacturing orders

  • Delivery blocks in sales orders and other delivery issues

  • Shipping blocks in deliveries and other shipping issues

  • Billing blocks, invoice issues, and accounting issues for invoices

  • Product compliance (product marketability status, dangerous goods status, safety data sheet status) and trade compliance issues

Support the following types of sales documents for mass changes:

  • Sales contracts

  • Sales scheduling agreements

  • Sales orders

  • Debit and credit memo requests

  • Customer returns

Support the following types of documents when analyzing and clearing your system of duplicates:

  • Sales quotations

  • Sales contracts

  • Sales orders

  • Customer returns

Business Benefits

  • Increase productivity in sales order processing

  • Provide a quick overview of the sales order processing status: all issues in the context of the various business objects can be displayed

  • Get a quick glance to see if products are partially delivered and not invoiced and reasons why this might be the case

  • Execute follow-up steps directly from the monitor to resolve these issues

  • Increase efficiency in making mass changes at a header and item level of sales documents through user-friendly capabilities to filter and prepare them

  • Process jobs transparently, and get efficient post processing

  • Lower your costs by reducing the number of redundant documents avoiding unnecessary handling time, shipping costs and return fees
processes.name: Sales Order Fulfillment Monitoring and Operations

processes.description:
Sales Order Processing – Project-Based Services (J14)

Overview

This scope item outlines the sales order maintenance and billing process within a project-based services scenario. It covers the creation of billing documents, including invoices, credit memos, manual credit memo requests, manual debit memos, and debit memo requests.

In the invoicing subprocess, the customer project management process initiates a billing document request, which is then converted into a customer invoice.

In the credit memo subprocess, a credit memo can be generated with or without referencing an existing customer invoice. A credit memo is subsequently created from a credit memo request.

In the manual debit memo subprocess, a debit memo request is manually created and sent to billing, where it results in a customer invoice.

Finally, these processes transfer to the Accounts Receivable process.

Key Process Flow

Create billing documents:

  • Create customer invoices and journal entry

Create credit memo:

  • Create credit memo with or without reference to customer invoice and journal entry

Create manual debit memo request:

  • Create manual debit memo request

  • Create customer invoice with reference to debit memo request and journal entry

Create manual credit memo request:

  • Create manual credit memo request

  • Create credit memo

Business Benefits

  • Streamline sales order processing for project-based services scenario

  • Control comprehensive billing subprocesses: Billing, Credit Memo, and Manual Debit Memo Request
processes.name: Sales Order Processing – Project-Based Services

processes.description:
Sales Order Processing – SEPA Direct Debit Handling (BKX)

Overview

For SEPA countries or regions, this business process includes checking the SEPA mandate during sales order processing and handling exceptions if the SEPA mandate doesn't exist.

During the SEPA implementation phase, internal sales representatives regularly check sales orders with missing SEPA mandates and coordinate the exception handling. If the SEPA mandate is received before delivery creation, the relevant SEPA mandate is maintained. Alternatively, payment terms that aren't SEPA-relevant can be agreed upon with the customer for this particular order. In this case, the internal sales representative changes the sales order accordingly. After performance of exception handling, delivery documents can be created. The billing document is then created. On the invoice form, the SEPA prenotification is displayed to inform the customer about the debit memo. The incoming customer payment is handled within accounts receivables.

Key Process Flow

  • Create and check sales orders if SEPA mandate exists

  • Handle exceptions for missing SEPA mandate

  • Create delivery

  • Execute picking

  • Post goods issue

  • Create billing document including SEPA prenotification

Business Benefits

  • Enforce definition of SEPA mandate for SEPA-relevant customer sales orders when using SEPA payment terms
processes.name: Sales Order Processing – SEPA Direct Debit Handling

processes.description:
Sales Order Processing for Non-Stock Material (2ET)

Overview

A non-stock material can be used in the Sales Order. Non-stock materials are not included in inventory management. With creation of a delivery, the goods issue is reflected by a confirmation posting. Non-stock items can be handled along with stock items on one sales order.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales inquiry, sales quotation, and sales order – including a non-stock item (Material type: NLAG)

  • Manage credit – Set customer credit / review of blocked sales orders

  • Perform outbound delivery

  • Add freight costs

  • Post goods issue (statistical confirmation)

  • Get proof of delivery

  • Perform billing of non-stock items

Business Benefits

  • Offer items to your customer that do not need maintenance in inventory, simplifying data entry for the items

  • Integrate sales of non-stock items fully in sales order processing
processes.name: Sales Order Processing for Non-Stock Material

processes.description:
Sales Order Processing for Sales Kits (31Q)

Overview

Companies often want to sell single products bundled into a sales kit (such as selling a PC together with monitor, keyboard, computer mouse, and so on). Sales kits are commonly used when the products that are part of the sales kit can also be sold independently as single products.

Customers want to have an easy way to use sales kits during order taking and follow up processes without a need to use production BOMs, variant configuration, or other functions that don't fit or are too complex for this use case.

There are multiple ways to process a bill of material in sales. Once you've entered a bill of material in a sales order, the system runs pricing and execution at the following levels:

  • Header level (ERLA): usually used when product is assembled

  • Item level (LUMF): usually used when product isn't assembled

  • Pricing on header level, logistics on item level (CPFH): usually used when product isn't assembled, but the header should carry the total price

  • Logistics on header level, pricing on item level (DISH): usually used for displays if the main item is inventory managed and the components carry the price

Key Process Flow

  • Process sales orders

  • Execute delivery (for example, picking, GI postings)

  • Perform billing

  • Support integration to other E2E processes (currently, sales kits are also supported for free of charge, inquiries, quotations, debit or credit processing, contract management, sales rebates management, and advanced return processing)

Business Benefits

  • Support sales kits with pricing and logistics on the header level or the item level of the sales kits

  • Support sales kits with pricing on header level but with logistics on item level

  • Support sales kits with logistics on header level but with pricing on item level

  • Use sales kits within other scope items
processes.name: Sales Order Processing for Sales Kits

processes.description:
Sales Order Processing with Customer Down Payment (BKJ)

Overview

In this process, you create requests for down payment, record the receipt of the down payment, and create a final invoice after the deduction of the received down payment and a receipt of the final amount due on the invoice. The process uses the billing plan functionality in Sales and Distribution. The integrated process allows the maintenance of proper document flow between the sales and financial transactions.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order and assign billing plan

  • Remove billing block

  • Create billing document

  • Post down payment

  • Create delivery

  • Execute picking

  • Post goods issue

  • Create billing document and down payment clearing

Business Benefits

  • System integrated sales order processing with customer down payment
processes.name: Sales Order Processing with Customer Down Payment

processes.description:
Sales Order Processing with Invoice List and Collective Billing (BKZ)

Overview

With invoice lists, you can send a list that involves several billing documents to a central payer with special discount applicable at specific time intervals. The process starts with the creation of several standard sales orders for different sold-to parties that share the same payer. After individual billing documents are generated and forwarded to Financial Accounting, invoice lists can be created with reference to multiple billing documents for the central payer. Factoring discount and possible taxes are posted to FI.

This scope item describes the usage of standard sales processing for mass-processing billing. For optimization of shipping costs, all sales orders that are delivered to the same customer are packed into one delivery document. For cost optimization, all deliveries due to be invoiced to the same customer are packed into one invoice document. The revenue is posted to accounting accordingly.

Key Process Flow

Sales order processing with invoice lists:

  • Create sales orders

  • Create deliveries

  • Create invoice lists

Sales order processing with collective billing:

  • Create sales orders

  • Create deliveries via collective run

  • Create billing documents via collective run

Business Benefits

  • Optimize cost by collecting customer orders due to be delivered to the same customer in one delivery via a collective run

  • Optimize costs by collecting deliveries to the same customer within one invoice via a collective run
processes.name: Sales Order Processing with Invoice List and Collective Billing

processes.description:
Sales Order Processing with Milestone Billing (7Z1)

Overview

This scope item demonstrates advanced down payment processing by initiating down payment requests, recording the receipt, and creating a final invoice that accounts for the down payments received. The final payment due is then recorded accordingly. This process utilizes the billing plan functionality in sales orders, supports order-related milestone billing with down payment settlement, and ensures seamless integration between sales and financial transactions through a clear and consistent document flow.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order and assign billing plan

  • Create down payment request

  • Remove billing block on milestones

  • Create customer invoice with down payment settlement

Business Benefits

  • Enhance liquidity

  • Enable more effective financial risk management with flexible customer down payment options
processes.name: Sales Order Processing with Milestone Billing

processes.description:
Sales Price Valuation for Retail (5FT)

Overview

Stock valuation for all articles carried in stores and distribution centers is mandatory, as it serves as foundation for balance sheet accounting and legally required financial closing statements. This cost-based stock valuation comes in two flavors: moving average cost (determined by averaging purchase cost in goods receipts) or standard prices (which are fixed during a validity period).

In addition to valuation at cost, many retailers require that valuation at expected sales prices is carried in parallel. This allows retailers to always have up-to-date margin information at hand as a basis for crucial merchandising decisions, such as how to build their assortments. Furthermore, having valuation at cost and sales prices in tandem is required for most planning and reporting activities. Valuation at sales prices can be used for both stores and distribution centers. Sales price values are determined for all article movements (for example goods receipts or goods issues), and stored in the respective article documents.

There are two basic reasons for sales price revaluations of stock:

  • The adjustment of planned sales prices (for example, as a result of a new sales price calculation). An automatic sales price revaluation can be performed to adjust the inventory valuation.

  • Sales price revaluation can be performed manually, due to the changed condition of an article (for example, if the article is outdated, or inventory is damaged).

In both scenarios, sales price revaluation documents are created to support reporting and auditing.

Key Process Flow

  • Run automatic sales price revaluation

  • Create sales price revaluation

  • List sales price revaluation documents

  • Display sales price revaluation document

  • Display stock overview including sales price values

  • Create sales price calculation (optional)

  • Display sales price overview (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Increase cash forecast accuracy by providing visibility to inventory values and allowing relevant merchandising decisions

  • Reduce days in inventory by providing a view into inventory values at all merchandise hierarchy levels so that issues can be resolved quickly

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Sales Price Valuation for Retail

processes.description:
Sales Pricing for Retail (3I4)

Overview

A key aspect of how retailers address the market is their pricing strategy for sales prices. Depending on the desired strategy, sales prices can be planned based on various factors such as purchasing prices and margin goals. Furthermore, sales prices can be specified for all sales channels at different levels, allowing an easy grouping of related stores. You can implement a price strategy that considers the way the merchandise is procured (directly from the supplier or via a distribution center). Thus, you can reflect distribution costs and support selling merchandise from distribution centers to stores (for example, in a franchise scenario).

Mass changes of sales prices can be executed for sets of articles, and multiple organizational levels, also in an automated manner. Retail price management can reflect the retailer’s requirements through roles and authorization of its employees. Once defined, sales prices must be communicated, for example, by transferring the relevant sales prices available to stores and all other sales channels. For more information, see the Store Connectivity – Outbound (3I2) scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • Create price point rounding rules (psychological prices, for example ending in .99), and assign them to distribution chains and price lists

  • Create planned markups for distribution chains and price lists

  • Create sales prices for stores, and wholesale channels (using planned markups, and applying price point rounding)

  • Create sales price calculations for distribution center-to-store distribution

  • Adjust sales prices (absolute adjustment or percentage of current sales price)

  • Create sales price documents and release them in two steps

  • Create sales prices in the background

  • Change, display, or list pricing documents

  • Display price overview (single and generic articles)

Business Benefits

  • Increase revenue share of new customers by executing the company’s pricing strategy aligned with the brand image

  • Increase customer retention by tracking competitor prices and setting prices strategically based on market variations and customer preferences.

  • Increase FTE efficiency by providing transparency across the entire sales price creation process

  • Reduce data integration costs and operational costs by using centrally created sales prices in all adjacent areas (POS, inventory valuation)

  • Increase FTE productivity by automating sales price creation in a batch process

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Sales Pricing for Retail

processes.description:
Sales Processing using Third-Party with Shipping Notification (BD3)

Overview

This scope item enables you to forward orders to third-party vendors who ship the goods directly to customers and then bill you directly. The standard sales order automatically creates a purchase requisition for the materials to be delivered by third-party vendors. Once vendors have sent a shipping notification, a statistical goods receipt can be posted. Once this has taken place, invoices can be created and issued based on the goods receipt quantities.

Key Process Flow

  • Create third-party sales order

  • Convert purchase requisitions to purchase order

  • Approve purchase orders

  • Post statistical goods receipt

  • Create billing document

  • Enter vendor invoice

Business Benefits

  • Reduces stock and cost, thus increasing efficiency

  • Transfer customer requirements directly to external suppliers

  • Invoice from trader to customer, based on quantities from statistical goods receipt

  • Fulfill customer requirements despite material shortage
processes.name: Sales Processing using Third-Party with Shipping Notification

processes.description:
Sales Processing using Third-Party with Variant Configuration (4R6)

Overview

With this process, the standard sales order automatically creates a purchase requisition for the materials to be delivered by third-party vendors.

The purchase requisition is transferred into a purchase order and sent to the vendor.

Once vendors have sent a shipping notification, a statistical goods receipt can be posted. Once this has taken place, customer invoices can be created and issued based on the goods receipt quantities.

After the shipping notification, the invoice receipt is posted based on the invoice sent from vendor.

You can also run the process without shipping notifications. In that case, you can create the customer billing document based on the invoice from the vendor.

Key Process Flow

  • Create third-party sales order with configurable material

  • Convert purchase requisitions to purchase order

  • Post statistical goods receipt

  • Create billing document

  • Enter vendor invoice

Business Benefits

  • Reduce stock and cost, thus increasing efficiency

  • Transfer customer requirements directly to external suppliers

  • Send invoice from trader to customer, based on quantities from supplier invoices

  • Fulfill customer requirements despite material shortage
processes.name: Sales Processing using Third-Party with Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Sales Processing Using Third-Party Without Shipping Notification (BDK)

Overview

This scope item enables you to automatically create a purchase requisition for the materials to be delivered by the third-party vendor. The incoming invoice from the vendor updates the billing quantity. You can only create the customer billing document after entering the invoice from the vendor.

Key Process Flow

  • Create third-party sales order

  • Convert purchase requisition to purchase order

  • Approve purchase order

  • Enter vendor invoice

Business Benefits

  • Reduce stock and cost, increasing efficiency

  • Transfer customer requirements directly to external supplier

  • Base invoice from trader to customer on quantities from supplier invoice

  • Fulfill customer requirements despite material shortage
processes.name: Sales Processing Using Third-Party Without Shipping Notification

processes.description:
Sales Quotation (BDG)

Overview

This scope item starts when requests for quotations are received from customers. Quotations are created in the system and can be either accepted or rejected by customers.

Key Process Flow

  • Create quotation

  • Send quotation to customer

Business Benefits

  • Assure your business partners that you plan to deliver a certain product configuration and quantity at a specific time and price

  • During sales order processing, sales employees can use a variety of sales functions and special quotation functions
processes.name: Sales Quotation

processes.description:
Sales Rebate Processing (1B6)

Overview

This scope item covers the subsequent settlement of rebate conditions agreed upon with customers. You use condition contracts to enter the rebate conditions, together with the process control parameters, business volume selection criteria, and settlement dates for partial and final settlement. You can create condition contracts for one customer or multiple customers.

Customer invoices are used to determine the business volume. In the case of multiple customers, the individual revenue of each customer assigned is used to calculate the settlement values. To pay out rebates to customers, you create settlement documents.

Settlement documents are usually immediately released to accounting. You can also create a condition contract for a two-step settlement procedure to collect and post settlement documents of different condition contracts in one journal entry to accounting.

Furthermore, you can choose how the system determines the taxation for the settlement items.

Key Process Flow

  • Create condition contract for one customer or multiple customers

  • Check business volume (optional)

  • Post accruals (optional)

  • Run partial settlement with reversal of accruals (optional)

  • Run a sell from stock process

  • Check business volume

  • Run final settlement with reversal of accruals

Business Benefits

  • Administer sales rebate agreements centrally

  • Create condition contracts for one or multiple customers

  • Create and settle different types of sales rebate agreements flexibly

  • Derive taxes flexibly

  • Settle customer rebates automatically

  • Provide enhanced transparency and flexibility along the whole contract lifecycle

  • Implement Sales Rebate Processing to cash processes, such as Sell from Stock
processes.name: Sales Rebate Processing

processes.description:
Sales Scheduling Agreement with Consignment (4LZ)

Overview

Customer Consignment is a specific logistics business where the supplier maintains a stock of material at a customer’s location. Consignment goods are stored at the customer location but owned by your company. The customer isn’t obliged to pay for these goods until they remove them from consignment stock. Otherwise, the customer can return consignment goods that aren’t required.

Consignment offers the partners several advantages. Customers store the consignment goods at their own warehouses. Customers can access the goods in the consignment warehouse at any time. They’re billed for the actual quantity taken when they’re removed from the warehouse.

Goods that aren’t required can be returned from the consignment stock to the central warehouse.

In some cases, goods are returned to the customer consignment stock after the consignment issue has already taken place.

This scope item uses scheduling agreements that can be run with or without an external service provider.

Key Process Flow

  • Fill up:

    • Create scheduling agreements for consignment

    • Monitor inbound forecast delivery schedule

    • Monitor material coverage

    • Order schedule lines due for delivery

    • Pick outbound delivery

    • Pack outbound deliveries

    • Post goods receipt

    • Support Batch item

  • Issue:

    • Create consignment issue order

    • Post goods issue

    • Create billing documents

  • Pick-up:

    • Create consignment pick-up order with reference to scheduling agreement

    • Receive goods from ESP/customer

    • Post goods receipt

  • Return:

    • Create consignment return order

    • Post goods receipt

    • Create billing documents

Business Benefits

  • Save costs on inventory for consignor

  • Restock as inventory sells – beneficial for both parties

  • Save time for consignor

  • Use the consignment stock to generate product exposure (especially new or unknown products) for their customers

  • Handle startup and discontinuation of end products
processes.name: Sales Scheduling Agreement with Consignment

processes.description:
Sales Scheduling Agreements (3NR)

Overview

The sales scheduling agreement is an outline agreement between the buyer and supplier. Forecast and JIT (Just-in-Time) delivery schedules are sent via EDI. These delivery schedules contain the delivery dates and quantities. The whole communication is based on cumulative quantities between buyer and supplier.

Planning delivery schedules can be generated to smooth the demand handed over to production.

The shipping specialist creates deliveries based on open quantities in the delivery outbound monitor.

After the completion of picking, the shipping specialist posts goods issue. This posting is the actual recording of the physical quantity that is being shipped to the customer.

With the goods issue posting, revenue is recognized and cost of goods sold is recorded in Financial Accounting.

Advanced shipping notifications are sent via EDI to the buyer.

Once goods are delivered, you can invoice the delivery. An EDI invoice message is sent to the buyer.

Key Process Flow

  • Create, change, and display sales scheduling agreements for component manufacturers

  • Manage cumulative quantities via electronic data interchange (EDI) or manually

  • Manage forecast, Just-in-Time (JIT), and planning delivery schedules

  • Perform ATP checks on the schedule line level within a line item on a scheduling agreement

  • Enable startup and discontinuation of end products

  • Monitor material coverage or compare delivery schedules leveraging analytical capabilities

  • Create delivery, execute picking, post goods issue, and send advanced shipping notification via EDI to buyer

  • Create invoice and send invoice via EDI to buyer

Business Benefits

  • Use sales scheduling agreements to reduce processing times and paperwork within your enterprise

  • Manage various types of delivery schedules (forecast, Just-in-Time (JIT), and planning delivery schedules)

  • Automate receipt and processing of delivery schedules per EDI

  • Update release history

  • Monitor changes

  • Use cumulative quantities between buyer and supplier

  • Search and access scheduling agreements via new Manage Scheduling Agreements application

  • Enable analytical capabilities to manage product demand and compare delivery schedules

  • Integrate with advanced availability check

  • Support startup and discontinuation end products
processes.name: Sales Scheduling Agreements

processes.description:
Sales-Based Rent (3F4)

Overview

With sales-based settlement, you have the ability to create a contract that captures terms and conditions of rental agreements including sales-based rent conditions. In this contract, one or more sales-based rent agreements are defined with valid rules for reporting and sales. These reporting and sales rules are then assigned to rent conditions.

Sales reports may be entered either for individual contracts (single entry) or as a collective entry for multiple contracts. Sales-based rents are then calculated and posted in Financial Accounting.

Key Process Flow

  • Create rental agreement with sales-based conditions

  • Assign reporting and sales rule to payment conditions

  • Enter sales results into sales report

  • Calculate and post results into Financial Accounting

Business Benefits

  • Track sales values to support analysis by sales type and rental agreement

  • Calculate amounts consistently based on the terms and conditions of the agreement, eliminating the use of spreadsheets and external calculation tools

  • Post sales results systematically to Financial Accounting, eliminating the need for manual general ledger postings and interfaces

  • Provide auditable results based on the terms and conditions of the rental agreement

  • Track changes made to the rental agreement

  • Trace changes to the user who made the change
processes.name: Sales-Based Rent

processes.description:
SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText Integration (7W6)

Overview

SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText provides archiving and document access functionality specifically designed for SAP solutions. This integration enables businesses to manage and access SAP-related data and documents efficiently, meeting compliance and regulatory requirements while optimizing IT resources. SAP Archiving and Document Access Core offers features like secure, long-term storage.

Key Process Flow

  • Scenario 1: Attaching Documents to Business Objects

    • Search and display business objects

    • Create business objects

    • Maintain business objects

    • Upload and download attachments

  • Scenario 2: Onboarding of Legacy Documents from Source SAP Systems to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

    • Migrate master data and transactional data from source SAP systems to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition via the Migration Workbench

    • Transform existing SAP Archiving and Document Access Core documents into documents compliant with the SAP Document Management service

    • Attach documents to business objects in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

      Note
      For this scenario, no content copying is required.

Business Benefits

  • Automate provisioning of a document repository during SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition onboarding

  • Choose advanced document management functionality from these scope items:

    • 7WC - SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration (described here)

    • 7WC - SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration

    • 7W6 - SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText Integration

    • 7Y0 - SAP Extended ECM by OpenText Integration

  • Use the Manage Documents (22P) scope item to:

    • Search and display Document Info Records (DIR)

    • Create a Document Info Record (DIR)

    • Add and edit DIR meta data

    • Upload and download attachments

  • Use SAP Archiving and Document Access Core in 2-tier SAP S/4HANA projects as an established solution for archive-compliant file storage (SEC17A-4 certification provided out of the box)

  • Secure the immutability of your files

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item configures the integration with SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText, which requires an additional license.
processes.name: SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText Integration

processes.description:
SAP Ariba Buying (4AI)

Overview

SAP Ariba Buying creates a simple, smart, and elegant purchasing experience that increases user engagement across all spend areas for indirect material procurement. SAP Ariba Buying serves as a central place where you as a buyer can find items across catalogs and shop goods. All spend contracted through supplier-provided catalogs and punch-out catalogs is available to search. Integration with the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system enables a simple and seamless fulfillment experience by providing you with the ability to convert purchasing requests to purchase orders and track the process end to end.

Note

SAP Ariba Buying is only available in a 3-system landscape.

Key Process Flow

  • Search multiple catalogs and create a purchase request in a guided way

  • Configure and manage approval workflows for the employee shopping

  • Publish the purchase requisition to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system

  • Track the progress of the purchased items

Business Benefits

  • Improve the buying experience for the employees

  • Simplify the purchasing process

  • Reduce manual effort for the purchasing department

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

As of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2602 release, this scope item is being phased out and is no longer available to new customers. If you are interested in these capabilities, we recommend choosing the successor scope item 7YM instead.
processes.name: SAP Ariba Buying

processes.description:
SAP Ariba Buying Base Edition (7YM)

Overview

SAP Ariba Buying creates a simple, smart, and elegant purchasing experience that increases user engagement across all spend areas for indirect material procurement. SAP Ariba Buying serves as a central place where you as a buyer can find items across catalogs and shop goods. All spend contracted through supplier-provided catalogs and punch-out catalogs is available to search. Integration with the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system enables a simple and seamless fulfillment experience by providing you with the ability to convert purchasing requests to purchase orders and track the process end to end.

When you select this solution process, SAP takes responsibility for the initial provisioning, integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, and operations. This includes tasks such as technical monitoring of the integrated product.

Note

SAP Ariba Buying is only available in a 3-system landscape.

Key Process Flows

  • Search multiple catalogs and create a purchase request in a guided way

  • Configure and manage approval workflows for the employee shopping

  • Publish the purchase requisition to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system

  • Track the progress of the purchased items

Business Benefits

  • Improve the buying experience for the employees

  • Simplify the purchasing process

  • Reduce manual effort for the purchasing department

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Customers can request this scope item if the functionality fits their business requirements.

processes.description:
SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration (7WC)

Overview

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, many processes require documents such as drawings, specifications, and contract documents. To efficiently manage these documents, you can integrate SAP Content Management Core by OpenText. This integration lets you store business documents in business workspaces that are assigned to the respective business objects in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. You can apply this setup to various business objects with these requirements, such as, for example, purchase contracts.

Key Process Flow

  • Scenario 1: Attaching Documents to Business Objects

    • Search and display business objects

    • Create business objects

    • Maintain business objects

    • Upload and download attachments

  • Scenario 2: Onboarding of Legacy Documents from Source SAP Systems to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

    • Migrate master data and transactional data from source SAP systems to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition via the Migration Workbench

    • Transform existing SAP Archiving and Document Access Core documents into documents compliant with the SAP Document Management service on SAP Business Technology Platform

    • Attach documents to business objects in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Scenario 3: Workspaces for Managing Content Related to Business Objects

    • Create a business object in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

    • Create a workspace in SAP Content Management Core based on the business object type. A workspace is a focused view on a business object.

    • Perform your knowledge work in the workspace of the business object

    • Save your changes: Changes to the business object are stored in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and unstructured content is stored in the SAP Content Management Core workspace.

    Note

    1. Due to limitations in key user extensibility, draft handling is not supported.

    2. Attachments uploaded with the SAP Attachment service in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition are read-only in the business workspace of SAP Content Management Core.

Business Benefits

  • Automate provisioning of a document repository during SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition onboarding

  • Choose advanced document management functionality from these scope items:

    • 7WC - SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration (described here)

    • 7WC - SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration

    • 7W6 - SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText Integration

    • 7Y0 - SAP Extended ECM by OpenText Integration

  • Use the Manage Documents (22P) scope item to:

    • Search and display Document Info Records (DIR)

    • Create a Document Info Record (DIR)

    • Add and edit DIR meta data

    • Upload and download attachments

  • Benefit from best-of-breed solutions by combining SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for business transactions together with SAP Content Management Core by OpenText

  • Integrate SAP Content Management Core into standard SAP Fiori apps in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition via key user extensibility

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item configures the integration with SAP Content Management Core by OpenText, which requires an additional license.
processes.name: SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration

processes.description:
SAP Document Management Service Integration (7XY)

Overview

The integration of SAP Document Management service on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) provides archiving and document access functionality specifically designed for SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud. This enables businesses to manage and access SAP-related data and documents efficiently, meeting compliance and regulatory requirements while optimizing IT resources.

Key Process Flow

Attaching Documents to Business Objects

  • Search and display business objects

  • Create business objects

  • Maintain business objects

  • Upload and download attachments

Business Benefits

During the on-boarding process for SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, the default option is the automatic provisioning of a document repository. Customers who require advanced document management functionality can choose between these scope items:

  1. 7XY - SAP Document Management Service Integration (described here)

  2. 7W6 - SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText Integration

  3. 7WC - SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration

  4. 7Y0 - SAP Extended ECM by OpenText Integration

With the Manage Documents scope item (22P), customers can also use these additional features:

  • Search and display Document Info Records (DIR)

With the SAP Document Management service, customers can integrate any third-party repository that implements the CMIS standard. In addition, it is used in custom projects with SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud and custom BTP apps to access the repository files via API.
Note
In these kinds of projects, the custom BTP app is responsible for ensuring the immutability of files.

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

processes.description:
SAP EWM Integration – Batch Management (2VN)

Overview

This scope item describes the basic integration of batches in the goods receipt process with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). It allows you to create batches in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and in the SAP EWM system as required. When creating batches in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the batch master record is distributed to the EWM system. During the creation of a purchase order, the business user can enter the batch number for each purchase order item. Once a purchase order is available, an inbound delivery is created and replicated to the SAP EWM system. The batch number is distributed as part of the delivery item. If you don't assign a specific batch in the purchase order / inbound delivery, you can search for a fitting batch or create a new one in SAP EWM. In this case, the batch data is transferred to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

Key Process Flow

Option 1: Create batch

  • Create purchase order

  • Create inbound delivery

Option 2: Create and assign batch in SAP EWM

Option 2: Maintain batches for product in SAP EWM (optional)

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create warehouse tasks for putaway

  • Putaway products

Business Benefits

  • Support your high-volume warehouse operations with an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and on-premise SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM)

  • Manage stock on a storage bin level

  • Work with homogeneous partial quantities of a material or product

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that want to integrate with SAP Extended Warehouse Management 9.5 FP02. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Batch Management

processes.description:
SAP EWM Integration – Customer Returns (2VO)

Overview

The process starts with the creation of a return order and a return delivery in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. The delivery is then transferred to SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). In SAP EWM, a goods receipt is posted for the delivery and warehouse tasks are created to put the received goods back to the warehouse. The process ends with the confirmation of the warehouse tasks.

Key Process Flow

  • Create return order

  • Return delivery

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create warehouse tasks for putaway

  • Putaway products

Business Benefits

  • Support your high-volume warehouse operations with an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and on-premise SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM)
