processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Customer Returns

processes.description:
SAP EWM Integration – Delivery-Based Production Integration (2VM)

Overview

In this scope item, you manage the staging and consumption of components from the warehouse to production and the receiving and storage of finished products from production into the warehouse. You trigger material staging that leads to the creation of an outbound delivery that is replicated to SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM).

The corresponding outbound delivery order (ODO) in SAP EWM serves as the main document for material staging. A warehouse clerk creates warehouse tasks for staging with reference to the ODO. The warehouse worker moves the goods to the production supply area and confirms the warehouse tasks. A goods issue is automatically posted by the system. The stock is transferred from the EWM-managed to the production storage location and is now available for consumption.

After the production process is finished, the generation of expected goods receipts (EGR) documents initiates the receiving of the finished goods from production into the warehouse.

Key Process Flow

  • Perform anonymous forecast and MRP

  • Convert to production orders

  • Release production order

  • Stage material for production order

  • Check outbound delivery for production order (optional)

  • Create warehouse tasks for staging

  • Confirm warehouse tasks for staging

  • Confirm production operations

  • Option 1: Generate expected goods receipt documents (Push)

  • Option 2: Generate or delete expected goods receipt (Pull)

  • Create an inbound delivery with reference to Expected goods receipt

  • Post goods receipts

  • Create warehouse tasks for putaway

  • Putaway products

Business Benefits

  • Support your high-volume warehouse operations with an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and on-premise SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM)

  • Manage stock on a storage bin level

  • Integrate warehouse execution tightly with manufacturing operations using a delivery-based production integration

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that would like to integrate with SAP Extended Warehouse Management 9.5 FP02. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Delivery-Based Production Integration

processes.description:
SAP EWM Integration – Inbound Processing from Supplier (2VJ)

Overview

This scope item enables you to order goods from suppliers and to perform the putaway in your warehouse. The process begins with the creation of a purchase order and an inbound delivery in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. If the delivery is relevant to processing in SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), the inbound delivery document is replicated to the SAP EWM system, where it generates an inbound delivery notification that in turn leads to an inbound delivery.

Alternatively, the warehouse can be informed about incoming goods by using an expected goods receipt (EGR) document. You can transfer the expected goods receipt information to the SAP EWM system in one of two ways: pull data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition from within SAP EWM, or push the data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud to SAP EWM. The EGR document contains data for a purchase order and enables you to create an inbound delivery in SAP EWM that is replicated to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Key Process Flow

  • Create purchase order

    • Option 1: Generate expected goods receipt and create an inbound delivery with reference to expected goods receipt

    • Option 2: Create inbound delivery

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create warehouse tasks for putaway products

Business Benefits

  • Support your high-volume warehouse operations with an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and on-premise SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM)

  • Manage stock on a storage bin level

  • Provide flexible variations of the inbound process: Create inbound deliveries in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition or work directly with the purchase orders (represented as Expected Goods Receipt) in SAP EWM

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that want to integrate with SAP Extended Warehouse Management 9.5 FP02. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Inbound Processing from Supplier

processes.description:
SAP EWM Integration – Outbound Processing to Customer (2VK)

Overview

In this process, you ship ordered goods to external customers using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition integrated to SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). This process starts with the creation of a sales order and an outbound delivery. The outbound delivery is replicated to the SAP EWM, where an outbound delivery order is created. This document serves as the starting point for the outbound processing within the warehouse. Warehouse tasks are created with reference to the outbound delivery order and the physical process for picking is executed. During the creation of warehouse tasks, the system determines the location for picking the stock and allocates the stock to the warehouse task. At the end of the process, the goods issue is posted. The goods issue information is transferred from SAP EWM to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. Subsequent process steps such as billing can be executed accordingly.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order

  • Create delivery

  • Check outbound delivery orders

  • Create warehouse tasks manually

  • Pick warehouse orders

  • Post goods issue for outbound delivery order

Business Benefits

  • Support your high-volume warehouse operations with an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and on-premise SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM)

  • Manage stock on a storage bin level

  • Provide on-time delivery performance by automating and integrating warehouse, sales, and distribution processes

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that want to integrate with SAP Extended Warehouse Management 9.5 FP02. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Outbound Processing to Customer

processes.description:
SAP EWM Integration – Stock Transport Orders (2VL)

Overview

Using stock transport orders, you can execute a stock transfer process from one plant to another within the same company code. The process starts with the creation of a stock transport order. A warehouse clerk at the shipping plant monitors the materials due for shipment and creates deliveries as required. Once a delivery is created, the system replicates it to the SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) system, where an outbound delivery order is created. Warehouse tasks are created with reference to the outbound delivery order and the physical process for picking is executed. After the goods issue is posted in the SAP EWM system and sent back to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, an inbound delivery is created and replicated to SAP EWM automatically. This document serves as the starting point for the inbound process in the receiving plant.

Key Process Flow

  • Create stock transport order

  • Create replenishment delivery for stock transport order

  • Check outbound delivery orders

  • Create warehouse tasks manually

  • Pick warehouse orders

  • Post goods issue for outbound delivery orders

  • Check status of stock transfer

  • Post goods receipt

  • Create warehouse tasks for putaway

  • Putaway products

Business Benefits

  • Support your high-volume warehouse operations with an integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and on-premise SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM)

  • Manage stock on a storage bin level

  • Process internal stock transfers efficiently

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is only relevant for customers that want to integrate with SAP Extended Warehouse Management 9.5 FP02. If you requested this scope item, see the set-up instructions in SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Stock Transport Orders

processes.description:
SAP EWM Integration – Warehouse Stock Handling (2YL)

Overview

This scope item covers core warehouse management processes, including scrapping, physical inventory, initial stock upload and their integration into SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The system communicates goods movements such as physical inventory differences, initial stock upload, and ad-hoc posting changes to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition by means of goods movement messages.

  • Perform physical inventory

  • Perform scrapping

  • Manage stock on a storage bin level

processes.name: SAP EWM Integration – Warehouse Stock Handling

processes.description:
SAP Extended ECM by OpenText Integration (7Y0)

Overview

Business processes in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition are based on structured as well as unstructured content - such as contracts, specifications, drawings, and emails. This unstructured content is often essential for driving business processes.

To empower SAP users with best-in-class content management capabilities, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition integrates seamlessly with SAP Extended Enterprise Content Management (ECM) by OpenText.

With SAP Extended ECM by OpenText, you can bridge content silos between SAP and non-SAP business users by bringing content in the context of the business process, even across business applications. Users benefit from built-in capabilities such as viewing services, document generation, integration with Microsoft Office 365, and more – streamlining content creation, editing, and management to accelerate the business processes.

Note
During the onboarding process for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, a document repository is automatically provisioned by default to support content management. Customers who require extended document management functionality can choose between these scope items:

  1. 7Y0 - SAP Extended ECM by OpenText Integration (described here)

  2. 7WC - SAP Content Management Core by OpenText Integration

  3. 7W6 - SAP Archiving and Document Access Core by OpenText Integration

  4. 7XY - SAP Document Management Service Integration

Key Process Flow

For business objects where basic integration as a repository is enabled, the key process flow works as described in SAP Document Management Service Integration (7XY) and Manage Documents (22P).

For business objects with extended integration based on business workspaces, the key process flows are supplemented by:

  • Create business workspaces for business objects automatically or manually

  • Manage content in business workspaces in SAP Fiori with built-in capabilities of SAP Extended Enterprise Content Management by OpenText

  • Upload attachments via SAP Attachment Service and publish in the corresponding business workspace

  • Manage content in business workspaces via Web UI or within another business application where the same business object exists as a digital twin

    Note

    1. Attachments uploaded via SAP Attachment Service in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition are read-only in the business workspace.

    2. Draft handling for business workspaces in Fiori apps is not yet supported due to limitations in key user extensibility.

Business Benefits

  • Improve your business efficiency with seamless access for SAP and non-SAP users to relevant unstructured content, speeding up decision making and task completion across departments and office locations

  • Increase user productivity with built-in tools, like document viewing and generation, Microsoft Office 365 integration, and more, to simplify content handling

  • Benefit from a centralized repository for all business content, regardless of origin

  • Ensure stakeholders work with current and relevant information

  • Achieve unprecedented consistency and control by leveraging SAP data, structures, and authorizations to organize and categorize unstructured content

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item configures the integration with SAP Extended Enterprise Content Management by OpenText, which requires an additional license.
processes.name: SAP Extended ECM by OpenText Integration

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item provides overview pages for the quality technician and the quality engineer. The quality engineer overview page displays important information and tasks related to quality inspection management with a focus on usage decisions (for example, inspection lots without usages decisions, or lots that are ready for usage decision), defects (for example, top defective materials, inspection lots with defects), action limits, quality levels, and quality tasks. The quality technician overview page focuses on processing of the inspection lot, executing the quality inspection, and processing of quality tasks. Further apps for the detailed analysis of the past and current quality situation are provided: You can analyze accepted and rejected inspection lots or inspection characteristics with respect to different KPIs and drill down by accounting for additional parameters. Defects and results history can be analyzed to deduce measures to improve the current quality situation.

Key Process Flow

  • Provide overviews for quality engineer and quality technician
  • Analyze accepted and rejected lots
  • Analyze skipped and non-skipped lots
  • Analyze inspection lots leveraging inspection lot detailed analytics
  • Analyze inspection characteristics
  • Analyze inspection characteristics leveraging inspection characteristic detailed analytics
  • Manage defects
  • Display results history
  • Display quality level history
  • Manage control charts
  • Manage quality tasks

Business Benefits

  • Provide a dashboard of information for quality engineer or quality technician to perform their daily activities smoothly
  • Provide high-level insights for the quality engineer to understand key figures and drill down to act on a variety of inspection-related information
  • Provide tools to analyze the past and current defect situation and inspection results to identify areas for improvement

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation

SAP Fiori Analytical Apps for Sales (1BS)

Overview

For sales and distribution scenarios, this scope item provides key information required for a sales manager or internal sales representative about the different stages of a sales order. The analytical apps provided highlights back orders, demand fulfillment, sales order fulfillment and delivery performance in the sales process. An SAP Fiori overview page is also available that provides the different insight to actions about sales quotations, customer returns, sales order fulfillment and more.

  • View delivery performance and sales order fulfillment as a mix of the table and chart visuals on the sales order process in the Analytical List Pages

  • Understand the key numbers with high-level insights for the sales manager to drill down to action

  • View a strategic and operational overview for the end-to-end sales order processes
processes.name: SAP Fiori Analytical Apps for Sales

processes.description:
SAP Fiori Analytical Apps for Treasury and Risk Management (1MN)

Overview

This scope item provides an overview page for the treasury and risk management related scenarios. The Foreign Exchange Overview page focuses on the financial status, foreign exchange rates, and so on, and how this can be visualized for to allow for better decision making by the treasury managers.

Key Process Flow

processes.description:
Seasons for Retail (6DI)

Overview

Season management forms an important aspect in the product lifecycle for the retail and fashion industry. Retail production is either predetermined or varies according to the manufacturing season. To ensure that the production life cycles are aligned with the demand, the concept of seasons as a temporal unit is used as a base for the production schedule.​

This scope item describes how to set up the season data and assign your defined seasons to products. It explains how the season data is processed for various documents individually.

In the Order-to-Cash process, this scope item starts with a customer order. Season data is assigned to products at a sales order item level. Subsequently, the season data is transferred to the follow-on documents.

In the Procure-to-Pay process, this scope item starts with a purchase order. Season data is assigned to products at a purchase order item level. Subsequently, the season data is transferred to the follow-on documents.

In the Stock Transfer distribution process, this scope item starts with a stock transport order. Season data is assigned to products at a stock transport order item level. Subsequently, the season data is transferred to the follow-on documents.

In the Advanced Intercompany process, season data from the original document is transferred to the follow-on documents. The season information copied to the follow-on documents cannot be changed in those documents.

In the Returns process, the season information is copied from the original document to the returns document.

Season Details

In retail, a season belongs to a season year and can be associated with collections. Collections can in turn be assigned to themes. Each of these entities (season, collection, theme) has a validity period. The existence of these features helps to further classify the offering for a season, apart from providing a concept for each segment of product offering.

The key attributes in product master for season functionality are season year, season, collection, theme.

The season can be maintained in the following three combinations:

  • Season Year and Season

  • Season Year, Season and Collection

  • Season Year, Season, Collection, and Theme

Season

A season is a reporting period in which a special assortment limited to a specific period is merchandised and maintained in a certain way in the information system (for example, Summer season, Christmas season, Easter season, Winter season).

Seasons are crucial for the fashion planning of product design and merchandising.

Collection

Collections are a selection of outfits that designers assemble for the upcoming season. They reflect trends, colors, cuts, and proportions.

Theme

Themes are based on collections in the season hierarchy, and the designers represent a theme that matches them. For example, a period in history, a foreign place, a range of colors, types of fabrics, and so on.

Note

An entity in the hierarchy is dependent on the higher-level entity. For example, a collection must be associated with a season and, likewise, a theme with a collection. Therefore, a collection or a theme can't be defined as a standalone entity in the above hierarchy. Also, a season can't be created without a season year. The timeframe is defined as an elementary attribute in the entities that indicates its applicability in a year (timeframe). You can view the hierarchy from the user menu and define a time period on one of the three levels. A sales period, purchasing period or stock transfer period defines the timeframe within which this entity (season, collection, or theme) is maintained to be valid for the corresponding application documents.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain season data

  • Assign season data to product master

  • Assign season in documents of the Order-to-Cash process

  • Assign season in documents of the Procure-to-Pay process

  • Assign season in documents of the Stock Transfer distribution process

Business Benefits

  • Assign multiple seasons to the product

  • Improve the visibility of the season usage across the entire supply chain

  • Control the Order-to-Cash processes by season, collection and theme

  • Control the Procure-to-Pay process by season, collection and theme

  • Control the Stock Transfer distribution process by season, collection and theme

Overview

In today’s increasingly customer-driven market, products must often be differentiated based on specific requirements such as quality levels, sourcing origins, or distribution strategies. Segmentation enables companies to logically categorize demand, inventory, and supply, supporting tailored planning, sourcing, and fulfillment processes.

At its core, segmentation organizes products and their associated requirements or stock into logical groups based on defined business criteria. These criteria may include product quality, region of origin, market channel, or other relevant characteristics.

Consider a retailer selling the same product across multiple sales channels - eCommerce, retail stores, and wholesale partners. Each channel carries distinct requirements. Through segmentation, the product can be logically divided into channel-specific segments. Incoming sales orders are automatically assigned to the appropriate demand segment based on the sales channel, while inventory is allocated and managed within corresponding stock segments. This ensures that goods designated for eCommerce, retail, or wholesale are planned, sourced, and consumed in alignment with their respective demand.

By precisely matching demand segments with stock segments, segmentation provides end-to-end visibility and control ensuring that supply consistently meets the right market demand across the entire logistics chain.

Key Process Flow

  1. Define segmentation characteristics.
  2. Maintain segmentation structures and segmentation strategies and assign to products.
  3. Maintain segmented stock within distribution centers.
  4. Create segmented requirements in business documents such as sales orders.
  5. Transfer segmentation attributes across the logistics chain to follow-on documents.
  6. Ensure that segmented stock fulfills the corresponding demand segments during fulfillment of the sales order.

Business Benefits

  • Improve demand fulfillment accuracy by fulfilling segmented requirements with segmented supply.
  • Enable precise handling of products.
  • Increase transparency across the supply chain.
  • Improve operational efficiency by ensuring that the correct stock fulfills the correct demand

processes.description:
Self-Billing (4H2)

Overview

In many sell-from-stock processes (for example, the Sell from Stock (BD9) and Sales Scheduling Agreements (3NR) scope items), the financial settlement is handled with a self-billing process with the customer. Instead of issuing an invoice to the customer, the supplier receives self-billing information from the customer, containing the reference document number, received quantity, and value to be credited to the supplier (as well as other information).

This scope item focuses on the sales-related supplier's side of the self-billing processes. The supplier validates the self-billing message received from the customer and simulates results. If there are differences, credit and debit memos are created respectively to settle the account. If the differences exceed the defined tolerances, credit and debit memos are created to show the open amounts. The existing invoices and accounting documents are updated with the transferred self-billing reference number. This ensures that the financial settlement can be automated once payment advice from the customer is received.

As legal requirements differ across regions, SAP provides two main self-billing applications:

  • Self-Billing with Automatic Posting (SBWAP): used in countries where billing documents are automatically created at goods issue.

  • Self-Billing with Invoice Creation (SBINV): used where suppliers must generate an invoice identical to the buyer’s self-billing document.

In Self-Billing with Invoice Creation, an initial invoice does not exist. Instead, it is simulated and created.

To use the processes covered by this scope item, activate the scope item and integrate your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system with SAP Self-Billing Cockpit. SAP Self-Billing Cockpit is available as a licensed product through the SAP Store. You can find it by searching for SAP Self-Billing Cockpit in the store. You can find additional information about the product and its features on the SAP Help Portal on the SAP Self-Billing Cockpit product page.

Key Process Flow

Self-Billing with Automatic Posting

  • Receive self-billing transmission from customers

  • Simulate incoming transmission to detect, any differences and correct internal reference documents

  • Update existing documents

  • Compare tax rate and price

  • Create billing documents (credit or debit memos) and related journal entries in finance

Self-Billing with Invoice Creation

  • Receive self-billing transmission from customers

  • Validate and retrieval data performed on self-billing transmission

  • Simulate billing document creation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition based on transmission

  • Compare the simulation results with the transmission to detect any differences

  • Modify value-added tax (VAT) code in case of tax amount differences (optional)

  • Create billing documents (invoice, credit or debit memos) and related journal entries in finance

Business Benefits

  • Receive self-billing information from customers

  • Simulate incoming information to detect any differences and correct internal reference documents

  • Update existing documents

  • Create billing documents (Invoice and credit debit memos) and related journal entries in finance

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is required if you want to use SAP Self-Billing Cockpit. It provides the manual configuration needed to integrate SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with SAP Self-Billing Cockpit.
processes.name: Self-Billing

Sell from Stock – Consumer Products (5HL)

Overview

The process described in this scope item is a sales process for Consumer Products industry flavored products with seamless integration to the production process described in the Quality Management in Discrete Manufacturing – Consumer Products (5HK) scope item.

The process starts with the creation of customer standard sales orders. A pricing condition may become relevant via the customer hierarchy. When the inventory is decided, the shipping specialist releases the inventory. The inventory is shipped to the customer, and the actual recording of the physical quantity is recorded.

When the goods issue is posted, cost of goods sold is recorded in Financial Accounting.

Once goods are delivered and the proof of delivery (POD) is confirmed by the ship-to-party, you can invoice the delivery. When the invoices are created, an invoice list is created for the central payer for both customers. An EDI invoice message is sent to the buyer when the billing document is saved.

In addition, this scope item allows you to use valuated stock in transit (VSIT) as described in TRM – Accounting (Stock) (5QM). After the goods issue is posted to an outbound delivery, the stock is transferred into VSIT. With the transfer of control of the delivered goods to the customer (for example, based on incoterms and transportation management), the goods issue from VSIT to the customer is posted. At this point in time, revenue and COGS can be recognized.

Key Process Flow

  • Check Batches (Optional)

Sell from Stock (BD9)

Overview

Sell-from-Stock provides a streamlined approach to order fulfillment. The Sell-from-Stock process is designed to efficiently manage and track the sales and shipment of existing inventory. It expedites order fulfillment, accurately recognizes revenue, and maintains precise financial accounting.

The process begins with the creation of a customer and a standard sales order, tailored to the specific customer and their requirements. Upon completion of order picking, the shipping specialist updates the inventory to reflect the outgoing stock. This inventory relief step documents the precise quantity of goods being shipped to the customer. With the posting of the goods issue, revenue is formally recognized, and the cost of goods sold is recorded in the financial accounting system. Once the goods are delivered, the delivery can be invoiced. For preliminary alignment with customers, an optional preliminary billing document can be generated from the billing due list items. This allows for any necessary adjustments before the final billing documents, which customers are expected to settle, are created.

For more information on bundling functionality relevant to IFRS 15, see SAP Note 2524569.

Key Process Flow

  • Create delivery

  • Execute picking

  • Post goods issue

processes.description:
Sell from Stock with Valuated Stock in Transit (5MQ)

Overview

This scope item allows you to use valuated stock in transit (VSIT). After the goods issue is posted to an outbound delivery, the stock is transferred into VSIT. With the transfer of control of the delivered goods to the customer (for example, based on incoterms and transportation management), the goods issue from VSIT to the customer is posted. At this point in time, revenue and COGS can be recognized.

The material movements are done based on configuration settings and are posted automatically through a process orchestration framework, called Value Change Management (VCM).

Key Process Flow

  • Create Sales Order

  • Create Outbound Delivery

  • Create Stock Transfer from physical stock to Valuated Stock in Transit (VSIT)

  • Post Goods Issue from VSIT to Customer

  • Create Customer Invoice

  • Use Value Chain Monitor to keep track of postings

Business Benefits

  • Support the use of existing sales document type, item category, and schedule line category

  • Support legal compliance with event-based revenue recognition (IFRS 15 matching principle)

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item sets up an advanced intercompany process and requires significant additional manual setup steps.

If you requested this scope item, check the set-up instructions in the SAP Signavio Process Navigator.
processes.name: Sell from Stock with Valuated Stock in Transit

processes.description:
Serial Number Management in Logistics (BLL)

Overview

This scope item enables you to serialize and thus differentiate between individual material items. The history of serialized items enables tracking during goods movements. In this way, it's possible to carry out root cause analysis for any issues with materials.

Key Process Flow

  • Assign serial number profiles and serializing procedures

  • Create serial number history

  • Manage status for serialized items

  • Maintain settings for physical inventory

Business Benefits

  • Identify and track individual material items in in-house operations

  • Improve inventory overview

  • Improve insight into logistic processes
processes.name: Serial Number Management in Logistics

processes.description:
Service and Material Procurement – Project-Based Services (J13)

Overview

This scope item covers all relevant procurement processes for the professional services scenario. It includes several possible subprocesses:

  • Service procurement: The company orders an external service. The external service provider confirms the purchase order and performs the service. The supplier then posts the expenses back, and the company creates and processes a supplier invoice.

  • Material procurement for consumption: A customer or internal project requests a consumption material. The company creates a purchase order and sends it to the supplier. The supplier sends the material to the company, and the company checks the goods receipt. Finally, the company creates a supplier invoice and pays it.

  • Procurement for third-party order processing: The purchaser at the ordering company orders a material from a supplier for an end customer. The supplier ships the material directly to the end customer.

Key Process Flow

  • Create purchase requisition

  • Create and approve purchase order

  • Send purchase order to supplier

  • Confirm service from supplier

  • Post expenses of service

  • Create supplier invoice

Procure material for consumption:

  • Create purchase requisition

  • Create and check purchase order

  • Send purchase order to supplier

  • Post and check goods receipt

  • Create supplier invoice

Procure for third-party order processing:

  • Create purchase requisition

  • Create and check purchase order

  • Send purchase order to supplier

  • Post and check goods receipt

  • Create supplier invoice

Create contracts:

  • Create contract from scratch

  • Create contract based on purchase requisition

Business Benefits

  • Optimize and streamline procurement process to professional services scenario requirements

  • Simplify procure-to-pay, invoice-to-pay

  • Integrate to the SAP supplier network natively (SAP Ariba Network)
processes.name: Service and Material Procurement – Project-Based Services

processes.description:
Service Contract (21R)

Overview

Lease contracts describe contractual agreements between two partners: the lessor and the lessee. The lessor owns an asset, whereas the lessee has a right to use this asset during the period agreed in the lease contract. The lessee pays lease payments for the use of the asset, as agreed upon in the lease contract.

This scope item helps you standardize and automate your lease service credit contract management activities for real estate, as well as for machinery, equipment, vehicles, and computer hardware.

You can easily create new contracts and execute periodic postings for existing contracts.

You can change the supplier for existing contracts, as well as run reports of existing contracts as part of your daily business.

You can create reminder rules for every contract, for example, to check the contract conditions, the contract term, or the renewal options, helping you to save time and effort and free up capacity for more strategic tasks.

Leveraging the reporting functions enables you to make better and more informed lease management decisions.

Key Process Flow

  • Create service contract and add valuation rule

  • Perform period posting for service contract and adjustment (optional)

  • Terminate service contract

  • Execute reports for contract management, valuation management, accounting, and adjustments

Business Benefits

  • Accelerate leasing processes

  • Standardize and automate your recurring lease administration activities

  • Gain full control and visibility of leases and critical dates

  • Monitor critical dates on your leases, such as lease notifications and renewals

  • Improve decision making

  • Help ensure compliance to the latest financial reporting standards, such as the new lease accounting standards IFRS 16 and FASB ASC 842
processes.name: Service Contract

processes.description:
Service Contract Management (3MO)

Overview

This scope item covers the creation of service contracts in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Service contracts are outline agreements that define services offered for a period and represent long-term service agreements with customers. Service contracts are billed on a periodic billing plan. Via price adaptations for service contracts, different prices within the contract periods are possible.

Customer-specific price agreements can be defined and handled within service contracts. Service contract determination is enabled for service orders that correspond with the service contract in predefined criteria – in this case, contract and price details from determined service contract are considered.

Customers can define service level agreements and maintain service and response profiles in service contracts.

If desired, you can renew an expiring service contract automatically for a predefined period at a predefined date. You can also manually renew service contracts and items. As part of the change process, you can change the sold-to party of a service contract and create a service contract automatically.

Furthermore, you can enable ad-hoc billing, a structured method of service contract billing that allows you to define billing values and billing dates manually.

This scope item includes situation handling for service contracts. Situation handling is functionality in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition that lets you bring certain circumstances (situations) to the attention of a relevant group of business users.

Key Process Flow

  • (Optional) Use the service contract template for creating service contracts

  • (Optional) Create service contract with configurable product

  • Create service contract and add service contract items with periodic and/or ad-hoc billing plan

  • Maintain product list and create price agreements for service product

  • Adapt service contract prices

  • Release service contract and service contract items

  • Create billing request lines (only valid for ad-hoc billing)

  • Create billing document request based on billing request lines from billing plan

  • Create invoice

  • Use the following service contract change processes:

    • Change sold-to-party in service contract (optional)

    • Renew entire service contract manually (optional)

    • Renew service contract item manually (optional)

    • Renew service contract item automatically (optional)

    • Cancel service contract or service contract item (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Increase service revenue by offering a flexible service contract management process

  • Increase service revenue by building long-term relationships with customers for additional recurring services

  • Provide guided service contract changes to keep your customer contracts up to date

  • Support compliance with SLAs by managing contracts of varying complexity over the entire life cycle

  • Generate an external view of your business transactions
processes.name: Service Contract Management

processes.description:
Service Contract Management with Advanced Variant Configuration (6GU)

Overview

This scope item covers service contract creation with configurable products using advanced variant configuration (AVC) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Customers can create service contracts with configurable products. Configurable products can be added as standard contract items, price adaptation items, and ad-hoc billing items. If you add a configurable product as a service contract item, it's required to configure the product that has been added. To configure the product, the customer navigates to the configuration user interface and selects the characteristics and characteristic values that are defined in the product master data. By default, the status of the configurable product is incomplete. When the product configuration is complete, the configuration status is changed to released. Depending on the product definition, the selection of characteristics and characteristic values of a configurable product can impact the price of a contract item based on the defined variant conditions.

After creating configurable products in service contracts, customers can follow the process of service contract management of the Service Contract Management (3MO) scope item to finalize service contract relevant steps.

Key Process Flow

  • (Optional) Use the Service Contract Template with Configurable Products for Creating Service Contracts

  • Create Service Contract with Configurable Products

  • Configure Item in Configuration User Interface

  • Check Net Value and Status of Configurable Product

Business Benefits

  • Increase flexibility in service contract product offerings with product configuration support ​

  • Offer more complex service contract products​
processes.name: Service Contract Management with Advanced Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Service Entry Sheet Based Accruals (63L)

Overview

This scope item lets you calculate and post accruals based on service entry sheets submitted against lean service purchase orders. You can replicate the lean service purchase orders as accrual objects based on service entry sheets submitted, but not yet approved, to propose the accrual amount. You can then review the accrual amount and generate periodic accrual journal postings and reverse the documents in the next period.

Key Process Flow

  • Display automatically generated accrual objects

  • Run job to propose accrual amount

  • Review accrual amount

  • Run job to post accruals to general ledger

Business Benefits

  • Automate the accrual process

  • Provide more accurate accrual amount for lean service procurement scenario

  • Improve financial process governance

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is designed for customers with a business need for period-end closing to post lean service purchase order accruals based on service entry sheets. Configuration settings are provided to tailor the functions to the individual requirements.
processes.name: Service Entry Sheet Based Accruals

processes.description:
Service Management with Advanced Variant Configuration (6GS)

Overview

With this scope item, customers can configure specific products and materials in service orders, service order templates, and service quotations. Configurable products allow users to select options for the service order item. The options are predefined as characteristics in the product master data before usage.

Prices can vary for different options. The configured options and their prices are visible to the user.

Before you can maintain configurable items, the service order or service order template must be in place. The results of the configuration and the pricing are transferred back to the service order.

This scope item uses advanced variant configuration (AVC).

Key Process Flow

  • Configure characteristics

  • Check price details

Business Benefits

  • Increase flexibility with the ability to configure service items based on variants.
processes.name: Service Management with Advanced Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Service Monitoring and Analytics (43B)

Overview

This scope item helps the customer service manager ensure on-time service delivery by monitoring incomplete or overdue service orders. This scope item also helps to compare the average repair time per product.

The customer service manager must also know how many service contracts will expire soon. The customer service manager can compare and view the service contracts from various dimensions, such as total contract value and profit margin. The customer service manager can also trigger actions to renew them.

This scope item helps to display and monitor a variety of issues in service contracts and service orders. It supports a detailed analysis of the issues by displaying the results by issue, service transaction, country, region, and sales organization. You can use various chart types, mini charts, and filters for analyzing, monitoring, and discovering additional information, and focusing on certain data, such as service transactions.

The manager can use the flexible analysis apps to analyze service orders and service-contract-related KPIs in multidimensional reports.

In addition, the service contracts dashboard helps the customer service manager to analyze the contracts in further detail.

As a sales manager, you can use the Order to Cash dashboard to analyze incoming and open service orders.

Key Process Flow

  • Review service contracts for expiry or renewal

  • Review service contracts by contract value and profit margin

  • Verify situation handling alerts for expiring service contracts

  • Review overdue service orders

  • Review incomplete service orders

  • Monitor average repair time by product

  • Use flexible combination of dimensions to analyze service contracts and service orders

  • Analyze service order and contract issues

  • Review order-to-cash dashboard – Incoming sales and service

Business Benefits

  • Provide a graphical overview of key service process data to gain insights into the current service situation

  • Display detailed information that helps to examine and analyze data across various dimensions

  • Provide an overview of service order or contract related issues

  • Combine sales and service data in the Order to Cash dashboard, providing a more holistic view of the business
processes.name: Service Monitoring and Analytics

processes.description:
Overview

This scope item covers service orders creation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. After planning, the service order is released for execution. Once the service order line items are released, a purchase requisition is created automatically for non-stock spare parts.

Service confirmations are posted against the service order line items. Based on the confirmation, time-sheet entries and expenses incurred are posted. Procurement costs can be copied into the confirmation from the supplier invoice or from the purchase order, so that the customer can be billed (Time & Material Service).

When a service order or confirmation is released for billing, a billing document request is created to invoice the customer.

The confirmation can be manually canceled, thus canceling the succeeding invoice and the billing document request (BDR).

Service orders can also be created automatically in the background as a follow-on from preceding processes, such as Service Quotations (4GA) or Recurring Services (4X5).

Key Process Flow

  • Create a service order (creation of service order via service order template optional)
  • Configure service products using Advanced Variant Configuration (AVC) (optional)
  • Assign service team (optional)
  • Create a service order automatically from service quotation (optional)
  • Simulate an ATP check for the stock service parts during creation (optional)
  • Release service order line items (optional)
  • Perform credit check (optional)
  • Create material reservation for the spare part either early reservation (optional) or at release (optional)
  • Use a product proposal if a reference object (equipment, product) is maintained with a BOM (optional)
  • Change service order (optional)
  • Release service order
  • Check planned cost and revenue (optional)
  • Perform output management (email or print) (optional)
  • Receive confirmation against the service order
  • Add unplanned items in service confirmation (optional)
  • Post the time sheet against the service technician and incurred expenses automatically based on the confirmation (creating inter-company invoice is supported in inter-company scenario)
  • Cancel the confirmation along with the follow-up documents (optional)
  • Release the service order (for fixed price services) or confirmation (for time and material services) for billing and automatic creation of billing document request
  • Copy procurement costs automatically in the confirmation, based on posted supplier invoice or purchase order for billing to the customer for time and material services
  • Create a billing document from the billing document request for invoicing the customer
  • Post revenues automatically against the service order line item (event-based revenue recognition is supported for fixed-price or time and material orders)
  • Analyze service order fulfillment (optional)
  • Run period-end overhead calculation for service orders (optional) if not using event-based overhead calculation

Business Benefits

  • Provide the functionality for planning and execution of field services
  • Post directly in the universal journal, meaning that no settlement of revenue carrying cost objects is required
  • Post time sheet and expenses automatically based on the confirmation (intercompany scenario supported)
  • Link procurement process (for non-stock spares or external workforce procurement) with service order execution
  • Post revenue automatically based on customer invoice (with event-based revenue recognition for fixed price or T&M Services)

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Service Order Management and Monitoring

processes.description:
Service Order Processing with SAP Field Service Management (49X)

Overview

This scope item describes end-to-end business scenarios between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition service order or repair order processing and SAP Field Service Management.

Once a service or repair order is created and released in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, a corresponding service call is created in SAP Field Service Management. An activity is created for each service item in the service or repair order, and spare part items are replicated as reserved materials.

An activity is assigned to a technician on the planning board in SAP Field Service Management. When the activity is released, the technician is automatically updated in the corresponding service/ repair order item in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

When confirmations such as efforts, expenses, or materials are approved in SAP Field Service Management, a service or repair confirmation is created and automatically completed in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Key Process Flow

  • Create service order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and release it to SAP Field Service Management

  • Create service order with items in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when service call or activity is created in SAP Field Service Management (optional)

  • Navigate from an SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition service order to SAP Field Service Management (optional)

  • Update service order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when service call or activity is updated in SAP Field Service Management (including planned start and end date, and executing service employee)

  • Rerelease service orders after changes from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to SAP Field Service Management.

  • Update execution status from SAP Field Service Management to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition service order

  • Create a completed service confirmation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when efforts, expenses, and spare parts are approved in SAP Field Service Management

  • Support unplanned effort, expense, and material confirmations from a service technician on a service activity.

  • Handle reassignment of service technician in SAP Field Service Management and update of the same on service order item level

  • Handle duplicate activities in SAP Field Service Management and update of the same on service order item level

  • Complete a service order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and technically complete the corresponding service call in SAP Field Service Management

  • Assign attachment to the service call or activity in the SAP Field Service Management system and replicate it to the corresponding service order (item) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

  • Update service call ID and activity ID in service order transaction history after replication

Business Benefits

  • Optimize your field service processes with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition service or repair order processing integration.

  • Ensure a seamless, fast, and flexible delivery of field services

  • Provide more efficient customer services

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

To use this scope item, you need an additional license to use SAP Field Service Management.
processes.name: Service Order Processing with SAP Field Service Management

processes.description:
Service Procurement with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass (4R2)

Overview

This scope item covers the creation and approval of purchase orders for services. Alternatively, the process can be triggered via the creation of a purchase requisition, which is later converted to a purchase order.

The service fulfillment can be steered and monitored with the supplier side statement of work, supplier time sheets, and service entry sheets. Afterwards, the invoicing process is triggered.

The scope item covers standard service items and can be conducted with different optional steps. Service procurement using free text description of services in procurement documents is also supported.

Key Process Flow

  • Manage purchase requisitions

  • Manage purchase orders

  • Manage supplier confirmations for services and start and end dates

  • Manage statement of work for services requested

  • Manage service provider time sheets for services performed

  • Manage service entry sheets

  • Manage invoices

Business Benefits

  • Provide efficient and cost-effective streamlined procurement processes as collaboration between buyers, purchaser, and suppliers

  • Ensure highly automated processes for the service procurement

  • Reduce manual effort greatly

  • Perform real-time monitoring of the service fulfillment

  • Monitor purchase order items with analytical list page

  • Handle service provider on-boarding and service task management in scope and service

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Software licenses in addition to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition license are required.
processes.name: Service Procurement with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass

processes.description:
Service Quotation (4GA)

Overview

This scope item covers the service quotation process in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The service quotations are used to provide legally binding offers with fixed conditions made to a customer for the performance of services.

Customer Service managers may use quotations to provide cost estimates before placing an order. Both Time and Material (T&M) and Fixed Price cost estimates are supported with validity period. The validity period of the service quotation can be changed by the customer service manager with an option to carry out repricing as per the new validity.

Upon finalizing the service quote with required services and price offered, the customer service manager can either print or generate the quote as a PDF, then attach it to an email to be sent to customer for negotiation.

The service quote can then be set to Accepted or Rejected. Finally, the service quote acceptance triggers the automatic creation or update of service orders as a follow-on process

Key Process Flow

  • Create or change service quotation

  • Include service items, external service Items, and pick-from-stock items, service bundles (fixed-price/time and material), mixed service bundle (both fixed-price and time and material items within T&M quotation) in quotation items

  • Send service quotation to customer

  • Review service quotation (change or update)

  • Attach necessary documents in quotation

  • Accept service quotation

  • Trigger service order (automatically)

  • Reject service quotation or reject Items in quotation with a rejection reason

Business Benefits

  • Share cost estimates for the services chosen by the customer (both time-and-material and fixed-price)

  • Negotiate, accept, or reject the quotation with reason (including partial acceptance)

  • Support repricing of the quotation after the expiry of validity period

  • Provide options to customer through output control to either print or generate the quote as a PDF and attach it to an email

  • Support automatic creation of the service order based on service quotation acceptance
processes.name: Service Quotation

processes.description:
Overview

Improve your company's product engineering, sales, and manufacturing performance with SAP software for integrated variant configuration and classification. Enable your business process to handle highly individualized products in sales and manufacturing.

A comprehensive simulation environment supports state-of-the-art configuration, sophisticated analysis of your configurable products, and real-time integration to the configurable BOM Explosion. Get support from integrated requirements management.

Key Process Flow

  • Create characteristics for class (to be used for variant configuration)
  • Create class (to be used for variant configuration)
  • Assign class to product
  • Create variant table
  • Maintain variant table content
  • Create configuration profile
  • Create and assign grouping
  • Create constraint net
  • Create and assign high-level dependencies
  • Create super BOM
  • Add stock item
  • Add class node item
  • Add low level dependencies
  • Simulate configurable BOM
  • Create and assign high-level dependencies
  • Perform simulation and root cause check

Business Benefits

  • Reduce costs and optimize usability with sophisticated variant configuration
  • Increase sales force efficiency by higher tool support within order configuration to allow the sales force to focus on selling
  • Increase modeling efficiency for new configured product modeling by effective simulation of new product variants and options
  • Reduce time to market for new products by advanced variant configuration modeling and effective simulation of new product variants and options
  • Establish efficient collaboration between requirements management and modeler

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Set Up Configurable Model Using Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Shareholding Management – Group Ledger IFRS (5WG)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for shareholding management – group ledger IFRS, you can use an additional valuation area other than your operational valuation area according to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS 9) phase I (Classification and Measurement).

Key Process Flow

  • Post to General Ledger

  • Perform Key Date Valuation

Business Benefits

  • Generate all general ledger postings

  • Update the general ledger according to IFRS 9 phase I (Classification and Measurement)
processes.name: Shareholding Management – Group Ledger IFRS

processes.description:
Shareholding Management – Group Ledger US GAAP (5WH)

Overview

By activating parallel valuation for Shareholding Management – Group Ledger US GAAP, you can use an additional valuation area besides your operational valuation area according to US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (US GAAP).

Key Process Flow

  • Post to General Ledger

  • Perform Key Date Valuation

Business Benefits

  • Generate all postings for the general ledger

  • Update the general ledger according to US GAAP

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

All starter, demo, and trial systems, by default, are set up with group ledger IFRS. This scope item is therefore excluded. Customers can decide to use this scope item in their systems based on the selected scope bundle.
processes.name: Shareholding Management – Group Ledger US GAAP

processes.description:
Shareholding Management (5WF)

Overview

The scope item helps you to better manage your shareholding instruments. You can automate labor-intensive processes, such as payment handling and accounting postings, giving you more time to focus on value-added activities. You can manage operational and accounting requirements.

The current scope covers the processes to create securities account and security class, and to purchase, bookkeep, and recognize dividends of and sell a shareholding transaction.

Key Process Flow

  • Create security account and class

  • Create shareholding purchase transaction

  • Set settlement status

  • Maintain and post cash dividend

  • Create and post corporate action

  • Perform period-end closing

  • Create shareholding sale transaction

  • Perform reporting

Business Benefits

  • Review the status for shareholding instruments easily

  • Support the management of shareholding, including creation of security class and security accounts, and the transactions, payments, recognition of dividend, and so on

  • Make better operational and strategic decisions using the comprehensive reporting and analysis tools

  • Improve internal operational compliance
processes.name: Shareholding Management

processes.description:
Sites for Retail (3I3)

Overview

This scope item describes how location master data can be maintained. In Retail, a location is typically referred to as a site and comes in one of two variations: store or distribution center.

A store serves the main purpose of presenting and selling merchandise to consumers. To enable this, additional planning and operational processes are needed, for example goods receipt and physical inventory counting. The task of a distribution center is handling the transfer of merchandise from external suppliers to stores along the supply chain as efficiently as possible. Parameters to be considered include, cost for procurement, transportation, and storing, as well as stock level agreements for stores, among others.

Depending on the detailed needs of a retailer, site-related processes need to be configured. The solution described in this scope item provides an easy way to maintain respective site data. Like other organizational data, sites are maintained using SAP Central Business Configuration.

For ease of maintenance purposes, a defaulting mechanism prefills many parameters, so they don't need to be maintained by the user.

Having consistent and high-quality site master data is crucial for ensuring reliable and smooth operation. SAP supports this by providing a quality assurance environment for testing and by ensuring consistent data replication to the productive environment.

Key Process Flow

  • Maintain business partner and master data for the site and test reference site in quality assurance environment

  • Copy business partner and master data from reference site

  • Transport tested data to the productive environment

  • Manage site blockings

  • Make ad-hoc changes of certain data in the productive environment

Business Benefits

  • Reduce data errors during site creation by using templates and reference sites

  • Increase efficiency of master data creation for locations by automating data generation

  • Increase data accuracy by leveraging best practice process content

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item is part of a bundle that requires a license for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail, fashion, and vertical business and the activation of business functions. This bundle includes several scope items that need to be activated together when you activate the bundle. To request the activation of the retail bundle from SAP cloud operations, create a ticket for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV.

As a prerequisite, configure your system using SAP Central Business Configuration as configuration environment. Projects using the Configure Your Solution configuration environment are not supported.
processes.name: Sites for Retail

processes.description:
Overview

Critical business situations, such as upcoming deadlines and pending confirmations, can negatively impact your business if users aren’t aware of them and don’t take action. Situation Handling speeds up the resolution of urgent issues by detecting them automatically, informing the right users, and proposing follow-up actions. With its monitoring capabilities, you can optimize your business processes by tracking the life cycle of situations from alert to solution.

With the standard framework, you can select from a wide range of predefined use cases and adapt them to your business requirements. By using Intelligent Situation Automation on SAP Business Technology Platform, you benefit from automatic resolution of situations.

With the extended framework, you can model your own situations from scratch by reusing existing application artefacts.

Key Process Flow

Standard Framework

  • Determine responsible users using integrated Responsibility Management (1NJ), based on team structures and rules
  • Adapt predefined use cases to fit your business needs
  • Receive situation notifications via SAP Fiori launchpad, email, in-app messages, or the My Situations app
  • Navigate from notifications to relevant business apps to view and act on situations
  • Monitor the life cycle and handling of situations
  • Collect situation data to support automated situation resolution (where applicable)

Extended Framework

  • Determine responsible users using integrated Responsibility Management (1NJ), based on team structures and rules
  • Model custom use cases
  • Receive situation notifications via SAP Fiori launchpad, email, or the My Situations – Extended app
  • Navigate from notifications to the My Situations – Extended app to view and act on situations
  • Monitor the life cycle and handling of situations

Business Benefits

  • Bring urgent situations to the attention of the right users
  • Provide users with contextual information and proposed actions in one place
  • Benefit from predefined use cases across lines of business
  • Create custom use cases with the extended framework
  • Get insight into the life cycle of situations and optimize business processes
  • Collect situation data for advanced analytics
  • Lay the foundation for automating the resolution of business situations with Intelligent Situation Automation on SAP Business Technology Platform

Exclude from Default Activation

Reason for Excluding from Default Activation
processes.name: Situation Handling

processes.description:
Solution Order – Advanced Product Bundling (6BU)

Overview

Solution bundles in Solution Order Management help customers evolve their business from selling single products to offering holistic solutions.

It enables selling different types of products in a single document and provides an overview of the fulfillment through individual follow-up documents.

The solution bundle can include groups of sales, services, subscription products​, and projects. It may also include configurable sales and service products.​ With an intuitive progress view, situation handling, and cross-object navigation, customers always have an overview of the fulfillment status of the different solution order items.

Key Process Flow

  • Create a solution order with a bundle product

  • Configure the solution bundle and its components (using scope items Set Up Configurable Model Using Variant Configuration (22T) or Set Up Advanced Solution Bundle (6W9))

  • Maintain the solution bundle items

  • Release the bundle item and orchestrate solution orders by following the Solution Order Management (4GT) and Solution Order Management with Advance Variant Configuration (6HY)

  • Create solution invoice

Business Benefits

  • Manage changes centrally for an easy user experience

  • Trigger activities that are related to the fulfillment of individual items

  • Determine profitability for the complete solution order and individual items
processes.name: Solution Order – Advanced Product Bundling

processes.description:
Solution Order Management (4GT)

Overview

Solution Order Management helps customers to evolve their business from selling single products to offering holistic solutions: they can manage complex solutions of physical goods, services, projects, and subscriptions in an integrated end-to-end order. With an intuitive progress view, situation handling, and cross object navigation, customers always have an overview of the fulfillment status of the different solution order items. Solution Order Management also comes with embedded pricing, omni-channel convergent billing, and seamless integration into revenue recognition and controlling. This gives customers a consolidated financial view of their solution portfolio. Solution Order Management is supported by a built-in analytics dashboard.

This process can be combined with the respective solution order management for configurable products (6HY).

Key Process Flow

  • Create solution orders and add sales, service, subscription, project, and service contract items

  • Release sales, service, subscription, project, and service contract items

  • Execute solution order orchestration followed by the Service Order Management and Monitoring (3D2), Service Contract Management (3MO), Subscription Management with Sales Billing (57Z) or Sales Order Management (BD9,BDN,BD3,BDK, 2EQ) scope items

  • Create invoice

Business Benefits

  • Use the solution order to act as the central document to the customer, combining sales, service orders, subscription, projects, and contracts for the specific customer offering

  • Determine profitability for the complete solution order and for individual items

  • Create combined invoices

  • Trigger activities that are related to the fulfillment of the individual items

  • Manage changes centrally for an easy user experience
processes.name: Solution Order Management

processes.description:
Solution Order Management with Advanced Variant Configuration (6HY)

Overview

Solution Order Management helps customers to evolve their business from selling single products to offering holistic solutions: they can manage complex solutions of physical goods, services, projects, and subscriptions in an integrated end-to-end order. With an intuitive progress view, situation handling, and cross object navigation, customers always have an overview of the fulfillment status of the different solution order items. Solution Order Management also comes with embedded pricing, omnichannel convergent billing, and seamless integration into revenue recognition and controlling. This gives customers a consolidated financial view of their solution portfolio. Solution Order Management is supported by a built-in analytics dashboard.

This scope item is a variant of the standard solution order management process in the Solution Order (4GT) scope item, which also supports configurable sales, service, and service contract items. It can be used with 4GT.

Key Process Flow

  • Create solution orders and add sales, service, subscription, project, and service contract items

  • Release configurable sales, service, and service contract items

  • Execute solution order orchestration followed by Make-to-Order Production with Variant Configuration (‏1YT‏), Service Management with Advanced Variant Configuration (6GS), and Service Contract Management with Advanced Variant Configuration (3MO/6GU)

  • Create invoice

Business Benefits

  • Use the solution order to act as the central document to the customer, combining sales, service orders, subscription, projects, and contracts for the specific customer offering

  • Manage changes centrally for an easy user experience

  • Allow for these ordered products to create combined invoices

  • Trigger activities that are related to the fulfillment of the individual items

  • Determine profitability for the complete solution order and individual items
processes.name: Solution Order Management with Advanced Variant Configuration

processes.description:
Solution Order Quotation Management with SAP CPQ (6BV)

Overview

This scope item enables seamless data integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP CPQ. You can create customer and product master data in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (including pricing). You can then use this data in SAP CPQ to create a quotation for physical products (including single-level configurable products) and service contract products (including configurable service contract products). After the customer accepts the quote, you can send it to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. A solution order is created to capture the order. Follow-up documents such as a sales order and service contract are automatically triggered from the solution order creation.

Key Process Flow

  • Create solution quotation in SAP CPQ

  • Place order in SAP CPQ

  • Review solution order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

Business Benefits

  • Integrate with business partner and product

  • Integrate with pricing and product configuration via SAP Variant Configuration and Pricing

  • Integrate with solution order seamlessly

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Customer must license SAP CPQ.
processes.name: Solution Order Quotation Management with SAP CPQ

processes.description:
Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing (4BL)

Overview

Connect your SAP S/4HANA digital core for sourcing and procurement to SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba Sourcing. This connection provides access to intuitive RFX tools for requests for information, proposals, and reverse auctions. You can connect with over two million companies, discover suppliers quickly and easily, and automate and adjust negotiation procedures.

Ensure event success by using the SAP Ariba Sourcing support desk and event-day management assistance. Evaluate the total cost impact of your sourcing decisions. Reduce the time and effort spent on administrative tasks. Handy wizards and tools help you launch events, collaborate, and negotiate. Choose from a variety of suppliers based on their profile information, ratings, and assessments. This helps you to develop a large supply base and backup sources, reducing supplier risks. Once you subscribe to SAP Ariba Sourcing, you can simply activate this scope item with guided configuration.

This scope item uses SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network for the integration. It covers the full functional scope of the Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing (1A0) scope item.

Key Process Flow

  • As a purchaser:

    • Create a request for quotations (RFQ) for purchase requisitions from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition that don’t automatically find a single source of supply

    • Send the RFQ to the SAP Ariba Sourcing application to trigger a sourcing request

  • As a sourcing manager:

    • Access your worklist and convert sourcing requests into sourcing projects

    • Monitor sourcing projects that result in (reverse) auctions, or requests for quotations, and provide these to suppliers on SAP Business Network

    • Monitor suppliers’ responses

    • Award one or more bids in SAP Ariba Sourcing

  • Send awarded bids automatically to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition where forwarded bids, purchase orders, or operational contracts are created

Business Benefits

  • Enjoy fast time-to-value and low total cost of ownership with cloud-based delivery.

  • Improve project management and compliance with advanced, automated workflow and approval routines.

  • Simplify and accelerate your configuration by taking advantage of built-in SAP Best Practices that guide you through the integration process step-by-step.

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

This scope item requires an additional license for SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing.
processes.name: Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing

processes.description:
Standard Cost Calculation (BEG)

Overview

This process enables you to update standard costs for products as part of annual operations planning. The costs are entered manually, and the costing run is created and executed.

This scope item also supports parallel standard costing.

Key Process Flow

  • Create costing run

  • Execute costing run

processes.name: Standard Cost Calculation

processes.description:
Statistical Sales Conditions (34B)

Overview

If you want to see statistical values such as warranties and cash discounts in Margin Analysis reports, align with your Sales and Distribution colleagues so that they include such statistical SD conditions in the pricing procedure. The scope item 34B has to be activated. Don’t forget to select extension ledger 0C as well when executing Margin Analysis reports.

After activation of this scope item, the system will calculate and transfer the values of statistical sales conditions from SD Sales and Distribution to Margin Analysis. The values are written to extension ledger 0C using General Ledger accounts. The account key is assigned to a statistical condition, posted to the G/L, and set as relevant for account determination in the SD pricing procedure. For example, a statistical cash discount is posted to the extension ledger during billing.

To use the functionality for other statistical SD condition use cases such as warranties and cash discounts, you make the following settings for the price condition: the price condition has been set for statistics only, that is, you have selected the Statistics indicator; an Account key that defines two accounts (the Accruals key is not considered).

Various self-service configuration steps are also available for your convenience.

Key Process Flow

  • Create sales order

  • Create delivery

  • Execute picking

  • Check batches (optional)

  • Post goods issue

  • Create billing document

Business Benefits

  • Transfer statistical conditions from SD to Margin Analysis

  • Get improved reporting in Margin Analysis with better visibility

This scope item is excluded from the default activation.

Only customers who want to include statistical sales conditions in their Margin Analysis need to activate this scope item. Typical statistical sales conditions used for margin analysis include, but are not limited to, warranties, delivery costs, discounts, commissions, bonus, and others.
processes.name: Statistical Sales Conditions

Stock Management (5OD)

Overview

The scope item helps you to better manage your stock instruments, enabling you to automate labor-intensive processes, such as payment handling and accounting postings, giving you more time to focus on value-added activities. You can manage operational and accounting requirements.

The current scope covers the processes to create securities account and security class, and to purchase, bookkeep, and recognize dividends of and sell a stock transaction.

Key Process Flow

  • Create security account and class

  • Create stock purchase transaction

  • Set settlement status

  • Maintain and post cash dividend

  • Create and post corporate action

  • Perform period-end closing

  • Create stock sale transaction

  • Perform reporting

Business Benefits

  • Review the status for stock instruments easily

  • Support the management of stock, including creation of security class, security accounts and the transactions, payments, recognize dividend, and so on

  • Make better operational and strategic decisions using the comprehensive reporting and analysis tools

  • Improve internal operational compliance
