processes.description:
Warehouse Physical Inventory (3BX)

Overview

In this scope item, you can plan, conduct, and confirm regular counts of actual product quantities in the warehouse and compare the physical stock to the data in the system. You first create physical inventory documents for a chosen number of storage bins or products or based on cycle counting indicators. The cycle counting method is used to count products at regular intervals during a year. You can set up counting intervals based on cycle count indicators. After the documents are created and printed, you count the stock in the warehouse. You enter the count result in the system and review discrepancies in the system quantities. By posting the PI documents, you adjust the book inventory in the storage bins to align it with the physical inventory counts. The inventory may be recounted until final counts are accepted. Finally, inventory differences are posted to reconcile stocks in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

Key Process Flow

  • Variant 1: Create and print counting document

  • Variant 2: Create and print cycle counting document

  • Enter count results

  • Confirm inventory count results

  • Analyze and post differences

Business Benefits

  • Ensure an accurate accounting of the inventory in the warehouse

  • Leverage several physical inventory methods

  • Map your warehouse complex in the system down to a storage bin level

  • Improve visibility and control in warehouse processes

processes.description:
Warehouse Posting Changes (3BU)

Overview

With this scope item, you can make posting changes (for example, unrestricted to blocked stock) in the warehouse. Posting changes can be triggered in two different ways.

  • When an inventory management posting initiates a posting change, it generates an outbound delivery. This delivery is then distributed to the warehouse, recognized as a posting change. Based on this document, you can, for example, create warehouse tasks to move the blocked/quality stock to the clarification zone.

  • You can also trigger posting changes by selecting stock and changing the stock type with the help of the warehouse monitor. By doing this, a posting change is triggered, and warehouse tasks are created to move the selected stock to the appropriate storage type, if necessary.

Key Process Flow

  • Option 1: Inventory Management

    • Create posting change in inventory management

    • Create warehouse tasks for posting change and print warehouse task lists

  • Option 2: Warehouse

    • Creating posting change in warehouse and print warehouse task lists as required

  • Confirm warehouse tasks

Business Benefits

  • Change a certain material stock type

  • Control and record movements of goods in the warehouse

  • Map your warehouse complex in the system down to a storage bin level

  • Improve visibility and control in warehouse processes

processes.description:
Warehouse Production Integration (3DV)

Overview

With this business process, you can integrate the supply of products to production and the receipt of finished products from production into your warehouse. You first trigger the staging of material that is requested by production. This activity results in an outbound delivery that is distributed to the warehouse as an outbound delivery order (non-WM-managed production supply area). Further process steps such as the creation of warehouse tasks are initiated based on these documents. A warehouse operative moves the material to the production supply area and confirms the warehouse tasks accordingly. If the production storage location is not WM-managed, the goods issue must be posted for the outbound delivery to make the material available for consumption at the production storage location. Finally, the finished goods from production – to be stored in the warehouse – are received and moved to the final bin.

Key Process Flow

  • Material staging for production

    • Release production order

    • Material staging for production order

    • Create staging warehouse tasks

    • Confirm staging warehouse tasks

    • Post goods issue for staging

  • Confirm production operations for subassembly

  • Delivery-based goods receipt from production

    • Create inbound delivery for production order

    • Create handling unit

    • Post goods receipt

    • Create putaway warehouse tasks

    • Confirm putaway warehouse tasks

Business Benefits

  • Integrate warehouse execution with manufacturing operations

  • Manage stock in production on storage bin level, if required

  • Attach files (for example, pictures) to inbound deliveries and outbound delivery orders

  • Control and record movements of products and handling units in the warehouse

  • Map your warehouse complex in the system down to a storage bin level

  • Improve visibility and control in warehouse processes

processes.description:
Warehouse Production Integration with Synchronous Goods Receipt (5HO)

Overview

This scope item describes the integration of warehouse production with synchronous goods receipt, where the produced products can post goods receipts directly into the warehouse without involving delivery documents. With this business process, you can integrate the supply of products to production and the receipt of finished products from production into your warehouse. You first trigger the staging of material that is requested by production. This activity results in a posting change delivery (warehouse-managed production supply area). Further process steps (such as the creation of warehouse tasks) are initiated based on this document. A warehouse operative moves the material to the production supply area and confirms the warehouse tasks accordingly. The produced products can post goods receipts directly into the warehouse without involving delivery documents. Finally, the finished goods from production – to be stored in the warehouse – are moved to the final bin.

Key Process Flow

  • Material staging for production

    • Release production order

    • Staging the release order parts for production

    • Staging pick parts for production

    • Create staging warehouse tasks

    • Material staging with ad-hoc movements (optional)

    • Confirm staging warehouse tasks

  • Confirm production operations for subassembly

  • Goods receipt from production with synchronous goods movements

    • Post goods receipt for production orders (optional)

    • Display material document (optional)

    • Pack finished material (optional)

    • Create HU putaway warehouse task (optional)

    • Create product putaway warehouse tasks (optional)

    • Confirm putaway warehouse tasks

Business Benefits

  • Post goods receipt directly into the warehouse without involving delivery documents

  • Integrate warehouse execution with manufacturing operations

  • Manage stock in production on storage bin level, if necessary

  • Attach files (such as pictures) to inbound deliveries and outbound delivery orders

  • Control and record movements of products and handling units in the warehouse

  • Map your warehouse complex in the system down to a storage bin level

  • Improve visibility and control in warehouse processes

processes.description:
Warranty Claim Management – Customer Claim Processing (63Y)

Overview

This scenario enables you to create a warranty claim for a reimbursement request of a supplier (based on a performed repair).

In this scenario, you create a claim, validate it for completeness and eligibility for reimbursement, and determine the correct prices for material, labor activities, and so on.

Based on the validation support of the system, the claim analyst can make a transparent decision on the claim and perform the financial reimbursement to the customer.

Key Process Flow

  • Create claim

  • Validate and submit claim

  • Discard claim

  • Adjust claims

  • Perform formal validation

  • Perform content validation

  • Post claim

  • Reverse posting

  • Reject claim

  • Close claims

Business Benefits

  • Keep transparency on requested and approved (reimbursement) amounts of a claim with the versioning concept

  • Save money by only paying claims that have a legal ground and by only paying the appropriate (negotiated) prices or rates
processes.name: Warranty Claim Management – Customer Claim Processing

processes.description:
Warranty Claim Management – Supplier Recovery Processing (5HR)

Overview

This scenario enables you to create a warranty claim that can then be forwarded to the respective supplier for a reimbursement. The scenario covers the relevant steps starting with the creation of a claim (based on a performed repair), continuing with the validation for completeness, eligibility for reimbursement, and the finding of the correct prices for material, labor activities, and so on.

Once the information is sent to the supplier and their response is received, the scenario supports the transparent maintenance of values and the posting of the negotiated amount.

Key Process Flow

  • Create, validate, and adjust claims

  • Set parts return relevance and check execution

  • Send claim to supplier

  • Maintain supplier's response

  • Post claim

  • Reverse posting

  • Reject, cancel, and close claims

Business Benefits

  • Increase your supplier recovery rate by easily creating claim for repairs, using the already available information in your system (materials, prices, and so on)

  • Save time and increase supplier satisfaction by only raising and sending out valid claims that are likely to get paid (by validating the claims with regards to master data and eligibility)

  • Keep transparency on requested and reimbursed amounts with the versioning concept and directly post the respective amounts to the appropriate accounts
processes.name: Warranty Claim Management – Supplier Recovery Processing

processes.description:
Waste Management (60H)

Overview

This scope item supports waste generators in managing waste disposal processes across one or more enterprise locations. It includes:

  • Managing hazardous and nonhazardous waste from the point of creation within a plant

  • Supporting waste compliance officers and environmental managers in coordination of waste shipments locally or globally

  • Supporting production operators in requesting waste pickup and movement

  • Performing plausibility checks to ensure compliance with issued permits and registered waste

  • Creating waste transportation documents

  • Performing waste analytics

Key Process Flow

  • Establish a process for waste identification including waste characterization, waste streams definition, waste disposal channels, and waste registration

  • Build on-site waste process, plan shipments accordingly, and organize transports

  • Make payment and cost allocation faster and easier

  • Report in a flexible manner on waste types and quantities

Business Benefits

  • Support waste generators to comply with country- or region-specific legal requirements for generation, transport, disposal, tracking, and regulatory reporting of hazardous and nonhazardous waste.

  • Minimize the risks to lives and to the environment.

  • Help to reduce waste by creating full transparency on the end-to-end business process that results in waste minimization and sustainable waste disposal.

  • Provide an important input for a more and more circular economy.
processes.name: Waste Management

processes.description:
Wave Management in Warehousing (6NH)

Overview

This scope item allows you to run and optimize the process of creating picking warehouse tasks by using wave management to extend the warehouse outbound process. The process starts with the creation of waves via the schedule background job report, which combines items from the outbound deliveries based on certain criteria. The Warehouse Clerk (EWM) releases the picking waves by using the warehouse monitor. The system determines the location for picking the stock and allocates the stock to the warehouse task. You can also check the log history of wave and warehouse tasks using the warehouse monitor.

Key Process Flow

  • Schedule background job for wave generation

  • Simulate wave (optional)

  • Release wave

  • Display wave release log and warehouse task (optional)

Business Benefits

  • Combine warehouse request items into waves based on criteria such as activity area, route, or product

  • Define capacity constraints such as maximum weight and volume for wave creation

  • Define time attributes such as the cutoff time for a wave

  • Start picking warehouse requests in one wave at the same time, to improve warehouse efficiency
